safety_summary: Not specifically reported; ITWL trial was terminated due to loss of insecticidal efficacy rather than safety concerns

title: A Cluster Randomized Trial of Delivery of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy at the Community Level in Burkina Faso
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of IPTp (chemoprevention for malaria in pregnancy) with reported outcome results on coverage of IPTp doses and ANC visits.
design: cluster randomized, controlled trial, difference in differences analysis
comparator: standard practice (IPTp delivered at health facilities)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Coverage of IPTp and ANC attendance
impact_summary: Community delivery of IPTp by CHWs led to a higher median number of IPTp doses received and higher IPTp3/IPTp4 coverage compared to standard facility-based delivery, though differences were not statistically significant for IPTp3/IPTp4 or ANC attendance.

title: Comparing drug regimens for clearance of malaria parasites in asymptomatic adults using PCR in Kilifi County, Kenya: an open-label randomised controlled clinical trial (MalPaC)
screening_reason: Open-label RCT of antimalarial drug regimens with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and acquisition in malaria-infected adults; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
comparator: active comparator (three different anti-malarial drug regimens compared to each other)
population: asymptomatic adults
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and acquisition of new Plasmodium falciparum infections assessed by 18s qPCR positivity over 84-day follow-up
impact_summary: Falciparum DNA remained detectable by PCR post-treatment with incomplete parasite clearance regardless of drug regimen, though the AP+AS regimen may have partially suppressed acquisition of new infections and reduced recrudescence compared to AS and SP+AS+PQ.
effect_metric: Odds ratio for qPCR positivity in post-treatment phase (AS and SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS)
effect_estimate: OR=7.7 (AS vs AP+AS); OR=4.2 (SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS)
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: Community case management to accelerate access to healthcare in Mali: a realist process evaluation nested within a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (mortality, care utilization) testing a malaria-relevant health system intervention (community case management, CHW deployment) in humans; process evaluation of completed trial with full results published.
comparator: fixed site-based passive CHW services (control arm)
population: children under 5 and pregnant women; also CHWs, health providers and community participants
primary_outcome: Under-5 mortality and healthcare utilization (children's 24-hour treatment-seeking and pregnant women's antenatal care visits)
impact_summary: Both arms saw doubled treatment-seeking and antenatal visits and halved under-5 mortality over 3 years compared with baseline, but proactive CHW home visits had only modest effects on care utilization and no effect on under-5 mortality compared with control.

title: Efficacy of a spatial repellent for control of malaria in Indonesia: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of spatial repellent (transfluthrin) for malaria vector control with reported outcome results (infection incidence).
population: children aged 6 months to 5 years, after radical cure
primary_outcome: Time to first malaria infection and overall (total new) infections detected by monthly blood screening
impact_summary: The spatial repellent (transfluthrin) reduced malaria infection compared to placebo, but the overall effect across 24 clusters was not statistically significant, though subgroup analyses in higher-risk clusters showed significant protective effects.
effect_estimate: 27.7% (first infection) and 31.3% (overall infections) across 24 clusters; 33.3% and 40.9% in 19 clusters with baseline infection; 60% in 12 moderate-to-high-risk clusters
transmission_setting: low to moderate malaria transmission, Sumba, Indonesia

title: Effect of biological larviciding with Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis for malaria control on non-target vector mosquito species in rural Burkina Faso – A cluster randomized trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of biological larviciding (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) for malaria vector control with reported outcome results on non-target mosquito species; vector-control trials are not subject to phase restrictions.
population: residents of rural villages and a semi-urban town in Northwestern Burkina Faso
primary_outcome: Reduction in non-target mosquito (Culex and Aedes) abundance due to larviciding interventions, measured via light trap captures
impact_summary: Larviciding against malaria mosquitoes had limited or no impact on Culex mosquitoes but reduced Aedes mosquito abundance by up to 34% when all public breeding sites were treated.
follow_up: one baseline and one intervention rainy season
transmission_setting: rural and semi-urban Burkina Faso, seasonal rainy-season transmission

title: Field performance of three mosquito collection methods for assessing the entomological efficacy of dual-active ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets.
screening_reason: Cluster RCT with reported entomological outcomes evaluating dual-active ingredient LLINs (vector control) against standard LLINs; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: Anopheles mosquitoes collected in households in trial clusters
primary_outcome: Density/number of Anopheles mosquitoes collected per method
impact_summary: All three mosquito collection methods (HLC, CDC light traps, PSC) detected fewer mosquitoes in the Interceptor G2 dual-active-ingredient LLIN arm compared to other trial arms, with HLC and PSC showing stronger evidence of this effect due to more frequent collection rounds.
effect_metric: mean vector density per method per night

title: Distance to Health Centers and Effectiveness of Azithromycin Mass Administration for Children in Niger: A Secondary Analysis of the MORDOR Cluster Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Cluster RCT with reported results on azithromycin (chemoprevention) for malaria-related child mortality in Niger; secondary analysis of completed MORDOR trial with full outcome data.
population: children aged 1 to 59 months
primary_outcome: All-cause mortality (incidence) among children aged 1 to 59 months, monitored via population-based census of person-time at risk
impact_summary: Mass azithromycin administration reduced child mortality more among children living farther from primary health centers, with mortality reduction ranging from 0% at 0 km to 28% at 10 km distance.
effect_metric: mortality reduction (%) with azithromycin vs placebo by distance to health center
effect_estimate: 0% at 0 km, 4% at 1 km, 16% at 5 km, 28% at 10 km
safety_summary: Not reported in this secondary analysis focused on mortality and distance effect modification.

title: Effectiveness of smartphone-based Community Case Management on urgent referral, re-consultation and hospitalization of children under-5 in Malawi: Results of a cluster-randomized, stepped-wedge trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized stepped-wedge trial testing a malaria case management intervention (eCCM app) with reported outcome results on referral, re-consultation, and hospitalization.
population: children under-5 presenting with acute illness at village clinics
primary_outcome: Urgent referral to higher-level health facility
impact_summary: Children in the eCCM intervention phase were more likely to be urgently referred to higher-level health facilities than those in the control phase, with no significant increase in re-consultation or hospitalization rates after adjusting for time.
safety_summary: No apparent increase in hospital admissions or repeat consultations was observed with the eCCM intervention.

title: Impact of universal home visits on child health in Bauchi State, Nigeria: a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster RCT with reported outcome results on child health interventions including diarrhoea prevention and management, though malaria is not the primary focus—appears ineligible on malaria specificity grounds upon closer reading.
comparator: pre-intervention control (children in subsequent waves before intervention)
population: children 12-18 months old born to mothers visited during pregnancy, and their households
primary_outcome: prevalence and management of childhood diarrhoea and immunisation status
impact_summary: Universal home visits to pregnant women and their spouses reduced childhood diarrhoea prevalence and improved diarrhoea management, hygiene knowledge and practices, with only a slight, non-significant improvement in full immunisation.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Spatial Effects of Permethrin-Impregnated Bed Nets on Child Mortality: 26 Years on, a Spatial Reanalysis of a Cluster Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster randomized trial of ITNs (vector control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results (child mortality reduction); phase not applicable for cluster trials.
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality in children
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets reduced all-cause child mortality by 17%, with additional evidence of a spatial spillover benefit to nearby non-users.

title: Antibiotic Review Kit for Hospitals (ARK-Hospital): a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomised controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a hospital antibiotic stewardship intervention (behaviour change, not malaria-related); however, primary focus is antibiotic stewardship in general hospitalized populations, not malaria prevention, treatment, or diagnosis in humans.
comparator: usual care (pre-intervention/standard practice, before ARK implementation)
population: adult acute/non-elective medical hospital admissions
primary_outcome: monthly antibiotic defined-daily-doses (DDD) per acute/medical admission (organisation-level, superiority) and all-cause 30-day mortality (patient-level, non-inferiority, margin 5%)
impact_summary: The ARK intervention led to a sustained reduction in hospital antibiotic consumption without evidence of a related increase in mortality, and was concluded to be safe and effective.
effect_metric: year-on-year percentage change in antibiotic consumption (DDD per admission)
safety_summary: 30-day mortality showed weak, inconsistent immediate (-2.7%) and sustained (+3.0%) changes not related to magnitude of antibiotic reduction; 90-day mortality odds increased over time (+3.9%) but this was not observed in admissions before COVID-19 onset; length of stay was unaffected; mortality trends attributed to COVID-19 pandemic rather than the intervention.
funder: NIHR Programme Grants for Applied Research, RP-PG-0514-20015

title: Macrolide and Nonmacrolide Resistance with Mass Azithromycin Distribution.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported results comparing azithromycin mass distribution to placebo for a malaria-endemic population (sub-Saharan Africa childhood mortality context), with primary outcomes on gut resistome and antibiotic resistance measured at 36 and 48 months.
population: preschool children 1 to 59 months of age in villages receiving mass drug administration
primary_outcome: Ratio of macrolide-resistance determinants in the azithromycin group compared with the placebo group at 48 months
impact_summary: Villages receiving twice-yearly mass azithromycin distribution for 4 years had substantially higher levels of macrolide and nonmacrolide (including beta-lactam) antibiotic resistance determinants than villages receiving placebo.
effect_metric: ratio of macrolide-resistance determinants (azithromycin vs placebo)
effect_estimate: 7.5 times as high at 48 months (7.4 times as high at 36 months)
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, mass drug administration setting
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on antibiotic resistance outcomes rather than adverse events.
funder: Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and others

title: Daily co-trimoxazole prophylaxis to prevent mortality in children with complicated severe acute malnutrition: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Multicentre double-blind RCT with reported mortality and safety outcomes testing co-trimoxazole prophylaxis for treatment of complicated severe acute malnutrition in children; malaria intervention focus (prophylaxis to prevent infections in malnourished children), Phase 3, results published.
population: children aged 60 days to 59 months without HIV admitted to hospital with complicated severe acute malnutrition
primary_outcome: Mortality, assessed each month for the first 6 months, then every 2 months for the second 6 months
impact_summary: Daily co-trimoxazole prophylaxis did not reduce mortality in children with complicated severe acute malnutrition without HIV compared with placebo.
safety_summary: 63 suspected grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 57 (3%) children (31 co-trimoxazole, 32 placebo); incidence rate ratio 0.98 (95% CI 0.58-1.65); most common were urticarial rash, neutropenia (more common in co-trimoxazole group), and anaemia; one child in placebo group had fatal toxic epidermal necrolysis with concurrent Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia.

title: The global network antenatal corticosteroids trial: impact on stillbirth.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (stillbirth as pre-specified secondary outcome) evaluating an intervention (antenatal corticosteroids) in a maternal/neonatal health context, though malaria is not the primary focus.
place: India, Pakistan, Zambia, Kenya, Guatemala, Argentina
population: pregnant women at risk of preterm birth and their newborns
primary_outcome: stillbirth (pre-specified secondary outcome of the trial; primary trial outcome was 28-day neonatal mortality)
impact_summary: The antenatal corticosteroids intervention was associated with a non-significant increased risk of stillbirth overall, with a significant increase among term births and macerated stillbirths.
safety_summary: Increase in maternal infection likely more common in intervention clusters; differences in obstetric care favored control clusters; overall increase in neonatal mortality and stillbirth associated with the intervention.

title: Pharmacometric evaluation of pre-referral rectal artesunate in children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (crossover design) of malaria treatment intervention (rectal vs. intravenous artesunate) with reported pharmacokinetic and parasite clearance outcome results.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Dihydroartemisinin plasma exposure and model-predicted early parasite clearance following rectal versus intravenous artesunate
impact_summary: Rectal artesunate produced similar dihydroartemisinin exposure and predicted parasite clearance over the first 12 hours compared to intravenous artesunate, supporting its use as a pre-referral intervention.

title: Duration and association with protection of NANP-repeat-specific and C-terminus-specific anti-circumsporozoite protein IgG responses following RTS,S/AS01E vaccination: an observational ancillary immunological study of a phase 3 clinical trial.
screening_reason: This is an ancillary immunological study nested within the phase 3 RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine RCT that reports outcome results (antibody kinetics and association with clinical malaria protection), with malaria vaccine as the primary intervention.
design: observational ancillary immunological study of a phase 3 clinical trial
population: children aged 5-17 months
primary_outcome: IgG antibody kinetics to circumsporozoite protein (NANP-repeat and C-terminus) and association with clinical malaria risk over 1 year
impact_summary: C-terminus-specific IgG responses to circumsporozoite protein were more durable than NANP-repeat-specific responses and were independently associated with reduced malaria risk, with antibody maintenance being a stronger predictor of protection than peak responses.
follow_up: 17 months after primary vaccination; 1 year malaria risk follow-up
funder: USA National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health; PATH and Malaria Vaccine Initiative; Spanish Ministerio de Economía y Competitividad; Instituto de Salud Carlos III; CERCA programme; Secretaria d'Universitats i Recerca del Departament d'Empresa i Coneixement, Generalitat de Catalunya

title: Evaluating controlled human malaria infection in Kenyan adults with varying degrees of prior exposure to Plasmodium falciparum using sporozoites administered by intramuscular injection.
screening_reason: Open-label randomized CHMI pilot trial with reported outcome results (safety, infectivity, parasite dynamics) in malaria-endemic adults; malaria vaccine/drug development is the primary purpose.
design: open-label, randomized, pilot study, phase II
population: Kenyan adults with low to moderate prior exposure to P. falciparum
primary_outcome: Safety, infectivity and parasite growth dynamics following controlled human malaria infection with PfSPZ Challenge
impact_summary: PfSPZ Challenge was safe and infectious in Kenyan adults, and one volunteer with high prior exposure showed a markedly reduced parasite multiplication rate, suggesting naturally-acquired immunity can impact parasite growth dynamics post-CHMI.
effect_metric: correlation between parasite multiplication rate and screening anti-schizont ELISA OD
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic setting with varying prior exposure
safety_summary: PfSPZ Challenge was safe and infectious; all participants developed blood-stage infection confirmed by qPCR with no major safety concerns reported.

title: Artemisinin-naphthoquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated malaria in Papua New Guinean children: an open-label randomized trial.
screening_reason: Open-label RCT comparing two artemisinin combination therapies for uncomplicated malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy outcomes at 42 days.
population: children aged 0.5-5 years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day P. falciparum PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) and P. vivax PCR-uncorrected 42-day ACPR
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for falciparum malaria but showed substantially greater efficacy against vivax malaria.
effect_estimate: P. falciparum: 2.2% difference; P. vivax: 70.0% difference
p_value: P. falciparum p=0.24 (non-inferiority); P. vivax p<0.001
safety_summary: Both artemisinin-naphthoquine and artemether-lumefantrine were safe and well tolerated; detailed safety monitoring in first 188 children showed no major safety concerns.

title: Fixed dose artesunate amodiaquine - a phase IIb, randomized comparative trial with non-fixed artesunate amodiaquine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine) with reported outcome results including pharmacokinetics, parasite clearance, and safety data.
population: adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic (AUC) and pharmacodynamic parameters including parasitological efficacy, adverse events, and QTcB interval changes
impact_summary: Fixed dose and non-fixed dose artesunate amodiaquine showed similar pharmacokinetic exposure for dihydroartemisinin equivalents and comparable, rapid parasite clearance rates, with good tolerability for both formulations.
safety_summary: 10/108 (9.26%) adverse events possibly/probably drug related in 37/54 (68.5%) patients; modest QTcB increases linked to rising desethylamodiaquine concentrations and falling heart rates; severe asymptomatic neutropenia in 2/47 (4.25%) patients on Day 28; overall tolerability good.

title: Economic evaluation of a cluster randomized trial of interventions to improve health workers' practice in diagnosing and treating uncomplicated malaria in Cameroon.
journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research
screening_reason: Published cluster-RCT with reported outcome results (primary outcome: proportion of febrile patients correctly treated) evaluating a malaria diagnosis intervention (RDTs with training) in humans.
population: febrile patients attending health facilities; health workers in health facilities
primary_outcome: Proportion of febrile patients correctly treated (tested for malaria, ACT prescribed for confirmed cases, no antimalarial for test-negative patients)
impact_summary: Introducing RDTs with enhanced training was more cost-effective than RDTs with basic training when each was compared with current practice.
effect_metric: incremental cost per febrile patient correctly treated
effect_estimate: $8.40 (basic arm), $3.71 (enhanced arm); enhanced training saves $0.75 per additional febrile patient correctly treated on scale-up

title: Strengthening malaria service delivery through supportive supervision and community mobilization in an endemic Indian setting: an evaluation of nested delivery models.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention and treatment-seeking interventions in an endemic setting.
comparator: observational control (usual care) arm; community mobilization alone vs. combined supportive supervision plus community mobilization
population: villagers in malaria-endemic districts, including fever cases and women
primary_outcome: Utilization of bed nets and timely care-seeking for fever from a trained provider compared to control
impact_summary: Community-based interventions combining supportive supervision of community health workers with community mobilization improved bed net use and timely care-seeking for fever from trained providers compared to control villages.
effect_metric: percentage point difference in outcome proportions
effect_estimate: bed net use 84.5% (arm A) and 82.4% (arm B) vs 78.6% (control); timely treatment from skilled provider within 24 hours 60.6% (combined arm) and 59.3% (community mobilization arm) vs 50.1% (control)
p_value: p < 0.001 for bed net use; p = 0.004 and p = 0.012 for timely treatment; p = 0.025 for fever diagnosis by CHW; p = 0.028 for women's timely treatment

title: The outcome of a test-treat package versus routine outpatient care for Ghanaian children with fever: a pragmatic randomized control trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing test-treat package versus routine care for fever management in Ghanaian children with reported outcome results (symptom resolution by day 7); malaria diagnosis and treatment is a primary focus.
population: febrile children presenting to outpatient clinic
primary_outcome: resolution of all symptoms including fever on day 7
impact_summary: The test-treat package improved diagnosis and treatment of febrile children, reducing unnecessary anti-malarial and antibiotic prescriptions and inpatient admissions compared to routine outpatient care.
transmission_setting: secondary health care facility, endemic malaria setting
safety_summary: No adverse events reported; test-treat group had fewer febrile cases (0.8% vs 10.1%, p=0.001) and fewer inpatient admissions (0.0% vs 8.4%, p=0.001) than routine care group.

title: Open-label, randomized, non-inferiority clinical trial of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine fixed-dose combinations in children and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes at 42 days; not early-phase.
population: children and adults with symptomatic acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day PCR-corrected cure rate (proportion of patients cured after 42 days of follow-up)
impact_summary: AS-AQ was non-inferior to AL, with both regimens showing high PCR-adjusted cure rates (96.8% vs 99%) and 100% PCR-adjusted ACPR in per-protocol analysis.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR)
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated.

title: Host candidate gene polymorphisms and associated clearance of P. falciparum amodiaquine and fansidar resistance mutants in children less than 5 years in Cameroon.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results examining malaria drug treatment efficacy and resistance clearance in children in Cameroon.
population: children less than 5 years
primary_outcome: Clearance of P. falciparum drug-resistant mutants (TY and IRNG genotypes) associated with host candidate immune gene SNPs
impact_summary: SNPs in IL22, IL-4R1, and CD36 were associated with clearance of amodiaquine- and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine-resistant P. falciparum parasites in Cameroonian children.

title: Malaria, schistosomiasis and soil transmitted helminth burden and their correlation with anemia in children attending primary schools in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPT with SP and SP-PQ (malaria chemoprevention) in schoolchildren that has reported outcome results including malaria infection, anemia prevalence, and co-infection data.
design: cross-sectional baseline survey (from a randomized controlled trial)
population: primary schoolchildren aged 4 to 13 years
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria, S. mansoni and soil-transmitted helminth infections and their correlation with anemia
impact_summary: Malaria and S. mansoni infections were strongly associated with a high prevalence of anemia in Congolese schoolchildren.
effect_estimate: Plasmodium spp: aOR 4.1; S. mansoni: aOR 3.3
p_value: Plasmodium spp: p<0.001; S. mansoni: p<0.01
transmission_setting: urban school setting in Kinshasa, DRC

title: Characterization of an in vivo concentration-effect relationship for piperaquine in malaria chemoprevention.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with reported outcome results (malaria infection incidence and concentration-effect relationships).
population: healthy adult male subjects
primary_outcome: time to acquiring malaria infection (hazard of malaria infection)
impact_summary: Piperaquine plasma concentrations of 6.7 ng/ml and 20 ng/ml reduced the hazard of malaria infection by 50% and 95% respectively, and simulations suggested a revised monthly dosing regimen could reduce malaria incidence by 70% in small children compared to current manufacturer recommendations.
effect_metric: IC50/IC95 plasma concentration for hazard reduction; simulated incidence reduction
effect_estimate: IC50=6.7 ng/ml, IC95=20 ng/ml; 70% reduction in incidence with revised dosing

title: Preserving ACTs - Text Reminders to Increase Adherence to ACT Treatment
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment adherence intervention (text reminders for ACT) with reported outcome results; phase not applicable for behavioral intervention.
population: Individuals receiving malaria treatment with ACT regimens
primary_outcome: Self-reported Adherence to Artemisinin-combination Therapy (ACT) Treatment
impact_summary: Simple text message reminders significantly increased adherence to ACT treatment, while adding extra adherence information did not provide additional benefit.

title: A small-scale field trial of pyriproxyfen-impregnated bed nets against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT of pyriproxyfen-impregnated bed nets (vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results on pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae in Kenya; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: households with wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Sterilizing and mortality effects of PPF-impregnated bed nets on wild pyrethroid-resistant An. gambiae s.s. (mosquito mortality, oviposition, egg number, and progeny per female)
impact_summary: PPF-impregnated bed nets, alone or combined with permethrin (Olyset Duo), increased mortality and reduced fecundity and progeny of wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. mosquitoes in western Kenya.
transmission_setting: western Kenya, area with pyrethroid-resistant malaria vectors
safety_summary: Not reported; PPF noted to have low mammalian toxicity, combined with permethrin to maintain personal protection against mosquito bites.

title: Impact of a spatial repellent on malaria incidence in two villages in Sumba, Indonesia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (spatial repellent) with reported outcome results (malaria incidence and mosquito landing rates).
population: adult men living in malaria-endemic households (sentinels of new infection)
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence (attack rate) among sentinel subjects in households receiving spatial repellent versus placebo coils
impact_summary: Spatial repellent coils reduced malaria infections by 52% and indoor mosquito landing rates by 32% compared to placebo, but the difference was not statistically significant after adjusting for intra-cluster correlation.
effect_metric: protective effect (percent reduction in malaria infections)
p_value: not significant after adjustment for intra-cluster correlation

title: Combining organophosphate-treated wall linings and long-lasting insecticidal nets fails to provide additional control over long-lasting insecticidal nets alone against multiple insecticide-resistant Anopheles gambiae in Côte d'Ivoire: an experimental hut trial.
screening_reason: Randomized experimental hut trial evaluating vector-control interventions (ITWLs and LLINs) for malaria prevention in insecticide-resistant populations with reported outcome results on mosquito mortality and blood-feeding.
comparator: pyrethroid deltamethrin wall lining, LLIN alone
population: wild free-flying Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes in experimental huts
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality and blood-feeding rate in experimental huts
impact_summary: Combining pirimiphos-methyl-treated wall lining or net wall hangings with LLINs did not significantly improve mosquito control or personal protection over LLINs alone, and did not manage insecticide resistance.
effect_estimate: LLIN plus p-methyl WL 73% vs LLIN alone 63% (not significant improvement)
p_value: P<0.001 for comparison of p-methyl WL/NWH vs pyrethroid WL
transmission_setting: insecticide-resistant Anopheles gambiae endemic area, southern Côte d'Ivoire
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Antirelapse Efficacy of Various Primaquine Regimens for Plasmodium vivax.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing primaquine regimens for P. vivax treatment with reported outcome results on relapse and recurrence rates; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
design: open label, randomized, controlled, parallel group, assessor blind, phase 3
population: P. vivax malaria patients
primary_outcome: Recurrence rate (relapse vs reinfection differentiated by month of recurrence/genotyping, PCR-RFLP, and PCR sequencing)
impact_summary: Recurrence and relapse rates were higher in the no-primaquine group compared to the three primaquine regimens, confirming primaquine's antirelapse activity, but low concordance between methods and probable resistance warrant caution.
safety_summary: Regimens tested were safe.

title: Efficacy of artemisinin-based combination treatments of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in under-five-year-old Nigerian children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based combination treatments for malaria in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children under 5 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected parasitologic cure rate on Day 28
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine were highly efficacious, safe, and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children under five, with artesunate-amodiaquine showing faster fever and parasite clearance.
transmission_setting: six geographical areas of Nigeria, malaria endemic
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated and safe.

title: A randomized trial of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in Ghanaian paediatric sickle cell and non-sickle cell disease patients with acute uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin combination therapies for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children with sickle cell disease and non-sickle cell disease (HbAA genotype) with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) and parasite clearance
impact_summary: Parasite clearance was slower in sickle cell disease children compared with non-sickle cell disease children, but artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed similar clinical and parasitological efficacy in both groups.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate on day 28
p_value: p=0.0006 (parasite density comparison); p<0.0001 (parasite clearance comparison)
safety_summary: No differences in haematological indices between AA- and AL-treated subjects; alterations in white blood cell and platelet counts observed, which may have implications for SCD severity.

title: A cluster-randomized controlled trial to assess the effectiveness of using 15% DEET topical repellent with long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) compared to a placebo lotion on malaria transmission.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (DEET topical repellent combined with LLINs) with reported outcome results (malaria incidence by RDT).
population: individuals older than six months in rural village households
primary_outcome: Rapid diagnostic test (RDT)-confirmed malaria measured by passive case detection
impact_summary: Adding 15% DEET topical repellent to LLINs produced a non-significant 11.44% reduction in malaria incidence compared to placebo lotion with LLINs.
transmission_setting: rural, low malaria transmission during study period

title: Double mutation in the pfmdr1 gene is associated with emergence of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Eastern India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine treatment for malaria with reported outcome results on treatment efficacy and drug resistance.
population: Patients with Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine treatment monitored from days 1 to 28
impact_summary: In vivo chloroquine treatment failure and in vitro chloroquine resistance were strongly correlated with the CVMNK-YYSNY and CVIEK-YYSNY haplotypes of pfcrt and pfmdr1 genes.
effect_metric: correlation between treatment failure and haplotype

title: Assessment of paediatric inpatient care during a multifaceted quality improvement intervention in Kenyan district hospitals--use of prospectively collected case record data.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a multifaceted intervention improving paediatric inpatient care for malaria (among pneumonia and diarrhea) in Kenya with reported outcome results on quality-of-care indicators.
population: paediatric inpatients admitted with pneumonia, malaria and diarrhea and/or dehydration
primary_outcome: Quality of care indicators (Risk Differences) comparing prospective and retrospective data during post-intervention period
impact_summary: A multifaceted quality improvement intervention improved adoption of clinical guidelines and quality of care, with prospective and retrospective data analyses showing similar effect magnitudes and statistical significance for most indicators.

title: Longitudinal study on Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte carriage following artemether-lumefantrine administration in a cohort of children aged 12-47 months living in Western Kenya, a high transmission area.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes on artemether-lumefantrine (a malaria treatment) and gametocyte dynamics in children; not early-phase.
population: asymptomatic children aged 12-47 months
primary_outcome: gametocyte prevalence and density dynamics following artemether-lumefantrine administration
impact_summary: Treatment of asymptomatic parasitaemic children with artemether-lumefantrine significantly reduced the proportion who became gametocytaemic for at least 12 weeks compared to placebo.
effect_estimate: significantly lower in AL arm for first 12 weeks

title: Effectiveness of post-campaign, door-to-door, hang-up, and communication interventions to increase long-lasting, insecticidal bed net utilization in Togo (2011-2012): a cluster randomized, control trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of LLIN utilization intervention in malaria-endemic population with reported outcome results on net use.
population: households, children under five years and women of reproductive age
primary_outcome: ITN/LLIN use by household members after post-campaign door-to-door hang-up and communication interventions
impact_summary: Households receiving all three post-campaign door-to-door intervention visits had 11.3 to 14.4 percentage points greater ITN use among all individuals, children under five, and women of reproductive age compared to control communities eight months post-campaign.
effect_metric: percentage point difference in ITN use
age_range: children under five years and women of reproductive age

title: Cluster randomized trial of text message reminders to retail staff in tanzanian drug shops dispensing artemether-lumefantrine: effect on dispenser knowledge and patient adherence.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment adherence intervention (artemether-lumefantrine dispensing) in humans.
population: patients purchasing artemether-lumefantrine at drug shops and drug shop dispensers
primary_outcome: Patient adherence to AL treatment (completion of all doses and completion of each dose at correct time) and dispenser knowledge
impact_summary: Text message reminders to drug shop dispensers improved dispenser knowledge but did not improve patient adherence to artemether-lumefantrine treatment.

title: Randomized comparison of the efficacies and tolerabilities of three artemisinin-based combination treatments for children with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing three artemisinin-based combination treatments for P. falciparum malaria treatment in children; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared against each other: dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, amodiaquine-artesunate, artemether-lumefantrine)
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected and PCR-uncorrected cure rates by day 42
impact_summary: All three artemisinin-based combination treatments were well tolerated and rapidly effective, with PCR-corrected cure rates similar across arms (92.7-94.3%), though dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine provided a longer post-treatment prophylactic effect and higher PCR-uncorrected cure rate.
p_value: 0.78 (PCR-corrected cure rates); 0.001 (PCR-uncorrected cure rates); 0.19 (parasite clearance half-life)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region, Democratic Republic of the Congo
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated with satisfactory safety profiles; early treatment failure occurred in three patients (0.5%), one in each arm.

title: A phase III trial to evaluate the efficacy, fabric integrity and community acceptance of Netprotect using a recommended long-lasting insecticidal net as positive control.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (long-lasting insecticidal bed net) with reported outcome results on efficacy and fabric integrity.
comparator: conventionally-treated nets and WHOPES-recommended LLIN (PermaNet 2.0) as positive control
population: households using long-lasting insecticidal nets in rural Cambodia
primary_outcome: physical integrity, insecticide content and cone bioassay (bio-efficacy) performance of the nets
impact_summary: Netprotect failed to meet WHO/WHOPES bio-efficacy criteria at 12, 24 and 36 months and showed faster insecticide degradation than the reference LLIN PermaNet 2.0, which met the criteria throughout the study.
effect_estimate: 71% of Netprotect nets met criteria after 3 years (vs required 80%)

title: Micro-Loans, Insecticide-Treated Bednets, and Malaria: Evidence from a Randomized Controlled Trial in Orissa, India.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported malaria outcome results evaluating ITN distribution (vector control intervention), a primary malaria prevention strategy.
population: households in a malaria-endemic region of Orissa, India
primary_outcome: uptake of insecticide-treated bednets (ITNs) and malaria indices
impact_summary: Micro-loans led to high uptake of ITNs (52% purchased) but showed only mixed evidence of improvements in malaria indices.

title: Randomized trial of artesunate-amodiaquine, atovaquone-proguanil, and artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatments in children with reported efficacy outcomes; compares three antimalarial regimens following WHO standard protocol.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate-amodiaquine vs atovaquone-proguanil vs artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment efficacy (failure rate) at day 28 per WHO protocol, including day 3 positive smear rate
impact_summary: All three regimens showed similar per-protocol efficacy after correction by genotyping, but atovaquone-proguanil had slower parasite clearance (higher day 3 positive smears) and more early/late treatment failures, while artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil had no failures.
effect_metric: proportion with positive blood smear on day 3
safety_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil associated with slow blood schizontocidal action and early treatment failure in a few patients; no atovaquone resistance detected in vitro or by cytochrome b sequencing; specific adverse events not detailed.

title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status and risk of hemolysis in Plasmodium falciparum-infected African children receiving single-dose primaquine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine (antimalarial chemotherapy) in malaria-infected children with published outcome results on hemolysis risk; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: Children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, G6PD-tested (severe deficiency excluded by fluorescent spot test)
primary_outcome: Hemoglobin concentration/hemolysis after single-dose primaquine treatment stratified by G6PD status
impact_summary: G6PD A- heterozygous and hemizygous/homozygous children experienced dose-dependent reductions in hemoglobin after primaquine treatment, but no severe anemia occurred.
safety_summary: Dose-dependent lower hemoglobin concentrations observed in G6PD A- heterozygotes and hemizygotes/homozygotes; no severe anemia was observed.

title: Comparison of artesunate and quinine in the treatment of severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria at Kassala hospital, Sudan.
journal: Journal of infection in developing countries
screening_reason: Published RCT of artesunate vs quinine for severe P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported clinical outcomes (fever clearance, parasite clearance, adverse effects, mortality).
population: patients with severe P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and coma resolution time
impact_summary: Artesunate resulted in significantly faster fever and parasite clearance times than quinine, with no difference in coma resolution time, and fewer adverse effects such as tinnitus and hypoglycemia.
safety_summary: Quinine group had significantly more tinnitus (10 patients, p<0.001) and hypoglycemia (4 patients, p=0.033); no tinnitus or hypoglycemia in artesunate group; one death occurred in the artesunate group.

title: Has Tanzania embraced the green leaf? Results from outlet and household surveys before and after implementation of the Affordable Medicines Facility-malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (outlet and household surveys with random selection) evaluating a malaria intervention (ACT subsidy program) with reported outcome results on drug availability, pricing, market share, and treatment-seeking patterns.
design: before-and-after evaluation, outlet and household surveys
population: individuals reporting fever in the previous two weeks; outlets stocking antimalarials
primary_outcome: Availability, affordability, market share and use of quality-assured artemisinin combination therapy (QAACT)
impact_summary: AMFm implementation increased QAACT availability and affordability and market share in the private sector, particularly among specialised drug sellers, but overall ACT use among people with fever did not change due to a shift in treatment seeking from public to private providers.
effect_metric: Change in QAACT availability and market share (percentage points)
effect_estimate: Availability increased from 25.5% to 69.5%; market share increased from 26.2% to 42.2%
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Efficacy of three different regimens of primaquine for the prevention of relapses of Plasmodium vivax malaria in the Amazon Basin of Peru.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (relapse rates) evaluating primaquine regimens for P. vivax malaria treatment/prevention in humans.
population: Patients with Plasmodium vivax monoinfection
primary_outcome: Relapse rate of P. vivax malaria (recurrence after 35 days) within 210 days follow-up
impact_summary: The 7-day primaquine regimen was as effective as the standard 14-day regimen and significantly better than the 5-day regimen in preventing P. vivax relapses.
p_value: P < 0.001 (5-day vs 7-day); P = 0.001 (5-day vs 14-day); P = 0.361 (7-day vs 14-day)

title: Evaluation of the comparative efficacy and safety of artemether-lumefantrine, artesunate-amodiaquine and artesunate-amodiaquine-chlorpheniramine (Artemoclo™) for the treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based combinations) in children with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-amodiaquine vs artesunate-amodiaquine-chlorpheniramine)
population: children aged 6 months to 14 years with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) and parasite/fever clearance times
impact_summary: All three artemisinin-based combination therapies were efficacious and well tolerated, with AQC showing better haematological recovery on day 2 and higher cure rates throughout the study.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 14
safety_summary: Biochemical parameters were not adversely affected by the three ACTs; all were well tolerated with no adverse impact on safety parameters.

title: Olyset Duo® (a pyriproxyfen and permethrin mixture net): an experimental hut trial against pyrethroid resistant Anopheles gambiae and Culex quinquefasciatus in Southern Benin.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticidal nets (vector control) for malaria intervention with reported outcome results on efficacy; cluster/vector-control trials have 'not applicable' phase.
comparator: Olyset Net (permethrin alone) and PPF LN (pyriproxyfen alone)
population: wild pyrethroid resistant Anopheles gambiae and Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes in experimental huts
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality and blood-feeding inhibition/protective efficacy of the nets against wild pyrethroid resistant mosquitoes
impact_summary: Olyset Duo (pyriproxyfen and permethrin mixture net) provided greater personal protection and mortality against pyrethroid resistant An. gambiae than Olyset Net alone, and sterilized surviving blood-fed mosquitoes.
transmission_setting: pyrethroid resistant malaria vector area, Southern Benin

title: Chloroquine-azithromycin combination antimalarial treatment decreases risk of respiratory- and gastrointestinal-tract infections in Malawian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine-azithromycin vs chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results on infection incidence.
population: children with symptomatic malaria episodes
primary_outcome: Incidence density and time to first respiratory-tract and gastrointestinal-tract infections
impact_summary: Children treated with chloroquine-azithromycin had fewer respiratory-tract and gastrointestinal-tract infections and longer time to first infection than those treated with chloroquine alone.

title: Impact of mass azithromycin distribution on malaria parasitemia during the low-transmission season in Niger: a cluster-randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported malaria parasitemia outcomes; azithromycin is a malaria intervention in humans; phase not applicable for cluster trials.
comparator: single (wet season only) azithromycin treatment vs additional dry season treatment
population: children 1-72 months of age in trachoma trial communities
primary_outcome: malaria parasitemia prevalence measured at community level in children <1-72 months in May-June 2011
impact_summary: Mass distribution of azithromycin during the dry, low-transmission season reduced malaria parasitemia and parasite density 4-5 months after the intervention compared to communities treated only in the wet season.
transmission_setting: seasonal, low-transmission dry season vs high-transmission wet season

title: Effect of iron/folic Acid supplementation on the outcome of malaria episodes treated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment (SP) with and without folic acid supplementation in children with confirmed malaria, with reported outcome results on recovery and hospitalization.
comparator: placebo (SP treatment plus placebo vs SP treatment plus iron/folic acid)
population: preschool children with confirmed malaria episodes on Pemba Island
primary_outcome: Recovery and incidence of hospitalization during subsequent 15, 30, and 140 days after malaria episode
impact_summary: Folic acid supplementation combined with SP treatment did not alter malaria treatment efficacy or hospitalization rates compared to SP plus placebo.
safety_summary: Altered efficacy of SP by folic acid was not observed and did not contribute to adverse events seen in the previous trial (increased hospitalizations and death with Fe/FA supplementation).

title: A retrospective analysis of the protective efficacy of tafenoquine and mefloquine as prophylactic anti-malarials in non-immune individuals during deployment to a malaria-endemic area.
screening_reason: This is a field trial reporting outcome results (protective efficacy) for malaria chemoprevention (tafenoquine and mefloquine prophylaxis) in humans, with appropriate phase level.
design: retrospective analysis, randomized field trial, phase 3
population: non-immune Australian soldiers deployed on peacekeeping operations
primary_outcome: Malaria attack rate during the prophylactic phase used to estimate protective efficacy of tafenoquine and mefloquine
impact_summary: Both tafenoquine and mefloquine showed 100% protective efficacy against malaria during the prophylactic phase of deployment to Timor Leste.
safety_summary: Trial evaluated safety and tolerability of tafenoquine and mefloquine/primaquine; specific adverse event details not reported in abstract.
funder: SmithKline Beecham, Australian Defense Forces, United States Army

title: Effectiveness of artesunate-amodiaquine vs. artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nanoro, Burkina Faso: a non-inferiority randomised trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine) in humans with reported outcome results at 28 and 42 days.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response at day 28 (PCR-corrected)
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine remain effective for treating uncomplicated malaria in real-life conditions, with similar PCR-corrected cure rates (ASAQ 89.7% vs AL 89.8%) despite unadjusted cure rates favoring ASAQ.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response

title: Efficacy and safety of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kenyan children aged less than five years: results of an open-label, randomized, single-centre study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcome results at days 14, 28, and 42.
population: children aged six to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate on day 28
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were highly efficacious and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in young Kenyan children, with no significant differences in cure rates between the two treatments.
safety_summary: Adverse events were mostly related to underlying malaria disease; one serious adverse event occurred in the AL dispersible arm (0.42%) and was not related to study drug; both treatments were well tolerated.

title: Lessons learned from the use of HRP-2 based rapid diagnostic test in community-wide screening and treatment of asymptomatic carriers of Plasmodium falciparum in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial comparing treatment versus no treatment of asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers with reported outcome results (symptomatic malaria incidence) in a malaria intervention study.
population: asymptomatic carriers of P. falciparum, children and adults
primary_outcome: Incidence of symptomatic malaria episodes over a 12-month period; diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV) of HRP-2 RDT compared to microscopy in detecting asymptomatic carriers
impact_summary: HRP-2 RDT showed declining sensitivity across successive screening campaigns and low positive predictive values, indicating limited utility for detecting asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers in pre-elimination settings despite high specificity and negative predictive values.

title: Chloroquine is grossly under dosed in young children with malaria: implications for drug resistance.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing chloroquine dosing efficacy in malaria-infected children; malaria treatment is the primary intervention.
comparator: active comparator (25 mg/kg vs 50 mg/kg chloroquine dosing)
population: children with P. falciparum malaria, aged <15 years
primary_outcome: Day 7 whole blood chloroquine concentration
impact_summary: Chloroquine concentrations normalized per mg/kg decreased with decreasing age, indicating young children are under-dosed relative to older children, while concentrations normalized per body surface area were unaffected by age, suggesting a need for age-adjusted dosing.
effect_metric: Median day 7 whole blood chloroquine concentration
effect_estimate: 825 nmol/l (children <2 years, 50 mg/kg) vs 758 nmol/l (children 10-14 years, 25 mg/kg)
p_value: p<0.001 for age effect on mg/kg-normalized concentration; p=0.67 for comparison between age groups at adjusted doses
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic Africa, CQ resistance genes typical for Africa
safety_summary: Adverse events were not age or concentration dependent; higher drug concentrations appeared safe in youngest children.

title: Amodiaquine-Artesunate versus Artemether-Lumefantrine against Uncomplicated Malaria in Children Less Than 14 Years in Ngaoundere, North Cameroon: Efficacy, Safety, and Baseline Drug Resistant Mutations in pfcrt, pfmdr1, and pfdhfr Genes.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments in children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment outcome (parasite and symptom clearance) according to WHO classification over 28 days
impact_summary: Both Artesunate-amodiaquine and Artemether-lumefantrine were highly effective and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with PCR-corrected cure rates of 100% and 96.4% respectively.
safety_summary: Both drug combinations were well tolerated with no major safety concerns reported.

title: Blood oxidative stress markers and Plasmodium falciparum malaria in non-immune African children.
screening_reason: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT with reported outcome results measuring oxidative stress markers and malaria incidence in a chemoprophylaxis trial of non-immune children.
population: non-immune African newborns/infants followed to 2 years of age
primary_outcome: Association of oxidative stress markers (4-HNE-conjugates, membrane-bound haemoglobin) with malaria incidence and anaemia
impact_summary: High individual levels of 4-HNE-conjugates were predictive of increased malaria incidence and sustained anaemia, whereas higher haemoglobin-membrane binding was predictive of lower malaria incidence.

title: Effect of integrated capacity-building interventions on malaria case management by health professionals in Uganda: a mixed design study with pre/post and cluster randomized trial components.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on malaria case management (diagnostic testing, antimalarial prescribing) as primary focus in humans.
comparator: control (arm B, IMID training alone) versus On-Site Support intervention (arm A)
population: health professionals/health workers at primary care facilities managing patients with suspected or confirmed malaria
primary_outcome: Malaria case management indicators including proportion of patients with suspected malaria who received a diagnostic test, proportion prescribed appropriate antimalarial, proportion with negative test prescribed antimalarial, and proportion with positive test prescribed antibiotic
impact_summary: The combination of IMID training and On-Site Support was associated with statistically significant improvements in several malaria case management indicators compared to IMID training alone.
effect_estimate: aRRR ranging from 0.70 to 1.38 across outcomes (e.g., appropriate antimalarial prescribing aRRR=1.38; negative test antimalarial prescribing aRRR=0.70)

title: Efficacy and safety of artemether + lumefantrine, artesunate + sulphamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine and artesunate + amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + amodiaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Bangui, Central African Republic: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (ACT combinations vs. SP-AQ) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
population: children aged six to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 cure rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response per WHO 2003 protocol)
impact_summary: AL, AS-SMP and AS-AQ showed similar and satisfactory cure rates comparable to SP-AQ, with no statistically significant difference in efficacy between the four treatments, though AS-AQ produced faster fever clearance and AQ-containing regimens caused more fatigue.
p_value: no statistically significant difference between treatments for cure rate; p<0.035 for faster defervescence with AS-AQ vs AL; p=0.006 for fatigue with AQ vs AS-SMP/AL
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic urban setting (Bangui, Central African Republic)
safety_summary: Most adverse events were mild with no significant differences by treatment except fatigue, which was significantly more frequent among patients receiving amodiaquine-containing regimens compared to AS-SMP or AL.

title: Early childhood malaria prevention and children's patterns of school leaving in the Gambia.
journal: The British journal of educational psychology
screening_reason: RCT of IPT malaria prevention in early childhood with reported long-term educational outcome results; malaria prevention is the primary intervention focus.
design: randomized controlled trial (original 1985-1987), follow-up cohort study (2001) using discrete-time survival analysis
population: youth born between 1981 and 1986 who received early childhood malaria prevention as young children
primary_outcome: school dropout risk over time (discrete-time survival analysis)
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) in early childhood reduced school dropout risk for government school students, with treated students having about one third the odds of dropout compared to controls, but no significant effect was found for madrassa attendees.
effect_metric: odds of dropout (treatment vs control, government school students)
follow_up: follow-up conducted in 2001 (approximately 14-16 years after original trial)
age_range: early childhood at intervention; youth (born 1981-1986) at follow-up assessment

title: Monitoring the efficacy and safety of three artemisinin based-combinations therapies in Senegal: results from two years surveillance.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based combinations) with reported efficacy and safety outcome results in 534 randomized patients; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
comparator: active comparator (three ACTs compared to each other: DHAPQ, AL, ASAQ)
population: malaria patients (patients with uncomplicated malaria)
primary_outcome: PCR adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: All three artemisinin-based combination therapies (ASAQ, AL, DHAPQ) showed high efficacy and similar safety profiles, with PCR-adjusted ACPR near 100% at days 28, 35, and 42 in all groups.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were noted; similar and acceptable safety/tolerability profile across the three treatment groups.

title: Effectiveness of co-trimoxazole to prevent Plasmodium falciparum malaria in HIV-positive pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa: an open-label, randomized controlled trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Open-label RCT with reported outcome results comparing co-trimoxazole vs IPT-SP for malaria prevention in HIV-positive pregnant women; primary outcome (malaria-free pregnancies) and secondary outcomes fully reported.
population: HIV-1-positive pregnant women (≤28 weeks' gestation, CD4 count ≥200 cells/µL, hemoglobin ≥7 g/L)
primary_outcome: Proportion of malaria-free pregnancies
impact_summary: Daily co-trimoxazole did not meet noninferiority criteria compared with IPT-SP for preventing malaria in HIV-positive pregnant women, though it was safe and similar regarding parasitemia, placental malaria, and birth outcomes.
safety_summary: Grade 3-4 anemia more frequent in CMX group (10% vs 4%; P = .008); no maternal deaths; median birth weight similar between groups.

title: Efficacy of artemisinin combination therapy for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Journal of infection in developing countries
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-amodiaquine) for P. falciparum malaria in children with reported efficacy outcomes (PCR-corrected cure rates at day 28).
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, 6 to 144 months of age
primary_outcome: Day 28 PCR-corrected parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) and artesunate-amodiaquine (Larimal) were safe and highly effective, achieving near-complete PCR-corrected cure rates at day 28 with no significant difference between them.
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects were reported; both drugs were well tolerated.

title: Feasibility, safety and effectiveness of combining home based malaria management and seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children less than 10 years in Senegal: a cluster-randomised trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, SMC coverage, ACT access) evaluating combined malaria prevention interventions (SMC and HMM) in children in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: children less than 10 years
primary_outcome: incidence of malaria attacks during the follow up period
impact_summary: Combining home-based malaria management with seasonal malaria chemoprevention reduced malaria attack incidence by 85% compared to home-based management alone.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were recorded; high SMC coverage and drug tolerability observed.

title: An open randomized controlled trial to compare the efficacy of two fixed dose combinations of artemesinin based combinations for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Bangladesh.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemisinin-based combinations) for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in humans with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety.
population: patients aged 12 to 60 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological response (treatment success), defervescence time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artesunate-Amodiaquine and Artemether-Lumefantrine showed no significant difference in efficacy and safety for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Bangladesh.
transmission_setting: high risk multi-drug resistant malaria prevalent areas
safety_summary: No serious adverse events observed; minor adverse events were not significantly different between the AA and AL treatment groups.

title: Do malaria vector control measures impact disease-related behaviour and knowledge? Evidence from a large-scale larviciding intervention in Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized cluster-sampled trial of a malaria vector control intervention (larviciding) with reported outcome results on bed net usage and malaria knowledge.
population: household residents and household heads in Dar es Salaam
primary_outcome: Bed net usage and household heads' knowledge of malaria symptoms and transmission
impact_summary: Larviciding intervention reduced bed net usage by 5% and decreased household heads' knowledge of malaria symptoms, with no effect on knowledge of malaria transmission.
transmission_setting: urban, malaria vector control intervention area (larviciding)

title: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis versus mefloquine intermittent preventive treatment to prevent malaria in HIV-infected pregnant women: two randomized controlled trials.
journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria prevention strategies (cotrimoxazole and mefloquine-IPTp) in HIV-infected pregnant women with reported outcome results (placental parasitemia and adverse events).
comparator: cotrimoxazole prophylaxis alone versus mefloquine IPTp alone versus combination
population: HIV-infected pregnant women
primary_outcome: microscopic placental parasitemia at delivery
impact_summary: Cotrimoxazole alone provided adequate protection against placental malaria and was noninferior in the CD4<350 trial, but the combination with mefloquine further reduced PCR-detected placental parasitemia, while mefloquine caused more dizziness and vomiting.
safety_summary: Dizziness and vomiting of moderate intensity reported by 34%-37% of women receiving mefloquine versus 0%-3% in cotrimoxazole groups (P < 0.0001); no serious adverse events related to the drugs were found.

title: Artemisinin-naphthoquine combination versus chloroquine-primaquine to treat vivax malaria: an open-label randomized and non-inferiority trial in Yunnan Province, China.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating antimalarial treatment (artemisinin-naphthoquine vs chloroquine-primaquine) for vivax malaria in humans.
population: patients with monoinfections of P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of patients free of recurrence at day 42 (and other timepoints)
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine was non-inferior to chloroquine-primaquine in preventing recurrence of vivax malaria and had milder side effects.
effect_estimate: 98.4% (ANQ) vs 96.1% (CQ-PQ) at day 42; 79.5% (ANQ) vs 82.8% (CQ-PQ) at day 365
safety_summary: Side effects of ANQ were mild compared with CQ-PQ; ANQ was safer than CQ-PQ.

title: A Community Setting Study of Malaria After Systematic Treatment of Symptomatic Carriers of P. Falciparum With COA566 (Coartem®)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention (systematic treatment of P. falciparum carriers) in humans with primary focus on malaria transmission and clinical episodes.
comparator: standard care (no systematic screening/treatment, control arm)
population: community members at risk of malaria, including infants, children <5 years and individuals ≥5 years
primary_outcome: Number of Symptomatic Malaria Episode, RDT-confirmed, With Parasitemia ≥5000/μL (SMRC5000s) Per Person-year in Infants and Children (<5 Years) in Post Community Screening Campaign (CSC) at Month 12 (Per Cluster)
impact_summary: Systematic screening and treatment of asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers did not reduce malaria transmission and was associated with increased susceptibility to symptomatic malaria after the campaigns ended.
effect_metric: logrank p-value for time to first symptomatic malaria episode
effect_estimate: lower probability of being free of symptomatic malaria in intervention arm after Week 11-12 post campaign 3
follow_up: approximately 1 year (through the malaria transmission season)
age_range: infants, children <5 years, and individuals ≥5 years

title: [Efficacy and safety of antimalarial combinations for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children in Bangui, Central African Republic].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three antimalarial treatments in children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
comparator: active comparator (three antimalarial combinations compared to each other)
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at Day 28 per WHO classification (ETF, LCF, LPF, ACPR)
impact_summary: All three artemisinin-based combinations (artemether-lumefantrine, amodiaquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, artesunate-amodiaquine) were highly effective and well tolerated, with no significant difference in ACPR rates at day 28.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic urban setting (Bangui, Central African Republic)
safety_summary: Antimalarial combinations were well tolerated in children under 5 years, with no significant differences in reduction of anemia, fever, or parasitemia between groups.

title: Entomological determinants of insecticide-treated bed net effectiveness in Western Myanmar.
screening_reason: This is a published cluster-randomized controlled trial of ITNs (a malaria vector control intervention) with reported entomological and efficacy outcome results.
population: children and general human population in Western Myanmar villages
primary_outcome: Malaria protective effect of insecticide-treated bed nets (ITN)
impact_summary: The malaria protective effect of ITN was highly variable and not statistically significant overall, likely due to outdoor and early-evening biting behaviour of local Anopheles vectors before people were under nets.
transmission_setting: forest-fringe/rural malaria-endemic area with multiple Anopheles vector species
safety_summary: Not reported; study focused on entomological and epidemiological effectiveness, no adverse events described.

title: The effect of insecticide-treated bed nets on the incidence and prevalence of malaria in children in an area of unstable seasonal transmission in western Myanmar.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of ITN vector control intervention with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, prevalence, and cost-effectiveness) in humans.
population: children under 10 years of age
primary_outcome: Incidence and prevalence of malaria (P. falciparum and P. vivax infections) in children
impact_summary: Village-wide deployment of insecticide-treated bed nets did not provide consistent protection against malaria in children in this area of unstable seasonal transmission in western Myanmar.
effect_metric: weighted mean difference in P. falciparum episodes per 1,000 weeks at risk
transmission_setting: unstable seasonal transmission, malaria endemic villages

title: Beyond buzzing: mosquito watching stimulates malaria bednet use-a household-based cluster-randomized controlled assessor blind educational trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector-control intervention (bednet use promotion) in humans.
design: household-based cluster-randomized controlled assessor blind educational trial
comparator: educational leaflets (indirect observation) versus no intervention/control
population: households owning but not using a bednet
primary_outcome: bednet use
impact_summary: Showing freshly captured mosquitoes led to a 13-fold increase in bednet use, while educational leaflets showing mosquitoes indirectly produced no change.

title: Integrated community case management of malaria and pneumonia increases prompt and appropriate treatment for pneumonia symptoms in children under five years in Eastern Uganda.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria intervention (integrated community case management) in humans; phase not applicable for community-based cluster trial.
comparator: community health workers treating malaria only (control areas)
population: children under five years with pneumonia symptoms treated by community health workers
primary_outcome: Prompt and appropriate antibiotics for pneumonia symptoms
impact_summary: Integrated community case management of malaria and pneumonia significantly increased the likelihood of children receiving prompt and appropriate antibiotics for pneumonia symptoms and improved treatment outcomes compared to malaria-only management.
p_value: 0.01 (for decrease in fast breathing between intervention and control)

title: Impact of treating young children with antimalarials with or without antibiotics on morbidity: a cluster-randomized controlled trial in Ghana.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine) in children with reported outcome results on anaemia, severe anaemia, and severe illness.
comparator: pre-intervention clusters (no intervention) and active comparator (AAQ vs AAQ+AMX)
population: children aged 2-59 months with fever
primary_outcome: reduction of mortality (this paper reports on morbidity: anaemia, severe anaemia and severe illness)
impact_summary: Treating fever with antimalarials (with or without antibiotics) significantly reduced anaemia, severe anaemia and severe illness compared to pre-intervention clusters, with no significant difference between AAQ alone and AAQ plus amoxicillin.
effect_estimate: AAQ: anaemia OR=0.20, severe anaemia OR=0.20, severe illness OR=0.46; AAQ+AMX: anaemia OR=0.23, severe anaemia OR=0.12, severe illness OR=0.38
effect_ci: AAQ anaemia 0.12-0.33; AAQ severe anaemia 0.09-0.45; AAQ severe illness 0.26-0.80; AAQ+AMX anaemia 0.15-0.36; AAQ+AMX severe anaemia 0.04-0.31; AAQ+AMX severe illness 0.22-0.63

title: The effect of screening doors and windows on indoor density of Anopheles arabiensis in south-west Ethiopia: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (house screening) with reported outcome results on indoor Anopheles arabiensis density.
population: households/houses in south-west Ethiopia
primary_outcome: Indoor density of Anopheles arabiensis mosquitoes collected via CDC light traps
impact_summary: Screening doors and windows with metal mesh and closing eve/wall openings with mud reduced indoor densities of An. arabiensis by 40%, with a 42% reduction among unfed mosquitoes.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in indoor mosquito density

title: Effect of malaria transmission reduction by insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) on the genetic diversity of Plasmodium falciparum merozoite surface protein (MSP-1) and circumsporozoite (CSP) in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Community-based RCT of ITN vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on parasite genetic diversity in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: children under 5 years old
primary_outcome: Genetic diversity (haplotype number, frequency, nucleotide and haplotype diversity) of MSP-1(19kDa) and CSP Th2R/Th3R genes before and after ITN introduction
impact_summary: Despite marked reductions in malaria transmission due to ITN use, high genetic diversity in MSP-1(19kDa) and CSP Th2R/Th3R genes was maintained over time with no significant difference in nucleotide and haplotype diversity between 1996 and 2001.
effect_estimate: no significant difference between 1996 and 2001 (diversity >0.7 for MSP-1, >0.9 and 0.75 for Th2R and Th3R respectively)
