transmission_setting: high malaria transmission, endemic area in western Kenya

title: Residual Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia in Kenyan children after artemisinin-combination therapy is associated with increased transmission to mosquitoes and parasite recurrence.
screening_reason: Published RCT testing artemisinin-combination therapy for malaria treatment with reported outcome results on parasitemia, gametocyte carriage, and mosquito transmission.
population: children with uncomplicated malaria treated with artemisinin-combination therapy
primary_outcome: Residual parasitemia detected by qPCR on day 3 after treatment initiation and its association with transmissibility to mosquitoes and parasite recurrence
impact_summary: Residual submicroscopic parasitemia after ACT treatment is common and is associated with longer gametocyte carriage, higher likelihood of infecting mosquitoes, higher parasite burden in mosquitoes, and increased risk of recurrent parasitemia.
follow_up: 7 days (mosquito feeding assay), longer for recurrence follow-up

title: Randomized controlled trial of levamisole hydrochloride as adjunctive therapy in severe falciparum malaria with high parasitemia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (levamisole as adjunctive therapy for severe falciparum malaria) with reported outcome results in adults.
comparator: no adjuvant (standard antimalarial treatment with intravenous artesunate alone)
population: adult patients with severe malaria and high parasitemia admitted to a referral hospital
primary_outcome: circulating late-stage parasites measured as median area under the parasite clearance curves
impact_summary: A single dose of levamisole hydrochloride as adjuvant to intravenous artesunate provided no benefit in the treatment of adults with severe falciparum malaria.
effect_metric: median area under the parasite clearance curve
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; no benefit observed and no explicit safety concerns described in the abstract.

title: A randomized trial of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria among children in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes; primary purpose is malaria intervention in humans.
population: children aged six to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected and PCR-uncorrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28 and day 42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine remained highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated malaria in children, with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine showing a lower rate of reinfection in the first 28 days due to piperaquine's longer half-life.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate at day 28
p_value: 0.001 (PCR-uncorrected ACPR at day 28, AL vs DP)
safety_summary: No early treatment failures were reported; all children except one had cleared parasites by day 3.

title: Efficacy of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine fixed-dose combinations for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria among children aged six to 59 months in Nimba County, Liberia: an open-label randomized non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (day 42 cure rates) comparing two antimalarial treatments for P. falciparum in children; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: children aged six to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: genotyping-adjusted day 42 cure rate
impact_summary: ASAQ was non-inferior to AL, with both drugs showing high day 42 cure rates and rapid parasite clearance, though re-infection rates were high in both arms.

title: Tolerability and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine fixed dose combinations for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria: two open-label, randomized trials in Nimba County, Liberia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety and tolerability data) for malaria treatment with artemisinin-based combination therapies in humans.
population: Study-T: patients over five years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria; Study-E: children aged six to 59 months
primary_outcome: Tolerability and safety (clinical- and laboratory-adverse events) recorded until day 28
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine were well tolerated across all age groups, with severe adverse events rare and mostly asymptomatic, though certain mild/moderate AEs such as fatigue, vomiting, nausea, and anaemia were more frequent with ASAQ than AL.
effect_estimate: fatigue 39.8% vs 16.3%; vomiting 7.1% vs 1.6%; nausea 3.2% vs 1.0%; anaemia 14.9% vs 9.8% (ASAQ vs AL)
age_range: over five years (Study-T); six to 59 months (Study-E)
safety_summary: Most patients experienced at least one adverse event; severe AEs were few, primarily asymptomatic blood system disorders or elevated liver enzymes; no treatment or study discontinuation occurred; no unexpected AEs.

title: Chloroquine and Post Malaria Anaemia Study
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (post-malaria anaemia recovery with chloroquine) in humans; phase 'not applicable' is acceptable.
population: children aged 12-72 months with uncomplicated malaria and post-malaria anaemia
primary_outcome: Changes in Haemoglobin Concentration From Day 3 Post Treatment of Malaria Episode to Day 90 in the Weekly Chloroquine and Placebo Arms
impact_summary: Weekly low-dose chloroquine after effective antimalarial treatment did not improve recovery from postmalarial anaemia compared to placebo.
effect_ci: CQ 95% CI 6.66 to 13.42; placebo 95% CI 2.88 to 12.35
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, rural West Kiang District
safety_summary: No safety concerns reported beyond standard antimalarial treatment; no effect of CQ on secondary outcomes assessed.
funder: Medical Research Council Unit, The Gambia

title: An artesunate-containing antimalarial treatment regimen did not suppress cytomegalovirus viremia.
journal: Journal of clinical virology : the official publication of the Pan American Society for Clinical Virology
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention (artesunate-containing regimen) in humans with results on primary outcomes measured.
population: Ugandan children with acute malaria infection
primary_outcome: Change in frequency and quantity of CMV DNA detected in blood before and after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: A standard 3-day artesunate-containing antimalarial regimen had no detectable effect on suppressing CMV viremia in children with malaria.
effect_metric: difference in CMV quantity (log10 copies per million cells) day 3 vs baseline
effect_estimate: 0.30 log10 copies per million cells higher on day 3

title: Efficacy of Quinine versus Artemether in the treatment of severe malaria.
journal: Journal of Nepal Health Research Council
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (Quinine vs Artemether) in severe malaria with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, coma resolution, fever clearance) in the target population.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance, parasitaemia clearance and coma resolution
impact_summary: Quinine and Artemether showed no significant difference in fever clearance, but Quinine had significantly faster coma resolution after 24 hours than Artemether, while parasitaemia clearance was slightly better with Artemether though not statistically significant.

title: Gametocyte dynamics and the role of drugs in reducing the transmission potential of Plasmodium vivax.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatments (artemisinin derivatives vs chloroquine/amodiaquine) in vivax-infected patients with reported outcome results on gametocyte dynamics and transmission potential.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine, artesunate + amodiaquine, artemether + lumefantrine vs dihydroartemisinin + piperaquine)
population: patients with P. vivax infection (some with concurrent P. falciparum parasitemia)
primary_outcome: Incidence and risk factors for P. vivax gametocytemia at enrollment and during follow-up after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Gametocyte carriage mirrored asexual parasitemia, with treatment with dihydroartemisinin + piperaquine associated with lower cumulative incidence of post-treatment gametocytemia than chloroquine or artesunate + amodiaquine.
effect_estimate: 6.92% (DHA+PIP) vs 29.1% (chloroquine) in Thailand; 33.6% (AS+AQ) vs 7.42% (AL) vs 6.80% (DHA+PIP) in Indonesia
transmission_setting: low-transmission northwestern Thailand and Papua, Indonesia (mixed P. falciparum/P. vivax area)

title: Treatment of Asymptomatic Carriers of Plasmodium falciparum with Artemether-Lumefantrine: Impact on the Prevalence of Anemia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine) with reported outcome results on anemia prevalence; cluster-RCTs are not early-phase.
comparator: no treatment of asymptomatic carriers (control arm)
population: asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers, children under 5 and adults, aged >6 months
primary_outcome: Change in hemoglobin level and prevalence of anemia among asymptomatic carriers from Day 1 to Day 28 of first campaign and over 12 months
impact_summary: Systematic screening and treatment of asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers with artemether-lumefantrine reduced anemia prevalence and improved hemoglobin levels in the short term (28 days), but this benefit was not sustained at 12 months.
transmission_setting: 18 villages in Burkina Faso, malaria-endemic community setting
age_range: children under 5 and adults, >6 months and older

title: Therapeutic efficacy of artemisinin combination therapies and prevalence of S769N mutation in PfATPase6 gene of Plasmodium falciparum in Kolkata, India.
journal: Asian Pacific journal of tropical medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin combination therapies (ACTs) for malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes.
population: Plasmodium falciparum positive patients
primary_outcome: In vivo therapeutic efficacy of ACT regimens over 42-day follow-up per WHO 2009 protocol
impact_summary: Both artemisinin combination therapy regimens (artesunate+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and artemether+lumefantrine) were highly effective in treating P. falciparum malaria in Kolkata, with no mutant S769N PfATPase6 allele detected in any isolate.

title: [Evaluating the effect of preventive medicine for residents living around mosquito breeding water during rest period of malaria].
journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention intervention in a high-endemic area; results show morbidity reduction comparing three groups over one year.
comparator: routine medicine treatment and no treatment (non-intervention)
population: residents living around mosquito breeding water in high malaria epidemic villages
primary_outcome: morbidity/incidence of malaria before and after intervention
impact_summary: Delimited preventive medicine treatment during the rest period of malaria significantly reduced malaria morbidity compared to routine treatment and no treatment.
transmission_setting: high epidemic area along and north of the Huai River
age_range: all ages, including groups 30-39, 50-59, 60-69, and ≥70 years old

title: High adherence to antimalarials and antibiotics under integrated community case management of illness in children less than five years in eastern Uganda.
screening_reason: Published results from a cluster-randomized trial of integrated community case management (antimalarials with/without antibiotics) in children under five, with reported outcome data on adherence.
comparator: antimalarials alone (control) vs antimalarials plus antibiotics (intervention)
population: children less than five years
primary_outcome: adherence to antimalarials and antibiotics as assessed by self reports and pill counts
impact_summary: Addition of antibiotics to antimalarials under ICCM did not lower adherence, with adherence in intervention areas (99%) similar between the two treatment groups and higher than in control areas (96%).

title: Cost-effectiveness of long-lasting insecticide-treated hammocks in preventing malaria in South-central Vietnam.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing efficacy of insecticide-treated hammocks for malaria prevention with reported cost-effectiveness outcomes; vector-control intervention in humans.
design: cost-effectiveness study conducted alongside a randomized controlled trial
comparator: standard care (insecticide-treated bednets and indoor residual spraying)
population: residents of forested, mountainous areas of central Vietnam at risk of malaria
primary_outcome: cost per malaria episode averted using long-lasting insecticide-treated hammocks
impact_summary: Long-lasting insecticide-treated hammocks were found to represent good value for money in preventing malaria in remote forested areas where bednets and indoor residual spraying are insufficient, though cost-effectiveness depends heavily on hammock lifespan.
effect_metric: total net societal cost per malaria episode averted
transmission_setting: forested, mountainous, low/residual transmission area in central Vietnam

title: Artesunate/amodiaquine malaria treatment for Equatorial Guinea (Central Africa).
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate/amodiaquine) with reported efficacy and safety outcome results in humans.
population: children 6-59 months of age with malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day clinical and parasitological response to artesunate/amodiaquine treatment
impact_summary: Combination artesunate/amodiaquine therapy showed good efficacy, with a real treatment efficacy of 97.3% after molecular correction.
safety_summary: Study evaluated safety and efficacy of AS/AQ; no specific adverse event details reported beyond efficacy outcomes.

title: The effect of three-monthly albendazole treatment on malarial parasitemia and allergy: a household-based cluster-randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on malarial parasitemia (primary outcome) in a malaria-endemic setting; not early-phase.
population: household members in an STH-endemic area; malaria assessed in participants >4 years, allergy (SPT) assessed in children aged 5-15 years
primary_outcome: prevalence of malarial parasitemia and skin prick test (SPT) reactivity to any allergen
impact_summary: Three-monthly albendazole treatment for 21 months reduced STH prevalence and was associated with a transient increase in malarial parasitemia at 6 months but no significant increase in allergy (SPT reactivity), with no adverse effects reported.
effect_metric: odds ratio (malarial parasitemia at 6 months post-treatment)
safety_summary: No adverse effects were reported.

title: Health impact and cost-effectiveness of a private sector bed net distribution: experimental evidence from Zambia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of ITN distribution (vector control) with reported health outcomes (fever and malaria reduction); phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
comparator: no ITN (control group, standard access to nets)
population: cotton farmers and their households
primary_outcome: Self-reported fever and self-reported confirmed malaria; bed net ownership and usage
impact_summary: Distribution of ITNs through a private-sector cotton company partnership increased bed net usage and significantly reduced self-reported fever and malaria among treatment households compared to controls.
effect_estimate: 42% reduction in self-reported fever; 49% reduction in self-reported malaria

title: Comparative evaluation of efficacy and safety of artesunate-lumefantrine vs. artemether-lumefantrine fixed-dose combination in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based malaria treatments with reported outcome results on parasite clearance, fever clearance, and safety in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
population: patients with confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Artesunate-lumefantrine FDC showed comparable efficacy and safety to artemether-lumefantrine FDC in treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in parasite or fever clearance times.
safety_summary: Both study medications were well tolerated; one early treatment failure occurred in the AMLF group as per WHO criteria.

title: The effect of an anti-malarial subsidy programme on the quality of service provision of artemisinin-based combination therapy in Kenya: a cluster-randomized, controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing a malaria treatment intervention (subsidized ACT and retailer training) in a real-world setting.
comparator: standard care (unsubsidized, untrained private retail outlets)
population: private retail outlet staff/providers serving patients with presumptive malaria
primary_outcome: provider practices related to malaria diagnosis and treatment, including provider knowledge of first-line treatment, stocking of AL, and prescribing of AL for presumptive malaria
impact_summary: Subsidizing artemether-lumefantrine and providing retailer training significantly increased provider knowledge, stocking, and prescribing of AL for presumptive malaria treatment in private retail outlets.
effect_estimate: provider knowledge +24.2%; AL stocking +31.7%; AL prescribing +23.6%
p_value: adjusted p=0.0001 for all three outcomes

title: A controlled, parallel, cluster-randomized trial of community-wide screening and treatment of asymptomatic carriers of Plasmodium falciparum in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention (screening and treatment of asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers) with reported outcome results on symptomatic malaria and parasitemia; phase not applicable for community-level cluster trial.
population: community members including asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers; children under 5 years for primary clinical outcome
primary_outcome: Symptomatic malaria with parasite density >5,000/μL per person-year in children <5 years; change in haemoglobin between day 1 and day 28 of campaign 1
impact_summary: Systematic screening and treatment of asymptomatic carriers at the community level did not reduce clinical malaria incidence in the subsequent transmission season, though it improved haemoglobin and reduced parasite/gametocyte carriage in the short term.
effect_metric: incidence of symptomatic malaria episodes per person-year
age_range: children under 5 years (primary outcome); all ages participated in community screening
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; treatment used was artemether-lumefantrine for asymptomatic carriers

title: The effect of antenatal monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, alone or with azithromycin, on foetal and neonatal growth faltering in Malawi: a randomised controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing IPTp (intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy) for malaria prevention in pregnant women, a valid malaria intervention.
comparator: two doses of SP (control) vs monthly SP vs monthly SP plus azithromycin
population: women with uncomplicated second trimester pregnancies
primary_outcome: Foetal and neonatal growth faltering (newborn size at birth and infant growth at four weeks of age)
impact_summary: Monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, especially combined with azithromycin, increased birthweight and length and reduced low birthweight, stunting and underweight at four weeks compared to standard two-dose SP.
effect_estimate: AZI-SP vs control: 140 g heavier at birth, 0.6 cm longer at 4 weeks, RR 0.61 for low birthweight, RR 0.60 for stunting, RR 0.48 for underweight; monthly SP vs control: 80 g heavier at birth, 0.3 cm longer at 4 weeks
effect_ci: birthweight 70-200 g; length 0.2-0.9 cm; low birthweight RR 0.40-0.93; stunting RR 0.44-0.81; underweight RR 0.29-0.79; monthly SP birthweight 20-140 g; length -0.0 to 0.6 cm

title: The effect of blood storage age on treatment of lactic acidosis by transfusion in children with severe malarial anaemia: a pilot, randomized, controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (lactic acidosis resolution) in children with severe malarial anaemia; blood transfusion is a malaria treatment intervention; pilot phase is acceptable as it has completed and reported results.
comparator: long storage age blood (21-35 days) vs short storage age blood (1-10 days)
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with severe malarial anaemia and lactic acidosis
primary_outcome: proportion of children whose lactic acidosis resolved (blood lactate <5 mmol/L) by four hours after transfusion
impact_summary: Blood storage age did not significantly affect resolution of lactic acidosis in children with severe malarial anaemia, with 92% resolving in the short storage arm versus 81% in the long storage arm.
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported beyond physiological monitoring; no adverse safety signals mentioned.

title: Efficacy of quinine, artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine as rescue treatment for uncomplicated malaria in Ugandan children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin combinations vs quinine) in children with reported efficacy outcomes; malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: quinine vs artemether-lumefantrine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (active comparators)
population: children with recurrent malaria infection after ACT treatment
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent malaria infection within 28 days post rescue treatment
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was more effective than quinine or artemether-lumefantrine as rescue therapy, with significantly lower risk of recurrent infection.
effect_estimate: HR = 3.9 (quinine vs DHAPQ); HR = 3.3 (AL vs DHAPQ)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported; 218 (99.1%) assessed for safety.

title: Understanding the impact of subsidizing artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs) in the retail sector--results from focus group discussions in rural Kenya.
screening_reason: This is a cluster randomized trial of subsidized ACT provision with reported outcome results (ACT availability, coverage, patient counselling, adherence) focused on malaria treatment intervention in humans; qualitative component documents the trial findings.
design: cluster randomized trial (with qualitative focus group study)
population: retailers and caregivers of children treated with ACT in rural retail sector
primary_outcome: Understanding retailer and caregiver experiences with the ACT subsidy intervention (qualitative), original trial primary outcome was ACT availability and coverage
impact_summary: The subsidy intervention increased ACT availability and coverage but patient counselling and adherence remained suboptimal due to supply, training, and caregiver-related barriers.

title: Artesunate + amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Colombian Pacific region: a noninferiority trial.
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: RCT comparing two artemisinin combination therapies for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with fully reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (28-day WHO validated design/definitions)
impact_summary: Artesunate + amodiaquine was noninferior to artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with 100% versus 99% adequate clinical and parasitological response rates.
effect_metric: difference in adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
p_value: p=0.002 for fever clearance time; p<0.001 for post-treatment abdominal pain
safety_summary: Abdominal pain occurred in 1.9% (AS+AQ) and 3.8% (AL) at baseline, and 1% (AS+AQ) versus 13.3% (AL) after treatment (p<0.001); fever clearance time was significantly shorter with AS+AQ (p=0.002); one late parasitological treatment failure occurred in the AL group.

title: Increased use of community medicine distributors and rational use of drugs in children less than five years of age in Uganda caused by integrated community case management of fever.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial testing a malaria treatment intervention (integrated community case management) in humans with reported outcome results on care-seeking and drug use; early phase exclusion does not apply to community-based cluster trials.
population: children 6-59 months of age
primary_outcome: Use of community medicine distributors and rational/appropriate drug use for malaria treatment
impact_summary: Integrated community case management increased use of community medicine distributors and rational drug use compared with home-based management.

title: Integrated community case management of fever in children under five using rapid diagnostic tests and respiratory rate counting: a multi-country cluster randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized effectiveness trial of malaria diagnostic testing and treatment in febrile children with reported outcome results; malaria is primary focus.
population: febrile children 4 to 59 months of age
primary_outcome: Fever clearance at Day 3 and Day 7; appropriate treatment (ACT and antibiotic prescribing) based on RDT results
impact_summary: Diagnostic-based management using RDTs and respiratory rate counting reduced ACT overuse but antibiotic overuse remained common and fever clearance was similarly high in both arms with no significant difference.
transmission_setting: variable across Burkina Faso, Ghana, and Uganda
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; focus was on treatment appropriateness rather than adverse events.

title: Impact of community management of fever (using antimalarials with or without antibiotics) on childhood mortality: a cluster-randomized controlled trial in Ghana.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (mortality) evaluating malaria treatment intervention (antimalarials with/without antibiotics) in children; cluster-randomized trials are Phase N/A.
population: children with fever, 2-59 months of age
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality
impact_summary: Community fever management with antimalarials (with or without antibiotics) significantly reduced under-five mortality compared with standard care, with a greater but not statistically significant reduction when an antibiotic was added.

title: Multicentre study evaluating the non-inferiority of the new paediatric formulation of artesunate/amodiaquine versus artemether/lumefantrine for the management of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Cameroon, Ivory Coast and Senegal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in children with reported efficacy and safety outcome results; phase and population appropriate for inclusion.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: The new paediatric formulation of artesunate/amodiaquine was non-inferior to artemether/lumefantrine in efficacy and tolerability for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children.
safety_summary: Clinical tolerance was good with no significant difference between groups; anaemia was significantly higher at day 7 compared to day 0 in both arms.

title: In vivo therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine alone or in combination with primaquine against vivax malaria in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, and polymorphism in pvmdr1 and pvcrt-o genes.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine ± primaquine) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes over 42-day follow-up.
comparator: chloroquine plus primaquine vs chloroquine alone
population: patients with P. vivax monoinfection
primary_outcome: In vivo therapeutic efficacy (adequate clinical and parasitological response) at day 42
impact_summary: Chloroquine alone or combined with primaquine remained highly effective against P. vivax malaria in Kolkata, with 99% efficacy in the chloroquine-only group and 100% ACPR in the chloroquine plus primaquine group.

title: Randomized, open-label trial of primaquine against vivax malaria relapse in Indonesia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results on relapse efficacy; primary purpose is malaria intervention (treatment/radical cure) in humans.
population: soldiers with acute P. vivax malaria returning from malarious Papua to malaria-free base in Java
primary_outcome: Relapse of P. vivax malaria over 12 months of follow-up
impact_summary: Primaquine given with quinine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was highly effective at preventing P. vivax relapse compared with artesunate alone, with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine plus primaquine showing the highest efficacy (98%).
transmission_setting: malarious region (Papua, Indonesia) with relapse observed after return to malaria-free base (Java)
safety_summary: Antirelapse therapy with primaquine begun a month after acute treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine proved safe.

title: Impact of anthelminthic treatment in pregnancy and childhood on immunisations, infections and eczema in childhood: a randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, immunization responses, infections, eczema); primary purpose includes malaria as a measured outcome in a helminth-malaria co-endemic setting where the intervention affects malaria incidence.
population: pregnant women and their offspring (children followed to age 5 years)
primary_outcome: post-immunisation recall responses to BCG and tetanus antigens, and incidence of malaria, diarrhoea, and pneumonia
impact_summary: Albendazole given during pregnancy increased the risk of eczema in children, while quarterly albendazole given during childhood reduced the incidence of clinical malaria; no consistent effects were seen on other outcomes.
effect_estimate: HR 1.58 (eczema, maternal albendazole); HR 0.85 (malaria, childhood albendazole)
transmission_setting: helminth and malaria co-endemic area, tropical developing country setting
age_range: children from birth to 5 years (offspring); pregnant women (maternal cohort)
safety_summary: Albendazole during pregnancy was associated with an increased rate of eczema in children; otherwise no other significant adverse effects were reported for the interventions.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of a new formulation of artesunate-mefloquine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in adult in Senegal: open randomized trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in humans.
population: adults with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: The new artesunate-mefloquine formulation was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine, with similar cure rates and tolerability, though dizziness was more frequent with artesunate-mefloquine.
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated with similar biological profiles at day 7; dizziness was more frequent in the artesunate-mefloquine arm.

title: Open-label trial of three dosage regimens of fixed-dose combination of artemisinin and naphthoquine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Calabar, Nigeria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemisinin-naphthoquine combination) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
comparator: active comparator (three dosage regimens compared against each other)
population: adolescents and adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: All three dosage regimens of artemisinin-naphthoquine achieved high cure rates, with an overall 28-day cure rate of 88.9%, though single-dose regimens raise concerns about resistance emergence.
safety_summary: Adverse events were few and mild, most commonly weakness and headache; no serious adverse events reported.

title: A community-randomized evaluation of the effect of intermittent preventive treatment in infants on antimalarial drug resistance in southern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of IPTi (chemoprevention) for malaria in infants with reported outcome results on drug resistance markers; cluster-randomized design with results published.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Prevalence of SP resistance markers (dhfr and dhps mutations) and SP blood levels in IPTi vs comparison areas
impact_summary: IPTi with SP did not increase drug pressure or selection of dhfr/dhps resistance mutations while SP was first-line treatment, but after switching to artemether-lumefantrine, dhfr mutations increased more in IPTi areas.
effect_metric: p-value for increase in dhfr and dhps mutations after AL introduction
effect_estimate: increase in dhfr mutations in IPTi areas

title: Molecular basis of allele-specific efficacy of a blood-stage malaria vaccine: vaccine development implications.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a blood-stage malaria vaccine (FMP2.1/AS02A) with reported efficacy results against clinical malaria in children.
population: Malian children
primary_outcome: Allele-specific efficacy against clinical malaria based on AMA1 sequence similarity to vaccine-type allele
impact_summary: The AMA1-based vaccine FMP2.1/AS02(A) showed allele-specific efficacy, being most protective against parasites with AMA1 alleles matching the vaccine strain at key polymorphic positions, particularly position 197 in the cluster 1 loop.
effect_estimate: highest against alleles identical to 3D7 at c1L positions

title: Effect of high-dose or split-dose artesunate on parasite clearance in artemisinin-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate dosing) with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and recrudescence.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance (parasitemia half-life)
impact_summary: Increasing or splitting the artesunate dose did not improve parasite clearance in either artemisinin-resistant (Pailin) or more sensitive (Wang Pha) P. falciparum infections.
p_value: P = .0001 (site difference); P = .68 (recrudescence between treatment arms)
transmission_setting: artemisinin-resistant (Pailin, Cambodia) and more sensitive (Wang Pha, Thailand) falciparum malaria border regions

title: Clinical trial in healthy malaria-naïve adults to evaluate the safety, tolerability, immunogenicity and efficacy of MuStDO5, a five-gene, sporozoite/hepatic stage Plasmodium falciparum DNA vaccine combined with escalating dose human GM-CSF DNA.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a malaria vaccine (MuStDO5 DNA vaccine) in humans with reported safety, immunogenicity and efficacy outcomes, but it is Phase I (first-in-human dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers); Phase I studies are explicitly excluded by the eligibility criteria.
design: open-label, dose-escalation, phase I, controlled human malaria infection challenge trial
comparator: escalating doses of hGM-CSF plasmid (0, 20, 100, 500 μg) within cohorts; no placebo control described
population: healthy malaria-naïve adults
primary_outcome: Safety, tolerability, immunogenicity and efficacy (protection from controlled human malaria infection) of MuStDO5 DNA vaccine combined with escalating dose hGM-CSF DNA
impact_summary: The MuStDO5 DNA vaccine plus hGM-CSF was safe and induced modest antigen-specific T cell interferon-γ responses but no antibodies, and did not protect any volunteers against controlled human malaria infection challenge.
follow_up: through controlled human malaria infection challenge administered 18 days after third vaccination (approximately 10 weeks post first dose)
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental challenge, non-endemic setting)
safety_summary: The vaccine was safe and well-tolerated across all dose cohorts.

title: Malaria vaccine trial shows lower efficacy in younger than in older infants.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria vaccine (primary intervention) in human participants.
population: infants
impact_summary: The malaria vaccine trial showed lower efficacy in younger infants compared to older infants.

title: Field evaluation of Icon®Life, a long-lasting insecticidal net (LLIN) against Anopheles culicifacies and transmission of malaria in District Gautam Budh Nagar (Uttar Pradesh), India.
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial (three randomly selected village arms: LLIN intervention, untreated nets, control) evaluating a malaria vector-control intervention (LLIN) with reported outcome results on entomological and malariometric indices.
population: residents of villages in a malaria endemic district
primary_outcome: Reduction in Anopheles culicifacies density and malaria prevalence
impact_summary: Villages using Icon®Life LLIN showed reduced mosquito entry rate, resting density, and parity rate of An. culicifacies, and fewer malaria cases compared to untreated net and no net villages.
safety_summary: No adverse health events were reported by households using the nets; high community compliance and acceptance.

title: In vivo susceptibility of Plasmodium falciparum to artesunate in Binh Phuoc Province, Vietnam.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemisinin doses for malaria treatment with reported primary and secondary efficacy outcomes; early-phase exclusion does not apply to treatment trials.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance half-life
impact_summary: Parasite clearance was slower with artesunate 2mg/kg/day than with 4mg/kg/day or DHA-PPQ, with higher treatment failure rates, indicating possible early signs of reduced artemisinin sensitivity in southern Vietnam.
transmission_setting: low transmission border area near Cambodia
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; early treatment failure occurred in 4% and late clinical failure in 2% of AS 2mg/kg group, none in other arms

title: Effect of vitamin A adjunct therapy for cerebral malaria in children admitted to Mulago hospital: a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results for a malaria intervention (vitamin A adjunct therapy for cerebral malaria treatment) in humans.
population: children aged 6-59 months admitted with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: coma recovery time, time for convulsions to stop, and parasite and fever clearance
impact_summary: Vitamin A as adjunct therapy did not significantly reduce coma duration or other primary outcomes but was associated with fewer deaths in the vitamin A arm compared to placebo.
effect_metric: relative risk (mortality, placebo vs vitamin A)
p_value: coma recovery p=0.44; convulsions p=0.37; fever clearance p=0.92; parasite clearance p=0.12
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; mortality was lower in the vitamin A group (8.1%) than placebo (16.2%).

title: Relapses contribute significantly to the risk of Plasmodium vivax infection and disease in Papua New Guinean children 1-5 years of age.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-primaquine) with reported outcome results comparing P. vivax infection and disease risk in children.
population: children aged 1-5 years
primary_outcome: Risk of P. vivax episodes (infection and disease) during follow-up
impact_summary: Artesunate plus primaquine reduced the risk of P. vivax episodes compared with artesunate alone or no treatment, with the benefit concentrated in the first 3 months, indicating hypnozoites are a major source of P. vivax burden in this population.
effect_estimate: 28% vs artesunate arm; 33% vs control arm

title: Effects of malaria volunteer training on coverage and timeliness of diagnosis: a cluster randomized controlled trial in Myanmar.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (RDT coverage, timeliness of diagnosis, mortality) evaluating a malaria diagnosis and treatment intervention (volunteer training on RDT and ACT use) in humans.
comparator: villages without trained volunteers (standard care); also compared with villages with midwives
population: residents of malaria-endemic villages without health staff
primary_outcome: coverage and timeliness of diagnosis and treatment, and malaria mortality
impact_summary: Training village volunteers increased the likelihood of receiving a blood test compared to comparison villages, but overall RDT coverage remained low and malaria mortality rates did not significantly differ between groups.
effect_metric: odds ratio for receiving a blood test
effect_estimate: OR 3.2 (intervention vs comparison); OR 5.4 (midwife vs comparison)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events described

title: Assessing the impact of scaling-up bednet coverage through agricultural loan programmes: evidence from a cluster randomised controlled trial in Katete, Zambia.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing bednet distribution (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans; phase not applicable for cluster trials.
comparator: standard bednet distribution (subsidised net loan program vs free distribution)
population: farming households in a rural, highly endemic malaria area
primary_outcome: self-reported all-cause morbidity and self-reported confirmed malaria
impact_summary: Distributing additional bednets through agricultural loan programmes substantially reduced self-reported all-cause morbidity and confirmed malaria compared to standard coverage.
effect_estimate: 40-42% reduction in all-cause morbidity odds; 53-60% reduction in confirmed malaria odds

title: Chloroquine Alone or in Combination for Malaria in Children in Malawi
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing chloroquine monotherapy and combinations for malaria treatment in children, a direct malaria intervention.
comparator: chloroquine monotherapy versus chloroquine combined with artesunate, azithromycin, or atovaquone-proguanil
population: children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Number of Clinical Malaria Episodes Per Year of Follow-up
impact_summary: Chloroquine remained highly efficacious against falciparum malaria in Malawi with no significant differences in malaria incidence between chloroquine monotherapy and chloroquine combined with artesunate, azithromycin, or atovaquone-proguanil, and pfcrt T76 resistance marker remained rare.
transmission_setting: endemic falciparum malaria area with predominant chloroquine susceptibility
safety_summary: Young children treated with chloroquine-azithromycin had higher hemoglobin concentrations at study end than those on chloroquine monotherapy; no other major safety differences reported.
funder: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)

title: Clinical tolerability of artesunate-amodiaquine versus comparator treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria: an individual-patient analysis of eight randomized controlled trials in sub-Saharan Africa.
screening_reason: This is a pooled analysis of eight randomized controlled trials comparing artesunate-amodiaquine to other antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (adverse events and efficacy data) in humans.
design: individual-patient pooled analysis of eight randomized controlled trials, phase 3
comparator: other anti-malarial treatments (other ACTs and non-ACT treatments including artemether-lumefantrine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, chloroquine-SP)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, 74% under 5 years of age
primary_outcome: Incidence and differences in adverse events (AE) and treatment emergent adverse events (TEAE) by Day 28
impact_summary: ASAQ was comparatively well-tolerated, with a similar overall safety profile to other anti-malarial treatments, though it had a higher rate of gastro-intestinal adverse events than artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine at two sites.
effect_metric: proportion of patients with at least one gastro-intestinal AE
p_value: p = 0.001 (Fisher test, AE vs pre-treatment symptom prevalence)
age_range: predominantly children under 5 years, with some older patients included
safety_summary: 8,542 AEs recorded overall; SAE incidence with ASAQ was 9 per 1,000 and mortality 1 per 1,000 (3 deaths, none drug-related), similar to other treatments; ASAQ had higher gastro-intestinal AE rates but no difference in other AEs.

title: Insecticide-treated plastic sheeting for emergency malaria prevention and shelter among displaced populations: an observational cohort study in a refugee setting in Sierra Leone.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with random deployment of insecticide-treated plastic sheeting for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (incidence rates, protective efficacy).
population: children up to 3 years of age, refugee camp residents
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum incidence rate in children up to 3 years of age
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated plastic sheeting significantly reduced malaria incidence compared to untreated sheeting, with protective efficacy of 61% when used as full shelter lining and 15% when used only as roof lining.
effect_estimate: 61% (Largo, full lining); 15% (Tobanda, roof lining); AOR 0.40 (Largo), AOR 0.85 (Tobanda)
transmission_setting: refugee camp setting, malaria endemic region
safety_summary: ITPS was found to be safe, and anemia rates improved under ITPS in both camps.

title: Effect of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria during infancy on serological responses to measles and other vaccines used in the Expanded Programme on Immunization: results from five randomised controlled trials.
screening_reason: This is a published analysis of five randomized controlled trials testing an IPTi malaria prevention intervention in infants with reported serological outcome results.
design: randomised controlled trials, double-blind, placebo-controlled, non-inferiority
population: infants receiving routine vaccinations under EPI schedule
primary_outcome: proportion of infants who did not attain protective measles antibody titres after vaccination
impact_summary: IPTi with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine or other antimalarial drugs did not adversely affect serological responses to measles vaccine or other EPI vaccines.
effect_metric: difference in proportion without protective antibody response
transmission_setting: moderate to high malaria transmission in sub-Saharan Africa
age_range: infants (8-10 weeks to 9 months of age)
safety_summary: No evidence of adverse effect of IPTi with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine or other antimalarial drugs on immune responses to EPI vaccines, including measles, yellow fever, polio, and other antigens.

title: Therapeutic efficacy and safety of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artesunate-mefloquine in uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results at 63 days.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 63-day PCR-corrected and uncorrected cure rate
impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artesunate-mefloquine were highly efficacious and well tolerated in India, with DP showing a significant post-treatment prophylactic effect reducing new infections compared to A+M.
safety_summary: Both DP and A+M were well tolerated, with most adverse events mild or moderate; post-treatment adverse events were slightly more frequent with A+M than DP.

title: Genotyping of Plasmodium vivax reveals both short and long latency relapse patterns in Kolkata.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (chloroquine ± primaquine) in vivax malaria with reported outcome results on recurrence/relapse patterns.
comparator: chloroquine alone vs chloroquine plus primaquine (5 or 14 days)
population: patients presenting with acute vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Recurrence of vivax malaria infections over 15 months follow-up, differentiated by genotyping into relapse vs new infection
impact_summary: Genotyping showed that unobserved primaquine (5 or 14 days) did not prevent relapse and revealed that long latency P. vivax relapse (8-10 month interval) is prevalent alongside short latency relapse in Kolkata.
effect_metric: proportion of recurrences classified as probable relapse
effect_estimate: 32 of 47 recurrences (68%) were probable relapses; 22 (69%) of these were genetically homologous
transmission_setting: endemic, tropical/temperate mixed zone (West Bengal, India)

title: Repeated artemisinin-based combination therapies in a malaria hyperendemic area of Mali: efficacy, safety, and public health impact.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (ACTs) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
comparator: artemether-lumefantrine, artesunate plus amodiaquine, and artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine compared against each other
population: patients 6 months of age and older with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Risk of subsequent malaria episodes and treatment efficacy of repeated ACT administration
impact_summary: AS+AQ and AS+SP significantly reduced the risk of subsequent malaria episodes compared to artemether-lumefantrine, while all treatments showed similarly high (>95%) efficacy and good tolerability.
safety_summary: All drugs were highly efficacious and well tolerated

title: The efficacy and tolerability of artemisinin-piperaquine (Artequick®) versus artesunate-amodiaquine (Coarsucam™) for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in south-central Vietnam.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based combination therapies) with reported outcome results (day 42 cure rates and parasite/fever clearance times).
population: children and adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 42, PCR-corrected, parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: Both artemisinin-piperaquine and artesunate-amodiaquine were highly efficacious with equal 98% cure rates at day 42, though parasite clearance was slower with artemisinin-piperaquine and fever clearance was slower with artesunate-amodiaquine.
p_value: P<0.001 for parasite clearance time; P=0.07 for fever clearance time
safety_summary: Both forms of ACT were well tolerated with no serious adverse events.

title: "Even if you know everything you can forget": health worker perceptions of mobile phone text-messaging to improve malaria case-management in Kenya.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (significant improvements in artemether-lumefantrine management) testing a malaria case-management intervention in humans.
design: cluster-randomized controlled trial; qualitative sub-study with in-depth interviews
population: health workers in government health facilities managing paediatric outpatient malaria cases
primary_outcome: correct artemether-lumefantrine (AL) case-management by health workers
impact_summary: The SMS text-messaging intervention led to significant improvements in correct artemether-lumefantrine management immediately after the intervention and 6 months later, with health workers reporting high acceptance of the intervention.
transmission_setting: Kenyan government health facilities, malaria-endemic setting
safety_summary: Not reported; study focused on qualitative perceptions and case-management outcomes, no adverse events mentioned.

title: Combination of malaria vector control interventions in pyrethroid resistance area in Benin: a cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster randomised controlled trial of malaria vector control interventions (LLINs, IRS, CTPS) with reported outcome results on clinical malaria incidence in children.
population: children younger than 6 years (and pregnant women received targeted LLINs)
primary_outcome: Incidence density rate of Plasmodium falciparum clinical malaria in children younger than 6 years
impact_summary: Combining LLINs with IRS or CTPS did not significantly reduce malaria morbidity, infection, or transmission compared with LLIN coverage alone.
p_value: ULLIN p=0.79; TLLIN+IRS p=0.15; ULLIN+CTPS p=0.77
transmission_setting: pyrethroid resistance area, malaria endemic villages in southern Benin
funder: Ministère Français des Affaires Etrangères et Européennes (FSP project 2006-22), Institut de Recherche pour le Développement, President's Malaria Initiative (PMI) of US Government

title: Effectiveness and durability of Interceptor® long-lasting insecticidal nets in a malaria endemic area of central India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (vector control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, vector density); phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
comparator: untreated polyester net and no net (no intervention)
population: tribal community residents in malaria endemic villages
primary_outcome: Slide positivity rate (SPR) and malaria incidence per 1000 population (PI) as measures of mosquito density reduction, blood feeding inhibition and malaria incidence
impact_summary: Interceptor long-lasting insecticidal nets significantly reduced malaria vector density and malaria incidence compared to untreated nets and no nets, and retained insecticidal efficacy and physical durability for up to three years of household use.
effect_metric: Slide positivity rate (SPR) and malaria incidence per 1000 population (PI)
effect_estimate: SPR: 3.7% (LN) vs 6.5% (untreated) vs 11% (no net); PI: 16.4 (LN) vs 24.8 (untreated) vs 44.2 (no net)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic tribal area of central India
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; nets retained effective alpha-cypermethrin concentration and >80% mosquito mortality in cone bioassays after 20 washes

title: Is home management of fevers a cost-effective way of reducing under-five mortality in Africa? The case of a rural Ghanaian District.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (deaths averted, DALYs averted) testing antimalarial-based home fever management as a malaria prevention strategy in children.
population: children aged 2-59 months with fever
primary_outcome: Cost-effectiveness measured via anaemia cases averted, under-five deaths averted, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) averted
impact_summary: Home management of under-five fevers using artesunate-amodiaquine alone or combined with amoxicillin was cost-effective in reducing under-five mortality in rural Ghana, with AAQ alone being more cost-effective than AAQ plus AMX.
transmission_setting: rural, endemic malaria setting in southern Ghana

title: Quality and safety of integrated community case management of malaria using rapid diagnostic tests and pneumonia by community health workers.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on malaria intervention (RDT-based diagnosis and artemether-lumefantrine treatment) in humans; vector control/community health worker trials are not early-phase.
comparator: alternative model of community-based management (comparison arm)
population: children under 5 years old with fever and/or fast/difficult breathing
primary_outcome: Quality and safety of CHW classification and treatment of malaria and pneumonia using RDTs
impact_summary: Community health workers in rural Zambia were able to use RDTs to classify and treat malaria and pneumonia with high accuracy and few adverse events, demonstrating safe and high-quality integrated case management.
safety_summary: Use of RDTs, amoxicillin, and AL was associated with few minor adverse events; 90% of febrile children with negative RDT results recovered after antipyretic treatment alone.

title: Effects of educational intervention on long-lasting insecticidal nets use in a malarious area, southeast Iran.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of LLIN educational intervention (vector-control malaria prevention) with reported outcome results on LLIN use and malaria knowledge.
population: households in a malaria-endemic rural district
primary_outcome: Use of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) the previous night, and knowledge/practice regarding malaria before and after educational program
impact_summary: An educational intervention significantly improved knowledge about malaria and increased use of LLINs, with regular use of LLINs (92.5%) higher than in control areas (87.1%) and above the WHO targeted coverage of 80%.
effect_metric: proportion using LLINs the previous night

title: Arterolane maleate plus piperaquine phosphate for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria: a comparative, multicenter, randomized clinical trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug combinations with reported outcome results (adequate clinical/parasitologic response at day 28) in patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria monoinfection with parasite densities 1000-100000 asexual parasites/µL
primary_outcome: Polymerase chain reaction-corrected adequate clinical and parasitologic response on day 28
impact_summary: AM-PQP showed no treatment failures and similar parasite and fever clearance times compared to Coartem, supporting further evaluation as a fixed-dose combination.
safety_summary: Safety was assessed as part of the trial; no major safety concerns reported, with 94.4% of AM-PQP and 96.3% of Coartem patients completing the trial.

title: Field evaluation of permethrin long-lasting insecticide treated nets (Olyset(®)) for malaria control in an endemic area, southeast of Iran.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (LLINs) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and vector density.
population: residents of malaria-endemic villages, all study population
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence measured by passive and active case detection, and indoor-resting density/abundance of anopheline vectors
impact_summary: Olyset LLINs significantly reduced indoor-resting vector density and human blood index, and reduced malaria incidence by 93.2% compared to the untreated net area during the intervention period.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: ITN protection, MSP1 antibody levels and malaria episodes in young children of rural Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (malaria episodes, MSP1 antibody levels) nested in an ITN trial; malaria prevention/vaccine development is the primary focus.
comparator: ITN protection from birth vs. protection from month six onwards
population: neonates/infants in a malaria endemic rural area
primary_outcome: Time to next malaria episode in relation to MSP1(42) antibody titres
impact_summary: MSP1(42) antibody titres were not associated with protection against subsequent malaria episodes in infants.
effect_estimate: 101 vs 97 days (May); 58 vs 84 days (September); 144 vs 161 days (March)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic, seasonal transmission, rural Burkina Faso

title: Impact of changing over of insecticide from synthetic pyrethroids to DDT for indoor residual spray in a malaria endemic area of Orissa, India.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control (IRS with different insecticides) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and parasitological endpoints.
comparator: synthetic pyrethroid IRS and insecticide-treated nets/long-lasting insecticidal nets
population: residents of malaria endemic villages in Sundergarh district
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence (slide positivity rate and adjusted incidence rate per 1000 population) measured through fortnightly domiciliary surveillance
impact_summary: Changing over indoor residual spraying from synthetic pyrethroids to DDT produced a similar epidemiological impact on malaria as continuing synthetic pyrethroid spraying or using insecticide-treated/long-lasting nets, provided spray quality and coverage were maintained.
effect_metric: percent reduction in slide positivity rate
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Efficacy and safety of artemisinin-naphthoquine versus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in adult patients with uncomplicated malaria: a multi-centre study in Indonesia.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT comparing two antimalarial drugs in adults with uncomplicated malaria; outcome results (efficacy, safety, parasitological responses) fully reported.
population: adult patients with uncomplicated symptomatic malaria
primary_outcome: PCR uncorrected and corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 42
impact_summary: Both artemisinin-naphthoquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were highly effective, safe and well tolerated for treatment of uncomplicated malaria, with similar cure rates though AN had slightly longer parasite clearance times.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (day 42)
safety_summary: Few and mild adverse events reported; abnormal haematology and blood chemistry values showed no clinical significance.

title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, chlorproguanil-dapsone with artesunate and post-treatment haemolysis in African children treated for uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results (haemoglobin drop post-treatment) for a malaria treatment intervention (artemisinin-based combination therapy) in children with uncomplicated malaria.
population: African children under 5 years of age with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Post-treatment haemoglobin drop ≥2 g/dl within the first four days (days 0-3) after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Neither G6PD deficiency nor CDA treatment alone was significantly associated with a post-treatment haemoglobin drop, but G6PD-deficient children treated with CDA showed a higher, though not statistically significant, frequency of haemolytic anaemia compared to those treated with other ACTs.
safety_summary: CDA treatment in G6PD-deficient children was associated with a higher, though not statistically significant, rate of haemolytic anaemia (56% vs 29% in other ACT groups); overall G6PD deficiency and CDA alone were not significantly associated with haemoglobin drop.

title: Antimalarial efficacy of a quantified extract of Nauclea pobeguinii stem bark in human adult volunteers with diagnosed uncomplicated falciparum malaria. Part 2: a clinical phase IIB trial.
screening_reason: Phase IIB RCT with reported outcome results comparing herbal antimalarial extract to standard treatment in malaria patients.
population: adult volunteers with diagnosed uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Antimalarial efficacy assessed via adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 14 according to WHO 2003 guideline
impact_summary: PR 259 CT1 (Nauclea pobeguinii extract) achieved 87.9% ACPR at day 14 compared with 96.9% for artesunate-amodiaquine, with fewer side effects and better tolerability for PR 259 CT1.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 14
safety_summary: No significant changes in vital signs, ECG, biochemical, or haematological parameters; PR 259 CT1 was better tolerated with fewer side effects than artesunate-amodiaquine.

title: Long-term effects of malaria prevention with insecticide-treated mosquito nets on morbidity and mortality in African children: randomised controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (mortality, malaria prevalence, morbidity) on ITN vector control for malaria prevention in African children.
population: neonates/children in a malaria holoendemic area
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality
impact_summary: There was no difference in mortality between children given ITN protection from birth versus from age 6 months, and individual ITN protection did not sufficiently reduce malaria prevalence in this high-transmission area.
age_range: neonates to children (birth cohort followed over years)
safety_summary: ITN protection in early infancy was not associated with increased mortality; no evidence of interference with immunity development leading to harm.

title: Consequences of gestational malaria on birth weight: finding the best timeframe for intermittent preventive treatment administration.
screening_reason: RCT comparing IPTp regimens (SP vs mefloquine) in pregnant women for malaria prevention with reported birth weight and placental infection outcomes.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) vs mefloquine; also early vs late timing of first SP dose
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Birth weight (low birth weight, LBW) and placental infection in relation to timing of IPTp-SP administration
impact_summary: Early intake of the first SP dose (at 4 months gestation) was associated with a lower risk of low birth weight compared to late intake (6-7 months), but with a borderline increased risk of placental infection.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (aOR) for low birth weight
safety_summary: Early SP administration showed a borderline increased risk of placental infection (aOR = 1.7, p = 0.1); no other major safety issues reported.

title: The effect of household heads training on long-lasting insecticide-treated bed nets utilization: a cluster randomized controlled trial in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on a malaria vector-control intervention (bed net utilization training) in humans; phase not applicable for cluster trials.
comparator: standard care (no household head training, free LLITN distribution only)
population: household members including under-five children in villages in southwest Ethiopia
primary_outcome: Utilization of long-lasting insecticide-treated bed nets (LLITN) at baseline, six and twelve months
impact_summary: Household head skill-based training on LLITN use led to a significantly greater increase in bed net utilization in intervention villages compared to control villages over 12 months.
effect_metric: percentage point increase in LLITN utilization
effect_estimate: 31.0 percentage points at 12 months (all age groups); 38.4 percentage points among under-five children

title: Artesunate-amodiaquine fixed dose combination for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in India.
screening_reason: RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes for malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine) in humans; phase not stated but not early-phase (efficacy trial).
population: Patients between six months and 60 years of age with Plasmodium falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: 28-day PCR-corrected parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: The fixed dose combination of artesunate-amodiaquine was more efficacious than amodiaquine alone, with cure rates of 97.51% versus 88.65%, and was found to be safe.
safety_summary: Seven serious adverse events reported in five patients, two related to treatment; all resolved without sequel.

title: Comparative efficacy of uncontrolled and controlled intermittent preventive treatment during pregnancy (IPTp) with combined use of LLTNs in high resistance area to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP chemoprevention for malaria in pregnancy with reported outcome results (low birth weight, placental malaria, anemia).
comparator: uncontrolled (unsupervised) IPTp-SP versus controlled (directly observed) IPTp-SP
population: pregnant women with pregnancy less than 28 weeks duration
primary_outcome: proportion of low birth weight infants (body weight < 2500 g)
impact_summary: Directly observed and unsupervised IPTp-SP administration produced similar rates of low birth weight, placental malaria, and anemia, indicating the two approaches are equivalent.
effect_metric: proportion of low birth weight infants
transmission_setting: high sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance area, suburban and rural sites
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse event data provided beyond efficacy/anemia outcomes.

title: An analysis of timing and frequency of malaria infection during pregnancy in relation to the risk of low birth weight, anaemia and perinatal mortality in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing two versus three doses of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp chemoprevention) in pregnant women with reported outcomes including malaria incidence, low birth weight, anaemia, and perinatal mortality.
comparator: two-dose intermittent preventive treatment (standard SP regimen)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Risk of low birth weight, maternal anaemia and perinatal mortality in relation to timing and frequency of malaria infection during pregnancy
impact_summary: Malaria infection occurring during the first trimester of pregnancy was associated with a significantly higher risk of low birth weight, while three-dose SP reduced malaria incidence compared to two doses, and timing of infection was not associated with maternal anaemia or perinatal mortality.
effect_estimate: 2.07 (first trimester infection vs later); crude IRR 3.56 (first trimester) and 1.72 (second trimester)
p_value: 0.002 (adjusted, first trimester); p<0.001 (crude, first trimester); p=0.034 (crude, second trimester)

title: Predicting the clinical outcome of severe falciparum malaria in african children: findings from a large randomized trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of artesunate versus quinine for severe malaria treatment in African children that has reported outcome results (mortality and clinical predictors).
population: children under 15 years hospitalized with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Predictors of death (mortality) in severe malaria
impact_summary: Base deficit, impaired consciousness, convulsions, elevated blood urea, and underlying chronic illness were independently associated with death, with mortality markedly increased when cerebral malaria combined with acidosis.
transmission_setting: African malaria-endemic settings (severe malaria in hospitalized children)

title: No evidence for spread of Plasmodium falciparum artemisinin resistance to Savannakhet Province, Southern Laos.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of artesunate efficacy for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times, cure rates, safety).
comparator: active comparator (2 mg/kg vs 4 mg/kg oral artesunate dosing regimens, both followed by artemether-lumefantrine)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time (PCT) and efficacy of artesunate treatment
impact_summary: No evidence of P. falciparum in vivo resistance to artesunate was found in southern Laos, with 100% PCR-corrected cure rates in both dosing groups.
transmission_setting: southern Laos, Savannakhet Province (border area with concern for spread of artemisinin resistance from Cambodia)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events developed during or after treatment in any patients.

title: [A randomized clinical trial comparing the effectiveness and tolerability of artemisinine-naphthoquine (Arco®) and artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem®) in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Benin].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in humans.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rates on days 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine single-dose regimen was as effective and well tolerated as artemether-lumefantrine in treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Beninese children.
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated without major side effects; safety assessed via post-treatment clinical and laboratory adverse events.

title: A phase III clinical trial of alpha, beta-arteether injection 150 mg/ml in patients of P falciparum malaria.
journal: Journal of the Indian Medical Association
screening_reason: Phase III RCT with reported outcome results (cure rate, parasite/fever clearance times, safety) evaluating an artemisinin antimalarial treatment for P. falciparum malaria in humans.
design: phase 3, multicentre, open label, single treatment study
population: patients with P falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: mean cure rate
impact_summary: Alpha, beta-arteether injection 150 mg/ml was highly effective and safe in treating P falciparum malaria, achieving a mean cure rate of 99.01%.
safety_summary: 6 of 101 patients had pain at injection site; no clinically significant changes in vitals or haematology parameters; no abnormal post-treatment values observed.

title: Comparative efficacies of artemisinin combination therapies in Plasmodium falciparum malaria and polymorphism of pfATPase6, pfcrt, pfdhfr, and pfdhps genes in tea gardens of Jalpaiguri District, India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three artemisinin combination therapies for P. falciparum malaria treatment with 42-day follow-up and reported outcome results (therapeutic efficacy rates).
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-mefloquine vs artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: patients with P. falciparum monoinfection uncomplicated malaria in tea gardens of Jalpaiguri District
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected clinical and parasitological therapeutic efficacy at day 42 per WHO protocol
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-mefloquine showed higher therapeutic efficacy than artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, which had a failure rate near the 10% threshold for drug policy change due to SP resistance mutations.
transmission_setting: tea garden areas of Jalpaiguri District, India

title: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine does not modify plasma cytokines and chemokines or intracellular cytokine responses to Plasmodium falciparum in Mozambican children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTi-SP) in children with reported outcome results on cytokine/immune responses and malaria incidence.
population: infants/children
primary_outcome: Effect of IPTi-SP on plasma cytokines/chemokines and intracellular cytokine responses to P. falciparum
impact_summary: IPTi-SP did not significantly modify plasma cytokine/chemokine levels or antigen-specific intracellular cytokine responses to P. falciparum compared to placebo, though IFN-γ:IL-4 ratios were higher in placebo recipients.
effect_metric: difference in cytokine/chemokine levels between treatment groups
safety_summary: IPTi-SP did not negatively affect the development of cellular immune responses during early childhood

title: Comparing changes in haematologic parameters occurring in patients included in randomized controlled trials of artesunate-amodiaquine vs single and combination treatments of uncomplicated falciparum in sub-Saharan Africa.
screening_reason: This is an individual-patient data analysis of seven completed randomized controlled trials comparing artesunate-amodiaquine to other treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans, with reported outcome results on haematologic parameters.
design: individual-patient data pooled analysis of randomized controlled trials
comparator: other forms of ACT, other combination therapy, mono-therapies
population: patients of all ages with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Occurrence and severity grade of haematologic changes (white cells total and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin/haematocrit, platelets) during follow-up
impact_summary: The effects of artesunate-amodiaquine on haematologic parameters (anaemia, thrombocytopaenia, neutropaenia, leucopaenia) were not significantly different from those of other anti-malarial treatments used in sub-Saharan Africa.
safety_summary: Pre-treatment leucopaenia (3%) and neutropaenia (6%) were infrequent; anaemia was common (39%) pre-treatment. TEAE incidence was 11% for neutropaenia, 6% for thrombocytopaenia with AS&AQ; anaemia TEAE was higher with AS&AQ (20%) and other ACT (22%) than non-artemisinin groups (4%). No systematic significant difference between treatments was detected; risks decreased with follow-up time (except neutropaenia which increased) and increased with baseline parasitaemia and parasitological reappearance; older patients had lower risk.
