title: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of monthly versus bimonthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine chemoprevention in adults at high risk of malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in adults with reported outcome results (malaria episodes and protective efficacy).
population: healthy adult male volunteers at high risk of malaria
primary_outcome: protective efficacy against malaria (incidence of malaria episodes) at 36 weeks
impact_summary: Monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine chemoprevention provided 98% protective efficacy against malaria and bimonthly dosing provided 86% efficacy, both significantly better than placebo.
transmission_setting: endemic area with P. vivax and multidrug-resistant P. falciparum
safety_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was well tolerated and safe to use; no major safety concerns reported.

title: Efficacy of different primaquine-based antimalarial regimens against Plasmodium falciparum gametocytemia.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatment regimens (primaquine-based) against P. falciparum gametocytemia in human participants.
comparator: active comparator (four regimens with and without primaquine)
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocytemia measured by thick smear on days 1, 4 and 8 after treatment initiation
impact_summary: Addition of primaquine to either amodiaquine-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine or mefloquine-artesunate regimens reduced P. falciparum gametocytemia more than the schizonticide alone, but none of the regimens fully cleared gametocytemia by day 8.

title: Randomized, prospective, three-arm study to confirm the auditory safety and efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine in Colombian patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine for malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: patients with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Percentage of patients with a baseline to Day-7 ABR Wave III latency increase of >0.30 msec
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was shown to be auditory-safe, with only 2.6% of patients exceeding the 0.30 msec ABR Wave III latency increase threshold, significantly below the prespecified 15% null hypothesis, and PCR-corrected cure rates were >95% to Day 42 in all groups.
effect_metric: percentage of patients exceeding 0.30 msec ABR Wave III latency increase
safety_summary: No apparent relationship found between drug exposure and ABR change; average improvements of 2-4 dB in pure-tone thresholds observed across all groups, supporting continued safe use of artemether-lumefantrine.

title: The effect of household heads training about the use of treated bed nets on the burden of malaria and anaemia in under-five children: a cluster randomized trial in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria and anaemia burden in children) testing a malaria vector-control intervention (bed net use training) with no early-phase restrictions.
comparator: standard care (control villages without household head training)
population: under-five children and household heads
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria and anaemia in under-five children assessed at baseline, six and 12 months
impact_summary: Training of household heads on proper use of long-lasting insecticide-treated bed nets significantly reduced the burden of malaria and anaemia in under-five children compared to control villages.
effect_estimate: 0.42 (malaria, high transmission season); 0.84 (anaemia, high transmission); 0.73 (anaemia, low transmission)
transmission_setting: high transmission/epidemic season and low transmission season

title: Similar efficacy and safety of artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem®) in African infants and children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria across different body weight ranges.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine treatment for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in African children with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: body weight dosing groups (within-treatment comparison, not placebo/active comparator)
population: African infants and children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day PCR-corrected cure rate
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine showed comparable 28-day PCR cure rates and similar safety/tolerability across all four body weight groups (5 to <35 kg).
safety_summary: No clinically relevant differences in safety or tolerability were observed between body weight groups.

title: Intermittent preventive therapy for malaria with monthly artemether-lumefantrine for the post-discharge management of severe anaemia in children aged 4-59 months in southern Malawi: a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial chemoprevention (artemether-lumefantrine) in children with severe malarial anaemia that has reported outcome results on mortality and hospital readmission.
population: children aged 4-59 months admitted for severe malarial anaemia after hospital discharge
primary_outcome: Composite of all-cause mortality or hospital readmittance because of all-cause severe anaemia or severe malaria between 1 and 6 months after enrolment
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive therapy with monthly artemether-lumefantrine after discharge reduced the risk of death or readmittance for severe anaemia or malaria by 31% between 1 and 6 months, with the protective effect concentrated during the 1-3 month IPTpd period and not sustained afterwards.
safety_summary: Safety of intermittent preventive therapy with artemether-lumefantrine was assessed; the trial reported on efficacy and safety, with no major safety concerns highlighted in the abstract beyond monitoring adverse events during the study.
funder: The Netherlands African Partnership for Capacity Development and Clinical Interventions Against Poverty Related Diseases, the UBS-Optimus Foundation, and the Gates Malaria Partnership

title: Age-dependent IgG subclass responses to Plasmodium falciparum EBA-175 are differentially associated with incidence of malaria in Mozambican children.
screening_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of intermittent preventive treatment in infants with reported outcome results (malaria incidence) as primary analysis.
population: infants and young children (Mozambican children)
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria in relation to IgG subclass antibody responses to EBA-175, MSP-1(19), and AMA-1
impact_summary: Higher cytophilic IgG1 and IgG3 responses to EBA-175 were associated with reduced malaria incidence, while higher noncytophilic IgG4 responses were associated with increased malaria incidence; no significant associations were found for antibodies to MSP-1(19) or AMA-1.

title: Impact of combining intermittent preventive treatment with home management of malaria in children less than 10 years in a rural area of Senegal: a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTc) combined with home-based management in children with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, parasitaemia prevalence, anaemia).
comparator: home management of malaria (HMM) alone (active comparator)
population: children less than 10 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of single episode of malaria attacks over 8 weeks of follow up
impact_summary: Combining seasonal intermittent preventive treatment with home management of malaria significantly reduced malaria incidence, parasitaemia prevalence, and anaemia compared to home management alone.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio for malaria incidence
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; no specific safety concerns mentioned in abstract

title: Declining responsiveness of Plasmodium falciparum infections to artemisinin-based combination treatments on the Kenyan coast.
screening_reason: RCT of artemisinin-based combination therapies for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, recrudescence rates).
population: children 6-59 months old with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological treatment response (residual parasitemia on day 1 and Kaplan-Meier estimated risk of recrudescent infection by day 84)
impact_summary: Parasite clearance rates to both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine declined significantly between 2005-2006 and 2007-2008 on the Kenyan coast.
transmission_setting: declining transmission setting on the Kenyan coast

title: Malaria vaccine cuts risk in half in late-stage trial.
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported outcome results showing efficacy in disease prevention.
impact_summary: A late-stage trial found the malaria vaccine reduced the risk of malaria by half.

title: A simple dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine based on arm span- or age range for childhood falciparum malaria: a preliminary evaluation.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, hematocrit) comparing two malaria treatment regimens (artesunate and amodiaquine) in children with falciparum malaria.
comparator: standard dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine calculated according to body weight (SDRAA)
population: children with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite and fever clearance and fall in hematocrit in the first 3 days
impact_summary: The arm span- or age range-based dose regimen (DRAAAS) was as effective and well tolerated as the standard weight-based dose regimen (SDRAA), showing similar parasite and fever clearance and hematocrit changes.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated.

title: Trial shows vaccine halves malaria episodes in children in Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported outcome results in human participants.
population: children
primary_outcome: malaria episodes
impact_summary: The vaccine reduced malaria episodes in children by about half.

title: Cost-effectiveness of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in infants (IPTi) for averting anaemia in Gabon: a comparison between intention to treat and according to protocol analyses.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results on IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants), a malaria chemoprevention intervention in humans; demonstrates efficacy on anaemia reduction.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Reduction of moderate anaemia (cost-effectiveness of IPTi)
impact_summary: IPTi was inexpensive and efficacious in averting cases of moderate anaemia in infants, though the impact on malaria itself was not statistically significant.
effect_metric: cost per episode of moderate anaemia averted

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus chloroquine in the treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria in Thailand: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments (DP vs chloroquine) for P. vivax malaria in humans with reported outcome results on efficacy and tolerability.
population: adults and children with acute P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy (recurrent infection/cumulative risk of recurrence) and tolerability of CQ vs DP for P. vivax malaria
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was more effective than chloroquine in preventing recurrent P. vivax infections, with faster fever and parasite clearance and lower recurrence rates.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for recurrence (CQ vs DP)
age_range: children and adults (including children <5 years old)
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated with no major safety concerns reported.

title: Circumsporozoite-specific T cell responses in children vaccinated with RTS,S/AS01E and protection against P falciparum clinical malaria.
screening_reason: Published Phase IIb randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine with reported outcome results showing efficacy against P. falciparum clinical malaria in children.
population: children 5-17 months of age
primary_outcome: Correlation between CS-specific T cell responses and protection from clinical malaria
impact_summary: TNFα(+) CD4+ T cell responses were independently associated with reduced risk of clinical malaria, and together with anti-CS antibody titers accounted for the protective effect of RTS,S/AS01E vaccination.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported in this immunology substudy; parent phase IIb trial reported acceptable safety profile.

title: Evidence for a useful life of more than three years for a polyester-based long-lasting insecticidal mosquito net in Western Uganda.
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial (LLIN vs conventionally treated nets) evaluating a malaria vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on net durability and insecticidal efficacy after three years of field use.
population: households/families in villages using mosquito nets
primary_outcome: Insecticidal effectiveness (bio-assay knock-down/mortality) and physical durability of nets over time
impact_summary: The polyester-based LLIN Interceptor retained sufficient insecticide and physical integrity to meet WHO phase III criteria, with an estimated useful life of three to four years, outperforming conventionally treated nets which lost insecticide rapidly.
effect_metric: proportion of nets meeting optimal bio-assay effectiveness (≥95% 60-min knock-down or ≥80% 24-hour mortality)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events mentioned

title: Evaluation of the impact of ZeroFly®, an insecticide incorporated plastic sheeting on malaria incidence in two temporary labour shelters in India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector-control intervention (insecticide-treated plastic sheeting) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence in humans; cluster design with temporary labour settlements as units; phase not early.
population: temporary labour settlement residents
primary_outcome: malaria incidence and resting density of malaria vectors (Anopheles culicifacies and An. stephensi)
impact_summary: ZeroFly insecticide-incorporated plastic sheeting substantially reduced mosquito resting density and malaria cases in labour camps compared to control camps using untreated plastic sheets.
effect_metric: reduction in malaria incidence and vector resting density
effect_estimate: almost complete reduction in resting density and reduction in malaria cases
transmission_setting: urban temporary labour settlements with malaria vector presence (Anopheles culicifacies and An. stephensi)
safety_summary: ZeroFly plastic sheeting was found safe for humans; some temporary complaints of skin irritation and itching were reported, no other adverse health effects; community acceptance was high.

title: Effects of amodiaquine and artesunate on sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine pharmacokinetic parameters in children under five in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP combinations) in children with reported pharmacokinetic outcome results.
comparator: SP alone vs SP+amodiaquine vs SP+artesunate
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Sulphadoxine and pyrimethamine pharmacokinetic parameters (day 7 concentrations, volume of distribution, elimination half-life)
impact_summary: SP exposure over the first seven days was similar across all three treatment arms despite differences in pyrimethamine volume of distribution and half-life, supporting continued use of SP with either AQ or AS in young Malian children.

title: Efficacy and effectiveness of mefloquine and artesunate combination therapy for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Peruvian Amazon.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy/effectiveness results for a malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine+artesunate) in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
comparator: non-directly observed therapy (effectiveness) vs directly observed therapy (efficacy)
population: patients aged 1 year and older with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitologic response (adequate clinical and parasitologic response) at day 28
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus artesunate combination therapy was highly efficacious and effective for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in the Peruvian Amazon.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; treatment well tolerated with no adverse events described

title: Maternal anemia in Benin: prevalence, risk factors, and association with low birth weight.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of IPTp (malaria chemoprevention intervention) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on low birth weight.
comparator: two drugs for IPTp compared to each other (equivalence trial)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: low birth weight (birth weight < 2,500 g)
impact_summary: Despite IPTp and supplementation, anemia remained highly prevalent during pregnancy, and severe anemia during the third trimester was associated with a nearly three-fold higher risk of low birth weight.

title: Randomized trials of artemisinin-piperaquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine phosphate and artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria in Cambodia-Thailand border area.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments reporting 28-day cure rates and clinical outcomes in malaria patients; Phase III treatment trial with published results.
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine vs artemisinin-piperaquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine phosphate)
population: uncomplicated falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: AP and DHP achieved higher 28-day cure rates than AL, with all three drugs remaining efficacious for treating multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria in the Cambodia-Thailand border area.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria epidemic area, Cambodia-Thailand border
safety_summary: All three drugs were well tolerated; self-limited side effects including anoxia, nausea, vomiting, headache and dizziness occurred in all groups with no remarkable differences between them.

title: Cognition, behaviour and academic skills after cognitive rehabilitation in Ugandan children surviving severe malaria: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a cognitive rehabilitation intervention in children with severe malaria; malaria is the primary focus; not early-phase safety-only.
population: Children aged 5 to 12 years surviving severe malaria
primary_outcome: Improvement in attention scores for the intervention group
impact_summary: Computerised cognitive rehabilitation training three months after severe malaria improved learning scores but not attention, working memory, academic skills, or behavior, with working memory scores actually lower in the intervention group.

title: Brain swelling and mannitol therapy in adult cerebral malaria: a randomized trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mannitol adjunctive therapy for cerebral malaria with reported outcome results (mortality and coma recovery); primary focus is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: adult patients with cerebral malaria and brain swelling on CT scan
primary_outcome: Coma recovery time and mortality with mannitol adjunctive therapy versus no adjunctive therapy
impact_summary: Adjunctive mannitol therapy for brain swelling in adult cerebral malaria prolonged coma recovery time and did not improve, and may have worsened, mortality.
p_value: .11 for mortality; .02 for coma recovery time
safety_summary: Mannitol therapy prolonged coma duration and may be harmful; mortality was higher with mannitol (30%) than without (13%), though not statistically significant.

title: Protective immunity induced with the RTS,S/AS vaccine is associated with IL-2 and TNF-α producing effector and central memory CD4 T cells.
screening_reason: Published RCT of RTS,S malaria vaccine with reported outcome results (protective immunity and immune correlates) in humans.
population: malaria-non-exposed adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Protection against controlled human malaria infection (sterile immunity) following sporozoite challenge
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS vaccination conferred sterile immunity against sporozoite challenge in 40% of subjects, and protection was associated with higher frequencies of IL-2 and TNF-α producing CD4 T effector/effector memory and central memory cells.
transmission_setting: non-endemic (malaria-naive volunteers, controlled human malaria infection)

title: Multicentric assessment of the efficacy and tolerability of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine compared to artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa.
screening_reason: Multicentric RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at day 28 follow-up.
population: patients aged two years and above with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Recovery rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response) by day 28
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was as effective and well-tolerated as artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with recovery rates of 99.5% versus 98.9% and no statistically significant difference.
effect_metric: recovery rate (PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response)
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; no serious adverse events reported; most adverse events were moderate and did not require treatment discontinuation.

title: Molecular markers of resistance to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine during intermittent preventive treatment of pregnant women in Benin.
screening_reason: Randomized clinical trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp with SP vs mefloquine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on efficacy and molecular resistance markers.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Prevalence of pfdhfr and pfdhps mutations and pfmdr1 copy number in P. falciparum before first and second IPTp administration and at delivery; efficacy of SP in preventing low birth weight
impact_summary: SP remained efficacious in preventing low birth weight despite a high prevalence of triple and quadruple pfdhfr/pfdhps mutations, and no correlation was found between these mutant genotypes and lack of SP efficacy or low birth weight/placental infection.

title: Superiority of 3 over 2 doses of intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the prevention of malaria during pregnancy in mali: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (placental malaria, LBW, preterm births) testing a malaria prevention intervention (IPTp-SP dosing regimen) in pregnant women.
population: pregnant women of all gravidity
primary_outcome: placental malaria
impact_summary: A third dose of IPTp-SP significantly reduced placental malaria, low birth weight, and preterm births compared to the standard 2-dose regimen.
transmission_setting: highly seasonal transmission with low levels of SP resistance
safety_summary: No significant differences in severe maternal skin reactions or neonatal jaundice between groups.

title: Comparative study of the efficacy and tolerability of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine-trimethoprim versus artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Cameroon, Ivory Coast and Senegal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (28-day efficacy, parasite clearance, adverse events).
population: patients at least two years of age with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria with fever
primary_outcome: Recovery rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response) at day 28 before and after PCR correction
impact_summary: DPT was non-inferior to AL, with both achieving 99% recovery rates at day 28 and similar tolerability, while DPT showed faster fever clearance and parasite clearance than AL.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic areas of Cameroon, Ivory Coast and Senegal
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; no serious adverse events reported; minor adverse events included vomiting, abdominal pain and pruritus, none requiring treatment discontinuation.

title: Clinical trial of extended-dose chloroquine for treatment of resistant falciparum malaria among Afghan refugees in Pakistan.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitological cure rates); not early-phase.
population: Afghan refugees with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure without recrudescence
impact_summary: Extended five-day chloroquine treatment (CQ40) resulted in significantly lower parasite recrudescence than standard three-day treatment (CQ25), but overall failure rates remained too high for CQ to be used as first-line therapy.
transmission_setting: refugee camp setting with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria
safety_summary: Fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and proportions gametocytaemic post-treatment were similar between treatment groups; no other adverse events reported.

title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics of a new pediatric formulation of artemether-lumefantrine in African children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine formulation) in children with P. falciparum malaria that has reported pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic outcome results.
population: African children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, weighing 5 to <35 kg
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC) of artemether, dihydroartemisinin, and lumefantrine after dispersible vs crushed tablet formulations
impact_summary: The new pediatric dispersible tablet formulation of artemether-lumefantrine provided similar systemic exposure to artemether, dihydroartemisinin, and lumefantrine compared to the crushed tablet formulation, with no apparent association between drug exposure and parasite clearance time or adverse events.
effect_estimate: Artemether: 175 vs 190 ng/ml; DHA: 64.7 vs 63.7 ng/ml; Lumefantrine: 6.3 vs 7.7 μg/ml (dispersible vs crushed)
safety_summary: No apparent association between lumefantrine Cmax and occurrence of adverse events or corrected QT interval changes

title: The impact of retail-sector delivery of artemether-lumefantrine on malaria treatment of children under five in Kenya: a cluster randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria treatment intervention (subsidized ACT delivery) with reported outcome results on prompt AL treatment coverage in children.
comparator: standard/unsubsidized retail sector access (control sublocations without subsidy intervention)
population: children aged 3-59 months with fever in the past 2 weeks
primary_outcome: proportion of children aged 3-59 months reporting fever in the past 2 weeks who started treatment with AL on the same day or following day of fever onset
impact_summary: Subsidizing artemether-lumefantrine through retail providers significantly increased the proportion of febrile children receiving prompt AL treatment compared to control areas.
effect_metric: difference in percentage points between arms
safety_summary: Not reported; no significant differences observed in adherence to AL between arms

title: Effect of the pre-erythrocytic candidate malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01E on blood stage immunity in young children.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of the malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01E in children with reported outcome results on antibody responses and clinical malaria risk.
population: young children
primary_outcome: Antibody concentrations to P. falciparum merozoite antigens (AMA-1, MSP-1(42), EBA-175, MSP-3) and growth inhibitory activity (GIA) over time
impact_summary: Vaccination with RTS,S/AS01E led to modest reductions in anti-merozoite antibody concentrations and no significant change in growth inhibitory activity, but these were not correlates of clinical immunity to malaria.
age_range: young children (up to 32 months of age)

title: Oral artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated hyperparasitaemic Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine) in children with P. falciparum, with reported outcome results (clinical recovery, haematocrit changes, parasitaemia decline); malaria treatment is the primary purpose and phase is not stated as early-phase.
population: children with uncomplicated hyperparasitaemic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy, changes in haematocrit and decline in parasitaemia
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine led to clinical recovery within 2 days without progression to severe malaria and similar declines in haematocrit and parasitaemia.
safety_summary: Falls in haematocrit in the first 3 days after treatment were similar between groups and less than 5%; no progression to severe malaria observed.

title: Evaluating indoor residual spray for reducing malaria infection prevalence in Eritrea: results from a community randomized control trial.
screening_reason: Community randomized controlled trial of indoor residual spray (a vector-control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria parasite infection prevalence.
comparator: control areas without indoor residual spray
population: individuals/households in Gash Barka Zone, an area with high ITN coverage and low malaria prevalence
primary_outcome: Malaria parasite infection prevalence
impact_summary: Indoor residual spraying showed no significant difference in malaria parasite infection prevalence between treatment and control areas, and IRS/ITN interventions alone appear insufficient to interrupt transmission.
effect_estimate: 0.5% overall, no significant difference between treatment and control
transmission_setting: low malaria parasite prevalence area with near universal ITN coverage

title: Efficacy of chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine either alone or in combination before introduction of ACT as first-line therapy in uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Jalpaiguri District, West Bengal, India.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions (chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates) in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
comparator: active comparator (Chloroquine vs Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine vs combination)
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate (early and late treatment failure) at day 28 by WHO protocol
impact_summary: Chloroquine had a high failure rate of 61%, exceeding the WHO threshold for drug policy change, while Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine alone (14%) and Chloroquine plus Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine (8%) had lower failure rates.
transmission_setting: Chloroquine-sensitive to resistant P. falciparum endemic district

title: Therapeutic efficacy and effects of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine coformulated or copackaged on malaria-associated anemia in children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Southwest Nigeria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results including fever clearance, parasite clearance, and anemia recovery.
population: children under 12 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Drug-attributable fall in hematocrit (DAFH) and resolution of malaria-associated anemia
impact_summary: AL, AAcf and AAcp cleared fever and parasitemia rapidly and had similar rates of resolution of malaria-associated anemia after treatment in Nigerian children.
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated.

title: Reduction of anti-malarial consumption after rapid diagnostic tests implementation in Dar es Salaam: a before-after and cluster randomized controlled study.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria rapid diagnostic test implementation with reported outcome results on anti-malarial consumption and prescription.
comparator: standard care (presumptive treatment without mRDTs, control health facilities without mRDTs)
population: clinicians and febrile patients including children under five years of age attending health facilities
primary_outcome: Anti-malarial consumption from routine statistics and anti-malarial prescription during observed consultations before and after mRDT implementation
impact_summary: Implementation of malaria rapid diagnostic tests drastically reduced anti-malarial over-treatment, with prescription decreasing significantly more in intervention health facilities than in control facilities, though antibiotic prescription increased.
age_range: all ages including children under five years
safety_summary: Adherence to test results was excellent with only 7% of mRDT-negative patients receiving an anti-malarial; however, antibiotic prescription increased from 49% to 72% after intervention, raising concerns about irrational antibiotic use.

title: A simple dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine based on age or body weight range for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children: comparison of therapeutic efficacy with standard dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment regimens (artesunate-amodiaquine variants and artemether-lumefantrine) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria; primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
comparator: standard dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine (SDRAA), fixed-dose artesunate-amodiaquine (FDAA), artemether-lumefantrine (AL)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria aged 15 years or younger
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance time and PCR-uncorrected cure rates on days 28-42
impact_summary: A new age/weight-based dose regimen of artesunate and amodiaquine (NDRAA) achieved faster parasite clearance and higher cure rates than standard-dose artesunate-amodiaquine, and was as efficacious as artemether-lumefantrine in children under 5 years.
safety_summary: Changes in hematocrit values and reported adverse events were similar between NDRAA and SDRAA groups; all drug regimens were well tolerated.

title: Efficacy and effectiveness of artemether-lumefantrine after initial and repeated treatment in children <5 years of age with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in rural Tanzania: a randomized trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes for artemether-lumefantrine treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: unsupervised intake of artemether-lumefantrine vs supervised intake of artemether-lumefantrine
population: children under 5 years of age with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate by day 56 (initial treatment) and day 42 (after retreatment), estimated by survival analysis
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was highly efficacious, well-tolerated and safe after both initial and repeated treatment, even when unsupervised, despite significantly lower lumefantrine blood concentrations compared with supervised intake.
effect_estimate: 98.1% (supervised) vs 95.1% (unsupervised) after initial treatment; 92.9% vs 97.6% after retreatment
follow_up: 56 days after initial treatment; 42 days after retreatment
safety_summary: Well-tolerated and safe; vomiting was the most commonly reported drug-related adverse event, occurring in 1% of patients after both initial and repeated treatment.

title: Effectiveness of a community intervention on malaria in rural Tanzania - a randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (anaemia prevalence, fever reduction) evaluating a malaria case management intervention in children in Tanzania.
comparator: standard care (control group without community intervention)
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: Anaemia prevalence
impact_summary: Anaemia prevalence decreased significantly after the community intervention, with a slightly greater decrease in the intervention group than in the control group.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Effects of lime juice on malaria parasite clearance.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (ACT with/without lime juice) with reported outcome results on parasite clearance.
population: children with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Time to achieve >75% reduction in parasite load and complete parasite clearance by 72 h
impact_summary: Adding lime juice to artemisinin combination therapy significantly reduced the time to parasite clearance and reduced early treatment failure compared to ACT alone.
safety_summary: No side effects were observed with the use of lime juice.

title: Cost-effectiveness of artemisinin combination therapy for uncomplicated malaria in children: data from Papua New Guinea.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial regimens in children with reported treatment outcomes; malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: conventional treatment with chloroquine plus sulfadoxine plus pyrimethamine (CQ+S+P)
population: children aged 6 to 60 months with Plasmodium falciparum and/or P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Incremental cost per incremental treatment success by day 42 and cost per life year saved
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was the most cost-effective regimen for P. falciparum malaria and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was the most cost-effective regimen for P. vivax malaria compared to conventional treatment.
effect_estimate: US$6.97 per treatment success for A+L (P. falciparum); ~US$58 per life year saved
transmission_setting: Papua New Guinea, endemic malaria region

title: Safety and efficacy of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Zambian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at 28 and 42 days.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28/42
impact_summary: DHA/PQP was as efficacious, safe and well tolerated as AL for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with higher PCR-uncorrected ACPR due to fewer new infections but similar PCR-corrected ACPR between arms.
effect_metric: odds ratio (PCR-corrected ACPR at day 42, DHA/PQP vs AL)
safety_summary: No differences in adverse events between arms except cough more frequent in DHA/PQP arm (p=0.04); two serious adverse events probably associated with AL treatment.

title: Clinical Trial Report: Double-Dose Chloroquine for Treatment of Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Guinea-Bissau.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (double-dose chloroquine) in humans.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria

title: Pharmacokinetic properties of conventional and double-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine given as intermittent preventive treatment in infancy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infancy) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention in infants that reports pharmacokinetic outcomes and malaria incidence results.
comparator: conventional dose vs double dose (active comparator)
population: infants aged 2 to 13 months
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic disposition (AUC, bioavailability, elimination half-life) of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine at conventional versus double dose
impact_summary: Double-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine produced higher plasma exposure (AUC) than conventional dose, was well tolerated with no adverse effects on hemoglobin or hepatorenal function, and fewer children developed malaria during follow-up in the double-dose group, supporting further study of double-dose IPTi.
effect_estimate: PYR: 4915 vs 2844 µg·day/L; SDX: 2434 vs 1460 mg·day/L (double vs conventional dose)
follow_up: 28 days (with additional sampling up to 21 days post-dose)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region of Papua New Guinea
safety_summary: Both conventional and double doses were well tolerated with no changes in hemoglobin or hepatorenal function; five children in the conventional dose group and three in the double-dose group developed malaria during follow-up.

title: Follow-up survey of children who received sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for intermittent preventive antimalarial treatment in infants.
screening_reason: Published follow-up results from a randomized controlled trial of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, a malaria chemoprevention intervention in humans with reported outcome findings.
population: infants who received IPTi
primary_outcome: Malariometric parameters and anti-Plasmodium falciparum lysate IgG antibody levels
impact_summary: Malariometric parameters were similar between SP and placebo groups, but anti-P. falciparum lysate IgG antibody levels remained lower in the SP arm, suggesting reduced overall parasite antigen exposure after IPTi.

title: Effect of artesunate and mefloquine in combination on the Fridericia corrected QT intervals in Plasmodium falciparum infected adults from Thailand.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: RCT comparing artesunate-mefloquine fixed vs. loose dosing in P. falciparum-infected adults with reported ECG outcome results; malaria treatment is primary purpose.
comparator: active comparator (fixed dose vs loose tablet artesunate-mefloquine combination)
population: Plasmodium falciparum infected adults
primary_outcome: Fridericia corrected QT (QTcF) interval changes on 12-lead ECG at days 0, 3, and 7
impact_summary: QTcF interval increases observed with artesunate-mefloquine treatment were best explained by slowing heart rate due to malaria resolution rather than mefloquine drug concentration.
p_value: P < 0.003 (D3 and D7 vs D0); P = 0.001 for heart rate as significant variable
safety_summary: One male patient in the loose tablet arm had a QTcF of 504 ms on day 3, but ECG intervals were otherwise similar between drug arms; no other significant safety concerns for Torsades de Pointe risk identified.

title: Artesunate/mefloquine paediatric formulation vs. artemether/lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum in Anonkoua kouté, Côte d'Ivoire.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate/mefloquine vs artemether/lumefantrine) in children with confirmed P. falciparum malaria reporting primary outcome results (28-day cure rates).
population: children with confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day PCR-corrected cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine paediatric formulation was as effective as artemether-lumefantrine, with both regimens showing high cure rates and good tolerability.
safety_summary: Both drug regimens were well tolerated.

title: Confirmed vivax resistance to chloroquine and effectiveness of artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of vivax malaria in Ethiopia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing chloroquine and artemether-lumefantrine for vivax malaria treatment with reported outcome results (28-day treatment failure rates).
population: outpatients with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: cumulative incidence of treatment failure at day 28
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine showed a higher treatment failure rate than chloroquine for vivax malaria, though findings were inconclusive due to unsupervised evening doses of AL.

title: An open randomized clinical trial in comparing two artesunate-based combination treatments on Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Nigerian children: artesunate/sulphamethoxypyrazine/pyrimethamine (fixed dose over 24 hours) versus artesunate/amodiaquine (fixed dose over 48 hours).
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two artemisinin-combination therapies for P. falciparum malaria treatment in children, with primary outcomes (PCR-corrected cure rates) and safety data clearly presented.
population: children aged 1 to 13 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected parasitological cure rate and clinical response at day 28
impact_summary: AS + SMP given over 24 hours had similar efficacy and safety to AS + AQ given over 48 hours for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Nigerian children, though re-infection rate was higher with AS + SMP.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported in either arm; laboratory values (packed cell volume, liver enzymes, bilirubin) remained within normal limits, though packed cell volume was significantly lower in the AS + SMP group.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of artesunate-amodiaquine combinations and the plasma and saliva concentrations of desethylamodiaquine in children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artesunate-amodiaquine for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (clinical recovery, parasite clearance, pharmacokinetic findings).
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (fever and parasite clearance) and plasma/saliva concentrations of desethylamodiaquine
impact_summary: Artesunate-amodiaquine coformulated and copackaged treatments were equally effective, with all children recovering clinically and remaining aparasitemic for at least 28 days, and desethylamodiaquine concentrations in saliva paralleled those in plasma.
safety_summary: All children recovered clinically with no adverse events reported.

title: Immunological consequences of intermittent preventive treatment against malaria in Senegalese preschool children.
screening_reason: Published RCT of IPTc (chemoprevention) in malaria-endemic children reporting immunological outcome results; not early-phase.
population: preschool children aged 6 months to 5 years
primary_outcome: Anti-Plasmodium falciparum schizont extract IgG antibody levels
impact_summary: Children who received IPTc had lower anti-Plasmodium IgG antibody levels than controls, but previous IPTc did not appear to interfere with the parasite-dependent acquired humoral immune response eight months after the last drug administration.

title: The clinical impact of combining intermittent preventive treatment with home management of malaria in children aged below 5 years: cluster randomised trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of IPTc (chemoprevention) for malaria in children with reported outcome results (fever incidence, parasitaemia prevalence).
population: children aged below 5 years
primary_outcome: Incidence rate of febrile episodes diagnosed presumptively as malaria by community-based drug distributors in each intervention group
impact_summary: Adding seasonal intermittent preventive treatment to home management of malaria lowered incidence of presumptive malaria fevers in children under 5, with the effect being statistically significant only among children who received all three IPTc courses.
follow_up: 1 year (including follow-up into the subsequent year for rebound morbidity)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no differences in anaemia or haemoglobin concentration between groups and no rebound morbidity observed in the following year.

title: HIV and placental infection modulate the appearance of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum in pregnant women who receive intermittent preventive treatment.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of IPTp (malaria chemoprevention in pregnancy) with reported outcome results on drug-resistance markers and clinical outcomes.
population: pregnant women receiving intermittent preventive treatment
primary_outcome: Prevalence of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) drug-resistance molecular markers (quintuple mutant infections) in peripheral and placental P. falciparum isolates
impact_summary: IPTp with SP increased the prevalence of drug-resistance markers in placental and peripheral P. falciparum isolates, particularly in HIV-infected women, but this was not associated with increased parasite density or worse clinical outcomes.
safety_summary: No association was found between mutant infections and increased parasite density or malaria-related morbidity in mothers and children.

title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of arterolane maleate following multiple oral doses in adult patients with P. falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (arterolane maleate) in humans; Phase II is not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (different dose levels of arterolane maleate: 50 mg vs 100 mg vs 200 mg)
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationship (AUC and parasite clearance indices: PC50, PC90, PCT, recrudescence)
impact_summary: A minimum 150-mg dose of arterolane maleate was recommended to optimize therapeutic benefit, with doses above 100 mg unlikely to further reduce recrudescence probability.

title: A phase III, randomized, non-inferiority trial to assess the efficacy and safety of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in comparison with artesunate-mefloquine in patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in southern Laos.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published Phase III RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria treatments in humans, meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 63-day cure rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response) by survival analysis
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was non-inferior to artesunate-mefloquine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Laos and was associated with fewer adverse effects.
effect_metric: difference in 63-day cure rates (AM minus DP)
safety_summary: Adverse events were more frequent with AM (44%, 38/87) than DP (31%, 57/182); relative risk 0.6, 95% CI 0.4-0.9, P = 0.04.

title: Effect of repeated treatment of pregnant women with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and azithromycin on preterm delivery in Malawi: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on preterm delivery and low birth weight.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) twice (control) vs monthly SP vs monthly SP plus two doses of azithromycin
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Incidence of preterm delivery
impact_summary: Monthly SP plus two doses of azithromycin significantly reduced preterm delivery and low birth weight incidence compared with the standard two-dose SP control.
p_value: 0.01 (preterm delivery, AZI-SP vs control); 0.02 (LBW, AZI-SP vs control); 0.32 (preterm delivery, monthly SP vs control)
safety_summary: Incidence of serious adverse events was low in all groups.

title: Efficacy of an insecticide paint against malaria vectors and nuisance in West Africa--part 2: field evaluation.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of an IRS vector-control product (insecticide paint) for malaria with reported entomological outcome results; Phase II evaluation per WHOPES procedures.
design: randomized, experimental hut trial, phase 2 (WHOPES phase II procedures)
population: experimental huts with local pyrethroid-resistant An. gambiae and Culex quinquefasciatus populations; mosquito release experiments with malaria-free reared An. gambiae females
primary_outcome: Entomological criteria including deterrence, excito-repellence, blood-feeding inhibition and mosquito mortality
impact_summary: The insecticide paint Inesfly 5A IGR showed sustained high mortality rates against pyrethroid-resistant An. gambiae and long-term residual efficacy over 12 months, suggesting potential as an additional vector control tool in areas of pyrethroid resistance.
effect_estimate: 90-100% at 6 months; 90-93% at 9 months (An. gambiae); 96-100% mortality at 1 meter distance up to 12 months
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic West Africa, pyrethroid-resistant vector setting
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; study focused on entomological outcomes, no adverse events mentioned

title: Early variations in plasmodium falciparum dynamics in Nigerian children after treatment with two artemisinin-based combinations: implications on delayed parasite clearance.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin-based malaria treatments in Nigerian children with reported efficacy and parasitaemia outcomes at multiple timepoints.
population: children aged 12 to 132 months with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Early parasite clearance dynamics and cure rates on days 3, 7, 14, 28, and 42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine were highly efficacious (>90% cure rates) and well tolerated, with a subset of children in both groups showing an early rise in peripheral parasitaemia within 0-4 hours of treatment before rapid clearance.
safety_summary: Both drug combinations were well tolerated with minimal side effects.

title: Plasmodium falciparum clearance with artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) in patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ACT treatment for malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance); phase not stated but treatment trial of primary malaria intervention is eligible.
comparator: artesunate plus mefloquine (Artequin) vs artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem), stratified by G6PD status
population: children and adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance after ACT treatment (day 1 and day 2) compared between G6PD-deficient and G6PD-normal participants
impact_summary: G6PD deficiency did not significantly influence the clearance of P. falciparum after ACT treatment in patients with uncomplicated malaria.

title: Artesunate versus quinine in the treatment of severe falciparum malaria in African children (AQUAMAT): an open-label, randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate vs quinine) in African children with severe falciparum malaria reporting mortality and clinical outcomes.
population: children under 15 years with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: in-hospital mortality, analysed by intention to treat
impact_summary: Artesunate substantially reduced in-hospital mortality compared with quinine in African children with severe malaria.
effect_metric: odds ratio for mortality (stratified for study site)
safety_summary: Artesunate was well tolerated with no serious drug-related adverse effects; it was associated with less frequent coma, convulsions, deterioration of coma score, and post-treatment hypoglycaemia compared with quinine.

title: Symptom-based diagnosis of malaria and its implication on antimalarial drug use in pregnancy in Central Uganda: results from a community trial.
journal: International journal of adolescent medicine and health
screening_reason: Community intervention RCT testing intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy with reported outcome results on diagnostic approaches and antimalarial drug use.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Sensitivity of symptom-based (fever-based) diagnosis of malaria and antimalarial drug use in pregnancy
impact_summary: Symptom-based diagnosis had low sensitivity (26.4%) for detecting malaria, resulting in substantial under-diagnosis and over-treatment with antimalarial drugs among pregnant women.

title: Is parasite clearance clinically important after malaria treatment in a high transmission area? A 3-month follow-up of home-based management with herbal medicine or ACT.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria treatments (herbal medicine vs ACT) in a high transmission area, measuring clinical efficacy and safety over 84 days.
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria treated at home
primary_outcome: association between residual parasitaemia at day 28 and subsequent malaria episodes and/or anaemia through day 84
impact_summary: Total parasite clearance at day 28 was not associated with subsequent incidence of uncomplicated or severe malaria or moderate anaemia, and clinical outcomes were similar between AM and ACT groups.
effect_estimate: 0.33 vs 0.31 episodes/patient (uncomplicated malaria, AM vs ACT)
age_range: children ≤5 years and older patients (age range not fully specified)
safety_summary: No significant differences in severe malaria (<6% per month in patients aged ≤5 years) or moderate anaemia (1.1% in both groups at day 84) between groups.

title: Influences of intermittent preventive treatment and persistent multiclonal Plasmodium falciparum infections on clinical malaria risk.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPT (intermittent preventive treatment) in malaria-endemic children with reported outcome results on clinical malaria risk and parasite diversity.
population: children 3-59 months
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria morbidity and anaemia during 12 months follow-up in relation to parasite genetic diversity
impact_summary: Seasonal intermittent preventive treatment temporarily reduced prevalence and genetic diversity of P. falciparum infections, and multiclonal infections were associated with protection from subsequent malaria only in children who did not receive intermittent treatment.
transmission_setting: high transmission, seasonal malaria transmission season

title: Persistence of Plasmodium falciparum parasites in infected pregnant Mozambican women after delivery.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of IPTp (intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy) with reported outcome results on malaria parasitemia persistence; malaria prevention in pregnancy is the primary focus.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Postpartum P. falciparum infection detected by qPCR and genetic relatedness of postpartum parasites to placental infection at delivery
impact_summary: Postpartum malaria infection was more common in women with placental infection at delivery and less common in older women, and half of matched infections shared parasite strains with those found in the placenta at delivery, suggesting persistence of infection after delivery.
effect_estimate: OR=4.20 (placental infection at delivery); OR=0.34 (older age)

title: Directly-observed therapy (DOT) for the radical 14-day primaquine treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (primaquine adherence via DOT) in humans with primary endpoint of P. vivax reappearance prevention.
population: Patients aged 3 years and older diagnosed with P. vivax malaria by microscopy
primary_outcome: Reappearance of P. vivax parasite within the 90-day follow-up period
impact_summary: Directly-observed therapy significantly reduced the reappearance rate of P. vivax malaria compared to self-administered therapy.
safety_summary: All patients recovered without serious adverse effects.

title: Social acceptability and durability of two different house screening interventions against exposure to malaria vectors, Plasmodium falciparum infection, and anemia in children in the Gambia, West Africa.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of house screening vector-control interventions for malaria with reported outcome results on social acceptability and durability.
comparator: screened ceilings vs full screening vs no screening
population: children and households in rural Gambia
primary_outcome: Social acceptability and durability of house screening interventions
impact_summary: House screening (full screening and screened ceilings) was well-appreciated by residents and durable over 12 months, effectively reducing mosquito and insect entry despite slightly increased indoor nighttime temperatures.
p_value: P = 0.05 (temperature difference full vs ceiling); P < 0.001 (temperature difference full vs none)
safety_summary: No adverse safety events reported; minor complaints about heat (9% full screening, 17% ceiling screening)

title: The effects of a pre-season treatment with effective antimalarials on subsequent malaria morbidity in under five-year-old children living in high and seasonal malaria transmission area of Burkina Faso.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment interventions (SP and AL) in children in a high-transmission area, with clear efficacy endpoints (time to re-infection, incidence density).
population: under five-year-old children
primary_outcome: time to first malaria infection and time to first malaria episode following pre-season treatment
impact_summary: Pre-season treatment with AL led to faster reinfection and higher incidence of subsequent malaria episodes compared to SP and untreated controls, suggesting radical parasite clearance may increase susceptibility to malaria.
effect_metric: incidence of malaria episodes per 1000 child days-at-risk
follow_up: not specified (transmission season, home visits twice weekly)
transmission_setting: high and seasonal malaria transmission area

title: A comparison of iron and folate with folate alone in hematologic recovery of children treated for acute malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (hematocrit recovery) in children treated for acute malaria; malaria is the primary focus.
population: children with smear-positive malaria and anemia (hematocrit < 33%)
primary_outcome: Hematologic recovery (change in hematocrit) at four weeks
impact_summary: Iron plus folate supplementation improved hematologic recovery more than folate alone in children treated for acute malaria.
effect_metric: mean increase in hematocrit at 4 weeks
safety_summary: No significant worsening of malaria severity reported; iron supplementation did not adversely affect outcomes.

title: Zambia Integrated Management of Malaria and Pneumonia Study
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine) with rapid diagnostics by community health workers in Zambia; phase not applicable for community-based intervention.
comparator: standard care (Ministry of Health policy: AL for all febrile children, referral for suspected pneumonia)
population: children 6 months to 5 years with fever and/or difficult/fast breathing
primary_outcome: Number of Children Who Received Early and Appropriate Treatment for Pneumonia.
impact_summary: Community health workers using rapid diagnostic tests reduced inappropriate AL use for fever and increased early appropriate antibiotic treatment for nonsevere pneumonia compared to standard care.
effect_estimate: 0.23 for AL use in fever; 5.32 for early appropriate pneumonia treatment
safety_summary: Two deaths occurred in the intervention arm and one in the control arm.

title: Impact of repeated four-monthly anthelmintic treatment on Plasmodium infection in preschool children: a double-blind placebo-controlled randomized trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT with reported outcome results on malaria (Plasmodium) infection in humans; anthelmintic intervention impacts malaria prevalence and parasite density in preschool children.
population: preschool children aged 12-59 months
primary_outcome: Plasmodium infection prevalence and parasite density over time
impact_summary: Repeated four-monthly albendazole treatment resulted in a significantly slower increase in Plasmodium infection prevalence compared to placebo over 14 months.
effect_metric: odds ratio (rate of increase in Plasmodium prevalence over time)

title: Comparison of artesunate and quinine in the treatment of Sudanese children with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artesunate vs quinine for treating severe malaria in children with reported outcomes (fever clearance, parasite clearance, mortality, adverse events).
population: children with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever, parasite clearance, and coma resolution times
impact_summary: No significant difference was found between intravenous artesunate and quinine in fever, parasite clearance, and coma resolution times, with fewer deaths in the artesunate group.
safety_summary: Three patients died (one in the artesunate group, two in the quinine group); one patient developed hypoglycaemia following quinine infusion.

title: Protective efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in infants (IPTi) using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and parasite resistance.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of SP-IPTi intervention for malaria prevention in infants with analysis of protective efficacy against resistance markers.
population: infants
primary_outcome: protective efficacy of SP-IPTi against clinical malaria at 35 days post the 9-month dose and up to 12 months of age
impact_summary: Higher frequency of dhfr triple and dhfr/dhps quintuple mutations was associated with reduced protective efficacy of SP-IPTi against malaria.
effect_estimate: inverse relationship between resistance mutation frequency and efficacy
p_value: borderline significant; significant for dhfr triple mutation and 35-day post 9-month dose efficacy
transmission_setting: varied endemic settings across sub-Saharan Africa

title: Comparative study of efficacy of artesunate plus cotrimoxazole and artesunate plus chloroquine in the treatment of malaria in Nigerian children: a preliminary report.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-based combinations) in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate on Day 14 (parasitological and clinical response), fever clearance time, parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artesunate plus cotrimoxazole showed similar efficacy to artesunate plus chloroquine, with both groups achieving 100% cure rates on Day 14 and similar fever and parasite clearance times.
safety_summary: Both drug combinations were well-tolerated in the small population of children.

title: Comparison of quinine and rabeprazole with quinine monotherapy in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment interventions (quinine ± rabeprazole) in humans with parasitological and clinical endpoints.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Addition of rabeprazole to quinine resulted in a significantly faster parasite clearance rate compared to quinine plus placebo, with no significant difference in fever clearance time or treatment failure.
safety_summary: No late clinical failure or late parasitological failure observed in either group; some patients lost to follow-up or withdrawn.

title: Effectiveness of five artemisinin combination regimens with or without primaquine in uncomplicated falciparum malaria: an open-label randomised trial.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing artemisinin combination therapies for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results on efficacy and gametocytocidal effects.
place: Myanmar (Burma) - Rakhine state, Kachin state, Shan state
comparator: active comparator (four fixed-dose ACTs and loose artesunate-mefloquine, with or without primaquine)
population: adults and children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria or mixed infection, older than 6 months and weighing more than 5 kg
primary_outcome: 63-day recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-amodiaquine had significantly higher recrudescence rates than the other ACT regimens, and adding a single dose of primaquine substantially reduced P falciparum gametocyte carriage, while all regimens were well tolerated.
age_range: older than 6 months, weighing more than 5 kg
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated; adverse events reported by 599 patients, most commonly vomiting and dizziness; other side-effects were less common and not related to specific treatment.
funder: Médecins sans Frontières (Holland) and the Wellcome Trust Mahidol University Oxford Tropical Medicine Research Programme

title: Multiplicity of Plasmodium falciparum infection following intermittent preventive treatment in infants.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results on IPTi-SP (chemoprevention intervention) for malaria in infants with measured primary endpoints on multiplicity of infection.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Multiplicity of Plasmodium falciparum infection (MOI) assessed by msp1 and msp2 genotyping
impact_summary: IPTi-SP had no significant effect on the multiplicity of P. falciparum infection compared to placebo at any age tested.
follow_up: 15 months of age (assessed at 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 months)

title: Artesunate suppositories: an option for severe malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT evaluating artesunate (a malaria treatment) with reported outcome results; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.

title: Bottlenecks for high coverage of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy: the case of adolescent pregnancies in rural Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized community-based trial with reported outcome results on IPTp-SP effectiveness (a malaria prevention intervention in pregnant women), not early-phase.
design: health center randomized, community-based trial with mixed-methods (quantitative + qualitative focused ethnography)
comparator: standard IPTp-SP delivery vs. additional promotional campaign
population: pregnant women, including adolescent primigravidae and secundigravidae, in rural setting
primary_outcome: IPTp-SP coverage (ANC visit attendance and SP uptake) and malaria infection risk by age group
impact_summary: Adolescent pregnant women had significantly higher risk of malaria infection but lower ANC attendance and SP uptake compared to adults, indicating adolescents are a bottleneck to achieving high IPTp-SP coverage.
effect_metric: odds ratio for malaria infection risk (adolescent vs adult primigravidae)
transmission_setting: rural, high malaria transmission season, sub-Saharan Africa

title: Safety and immunogenicity of the malaria vaccine candidate GMZ2 in malaria-exposed, adult individuals from Lambaréné, Gabon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine candidate with reported safety and immunogenicity outcome results in humans.
population: malaria-exposed adults
primary_outcome: Safety and immunogenicity (anti-GMZ2 antibody levels) one month after full vaccination course
impact_summary: GMZ2 vaccination was well tolerated and induced higher antibody levels and more specific memory B-cells than the rabies control vaccine in malaria-exposed adults.
effect_metric: fold increase in baseline-corrected anti-GMZ2 antibody levels
follow_up: 1 month after full vaccination course (approximately 3 months total)
safety_summary: Both GMZ2 and rabies control vaccines were well tolerated

title: Sickle-cell disease and malaria: evaluation of seasonal intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in Senegalese patients-a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention (intermittent preventive treatment) in a malaria-endemic population.
population: sickle-cell disease patients
primary_outcome: malaria incidence and morbidity of sickle-cell anemia
impact_summary: Monthly seasonal intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine reduced malaria prevalence to zero cases in the SP arm compared to four cases in the placebo arm, and reduced patients' complaints and blood transfusion requirements, with no impact on vaso-occlusive crisis or hospitalization.
effect_estimate: 0% in SP arm vs cases in placebo arm (overall prevalence 6.6%)
transmission_setting: seasonal, high transmission during rainy season (July-October) in malaria endemic area
safety_summary: SP treatment was well tolerated; only one patient (1.6%) in the SP arm reported pruritus; no patient deaths occurred during the study.

title: An open-label, randomised study of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artesunate-mefloquine for falciparum malaria in Asia.
screening_reason: This is a published randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination treatments for P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: Patients aged 3 months to 65 years with Plasmodium falciparum mono-infection or mixed infection
primary_outcome: Day-63 PCR genotype-corrected cure rate
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was non-inferior to artesunate-mefloquine for curing falciparum malaria, with fewer new infections but higher gametocyte carriage.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria endemic areas in Asia
safety_summary: Fifteen serious adverse events reported: 12 (1.6%) in DHA/PQP group and 3 (0.8%) in AS+MQ group; six (0.8%) considered related to DHA/PQP and three (0.8%) to AS+MQ.

title: Use of area under the curve to evaluate the effects of antimalarial drugs on malaria-associated anemia after treatment.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug regimens with reported outcome results (anemia recovery metrics) in malaria-infected children.
comparator: artesunate-mefloquine vs mefloquine alone; artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-artesunate
population: anemic children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Area under the curve (AUC) of hematocrit deficit over time as a measure of malaria-associated anemia resolution
impact_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine resulted in significantly lower anemia exposure (AUC) than mefloquine alone, while artemether-lumefantrine and amodiaquine-artesunate showed similar anemia resolution times and AUC.
effect_estimate: 35.5 vs 49.8 (artesunate-mefloquine vs mefloquine); 57.1 vs 46.3 (artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-artesunate)

title: Successful field trial of attractive toxic sugar bait (ATSB) plant-spraying methods against malaria vectors in the Anopheles gambiae complex in Mali, West Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ATSB vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on malaria vector population density and longevity.
design: field trial, controlled, non-randomized (control and treatment site comparison)
comparator: ASB (Attractive Sugar Bait without toxin) sprayed in control site
population: wild mosquito populations of Anopheles gambiae complex (An. gambiae and An. arabiensis)
primary_outcome: Relative abundance and age-grading (gonotrophic cycle completion) of female and male An. gambiae s.l. mosquitoes before and after ATSB treatment
impact_summary: A single application of ATSB plant-spraying reduced the relative abundance of male and female An. gambiae s.l. by about 90% and reduced vector longevity in the treatment site, while the control site sprayed with non-toxic ASB showed increased longevity.
effect_metric: percent reduction in relative mosquito abundance
transmission_setting: semi-arid, malaria-endemic rural district with man-made pond larval habitats
safety_summary: ATSB described as environmentally safe; no adverse events reported as this was an entomological field trial, not a human safety trial

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine, in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in central Sudan.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response / cure rate by day 28
