impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine were highly effective, with cure rates of 100% and 98.7% respectively, and the difference was not statistically significant.
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa malaria-endemic area, central Sudan
safety_summary: Adverse effects were mild (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dizziness and/or rash), resolved spontaneously, and occurred in only five patients in each treatment arm.

title: Impact of promoting longer-lasting insecticide treatment of bed nets upon malaria transmission in a rural Tanzanian setting with pre-existing high coverage of untreated nets.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of longer-lasting insecticide-treated bed nets (a vector-control malaria intervention) with reported entomological outcome results comparing EIR across conditions.
comparator: untreated bed nets / historical baseline transmission
population: rural villagers in Namawala and Idete villages, all age groups
primary_outcome: entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
impact_summary: Longer-lasting insecticide treatment of bed nets combined with high coverage further reduced malaria transmission intensity by 4.6-fold beyond the reduction achieved by untreated nets alone.
effect_metric: fold reduction in entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
transmission_setting: high-transmission rural setting in southern Tanzania, historically extremely high malaria transmission

title: Effect of incentives on insecticide-treated bed net use in sub-Saharan Africa: a cluster randomized trial in Madagascar.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial testing a malaria vector-control intervention (ITN use incentives) with reported outcome results on net use and ownership.
population: households in villages following free ITN distribution campaign
primary_outcome: ITN use (visual confirmation of a mounted ITN) at one month and six months
impact_summary: Household-level incentives significantly increased ITN use in the short term (one month) but this effect diminished by six months, with no overall difference in use between groups at six months.
effect_estimate: 1.24 at one month; 0.97 at six months

title: Prevention of the recurrence of anaemia in Gambian children following discharge from hospital.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprevention (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results in a malaria-endemic setting; phase not stated but study design appropriate for systematic review inclusion.
population: children with moderate or severe anaemia (Hb <7 g/dL) discharged from hospital
primary_outcome: proportion of children with moderate or severe anaemia at the end of the malaria transmission season
impact_summary: Intermittent monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine did not reduce the proportion of previously anaemic children with moderate or severe anaemia at the end of the malaria season, but it did reduce clinical malaria episodes.
follow_up: until end of malaria transmission season (2003 or 2004)
safety_summary: SP was safe and well tolerated; no serious adverse events related to SP administration were observed; mortality was low in both groups (6 in SP group, 9 in placebo group).

title: Analysis of an ordinal outcome in a multicentric randomized controlled trial: application to a 3- arm anti- malarial drug trial in Cameroon.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing three antimalarial drug treatments in 538 children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported outcome results on efficacy analyzed using ordinal regression methods.
design: three-arm, multicentric (three-centre), randomized controlled trial, phase 3
comparator: active comparator (Amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs combination)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: WHO four-category ordered criterion of therapeutic efficacy (clinical and parasitological response)
impact_summary: SP alone showed significantly lower efficacy than AQ, while the AQ+SP combination showed equal effectiveness to AQ alone.
effect_estimate: SP vs AQ: OR 0.14, HR 0.605; AQ+SP vs AQ: OR 1.70, HR 1.40

title: New fixed-dose artesunate-mefloquine formulation against multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum in adults: a comparative phase IIb safety and pharmacokinetic study with standard-dose nonfixed artesunate plus mefloquine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (artesunate-mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results (safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetic parameters) over 28 days.
comparator: nonfixed artesunate plus mefloquine (standard-dose, weight-based dosing)
population: adults hospitalized with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety (clinical laboratory, ECG, adverse events) and pharmacokinetic parameters over 28 days
impact_summary: The new fixed-dose artesunate-mefloquine formulation was well tolerated and had pharmacokinetic profiles broadly similar to standard nonfixed artesunate plus mefloquine, supporting its use as a suitable replacement.
p_value: P <= 0.0027 for QT prolongation; P <= 0.0003 for heart rate decrease
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with no drug-related adverse events; two serious adverse events of malaria-induced hypotension occurred in the AS-MQ arm requiring rescue treatment; no significant changes in hematology, biochemistry, or PR/QRS intervals; significant QT prolongation and heart rate decrease observed in both arms.

title: Phase II trial on the use of Dextran 70 or starch for supportive therapy in Kenyan children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Published Phase II RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (fluid resuscitation) in humans; not early-phase.
population: children with severe falciparum malaria and acidosis (base deficit >8 mmol)
primary_outcome: resolution of shock over 8 hours
impact_summary: No significant difference was found between Dextran 70 and hydroxyethyl starch in resolving shock at 8 hours, and both fluids were associated with low mortality, suggesting they are safe options for volume resuscitation in severe malaria.
effect_metric: proportion with shock resolution at 8 hrs
safety_summary: Four deaths (5%), two per arm, including three deaths in the coma subgroup; no other new adverse events (allergic reactions, pulmonary edema, neurologic sequelae) were reported.

title: Effect of ivermectin on Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes fed on humans: the potential of oral insecticides in malaria control.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ivermectin as a malaria vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on mosquito mortality.
population: adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Survival of Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes fed on treated versus untreated volunteers
impact_summary: Ivermectin significantly reduced mosquito survival compared to controls when mosquitoes fed on treated volunteers shortly after treatment, but this effect was not present after 14 days.
safety_summary: Ivermectin was reported to be safe.

title: Wash-resistance and field evaluation of alphacypermethrin treated long-lasting insecticidal net (Interceptor) against malaria vectors Anopheles culicifacies and Anopheles fluviatilis in a tribal area of Orissa, India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (vector control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results on vector efficacy and feeding rates; phase not applicable for cluster-randomized vector-control trial.
population: residents of tribal villages in a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Entomological indices including mosquito entry rate, mortality, knockdown effect, feeding success rate, parity rate and human blood index of Anopheles culicifacies and Anopheles fluviatilis
impact_summary: Interceptor long-lasting insecticidal nets significantly reduced mosquito entry rate, feeding success, parity rate and human blood index of malaria vectors compared to untreated or no nets, with sustained 100% mortality even after 20 washings.

title: Community effectiveness of intermittent preventive treatment for infants (IPTi) in rural southern Tanzania.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Large-scale cluster-randomized effectiveness trial of IPTi (malaria chemoprevention in infants) with reported outcome results on parasitemia prevalence.
population: infants aged 2-11 months
primary_outcome: parasitemia prevalence and anemia among children aged 2-11 months
impact_summary: IPTi implemented through routine health services reduced malaria parasitemia prevalence, with a 19 percentage point reduction observed among children who had recently received IPTi in a per-protocol analysis.
transmission_setting: rural, endemic malaria transmission in southern Tanzania

title: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate or artemether in Vietnamese adults with severe falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin derivatives for severe falciparum malaria treatment in humans with reported mortality and parasitaemia outcomes.
population: adults with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality (death) and parasite clearance in patients treated with intramuscular artesunate vs artemether
impact_summary: Intramuscular artesunate resulted in a lower death rate (7%) than intramuscular artemether (13%) and more rapid parasite clearance, suggesting artesunate may be superior, though the mortality difference did not reach statistical significance.
safety_summary: Both drugs were very well tolerated.

title: A comparison of two short-course primaquine regimens for the treatment and radical cure of Plasmodium vivax malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine treatment for P. vivax malaria with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, relapse rates); malaria treatment is the primary purpose; phase is not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (primaquine 30 mg vs 60 mg daily for 7 days)
population: Thai adult males with acute Plasmodium vivax malaria and normal G6PD screening
primary_outcome: Cumulative 28-day relapse rate by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis
impact_summary: The 60 mg/day primaquine regimen resulted in a significantly lower 28-day relapse rate than the 30 mg/day regimen.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; all patients recovered fully; two patients (one from each group) had a 30% reduction in hematocrit; adverse effects were similar between groups.

title: Evaluation of Interceptor long-lasting insecticidal nets in eight communities in Liberia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of Interceptor LLINs for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (residual insecticide, utilization, parasitaemia prevalence).
population: households in rural returnee villages
primary_outcome: Residual alpha-cypermethrin concentration measured by HPLC and participant utilization/acceptability of the ITNs
impact_summary: Interceptor LLINs retained insecticide better than conventionally treated nets, maintained high utilization and retention, and were associated with a decrease in parasitaemia prevalence over one year.
effect_metric: Chemical residue loss after one year
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events mentioned

title: Efficacy and tolerability of artesunate-amodiaquine (Camoquin plus) versus artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) against uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria: multisite trial in Senegal and Ivory Coast.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and tolerability results comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria; Phase IV trial is not early-phase.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria over age 7 years
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: Artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed similar high efficacy and tolerability against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with no statistically significant difference in ACPR rates.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events observed; minor adverse events were significantly more frequent in the AS+AQ arm; no significant biological parameter changes between D0 and D7 except anaemia.

title: Community-wide benefits of targeted indoor residual spray for malaria control in the western Kenya highland.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of targeted indoor residual spray (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results on malaria prevalence, incidence, and vector density.
design: cluster-based intervention study, community-wide targeted spray with intervention vs nonintervention area comparison
population: children aged 1-5 years (cohort study) and school children aged 6-13 years (parasitological surveys)
primary_outcome: Malaria prevalence and incidence in children, and vector density, in intervention versus nonintervention areas
impact_summary: Targeted indoor residual spraying of malaria transmission hotspots in valley bottoms reduced malaria prevalence, incidence, and vector densities not only in the sprayed valley areas but also indirectly in the more densely populated uphill areas.
effect_estimate: 64.4% (valley) and 46.3% (uphill) reduction in school children prevalence; 65.4% (valley) and 46.4% (uphill) reduction in cohort incidence rate by week 14
species: Plasmodium (species not specified, presumably P. falciparum)
transmission_setting: Highland malaria transmission hotspots (valley bottoms) in western Kenya

title: The effect of food consumption on lumefantrine bioavailability in African children receiving artemether-lumefantrine crushed or dispersible tablets (Coartem) for acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine) in children with reported efficacy results (28-day cure rate primary endpoint).
comparator: crushed tablets vs dispersible tablets; food vs no food intake
population: infants and children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day PCR-corrected cure rate
impact_summary: Concomitant food intake, particularly milk, increased lumefantrine bioavailability in children receiving artemether-lumefantrine, but did not affect the high 28-day PCR-corrected cure rate.
effect_metric: increase in lumefantrine bioavailability with milk intake vs no food

title: Efficacy of non-artemisinin- and artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Cameroon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing artemisinin-based and non-artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (multiple ACT and non-ACT drug combinations compared against each other)
population: children with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (PCR-uncorrected on day 14 and PCR-corrected on day 28)
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine appeared to be the most effective treatment with no treatment failure due to recrudescence, closely followed by dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, while artesunate-amodiaquine was as effective as other drug combinations.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, endemic with chloroquine and emerging antifolate resistance
safety_summary: Further studies are needed to evaluate the clinical efficacy and tolerance of these combinations in different epidemiological contexts.

title: Is mosquito larval source management appropriate for reducing malaria in areas of extensive flooding in The Gambia? A cross-over intervention trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (cross-over design) of a malaria vector-control intervention (larviciding) with reported outcome results including larval/adult mosquito densities and clinical malaria incidence.
population: rural villages in flood-prone areas along the Gambia River
primary_outcome: clinical malaria incidence and anemia; larval and adult mosquito densities
impact_summary: Larviciding reduced late-stage anopheline larval densities by 88% but had no significant effect on adult mosquito densities, clinical malaria, or anemia.
transmission_setting: rural, seasonal flooding, riverine, seasonal transmission
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events on humans mentioned.

title: The use of placebo in a trial of rectal artesunate as initial treatment for severe malaria patients en route to referral clinics: ethical issues.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (mortality/disability) for a malaria treatment intervention (rectal artesunate for severe malaria).
population: severe malaria patients en route to referral clinics
primary_outcome: death or permanent disability
impact_summary: A single artesunate suppository significantly reduced death or permanent disability among patients who could not reach a clinic rapidly, with no difference between artesunate and placebo among those who reached clinic rapidly.

title: Doxycycline-chloroquine vs. doxycycline-placebo for malaria prophylaxis in nonimmune soldiers: a double-blind randomized field trial in sub-Saharan Africa.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT comparing malaria chemoprophylaxis regimens with reported outcome results (adverse effects, compliance, malaria cases) in a primary malaria prevention intervention.
population: nonimmune French soldiers deployed in Africa
primary_outcome: Tolerability (adverse effects) of doxycycline-chloroquine combination vs. doxycycline alone for malaria prophylaxis
impact_summary: The doxycycline-chloroquine combination showed similar tolerability and efficacy to doxycycline alone, with a higher proportion of nausea or vomiting in the combination group.
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, deployed nonimmune military personnel
safety_summary: About 57% of volunteers in both groups reported at least one adverse effect; tolerability was similar except for a higher proportion of nausea or vomiting in the doxycycline-chloroquine group; no significant decrease in overall tolerability.

title: [Therapeutic efficacy of a regimen of artesunate-mefloquine-primaquine treatment for Plasmodium falciparum malaria and treatment effects on gametocytic development].
journal: Biomedica : revista del Instituto Nacional de Salud
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-mefloquine-primaquine) with reported clinical and parasitological outcome results.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical response and parasite elimination efficacy (parasitological cure) assessed on days 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, and 42
impact_summary: Both AS-MQ and AS-MQ-PQ achieved 100% clinical and parasitological efficacy, and adding primaquine improved and accelerated gametocyte clearance compared to AS-MQ alone.

title: [Changes in retinol, hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations in Colombian children with malaria].
journal: Biomedica : revista del Instituto Nacional de Salud
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (antimalarial drugs) as the primary intervention in humans, not early-phase.
comparator: antimalarial treatment alone (Group M) vs combinations with retinol supplement and/or anti-parasitic drug
population: children with malaria, aged 4-10 years
primary_outcome: Changes in hemoglobin, ferritin, retinol and C reactive protein concentrations from day 0 to day 30 after treatment
impact_summary: Simultaneous administration of retinol supplement and anti-parasite treatment prevented the hemoglobin reduction observed on day 8, but no significant differences among groups were found by day 30.
effect_metric: mean hemoglobin concentration difference between groups on day 8
effect_estimate: Group MAP higher than other groups
p_value: significant on day 8 (p<0.05, exact value not reported)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events described.

title: Efficacy of amodiaquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and their combination for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Cameroon at the time of policy change to artemisinin-based combination therapy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported efficacy outcomes in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
comparator: active comparator (AQ vs SP vs AQ+SP combination)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological outcome (ETF, LCF, LPF, ACPR) on day 28 per WHO criteria, corrected for reinfection by PCR
impact_summary: AQ, SP and AQ+SP treatments were well tolerated but showed low efficacy, with adequate clinical and parasitological response rates ranging from about 62% to 82% depending on site and drug, indicating alternative treatments were needed in Cameroon since 2005.
effect_metric: Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) rate on day 28
p_value: p < 0.001 (for SGK haplotype prevalence variation between sites)
transmission_setting: Three ecologically different regions: littoral equatorial forest (Mutengene), forest-savannah mosaic (Yaoundé), guinea-savannah (Garoua)
safety_summary: AQ, SP and AQ+SP treatments were well tolerated

title: Active malaria morbidity management has limited impact on height status of preschool Senegalese children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) in preschool children with reported outcome results on growth/stunting endpoints.
comparator: placebo (in original IPT trial); control group not part of malaria trial (in this follow-up study)
population: preschool children aged 2-5 years
primary_outcome: Mean height-for-age Z-score and stunting prevalence in September 2004
impact_summary: Active malaria morbidity management and IPT trial participation did not significantly improve overall height-for-age Z-scores compared to controls, though children aged 36-47 months in the trial group had lower stunting prevalence than controls.
follow_up: 15 months (original IPT trial), assessed again in September 2004

title: Gel versus capillary electrophoresis genotyping for categorizing treatment outcomes in two anti-malarial trials in Uganda.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing two anti-malarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs. dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in humans with reported efficacy outcome results (treatment failure rates).
design: randomized controlled trial, comparative genotyping methodology substudy
comparator: artemether-lumefantrine (AL) vs. dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP); gel vs. capillary electrophoresis genotyping
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria enrolled in anti-malarial treatment trials
primary_outcome: 42-day risk of treatment failure (recrudescence vs. new infection) as classified by gel versus capillary electrophoresis genotyping
impact_summary: Gel electrophoresis overestimated the risk of recrudescence compared to capillary electrophoresis in the high-transmission site (Apac), while results were similar in the moderate-transmission site (Kanungu), indicating capillary electrophoresis provides more accurate treatment outcome classification in high-transmission areas.
effect_estimate: Kanungu: AL 6.9% (gel) vs. 5.5% (capillary); DP 2.4% vs. 2.9%. Apac: AL 17.0% (gel) vs. 10.7% (capillary); DP 8.5% vs. 3.4%
p_value: Kanungu: AL p=0.4, DP p=0.5; Apac: AL p=0.02, DP p=0.03

title: A randomized trial of artesunate mefloquine versus artemether lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Senegalese children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments with reported efficacy and safety outcome results at 28 days follow-up.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (cure rate) at Day 28
impact_summary: Both artesunate mefloquine and artemether lumefantrine achieved high cure rates with artesunate mefloquine showing slightly higher efficacy and good tolerability in Senegalese children.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response at Day 28 (PCR-corrected, per protocol)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported; most frequent AE was vomiting (30% in AS+MQ arm vs 36% in AL arm); no clinically significant abnormal laboratory values related to study drug.

title: Molecular markers of resistance to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine one year after implementation of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in infants in Mali.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (22 health sub-districts randomized 1:1 to intervention vs control) with reported outcome results on molecular markers of SP resistance following IPTi implementation for malaria prevention in infants.
population: children aged 0-5 years
primary_outcome: Prevalence of molecular markers (dhfr and dhps mutations) associated with SP resistance in Plasmodium falciparum
impact_summary: One year after implementation of IPTi with SP, there was no significant increase in the frequency of molecular markers of SP resistance compared to the non-intervention zone.
effect_metric: prevalence of quadruple mutants (triple dhfr-mutants + dhps-437G)

title: Intermittent preventive treatment of malaria with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine during pregnancy in Burkina Faso: effect of adding a third dose to the standard two-dose regimen on low birth weight, anaemia and pregnancy outcomes.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP chemoprevention in pregnant women with reported outcome results (LBW, anaemia, premature birth) in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: pregnant women in 2nd or 3rd trimester
primary_outcome: prevalence of low birth weight (<2500 g), severe anaemia (Hb <8 g/dL) and premature birth
impact_summary: A third dose of IPTp-SP significantly reduced the risk of severe anaemia compared to the standard two-dose regimen, but did not significantly reduce low birth weight, likely due to low uptake of the intervention.
effect_metric: adjusted Incident Rate Ratio (AIRR) for severe anaemia

title: A cluster randomized controlled cross-over bed net acceptability and preference trial in Solomon Islands: community participation in shaping policy for malaria elimination.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of bed net vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on LLIN acceptability and preference for malaria elimination.
comparator: three LLIN brands compared against each other (Olyset, PermaNet, DuraNet)
population: community members in Malaita Province selected via three-stage sampling
primary_outcome: Bed net acceptability and preference evaluated through surveys at three defined time points after short and longer-term trial of each LLIN
impact_summary: PermaNet had significantly higher acceptability after short-term use than Olyset and DuraNet, while DuraNet's acceptability increased over time due to fewer adverse events and Olyset's decreased due to net wrinkling/shrinkage after washing.
effect_estimate: PermaNet 96.5% vs Olyset 67.3% vs DuraNet 69.8%; perceived non-protective nets OR 0.15; pleasant sleep OR 6.3; soft texture OR 5.7
safety_summary: Minor adverse events were noted with LLIN use; DuraNet showed reduction in minor adverse events following longer-term use, contributing to increased acceptability.

title: Effect of joint iron and zinc supplementation on malarial infection and anaemia.
journal: East African journal of public health
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results on a malaria prevention intervention (chemoprophylaxis augmented with zinc supplementation) in pregnant women; primary malaria focus with results published.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: malaria parasitaemia and maternal iron status (serum ferritin, Hb concentrations)
impact_summary: Joint iron and zinc supplementation reduced malaria parasite densities and prevented decline in maternal iron stores compared to iron-only supplementation in pregnant women.
effect_metric: adjusted geometric mean serum ferritin concentration

title: Therapeutic efficacy and effects of artesunate-mefloquine and mefloquine alone on malaria-associated anemia in children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in southwest Nigeria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-mefloquine vs mefloquine) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results including efficacy and anemia endpoints.
population: children aged 10 years or younger with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment efficacy (parasite/fever clearance and cure rates) and effects on malaria-associated anemia
impact_summary: Both artesunate-mefloquine and mefloquine alone effectively treated uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with AMQ clearing parasitemia and gametocytes faster and causing less fall in hematocrit, though rates of anemia resolution were similar.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; all children recovered clinically.

title: Chlorproguanil-dapsone-artesunate versus chlorproguanil-dapsone: a randomized, double-blind, phase III trial in African children, adolescents, and adults with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published Phase III RCT comparing malaria treatment interventions (CDA vs CPG-DDS) in African children and adults with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: children, adolescents, and adults with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 PCR-corrected parasitologic cure rate (per-protocol population)
impact_summary: CDA achieved a higher day 28 PCR-corrected cure rate than CPG-DDS but caused significant hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients, limiting further development.
effect_metric: treatment difference in day 28 PCR-corrected cure rate
safety_summary: No deaths occurred; hemolytic composite hemoglobin safety endpoint occurred in 30% of G6PD-deficient CDA patients and 29% of G6PD-deficient CPG-DDS patients, versus <1% and 3% respectively in G6PD-normal patients, indicating hemolytic risk with CDA in G6PD-deficient individuals.

title: Randomized, double-blind study of the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of tafenoquine versus mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis in nonimmune subjects.
screening_reason: Published Phase III RCT of tafenoquine versus mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis with reported efficacy and safety outcome results in human subjects.
population: nonimmune adult soldiers (malaria prophylaxis)
primary_outcome: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of tafenoquine versus mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis
impact_summary: No malaria diagnoses occurred in either group during deployment, but a small number of P. vivax infections occurred after prophylaxis discontinuation in both groups, with similar rates between tafenoquine and mefloquine, and tafenoquine was found to be safe, well tolerated, and highly efficacious.
effect_metric: proportion with P. vivax infection post-deployment
follow_up: 20 weeks after discontinuation of medication (up to 1 year for keratopathy resolution)
safety_summary: Treatment-related adverse events similar between groups (tafenoquine 13.4%, mefloquine 11.7%); no clinically significant hematological/biochemical differences; 0.6% of tafenoquine subjects discontinued due to possible drug-related adverse events; mild vortex keratopathy occurred in 93% of tafenoquine subjects with no effect on visual acuity, fully resolved by 1 year.

title: Field evaluation of ZeroFly--an insecticide incorporated plastic sheeting against malaria vectors & its impact on malaria transmission in tribal area of northern Orissa.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a vector-control intervention (insecticide-treated plastic sheeting) against malaria with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and mosquito density.
comparator: untreated plastic sheet and no sheet (standard practice)
population: tribal community residents in a highly malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: malaria incidence in the study villages
impact_summary: ZeroFly deltamethrin-treated plastic sheeting significantly reduced mosquito entry, feeding success, and malaria incidence compared to untreated plastic sheet and no sheet areas.
transmission_setting: highly endemic, tribal area with Anopheles culicifacies and An. fluviatilis as vectors

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated malaria in African children: a randomised, non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (ACTs) in African children with reported outcome results (day 28 PCR-corrected cure rates and safety data).
place: Burkina Faso, Kenya, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia
countries: Burkina Faso; Kenya; Mozambique; Uganda; Zambia
population: children 6-59 months old with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 PCR-corrected cure rate
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in African children, with a comparable safety profile and fewer new infections by day 42.
effect_metric: difference in day 28 PCR-corrected cure rate (DHA-PQP vs AL)
p_value: p<0.0001 (for new infection incidence by day 42)
safety_summary: DHA-PQP showed a comparable safety profile to artemether-lumefantrine

title: Impact of RTS,S/AS02(A) and RTS,S/AS01(B) on genotypes of P. falciparum in adults participating in a malaria vaccine clinical trial.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of RTS,S malaria vaccines with reported outcome results on parasite genotypes and multiplicity of infection in vaccinated vs control adults.
population: semi-immune adults
primary_outcome: Multiplicity of infection (MOI) and csp allelic characteristics of parasite isolates at baseline and break-through infections
impact_summary: Both RTS,S/AS02(A) and RTS,S/AS01(B) vaccines were associated with reduced multiplicity of infection compared to a rabies vaccine comparator, but did not show preferential effects against csp alleles similar to the 3D7 vaccine strain.
effect_metric: median number of parasite genotypes (multiplicity of infection)
transmission_setting: Kombewa District, western Kenya, malaria-endemic area

title: Selection of parasites with diminished drug susceptibility by amodiaquine-containing antimalarial regimens in Uganda.
screening_reason: Published RCT of antimalarial regimens (AQ-SP, AS-AQ, AL) in Ugandan children with malaria, reporting in vitro susceptibility and parasitological outcome results.
population: Ugandan children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: In vitro susceptibility (IC50) to monodesethylamodiaquine (MDAQ) of parasites collected from children treated with different antimalarial regimens
impact_summary: Prior treatment with amodiaquine-containing regimens (AQ-SP or AS-AQ) selected for Plasmodium falciparum parasites with diminished in vitro susceptibility to monodesethylamodiaquine compared to parasites from untreated or non-AQ treated patients.
effect_estimate: 62.9 nmol/L (AQ-exposed) vs 37.5 nmol/L (not treated within 12 weeks) vs 28.8 nmol/L (non-AQ arm)

title: [Sensitivity of Plasmodium vivax to chloroquine in Laza City, Myanmar].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine treatment for P. vivax malaria with reported efficacy outcomes; phase not stated but treatment trials with no mention of early phase are acceptable.
population: patients infected with Plasmodium vivax
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and cure rate on day 28
impact_summary: P. vivax remained fully sensitive to chloroquine, with all patients clearing parasites within 3 days and achieving a 100% cure rate by day 28.
transmission_setting: China-Myanmar border, imported vivax malaria cases

title: Use of short message service (SMS) to improve malaria chemoprophylaxis compliance after returning from a malaria endemic area.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (compliance indicators) for a malaria chemoprophylaxis intervention (doxycycline) in humans; not early-phase.
population: French soldiers returning from a malaria endemic area (Côte d'Ivoire)
primary_outcome: Chemoprophylaxis compliance assessed by electronic medication monitoring device (daily proportion of compliant individuals, average number of pills taken, early discontinuation)
impact_summary: Daily SMS reminders did not significantly improve malaria chemoprophylaxis compliance compared to control, though they were well received and considered useful.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine and chloroquine plus primaquine for the treatment of Plasmodium vivax in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs chloroquine plus primaquine for P. vivax) with reported outcome results on efficacy and relapse rates.
place: Ethiopia (Debre Zeit and Nazareth, East Shoa)
comparator: chloroquine alone vs chloroquine plus primaquine
population: patients with microscopically confirmed P. vivax malaria presenting to outpatient settings
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (cumulative incidence of therapeutic failure at day 28) and relapse rate by day 157
impact_summary: Both chloroquine and chloroquine plus primaquine showed similar treatment failure rates at day 28, but chloroquine plus primaquine significantly reduced the cumulative risk of relapse by day 157 compared to chloroquine alone.
effect_metric: cumulative risk of relapse at day 157
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; treatment failures and relapses were monitored, with no major safety concerns reported beyond efficacy outcomes.

title: Ursodeoxycholic acid and artesunate in the treatment of severe falciparum malaria patients with jaundice.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate) with reported outcome results on liver function in severe P. falciparum patients; primary purpose is malaria intervention.
population: severe P. falciparum malaria patients with jaundice, aged >=15 years
primary_outcome: Percentage change in liver tests (total bilirubin, aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase) over 4 weeks
impact_summary: Combined UDCA and artesunate therapy was safe but did not significantly improve liver tests compared to placebo and artesunate, except for a smaller increase in alkaline phosphatase at week 1.
effect_metric: median percentage change in alkaline phosphatase at week 1
effect_estimate: less increment in UDCA group vs placebo
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were observed during the 4 weeks of follow-up.

title: Placental malaria and low birth weight in pregnant women living in a rural area of Burkina Faso following the use of three preventive treatment regimens.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria chemoprevention regimens (IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcome results (placental malaria, low birth weight).
comparator: chloroquine weekly chemoprophylaxis (CWC/CQ) and intermittent preventive treatment with chloroquine (IPTp/CQ)
population: pregnant women attending first antenatal care visit in a rural area
primary_outcome: Placental malaria and low birth weight at delivery
impact_summary: IPTp with sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine was superior to IPTp with chloroquine and classical chloroquine chemoprophylaxis in reducing placental malaria, maternal infection, and low birth weight.
follow_up: from first antenatal visit until delivery
transmission_setting: rural, malaria-endemic area of Burkina Faso

title: Potential toxicity of chlorpheniramine plus chloroquine for the treatment of childhood malaria.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rate, adverse effects) testing malaria treatment in humans; phase is not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
comparator: active comparator (higher dose chlorpheniramine plus chloroquine vs high dose chlorpheniramine plus chloroquine)
population: children with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: vital signs, clinical response and parasite clearance on days 0-7 and day 14
impact_summary: The higher dose chlorpheniramine plus chloroquine regimen had no additional benefit over the high dose regimen but caused more drowsiness and lower respiratory rates, suggesting increased risk without added benefit.
safety_summary: Drowsiness occurred in 66.7% of high dose and 86.3% of higher dose CP+CQ subjects (p=0.05); higher dose group had significantly lower respiratory rates on days 2, 6, and 14, raising safety concerns.

title: Efficacy of four insect repellents against mosquito bites: a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled field study in Senegal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector-control intervention (insect repellents) with reported outcome results on mosquito-bite protection in humans.
population: healthy male and female volunteers experienced with mosquito capture
primary_outcome: Protection against mosquito bites (number of mosquito bites/landings) after skin application of repellent compared to placebo
impact_summary: All four repellents (icaridine 20%, PMD 20%, PMD 50%, DEET 50%) provided significant and similar protection against mosquito bites compared to placebo, lasting 8 hours.
transmission_setting: field study in two villages in Senegal
safety_summary: No serious adverse drug reaction was noticed

title: Argemone mexicana decoction versus artesunate-amodiaquine for the management of malaria in Mali: policy and public-health implications.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing a malaria treatment intervention (Argemone mexicana decoction) to standard ACT in humans with uncomplicated malaria, meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: patients with presumed uncomplicated malaria (median age 5 years) in a remote Malian village
primary_outcome: Requirement for second-line treatment within 28 days
impact_summary: Argemone mexicana decoction was less effective than artesunate-amodiaquine at preventing need for second-line treatment (89% vs 95%), but was well tolerated with low rates of severe malaria.
age_range: median age 5 years; children </=5 years and >5 years analyzed
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated; deterioration to severe malaria occurred in 1.9% of children aged </=5 years in both groups, with no cases in patients >5 years and no coma/convulsions.

title: Effect of two different house screening interventions on exposure to malaria vectors and on anaemia in children in The Gambia: a randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (house screening) with reported outcome results (mosquito entry, anaemia, parasitaemia) in humans.
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years living in study houses
primary_outcome: Number of female Anopheles gambiae sensu lato mosquitoes collected per trap per night
impact_summary: House screening (full screening or screened ceilings) substantially reduced indoor malaria vector density and reduced the frequency of anaemia in children compared with unscreened control houses.
effect_metric: ratio of means (mosquito density) and adjusted odds ratio (anaemia)
effect_estimate: 0.41 (full screening) and 0.53 (screened ceilings) for mosquito density; OR 0.53 (full screening) and OR 0.51 (screened ceilings) for anaemia
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, low bednet use

title: The neurological assessment in young children treated with artesunate monotherapy or artesunate-mefloquine combination therapy for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate monotherapy vs. combination therapy) with reported neurological outcome results in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
comparator: artesunate monotherapy vs artesunate-mefloquine combination therapy, with non-febrile healthy controls
population: young children aged 3 months to 5 years with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Neurological testing targeting coordination and behaviour at multiple timepoints
impact_summary: Antimalarial treatments (artesunate alone or artesunate-mefloquine) were not associated with worsening neurological performance, and treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria led to improvement in neurological performance, while mefloquine reduced recurrent malaria infection compared to artesunate alone.
effect_metric: proportion with recurrent malaria infection during follow-up
effect_estimate: lower in mefloquine combination group vs artesunate monotherapy
safety_summary: No significant CNS effects detected from artesunate or mefloquine on coordination and behaviour testing; study could not exclude subtle or rare CNS effects.

title: The TLR9 agonist CpG fails to enhance the acquisition of Plasmodium falciparum-specific memory B cells in semi-immune adults in Mali.
screening_reason: Published RCT testing a malaria vaccine (blood-stage subunit vaccine with TLR9 agonist CpG) in humans with reported outcome results on memory B cell acquisition.
population: semi-immune adults
primary_outcome: Acquisition of Plasmodium falciparum-specific memory B cells
impact_summary: The TLR9 agonist CpG failed to enhance the acquisition of P. falciparum-specific memory B cells in semi-immune adults in Mali, unlike its effect in nonimmune U.S. volunteers.

title: Measurement of adherence, drug concentrations and the effectiveness of artemether-lumefantrine, chlorproguanil-dapsone or sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Malawi.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing three antimalarial treatments (AL, CPD, SP) in uncomplicated malaria with reported outcome results (day-28 and day-42 ACPR rates); malaria treatment is the primary focus; phase not stated but consistent with Phase III effectiveness trial.
population: children ≥12 months and adults with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Day-28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine achieved higher day-28 and day-42 ACPR rates than chlorproguanil-dapsone or sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, and remained effective even with unsupervised dosing and imperfect adherence.
p_value: p ≤ 0.002 for AL vs CPD/SP comparisons; p=0.01 for CPD vs SP on day 28
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed beyond efficacy and adherence outcomes; no major safety concerns reported.

title: Efficacy of artesunate-amodiaquine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa: a multi-centre analysis.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes comparing artesunate-amodiaquine for malaria treatment in humans; outcome results fully available.
place: sub-Saharan Africa (16 countries, 33 sites, including Uganda and Rwanda)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, 75% under 5 years old
primary_outcome: Day 28 PCR-adjusted treatment efficacy (survival analysis, modified intent-to-treat)
impact_summary: AS&AQ met the WHO efficacy criteria (PCR-adjusted efficacy >90%) in 11 of 16 sub-Saharan African countries studied, with efficacy varying between and within countries.
transmission_setting: varied endemicity across 16 sub-Saharan African countries
age_range: 75% under 5 years old, mixed ages included
safety_summary: Anaemia recovery was similar across comparator groups except in one Rwandan site where DP-treated patients had slower recovery; no other major safety differences reported.

title: Population pharmacokinetics of artesunate and amodiaquine in African children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate-amodiaquine (malaria treatment) in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; phase not explicitly stated but bioequivalence/efficacy trial in treated patients indicates Phase 3.
comparator: active comparator (separate artesunate and amodiaquine tablets)
population: children aged six months to five years with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Population pharmacokinetic properties (AUC) of artesunate/DHA and amodiaquine/desethylamodiaquine comparing fixed dose combination versus loose formulation
impact_summary: The fixed dose combination of artesunate and amodiaquine had similar pharmacokinetic properties and efficacy compared to the same drugs given as separate tablets in young children with acute malaria.
effect_metric: AUC ratio (loose formulation to fixed co-formulation)
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; no child developed severe post-treatment neutropaenia (<1,000/muL); no evidence of AQ dose-related hepatotoxicity, though one patient had an asymptomatic rise in liver enzymes resolving by Day 28.

title: Artemisinin-naphthoquine combination (ARCO) therapy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in adults of Papua New Guinea: a preliminary report on safety and efficacy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing an artemisinin-based antimalarial combination to a control regimen for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans.
population: adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 1, 2, 3, 7, 14 and 28-day cure rates
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine combination (ANQ) achieved higher cure rates than chloroquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and was safe and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in adults in Papua New Guinea.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with no serious adverse events reported.

title: Prevention of Plasmodium vivax malaria recurrence: efficacy of the standard total dose of primaquine administered over 3 days.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing primaquine for malaria treatment (P. vivax recurrence prevention), a core malaria intervention in humans; phase unstated but treatment efficacy trial is appropriate for inclusion.
comparator: standard total dose over 14 days (STD-14) vs alternative dosing regimens (STD-3, 71%STD-3, 50%STD-3)
population: patients with P. vivax malaria in an endemic zone of Colombia
primary_outcome: Recurrence of P. vivax malaria within 120 days after primary episode
impact_summary: The standard primaquine dose given over 14 days (STD-14) was more effective at preventing P. vivax recurrence than the same total dose given over 3 days or lower doses over 3 days, which were largely ineffective.
safety_summary: High daily doses (1.17 mg/kg/day) were well tolerated.

title: Safety and efficacy of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in falciparum malaria: a prospective multi-centre individual patient data analysis.
screening_reason: Multi-centre individual patient data analysis of seven published RCTs comparing dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine to comparator antimalarials in falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
place: Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Uganda, Rwanda
countries: Cambodia; Laos; Myanmar; Rwanda; Thailand; Uganda
design: prospective, multi-centre, individual patient data analysis, phase 3
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, including children under five years and adults
primary_outcome: PCR genotype corrected efficacy (survival analysis) at Day 28
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was safe, well tolerated, and highly effective, with superior efficacy to comparator drugs against P. falciparum recurrence and recrudescence, but higher gametocyte carriage than mefloquine-artesunate.
effect_metric: PCR genotype corrected efficacy at Day 28
transmission_setting: varied endemic settings in Africa and South East Asia
age_range: children under five years and adults
safety_summary: DP was well tolerated with 1.7% early vomiting; fewer adverse events than MAS3 except for diarrhea (ORs 2.74 and 3.11 in children and adults respectively).

title: Efficacy of permethrin treated long-lasting insecticidal nets on malaria transmission and observations on the perceived side effects, collateral benefits and human safety in a hyperendemic tribal area of Orissa, India.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated LLINs for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (65-70% reduction in malaria incidence).
population: tribal population in a hyperendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence measured through longitudinal active surveillance at fortnightly intervals
impact_summary: Olyset long-lasting insecticidal nets reduced malaria incidence by 65-70% and malaria prevalence by 45.7% compared to untreated net and no net control areas, with minimal and transient side effects.
safety_summary: Minimal transient side effects reported: skin irritation (4%), itching (8%), eye irritation (1.2%), lasting only a few hours after first use; no adverse events attributable to net use were recorded.

title: A comparative, randomized clinical trial of artemisinin/naphtoquine twice daily one day versus artemether/lumefantrine six doses regimen in children and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans with reported efficacy outcomes at 28 days.
population: children and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, aged 6 months or more
primary_outcome: Risk of treatment failure within 28 days (unadjusted or PCR-adjusted to distinguish recrudescence from new infection)
impact_summary: Both artemisinin/naphtoquine and artemether/lumefantrine were highly effective, with day 28 cure rates of 100% and 98.4% respectively, showing rapid fever and parasite clearance.
safety_summary: Both artemisinin-based combinations were well tolerated with rapid fever and parasite clearance; no major safety concerns reported.

title: A randomized, controlled trial of artemisinin-piperaquine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine phosphate in treatment of falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-piperaquine compounds) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates, adverse events).
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate, parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, and parasite recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Both artemisinin-piperaquine (Artequick) and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine phosphate (Artekin) achieved 100% 28-day cure rates with no recrudescence, but Artequick was more convenient to administer and caused fewer gastrointestinal side effects.
safety_summary: No serious adverse reactions in either group; Artekin associated with higher incidence of gastrointestinal side effects compared to Artequick.

title: Antibodies to variant surface antigens of Plasmodium falciparum-infected erythrocytes are associated with protection from treatment failure and the development of anemia in pregnancy.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results on malaria treatment and pregnancy outcomes; primary focus is malaria parasitemia, anemia, and treatment failure in pregnant women.
comparator: antimalarial treatment comparison (original trial); here comparison by antibody level
population: pregnant women with parasitemia
primary_outcome: Association between antibody levels (IgG to VSA-PAM and opsonizing antibodies) and treatment failure/anemia at delivery
impact_summary: Higher levels of IgG to VSA-PAM and opsonizing antibodies were associated with reduced maternal anemia and reduced treatment failure/parasite clearance in pregnancy malaria.
effect_estimate: 0.66 (anemia, IgG VSA-PAM); 0.78 (parasitological failure, IgG VSA-PAM); 0.31 (anemia, opsonizing antibodies); 0.48 (treatment failure, opsonizing antibodies)

title: Intermittent preventive treatment using artemisinin-based combination therapy reduces malaria morbidity among school-aged children in Mali.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: RCT of IPT (artemisinin-based combination therapy) for malaria prevention in school children with reported outcome results including clinical malaria incidence, parasitemia, and anemia.
population: school-aged children
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with SP/AS or AQ/AS significantly reduced clinical malaria incidence, asymptomatic parasitemia, and anaemia compared to vitamin C among school-aged children in Mali.
safety_summary: Not explicitly detailed; treatment appeared well tolerated with high retention (99.3%) and no reported serious adverse events.

title: Importance of eaves to house entry by anopheline, but not culicine, mosquitoes.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with crossover design reporting outcome results (mosquito entry reduction) for a malaria vector-control intervention (eave screening).
population: households with single adult male occupants
primary_outcome: Number of mosquitoes (anopheline and culicine) caught indoors via CDC light traps
impact_summary: Blocking eaves reduced indoor Anopheles gambiae s.l. catches three-fold but did not reduce culicine mosquito numbers, showing eaves are the main entry route for An. gambiae while culicines enter via doors and windows.
effect_metric: fold-reduction in Anopheles gambiae s.l. indoor catches
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area with An. gambiae s.l. as primary vector
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Effect of malaria rapid diagnostic tests on the management of uncomplicated malaria with artemether-lumefantrine in Kenya: a cluster randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria diagnosis intervention (RDTs) on treatment management in humans.
comparator: training, guidelines, and supervision (TGS) alone (without RDTs)
population: outpatients aged 5 years and older presenting with suspected malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of patients with malaria prescribed AL (recommended treatment) and proportion of patients without malaria prescribed AL (overtreatment)
impact_summary: Providing malaria rapid diagnostic tests with training, guidelines, and supervision reduced recommended treatment (appropriate AL prescription for confirmed malaria) by 63 percentage points due to reduced presumptive AL treatment, but did not significantly reduce overtreatment.
transmission_setting: Kenya, endemic setting shortly after AL introduction as first-line treatment

title: Impact of ministry of health interventions on private medicine retailer knowledge and practices on anti-malarial treatment in Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of a malaria treatment intervention (retailer training on anti-malarial use) with reported outcome results; phase not applicable for this implementation science trial.
comparator: standard care (control retailers without MoH training program)
population: private medicine retailers
primary_outcome: Retailer knowledge and practices on anti-malarial (amodiaquine) treatment, including correct advice given to surrogate clients and correct knowledge on dosing
impact_summary: Large-scale MoH retailer training programs significantly improved retailers' knowledge and practices on anti-malarial treatment compared to control retailers across three districts in Kenya.
effect_estimate: 8.8 (correct advice on use); 29.8 (correct knowledge on dosing)

title: House design modifications reduce indoor resting malaria vector densities in rice irrigation scheme area in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of house design modifications (vector control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results on indoor resting vector densities.
population: rural households in a rice irrigation scheme area
primary_outcome: Indoor resting density of Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus mosquitoes
impact_summary: House ceiling modifications with papyrus mats and insecticide-treated netting significantly reduced indoor resting densities and odds of presence of malaria vector mosquitoes compared to unmodified houses.
transmission_setting: rice irrigation scheme area, lowlands of western Kenya, malaria-endemic
safety_summary: Not reported; residents responded favourably to the intervention with no adverse effects mentioned

title: Mefloquine pharmacokinetics and mefloquine-artesunate effectiveness in Peruvian patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine-artesunate combination therapy (a malaria treatment intervention) in humans with reported efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcome results by day 56.
comparator: active comparator (different mefloquine brands: Lariam, Mephaquin, Mefloquina-AC Farma)
population: non-pregnant adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: In vivo efficacy (parasite clearance and recrudescence through Day 56) and pharmacokinetic parameters of three mefloquine formulations given with artesunate
impact_summary: All three mefloquine formulations combined with artesunate rapidly cleared parasitaemia by day 3-4 with no recrudescence by Day 56, and had generally similar pharmacokinetics except for a significant difference in Cmax between Mephaquin and Lariam.
effect_estimate: Lariam 2,820 ng/ml; Mephaquin 2,500 ng/ml; Mefloquina AC Farma 2,750 ng/ml
effect_ci: Lariam 2,614-3,108; Mephaquin 2,363-2,713; Mefloquina AC Farma 2,550-3,000 (interquartile ranges)
safety_summary: Not detailed; no adverse events reported in abstract, focus was on efficacy and pharmacokinetics

title: Field evaluation of Olyset nets: a long-lasting insecticidal net against malaria vectors Anopheles culicifacies and Anopheles fluviatilis in a hyperendemic tribal area of Orissa, India.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (long-lasting insecticidal nets) with reported outcome results on entomological endpoints.
comparator: untreated net and no net clusters
population: residents of tribal villages in a hyperendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: Entry rate, feeding success rate, and mortality of malaria vector mosquitoes (An. culicifacies and An. fluviatilis) in Olyset net villages compared to untreated net and no net villages
impact_summary: Olyset nets significantly reduced mosquito entry rates and feeding success and increased mortality of malaria vectors compared to untreated or no nets, demonstrating effective personal protection.
effect_metric: percent reduction in mosquito entry rate
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on entomological and efficacy outcomes rather than adverse events in humans

title: [Change of antimalarial first-line treatment in Burkina Faso in 2005].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, reporting efficacy outcomes (treatment failure rates) over 28 days.
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate at day 28 (PCR-adjusted), using modified WHO protocol
impact_summary: Chloroquine had a much higher PCR-adjusted treatment failure rate (63.4%) than sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (13.8%), supporting the 2005 change in Burkina Faso's antimalarial treatment policy.

title: Open label randomized comparison of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artesunate-amodiaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in central Vietnam.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes comparing two antimalarial drugs for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
population: children and adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day PCR-adjusted cure rate
impact_summary: DHP and AAQ showed similarly high 42-day cure rates for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with DHP showing fewer reinfections suggesting greater post-treatment prophylactic activity.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, central Vietnam
safety_summary: Both drug combinations were well tolerated in all age groups with no obvious drug-associated adverse events.

title: The efficacy and safety of a new fixed-dose combination of amodiaquine and artesunate in young African children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (efficacy and safety) of a fixed-dose antimalarial combination for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children; non-early-phase therapeutic trial.
population: young children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, aged 6 months to 5 years
primary_outcome: Day 28, PCR-corrected, parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: Fixed-dose artesunate/amodiaquine was non-inferior to the loose combination in efficacy and was well tolerated in young children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected cure rate difference (Delta, AS+AQ - AS/AQ)
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated; drug-induced vomiting occurred in 2.1% (fixed) and 1.6% (loose) of patients (p=0.59); one patient developed asymptomatic CTC grade 4 hepatitis; neutropaenia risk could not be assessed due to technical difficulties.

title: Five-year safety and immunogenicity of GlaxoSmithKline's candidate malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS02 following administration to semi-immune adult men living in a malaria-endemic region of The Gambia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine candidate RTS,S/AS02 with reported safety and immunogenicity outcomes over five years in semi-immune adults.
population: semi-immune adult men, aged 18 to 45 years
primary_outcome: long-term safety and immunogenicity (anti-CS and anti-HBs antibody persistence) over 58 months
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS02 was safe over five years of follow-up with no vaccine-attributable fatal SAEs, and anti-CS and anti-HBs antibody titres persisted though waned from post-booster levels compared to control.
safety_summary: Nine subjects in RTS,S/AS02 group and seven in rabies group experienced serious adverse events; seven had fatal outcomes (five RTS,S/AS02, two rabies), none attributed to study vaccine.

title: Community-based promotional campaign to improve uptake of intermittent preventive antimalarial treatment in pregnancy in Burkina Faso.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP (intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy, a malaria chemoprevention intervention) with reported outcome results on ANC attendance and treatment uptake.
population: pregnant women (primigravidae and secundigravidae)
primary_outcome: Antenatal clinic attendance (>=3 ANC visits) and uptake of IPTp-SP
impact_summary: Community sensitization/promotion increased antenatal clinic attendance and complete uptake of IPTp-SP compared to no promotion, though adolescents remained the hardest group to reach, especially during high transmission season.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (uptake of SP, low vs high transmission season)
transmission_setting: rural, seasonal malaria transmission (high and low transmission seasons)

title: A randomised controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine versus artesunate for uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum treatment in pregnancy.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate for malaria treatment in pregnancy, a direct malaria intervention in humans.
population: Karen women with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in second and third trimesters of pregnancy
primary_outcome: P. falciparum PCR-adjusted cure rate assessed at delivery or by day 42, whichever occurred later, estimated by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was well tolerated and safe but had inferior efficacy compared to 7-day artesunate monotherapy for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in pregnancy.
effect_estimate: AS7 89.2% vs AL 82.0% (ITT); AS7 89.7% vs AL 81.2% (per-protocol)
follow_up: delivery or day 42; infants followed to 1 year of age
transmission_setting: border area of northwestern Thailand, malaria-endemic region
age_range: pregnant women, second and third trimesters
safety_summary: Both regimens were very well tolerated; birth outcomes and infant outcomes up to age 1 year did not differ significantly between groups.

title: Extended high efficacy of the combination sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine with artesunate in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria on the Benin coast, West Africa.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (SP-AS combination) in children with reported outcome results (day-90 clinical failure rates) in a malaria-endemic population.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected clinical treatment failure at day 90
impact_summary: Combining artesunate with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine dramatically increased treatment efficacy compared to SP alone or chloroquine alone, even with extended follow-up to day 90.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected clinical failure rate at day 90
transmission_setting: West Africa, Benin coast, malaria endemic

title: Efficacy of chloroquine, amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria: revisiting molecular markers in an area of emerging AQ and SP resistance in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine, amodiaquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported efficacy outcome results at day 28.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR), with and without molecular correction for reinfection
impact_summary: Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine was the most efficacious treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, followed by amodiaquine, while chloroquine showed low efficacy due to resistance.
effect_metric: corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (cACPR)
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission area, Kolle, Mali
safety_summary: Not specifically reported in abstract; study focused on efficacy and molecular resistance markers

title: High resistance of Plasmodium falciparum to sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine in northern Tanzania and the emergence of dhps resistance mutation at Codon 581.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of SP efficacy in malaria-infected children with reported outcome results; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
population: symptomatic children 6-59 months with uncomplicated malaria and asymptomatic infants 2-10 months
primary_outcome: In vivo treatment failure (PCR-corrected early and late treatment failure) with SP by day 28
impact_summary: SP showed very high treatment failure rates in both symptomatic children and asymptomatic infants in northern Tanzania, with emergence of a new triple dhps/dhfr mutation combination associated with earlier failure.
effect_estimate: 82.2% total failure by day 28 (early treatment failure 38.8%)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Reduced efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in malnourished children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTi-SP (a malaria chemoprevention intervention) in infants with reported outcome results (malaria incidence and protective efficacy).
population: infants and young children, including malnourished subgroups
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria and protective efficacy of IPTi-SP stratified by nutritional status
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTi-SP) was significantly less protective against malaria in malnourished children than in nonmalnourished children, and severe malaria rates appeared increased among malnourished children receiving IPTi.
effect_metric: protective efficacy against malaria incidence in first year of life
safety_summary: Malnutrition was associated with increased risks of severe anemia and death; malnourished children receiving IPTi appeared to have an increased rate of severe malaria compared to nutritionally advantaged children.

title: Rapid malaria diagnostic tests vs. clinical management of malaria in rural Burkina Faso: safety and effect on clinical decisions. A randomized trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (persistence of fever, treatment frequencies) evaluating a malaria diagnostic intervention (RDT) in humans in a resource-limited setting.
comparator: presumptive clinical management without diagnostic test
population: febrile patients presenting at rural health centres
primary_outcome: persistence of fever at day 4
impact_summary: The trial was inconclusive on RDT safety due to poor compliance with negative test results, with 80-85% of RDT-negative patients still being diagnosed and treated for malaria despite the negative result.
p_value: P = 0.00 for diagnosis and treatment differences between RDT positive and negative patients in rainy season
transmission_setting: seasonal, rural Burkina Faso, dry and rainy season comparison
safety_summary: Study was inconclusive on RDT safety due to exceedingly low compliance with negative test results, leading to continued antimalarial treatment despite negative RDT.

title: In vivo selection of Plasmodium falciparum parasites carrying the chloroquine-susceptible pfcrt K76 allele after treatment with artemether-lumefantrine in Africa.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results comparing artemether-lumefantrine to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for P. falciparum malaria treatment, analyzing drug-specific resistance markers.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Selection of pfcrt and pfmdr1 alleles among recurrent infections after treatment
impact_summary: Treatment with artemether-lumefantrine selected for the chloroquine-susceptible pfcrt K76 allele and, to a lesser extent, the pfmdr1 N86 allele among recurrent infections, while these genotypes were not selected during SP treatment.
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria endemic area

title: Submicroscopic gametocytes and the transmission of antifolate-resistant Plasmodium falciparum in Western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of SP alone versus SP+artesunate or SP+amodiaquine in malaria-infected children, with reported outcome results on gametocytemia and transmission.
comparator: SP alone vs SP combined with artesunate or amodiaquine
population: children with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Submicroscopic gametocytemia (Pfs25 QT-NASBA) and malaria transmission to mosquitoes via membrane-feeding assays
impact_summary: Additional dhfr/dhps mutations beyond the double mutant were not associated with increased submicroscopic gametocytemia or enhanced transmission, but addition of artesunate to SP reduced gametocytemia and transmission during follow-up.
effect_metric: gametocyte prevalence/density and mosquito infection/oocyst burden
effect_estimate: not significantly different by mutation number; reduced with AS addition

title: Short report: comparison of chlorproguanil-dapsone with a combination of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and chloroquine in children with malaria in northcentral Nigeria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments in children with malaria, with reported outcome results on parasitemia clearance and clinical response.
population: children under 5 years with malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitologic response at day 14
impact_summary: Chlorproguanil-dapsone and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus chloroquine showed similar antimalarial efficacy in children with uncomplicated malaria in northcentral Nigeria.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitologic response rate

title: Methemoglobinemia and adverse events in Plasmodium vivax malaria patients associated with high doses of primaquine treatment.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of primaquine dosing in P. vivax malaria patients with reported outcome results (methemoglobinemia levels and adverse events); primary malaria treatment purpose.
population: Plasmodium vivax malaria patients
primary_outcome: Methemoglobin (MetHB) levels after primaquine treatment
impact_summary: High-dose primaquine (up to 1.17 mg/kg/d) caused transient methemoglobinemia and mild adverse events but did not pose a serious risk under controlled conditions.
safety_summary: Only subjects receiving the highest primaquine doses had mild and brief adverse events, with 17% of these associated with treatment; no serious risk of high methemoglobin levels observed under normal G6PD activity, non-pregnant status, and with a light meal.

title: Cost-effectiveness of artesunate for the treatment of severe malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artesunate versus quinine for severe malaria treatment with reported mortality outcome results.
population: patients with severe malaria
primary_outcome: mortality
impact_summary: Artesunate was more cost-effective than quinine for treating severe malaria, with an incremental cost per death averted of approximately 140 USD.

title: Individual efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in primi- and secundigravidae in rural Burkina Faso: impact on parasitaemia, anaemia and birth weight.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
