screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP for malaria prevention in pregnant women with reported outcome results on parasitaemia, anaemia, and birth weight.
comparator: fewer than two doses of SP (0-1 doses) versus two or more directly observed doses
population: primigravidae and secundigravidae (pregnant women) attending rural health centres
primary_outcome: Prevalence of peripheral and placental parasitaemia, anaemia (PCV <33%), low-birth weight (<2500 g), mean PCV and birth weight in relation to number of directly observed SP doses
impact_summary: Two or more doses of IPTp-SP significantly reduced placental parasitaemia and anaemia at delivery, and reduced low birth weight risk in primigravidae but not secundigravidae, while increasing mean PCV and birth weight in both groups.
effect_estimate: AOR=0.11 (LBW in primigravidae); AOR=0.31 (anaemia at delivery); AOR=0.04 (placental parasitaemia)

title: Intrarectal quinine versus intravenous or intramuscular quinine for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
screening_reason: This is a systematic review of randomized controlled trials comparing intrarectal versus intravenous/intramuscular quinine for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria; however, systematic reviews are excluded per protocol as they are not themselves RCTs.
design: systematic review of randomized and quasi-randomized controlled trials
population: children with uncomplicated and severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: death, parasite clearance, fever clearance time, coma recovery time, duration of hospitalization, time to drinking
impact_summary: No statistically significant difference was found between intrarectal and intravenous or intramuscular quinine routes in efficacy outcomes, though intrarectal administration may be less painful.
safety_summary: One large trial (898 children) reported intrarectal administration was less painful than intramuscular administration; no significant differences in death rates detected between routes.

title: [Artesunate in interrupting the transmission of Plasmodium falciparum].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate (malaria treatment/transmission-blocking intervention) in humans with published outcome results on gametocyte clearance and mosquito infectivity.
population: volunteers with falciparum malaria and gametocytaemia
primary_outcome: Infectivity of Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes to Anopheles dirus mosquitoes and gametocyte clearance time
impact_summary: Oral artesunate (1000 mg over 6 days) cleared gametocytes faster and inhibited the infectivity of P. falciparum gametocytes to mosquitoes more effectively than quinine or placebo.

title: Artemisinin-based combinations versus amodiaquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Faladje, Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions with reported outcome results (ACPR, parasitaemia, haemoglobin); published.
comparator: artesunate-amodiaquine and artesunate plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (active comparators)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) rate at Day 28, with and without PCR correction
impact_summary: After PCR correction, all three combinations (AS+AQ, AS+SP, AQ+SP) showed similarly high efficacy (95.4%, 96.9%, 99.2% ACPR respectively), with AQ+SP providing a low-cost alternative with longer protective effect against new infection.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) rate
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region with chloroquine resistance, Mali
safety_summary: No significant difference in gametocyte carriage between groups; haemoglobin concentration increased across all treatment groups from Day 0 to Day 28, with greatest improvement in the AQ+SP group; no other safety concerns reported.

title: Adherence to Artesunate-Amodiaquine Therapy for Uncomplicated Malaria in Rural Ghana: A Randomised Trial of Supervised versus Unsupervised Drug Administration.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine) in humans with reported outcome results (adherence, parasite clearance, side effects); not early-phase.
comparator: unsupervised drug administration (active comparator, same drug regimen)
population: adolescent and adult patients with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Adherence to AS+AQ treatment regimen assessed by direct observation of blister package on day 2
impact_summary: Both supervised and unsupervised administration of artesunate-amodiaquine resulted in similarly high adherence and treatment outcomes, with no significant difference between groups.
safety_summary: Commonest side-effects reported on day 2 were headaches and body weakness in both groups.

title: N-acetylcysteine as adjunctive treatment in severe malaria: a randomized, double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT testing a malaria treatment intervention (NAC adjunctive therapy for severe falciparum malaria) with reported outcome results.
population: adult patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality, lactate clearance time, coma recovery time
impact_summary: N-acetylcysteine as an adjunct to intravenous artesunate had no significant effect on mortality, lactate clearance time, or coma recovery time in patients with severe falciparum malaria, though it modestly increased parasite clearance time likely due to baseline parasitemia differences.
safety_summary: NAC was studied for safety as adjunctive treatment; no significant adverse effect on mortality or red cell rigidity was noted, but specific safety/adverse event data were not detailed beyond outcome measures.

title: A randomized trial on effectiveness of artemether-lumefantrine versus artesunate plus amodiaquine for unsupervised treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Ghanaian children.
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate plus amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine)
population: children under five years of age with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) and late clinical failure by day 28
impact_summary: Unobserved AL and ASAQ treatment both showed high adequate clinical and parasitological responses, but AL was inferior to ASAQ in preventing late clinical failures.
effect_metric: Hazard Ratio (late clinical failure, AL vs ASAQ)
safety_summary: Haematological recovery and drug tolerability were not significantly different between the two treatment arms.

title: A trial of combination antimalarial therapies in children from Papua New Guinea.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (antimalarial therapies) in children with reported outcome results (adequate clinical and parasitologic response rates); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention.
comparator: chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine (active comparators)
population: children with falciparum or vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Rate of adequate clinical and parasitologic response at day 42 for P. falciparum, after PCR correction for reinfections
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was the most effective regimen against P. falciparum (95.2% adequate response) and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was most effective against P. vivax (69.4% adequate response), both significantly better than the other regimens.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitologic response rate at day 42
p_value: P=0.003 (vs chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine), P=0.02 (vs artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine), P=0.06 (vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) for P. falciparum comparisons
transmission_setting: intense year-round transmission of multiple Plasmodium species
safety_summary: Rash occurred more often with artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine than with chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (P=0.004 for both comparisons).

title: Pre-referral rectal artesunate to prevent death and disability in severe malaria: a placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing rectal artesunate (malaria treatment intervention) in humans with pre-specified primary endpoints (mortality and permanent disability); phase not stated but treatment trials are considered eligible.
population: patients with suspected severe malaria unable to be treated orally, being referred to clinics for injections
primary_outcome: Mortality (assessed 7-30 days later) and permanent disability (reassessed periodically)
impact_summary: Pre-referral rectal artesunate did not significantly reduce overall mortality but significantly reduced death or permanent disability, especially in patients who took more than 6 hours to reach clinic.
effect_estimate: 0.49 (in patients >6h to clinic); 0.86 (in patients <6h to clinic)
p_value: 0.0013 (>6h subgroup); 0.35 (<6h subgroup); 0.1 (overall mortality); 0.0484 (dead or disabled overall)
follow_up: 7-30 days for mortality; periodic reassessment for disability
transmission_setting: rural areas with limited access to injectable antimalarial treatment
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed beyond disability outcomes; no mention of adverse events distinct from disease progression.
funder: UNICEF/UNDP/World Bank Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (WHO/TDR); WHO Global Malaria Programme (WHO/GMP); Sall Family Foundation; the European Union (QLRT-2000-01430); the UK Medical Research Council; USAID; Irish Aid; the Karolinska Institute; and the University of Oxford Clinical Trial Service Unit (CTSU)

title: dhfr and dhps genotype and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failure in children with falciparum malaria in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment regimens (SP, AQSP, ASSP) in children with falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results (treatment failure rates) with genotypic analysis.
comparator: active comparator (SP vs AQSP vs ASSP)
population: children under 5 years old with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure at day 14 after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Dhps-437 and dhps-540 mutations were strongly associated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failure, especially in children with high parasite density.

title: Impact of lambdacyhalothrin capsule suspension treated bed nets on malaria in tribal villages of Malkangiri district, Orissa, India.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and parasite rates.
population: tribal villagers in malaria-endemic foothill villages
primary_outcome: changes in vector density, parous rate, malaria incidence and parasite rates
impact_summary: Lambdacyhalothrin-treated bed nets reduced vector density, malaria parasite rates by about 65%, and provided an estimated 86% protective factor against malaria incidence compared to no nets.
transmission_setting: highly endemic for falciparum malaria, foothill villages
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; nets were acceptable to the community with no adverse events mentioned.

title: Sublingual sugar for hypoglycaemia in children with severe malaria: a pilot clinical study.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes testing a malaria treatment intervention (hypoglycaemia management in severe malaria) in humans; not early-phase.
population: children with hypoglycaemia and severe malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment response, defined as reaching a blood glucose concentration >= 3.3 mmol/l (60 mg/dl) within 40 minutes after admission
impact_summary: There was no significant difference in treatment response between sublingual sugar and intravenous glucose groups, though sublingual sugar appeared to be a promising, child-friendly method of raising blood glucose.
safety_summary: One fatality occurred in each group; treatment failures in SLS were related to clenched teeth or swallowing sugar, while IVG failures were due to delays in starting infusion (median 17.5 min, range 3-40); sublingual sugar was described as well-tolerated.

title: Biological and haematological safety profile of oral amodiaquine and chloroquine in healthy volunteers with or without Plasmodium falciparum infection in northeast Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of an antimalarial drug (amodiaquine) in humans with reported outcome results (safety, tolerability, and parasitological efficacy); malaria treatment/prevention is the primary purpose.
population: indigenous semi-immune healthy adult male volunteers with or without Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: biological and haematological safety, tolerability, and parasitological efficacy
impact_summary: Amodiaquine achieved 100% parasitological clearance versus 70% with chloroquine, with no agranulocytosis or hepatic toxicity observed and only mild, transient adverse effects.
safety_summary: No agranulocytosis or hepatic toxicity detected; haematological and hepatological values pre- and post-trial showed only marginal differences within normal limits; clinical adverse effects were mostly mild and transient (33.3% CQ-aparasitaemic, 23.8% CQ-parasitaemic, 28.6% AQ-parasitaemic, 14.3% AQ-aparasitaemic).

title: A randomized trial to monitor the efficacy and effectiveness by QT-NASBA of artemether-lumefantrine versus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for treatment and transmission control of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of two malaria treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance and parasitaemia in humans.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte clearance and carriage as detected by QT-NASBA and microscopy after treatment
impact_summary: NASBA detected significantly more gametocyte carriers than microscopy, and gametocyte clearance was significantly faster with artemether-lumefantrine than with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine at days 3, 7 and 14, though no difference remained by day 28.
effect_metric: gametocyte carriage difference between treatment arms
effect_estimate: higher and longer gametocyte persistence in DP group at days 3, 7, 14; no difference at day 28

title: Effects of amodiaquine, artesunate, and artesunate-amodiaquine on Plasmodium falciparum malaria-associated anaemia in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions (amodiaquine, artesunate, artesunate-amodiaquine) in children with reported outcome results on haematocrit changes and anaemia recovery.
comparator: active comparator (amodiaquine vs artesunate vs artesunate-amodiaquine)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Malaria-associated anaemia and drug-attributable fall in haematocrit following treatment
impact_summary: Artesunate-treated children had significantly less drug-attributable fall in haematocrit than amodiaquine-treated children, suggesting artemisinin drugs may attenuate malaria-associated anaemia.
safety_summary: Drug-attributable fall in haematocrit was significantly higher with amodiaquine; artesunate associated with lower rate of haematocrit decline; no serious adverse events reported.

title: A randomized trial of artesunate-mefloquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mali.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcome results (28-day cure rates).
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria weighing >= 10 kg
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine had a higher unadjusted 28-day cure rate than artemether-lumefantrine, but after correction for reinfection, cure rates were similar between the two groups, and artesunate-mefloquine prevented more new infections.
safety_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine was well-tolerated.

title: A randomized, comparative study of supervised and unsupervised artesunate-amodiaquine, for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Ghana.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate-amodiaquine for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance, clinical response) at multiple timepoints.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: adequate clinical and parasitological response by day 28
impact_summary: Supervised artesunate-amodiaquine treatment resulted in a significantly higher adequate clinical and parasitological response rate than unsupervised treatment at days 21 and 28, though both were effective overall.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
effect_estimate: 91.3% (supervised) vs 84.1% (unsupervised) at day 21; 80.0% vs 64.9% at day 28
safety_summary: Adverse effects and haemoglobin recovery trends were similar between supervised and unsupervised arms.

title: A community effectiveness trial of strategies promoting intermittent preventive treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in pregnant women in rural Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP chemoprevention in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria parasitemia, placental infection, and birth outcomes.
comparator: weekly chloroquine (control) and IPTp-SP without promotion (Intervention B)
population: pregnant women (primigravidae and secundigravidae)
primary_outcome: peripheral parasitaemia during pregnancy and at delivery, placental malaria, maternal anaemia, mean and low birth weight
impact_summary: Community promotion increased IPTp-SP coverage substantially and reduced malaria infection prevalence compared to control, but did not significantly improve maternal anaemia or birth weight outcomes.
effect_metric: odds ratio for peripheral parasitaemia (Intervention B vs Control)

title: Ototoxicity of artemether/lumefantrine in the treatment of falciparum malaria: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether/lumefantrine vs. comparators) with reported outcome results on ototoxicity and efficacy in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: patients with uncomplicated slide-confirmed falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Ototoxicity assessed by pure tone audiometry, otoacoustic emissions (TE-OAE, DP-OAE), and brain stem evoked response audiometry (BERA) at days 7, 28, and 90
impact_summary: Artemether/lumefantrine showed no detrimental effect on hearing or brainstem auditory pathways, whereas quinine caused transient cochlear hearing loss.
effect_estimate: no significant hearing loss with AL; transient hearing loss (>30 dB in 3 patients) with quinine
safety_summary: Quinine caused transient cochlear hearing loss due to temporary outer hair cell dysfunction; artemether/lumefantrine and atovaquone/proguanil showed no ototoxicity; no drug-induced brainstem lesions detected by BERA.

title: Distribution systems of insecticide-treated bed nets for malaria control in rural Burkina Faso: cluster-randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of ITN distribution (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on ITN household ownership.
population: Rural households, with free ITN distribution targeted to pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Serena ITN household ownership
impact_summary: Free distribution of ITNs to pregnant women through antenatal care services in addition to social marketing substantially improved ITN household ownership compared to social marketing alone.
effect_estimate: Group A: 13% to 35%; Group B: 18% to 23%
transmission_setting: highly endemic for malaria, rural sub-Saharan Africa

title: [Gametocytemia in falciparum malaria treated with amodiaquine or artesunate].
journal: Biomedica : revista del Instituto Nacional de Salud
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments (amodiaquine and artesunate combinations) for P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results on gametocytemia and therapeutic efficacy.
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: therapeutic efficacy and gametocyte clearance at day 21/28
impact_summary: The three treatment regimens (amodiaquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and amodiaquine-artesunate) had similar therapeutic efficacy, but amodiaquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was less effective than artesunate-based treatments in reducing gametocyte load, and none of the treatments eliminated gametocytes by day 7.
transmission_setting: endemic, Colombia (Turbo, El Bagre, Zaragoza, Antioquia)

title: [Efficacy of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Hainan, China].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin combinations) with reported outcome results (ACPR, fever/parasite clearance times); phase not stated but treatment efficacy trials are not phase-gated.
population: patients aged 1 to 60 with uncomplicated P. falciparum infection and parasite density 1,000 to 200,000 parasites/microl
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine achieved 100% adequate clinical and parasitological response with no significant difference in fever or parasite clearance times and no recrudescence or serious adverse effects.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate
transmission_setting: area with high level chloroquine resistance of P. falciparum
safety_summary: No recrudescence or serious adverse effects observed among participants.

title: Reduction of transmission from malaria patients by artemisinin combination therapies: a pooled analysis of six randomized trials.
screening_reason: Pooled analysis of six randomized controlled trials testing artemisinin combination therapies versus non-artemisinin antimalarials for malaria treatment with reported transmission outcomes.
design: pooled analysis of six randomized trials
population: symptomatic patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: gametocyte carriage, mosquito infection, and area under the curve of gametocyte density during 28 days follow up
impact_summary: Treatment with ACT significantly reduced gametocytaemia, transmission to mosquitoes, and infectiousness of patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria compared to previous first-line non-artemisinin treatments.
p_value: p < 0.001 (for effect of pre-treatment gametocytaemia on ACT impact)
transmission_setting: high transmission (Kenya) and lower transmission (The Gambia)

title: Adherence and efficacy of supervised versus non-supervised treatment with artemether/lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Bangladesh: a randomised controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with published outcome results comparing treatment modalities for uncomplicated malaria in humans; primary purpose is malaria treatment efficacy and not early-phase.
comparator: non-directly observed treatment (NDOT) vs directly observed treatment (DOT)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected 42-day parasitological and clinical cure rate
impact_summary: DOT and NDOT with artemether/lumefantrine showed similarly high efficacy and adherence for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Bangladesh, with no significant difference in cure rates or time to recurrence.
transmission_setting: Bandarban Hill Tract District, Bangladesh (malaria-endemic hill tract region)

title: Effects of artesunate-cotrimoxazole and amodiaquine-artesunate against asexual and sexual stages of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate combinations) in humans with reported outcome results (clinical recovery, parasite clearance, gametocyte carriage).
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance time, gametocyte carriage rates
impact_summary: Both artesunate-cotrimoxazole and artesunate-amodiaquine achieved rapid parasite clearance (<2 days) and reduced gametocyte carriage, with no significant difference in fever clearance time between groups.
safety_summary: Clinical recovery from illness occurred in all children; no adverse events reported.

title: Efficacy of Artequick versus artesunate-mefloquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial regimens for acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate (efficacy, safety and tolerability)
impact_summary: Artequick was as effective and well tolerated as artesunate-mefloquine, with similarly high 28-day cure rates (98.5% vs 100%) and no significant differences in fever- and parasite-clearance times.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria region of Southeast Asia
safety_summary: All treatments were well tolerated, and no serious adverse effects occurred.

title: Activities of artemether-lumefantrine and amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine against sexual-stage parasites in falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of two antimalarial combination therapies with reported outcome results on gametocyte carriage and sexual-stage parasite activity in children with malaria.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and gametocytaemia before, during or after treatment
primary_outcome: Gametocyte carriage and gametocytaemia (area under the curve) following treatment with artemether-lumefantrine or amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Both combination therapies had moderate effects on gametocyte carriage, but artemether-lumefantrine was more potent than amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine at reducing post-treatment gametocyte density and altering gametocyte sex ratio, suggesting greater reduction in transmissibility.
effect_metric: area under the curve of gametocytaemia
effect_estimate: 8-fold higher in amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine group than artemether-lumefantrine group
safety_summary: Clinical recovery from illness occurred in all children who carried gametocytes; no adverse events reported

title: Artemether-lumefantrine versus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for treating uncomplicated malaria: a randomized trial to guide policy in Uganda.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments (AL vs DP) for uncomplicated malaria in humans with complete outcome results reported.
population: patients aged 6 months to 10 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent parasitaemia and treatment failure due to recrudescence by day 42
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent parasitaemia and post-treatment gametocytaemia than artemether-lumefantrine, though there was no significant difference in recrudescence-based treatment failure.
safety_summary: Both drugs were safe and well tolerated.

title: The efficacy and tolerability of three different regimens of tafenoquine versus primaquine for post-exposure prophylaxis of Plasmodium vivax malaria in the Southwest Pacific.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing tafenoquine regimens versus primaquine for P. vivax post-exposure prophylaxis with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: Australian Defence Force personnel
primary_outcome: Relapse rate of P. vivax malaria after post-exposure prophylaxis
impact_summary: Tafenoquine regimens showed relapse rates comparable to or lower than primaquine plus doxycycline, with the lowest dose producing adverse event rates equivalent to primaquine plus doxycycline.
effect_estimate: 1.2%-11.0% across tafenoquine regimens vs 3.4%-10.0% for primaquine plus doxycycline
transmission_setting: endemic areas in Bougainville and Timor-Leste
safety_summary: Most frequent adverse events were nausea, abdominal distress and diarrhoea; dose-dependent reduction in adverse events with lower tafenoquine doses, with lowest dose producing rates equivalent to primaquine plus doxycycline.

title: Taste-masked quinine sulphate pellets: bio-availability in adults and steady-state plasma concentrations in children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of a malaria treatment formulation (quinine sulphate pellets) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that reports outcome results (steady-state plasma concentrations and clinical recovery).
comparator: commercially available tablets (active comparator, in adults); no comparator arm in children
population: healthy adult volunteers and children under 5 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Oral bio-availability (Cmax, AUC) of QS taste-masked pellets in adults and steady-state plasma concentrations of quinine in children
impact_summary: QS taste-masked pellets showed higher but still therapeutic bioavailability than tablets in adults, and achieved therapeutic steady-state plasma concentrations in children, all of whom recovered.
effect_estimate: Pellets: Cmax 4.7 microg/ml, AUC(0-24) 63.5 microg.h/ml; Tablets: Cmax 3.7 microg/ml, AUC(0-24) 52.4 microg.h/ml
age_range: children under 5 years; healthy adult volunteers
safety_summary: All children recovered and completed the 14-day follow-up; plasma concentrations remained within therapeutic limits for quinine in both adults and children

title: Impact of intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine on antibody responses to erythrocytic-stage Plasmodium falciparum antigens in infants in Mozambique.
screening_reason: RCT of IPTi with SP (malaria chemoprevention intervention) in infants with reported outcome results on antibody responses and malarial illness reduction.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Antibody responses (IgM and IgG subclass) to erythrocytic-stage P. falciparum antigens (whole asexual parasites, MSP-1(19), AMA-1, EBA-175) measured at ages 5, 9, 12, and 24 months
impact_summary: IPTi with SP given through the Expanded Program on Immunization reduced malarial illness while not impairing, and in some cases enhancing, the development of naturally acquired antibody responses to P. falciparum antigens compared to placebo.
effect_estimate: IgG and IgG1 responses to AMA-1 and/or MSP-1(19) significantly higher in SP group than placebo at ages 5, 9, and/or 24 months; no significant difference for other antibody responses at any time point

title: Duration of protection against malaria and anaemia provided by intermittent preventive treatment in infants in Navrongo, Ghana.
screening_reason: This is a secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised, placebo-controlled RCT of IPTi (chemoprevention for malaria in infants) with fully reported outcome results showing protective efficacy against malaria and anaemia.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy of IPTi against clinical malaria and anaemia in defined time strata following administration of IPTi
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment in infants using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine provided substantial but short-lived protection against malaria and anaemia, lasting only 4-6 weeks after each dose, with no evidence of benefit thereafter.
effect_estimate: 75.2% against malaria (within four weeks); 78.9% against high parasite density malaria; 93.8% against anaemia
safety_summary: IPTi has been shown to give effective and safe protection against malaria; no specific adverse events reported in this secondary analysis.

title: High-dose primaquine regimens against relapse of Plasmodium vivax malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (primaquine regimens) as primary purpose in humans.
population: patients with acute, symptomatic P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate (relapse prevention)
impact_summary: High-dose primaquine (30 mg twice daily for 7 days) combined with artesunate was highly effective, well-tolerated, and equivalent or superior to the standard 14-day primaquine regimen in preventing relapse of P. vivax malaria.
safety_summary: High-dose primaquine regimens were well-tolerated with no major safety concerns reported.

title: Herba Artemisiae annuae tea preparation compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in adults: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (Artemisia annua tea vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (cure rates at days 7, 14, and 28).
population: semi-immune adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 7, 14 and 28
impact_summary: Both Artemisia annua tea and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine had low and declining cure rates over 28 days, with no clear superiority of either treatment.

title: Enhanced efficacy of amodiaquine and chlorpheniramine combination over amodiaquine alone in the treatment of acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment regimens in children with reported outcome results (cure rates at days 7 and 14); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention.
population: children aged 6 months to 12 years with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rates at day 7 and day 14 using the 14-day modification of the WHO field test
impact_summary: The combination of amodiaquine plus chlorpheniramine was significantly more effective than amodiaquine alone in curing acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children.
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated; no patient was withdrawn due to recurrent vomiting or drug-related adverse events.

title: Impact of pre-packaging antimalarial drugs and counselling on compliance with malaria treatment at Port Moresby General Hospital Adult Outpatient Department.
journal: Papua and New Guinea medical journal
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatment compliance interventions with outcome results reported; malaria treatment is the primary focus; not early-phase.
population: adult outpatients with clinical and microscopic diagnosis of malaria
primary_outcome: Compliance with prescribed antimalarial drug treatment assessed on day 4 post treatment
impact_summary: Pre-packaging antimalarial drugs combined with counselling increased compliance with treatment by 18% compared to standard care with no pre-packaging or counselling, while counselling alone increased compliance by 16%.
effect_estimate: 18% (intervention) and 16% (counselling only control A) vs control B
safety_summary: Pre-packaging likely reduces dispensing errors and contamination; no adverse events reported.

title: Assessment of the efficacy of antimalarial drugs recommended by the National Malaria Control Programme in Madagascar: up-dated baseline data from randomized and multi-site clinical trials.
screening_reason: Multi-site RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial drugs for malaria treatment in children; primary purpose is malaria intervention (treatment).
comparator: chloroquine (CQ), sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP), amodiaquine (AQ) as active comparators to artesunate plus amodiaquine (ASAQ)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day-14 and day-28 risk of parasitological failure (unadjusted or adjusted by genotyping)
impact_summary: All treatment regimens except chloroquine achieved clinical cure rates above 97.6% by day-14 and 96.7% by day-28, supporting ASAQ as first-line treatment while showing antimalarial resistance remains low in Madagascar except for chloroquine.
transmission_setting: eight sentinel sites, national malaria endemic setting
safety_summary: No severe side-effects were observed during the follow-up period.

title: Process and effects of a community intervention on malaria in rural Burkina Faso: randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (anaemia prevalence, malaria parasitaemia, fever, splenic enlargement) evaluating a malaria treatment intervention in children in rural Burkina Faso.
comparator: standard care (no home-based CQ treatment intervention)
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: proportion of moderate to severe anaemia in children aged 6-59 months
impact_summary: The community-based home treatment intervention with chloroquine did not show effectiveness in reducing malaria morbidity or anaemia compared to control villages, likely due to contamination, pre-existing differences, and rising chloroquine resistance.
effect_metric: prevalence of anaemia (no significant difference between intervention and control)
effect_estimate: 29% vs 16% (baseline vs follow-up, both groups combined)
p_value: p < 0.0001 (baseline vs follow-up change, not intervention vs control)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; chloroquine treatment was administered by mothers under supervision of women group leaders and local health workers.

title: Long-term field performance of a polyester-based long-lasting insecticidal mosquito net in rural Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (vector-control intervention for malaria prevention) with reported outcome results on insecticide retention and bioassay performance after 3 years of field use.
population: households in rural Uganda using bed nets
primary_outcome: Deltamethrin residue and bioassay performance (60 minute knock-down and 24 hour mortality after a three minute exposure) using a pyrethroid-sensitive Anopheles gambiae s.s. strain
impact_summary: Second generation PermaNet retained insecticide and maintained high vector knockdown and mortality rates over 36 months, meeting WHOPES criteria for LLIN, whereas conventionally treated nets and first generation PermaNet lost insecticide and efficacy rapidly.
effect_metric: percentage of nets meeting WHOPES threshold (knockdown ≥95% or mortality ≥80%)

title: High efficacy of two artemisinin-based combinations (artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate plus amodiaquine) for acute uncomplicated malaria in Ibadan, Nigeria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemisinin-based malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years with acute uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate plus amodiaquine was as effective as artemether-lumefantrine, with similar day 28 cure rates and both regimens well tolerated.
effect_metric: odds ratio (day 28 cure rate, PP population)
safety_summary: Both drugs were well-tolerated.

title: Single-day, three-dose treatment with fixed dose combination artesunate/sulfamethoxypyrazine/pyrimethamine to cure Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (artesunate-based combination therapy) with reported outcome results (28-day efficacy and safety).
comparator: same drug regimen given over 3 days with 24-hour dose interval (active comparator, alternative dosing schedule)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment success on day 28 (absence of recrudescence and parasitemia) per WHO 28-day protocol
impact_summary: Both the 24-hour and 3-day dosing regimens of artesunate/sulfamethoxypyrazine/pyrimethamine were highly efficacious and safe, with success rates of 99% and 100% respectively.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events or significant laboratory abnormalities were observed in either treatment group.

title: Efficacy, safety, and selection of molecular markers of drug resistance by two ACTs in Mali.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (ACTs) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: AS monotherapy (5 days) as active comparator; AS+AQ vs AS+SP vs AS monotherapy
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected parasitological cure rate (efficacy) at Day 14 and Day 28
impact_summary: Both ACTs (AS+AQ and AS+SP) achieved nearly 100% efficacy at Day 14 and Day 28, similar to AS monotherapy, but selected molecular markers of resistance to their partner drugs.
effect_estimate: ~100% (ACTs) vs 98.3% and 96.5% (AS monotherapy) at Day 14 and Day 28
safety_summary: No significant adverse event attributable to any of the study drugs was found.

title: Efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in preventing anaemia in pregnancy among Nigerian women.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of IPTp (intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy) with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention that reports outcome results (anaemia incidence at 34 weeks gestation).
population: primigravid and secondigravid pregnant women, 16-30 weeks gestation
primary_outcome: Anaemia (haematocrit<30) at 34 weeks of gestation
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine significantly reduced the incidence of anaemia in pregnancy compared to chloroquine.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine-based combinations for malaria: a randomised blinded trial to compare efficacy, safety and selection of resistance in Malawi.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (day 28 ACPR efficacy, safety, resistance outcomes) testing malaria treatment combinations in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) alone versus combination therapies (CQ+SP, ART+SP, AQ+SP)
population: children aged 1-5 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate
impact_summary: All three combination therapies (AQ+SP, CQ+SP, ART+SP) were superior to SP alone in achieving day 28 ACPR, with AQ+SP showing the highest efficacy (97%) but also more frequent neutropenia.
effect_metric: Day 28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate
safety_summary: Nineteen children developed neutropenia (≤0.5x10^3 cells/microl) by day 14, more common with AQ+SP (p=0.03); no re-emergence of pfcrt 76T mutation detected.

title: Sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine versus amodiaquine for treating uncomplicated childhood malaria in Gabon: a randomized trial to guide national policy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP vs AQ) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria that has reported efficacy outcome results at day 28.
population: children under five years of age with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day-28 PCR-adjusted treatment failure rate (28-day WHO therapeutic efficacy test)
impact_summary: Sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine was significantly more effective than amodiaquine in treating uncomplicated childhood falciparum malaria in Gabon, with lower day-28 PCR-adjusted treatment failure rates.
safety_summary: Both treatments were safe and well-tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions recorded.

title: [Comparative impact of three malaria preventive regimens during pregnancy on maternal anemia due to malaria in Burkina Faso].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria prevention (IPTp) during pregnancy with reported outcome results on maternal anemia.
comparator: weekly chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine vs intermittent preventive treatment with chloroquine (3 doses) vs intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (3 doses)
population: pregnant women of any parity
primary_outcome: reduction of anemia between first and third antenatal consultations
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with three doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was more effective than chloroquine-based regimens (weekly chemoprophylaxis or intermittent chloroquine) in reducing maternal anemia during pregnancy in Burkina Faso.
effect_metric: hemoglobin change and prevalence of moderate anemia
effect_estimate: hemoglobin increased from 10.3 g/dl to 11.4 g/dl; moderate anemia reduced from 65.6% to 36.7% in SP arm
p_value: 0.014 (third antenatal consultation, SP arm); 0.069 (second antenatal consultation, SP arm); 0.72 and 0.55 (chloroquine arms)
follow_up: from first to third antenatal consultation

title: [Randomized clinical trial of two malaria prophylaxis regimens for pregnant women in Faladie, Mali].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria chemoprevention (IPTp) regimens in pregnant women in an endemic area.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Malaria infection at delivery
impact_summary: Intermittent presumptive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was more effective than chloroquine in reducing malaria infection, anemia, and placental infection in pregnant women and their newborns.
effect_metric: reduction in malaria infection at delivery
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; low birth weight observed in 16.7% of newborns overall, with 70.4% in the CQ group.

title: Randomized, comparative study of the efficacy and safety of artesunate plus amodiaquine, administered as a single daily intake versus two daily intakes in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate plus amodiaquine) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; phase not stated but not early-phase exclusion criteria met.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate plus amodiaquine administered as two daily intakes vs single daily intake)
population: patients weighing more than 10 kg with uncomplicated falciparum malaria confirmed by parasitaemia >=1,000/microl
primary_outcome: Adequate response to treatment on Day 14 (WHO definition), PCR-corrected
impact_summary: Artesunate plus amodiaquine given as two daily intakes was non-inferior to the standard single daily intake regimen, with similarly high cure rates and comparable tolerability.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response rate (PCR-corrected) on D14
safety_summary: Drug was well tolerated; main adverse events were gastrointestinal disorders (2.5%) and pruritus (2.5%); safety profiles were similar between groups.

title: The antischistosomal efficacies of artesunate-sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine and artemether-lumefantrine administered as treatment for uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemisinin derivatives) with reported outcome results in humans; primary purpose is malaria intervention (treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum).
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria co-infected with Schistosoma mansoni
primary_outcome: Schistosoma mansoni egg-negative stool status at follow-up after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: All 14 patients co-infected with Schistosoma mansoni became stool-negative for schistosome eggs after treatment with either artesunate-sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine or artemether-lumefantrine for their malaria.
transmission_setting: eastern Sudan, malaria-endemic with schistosomiasis co-endemicity
safety_summary: Not reported

title: A randomized clinical trial comparing safety, clinical and parasitological response to artemether-lumefantrine and chlorproguanil-dapsone in treatment of uncomplicated malaria in pregnancy in Mulago hospital, Uganda.
journal: Journal of infection in developing countries
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine vs chlorproguanil-dapsone) in pregnant women with reported clinical and parasitological outcome results; phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
population: pregnant women in second and third trimester with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological response assessed on days 0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28
impact_summary: Artemether-Lumefantrine and Chlorproguanil-Dapsone showed comparable, high cure rates and similar safety profiles for treating uncomplicated malaria in pregnancy.
effect_metric: clinical and parasitological response (no significant difference by Day 4)
effect_estimate: mean fever clearance time 3.0 days (Lapdap) vs 2.5 days (Coartem); mean parasite clearance time 2.4 vs 2.2 days
safety_summary: Adverse effects were comparable between the two treatment groups.

title: Confirmation of the protective effect of Ascaris lumbricoides on Plasmodium falciparum infection: results of a randomized trial in Madagascar.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (P. falciparum densities) testing an intervention (anti-helminthic treatment) in a malaria-endemic population; malaria outcomes are primary focus.
population: rural population co-infected with Ascaris lumbricoides, Plasmodium falciparum, and Schistosoma mansoni, including children and adults
primary_outcome: P. falciparum parasite density in treated versus control subjects
impact_summary: Levamisole treatment reduced Ascaris egg loads but was associated with a significant increase in P. falciparum densities in subjects aged 5-14 years compared to controls, with no effect in younger children or adults.
effect_estimate: significant increase in treated group aged 5-14 years
transmission_setting: rural Madagascar, lower malaria transmission compared to another Malagasy population studied
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; levamisole was effective in reducing Ascaris egg loads with no reported adverse effects mentioned

title: Adding artesunate to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine greatly improves the treatment efficacy in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria on the coast of Benin, West Africa.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates) comparing antimalarial drug combinations in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected treatment failure at day 28
impact_summary: Adding artesunate to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine greatly reduced treatment failure compared to chloroquine or sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.

title: [Randomized and controlled observation on acupuncture and moxibustion combined with western medicine for treatment of malaria of children in Africa].
journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention in humans with reported outcome results; acupuncture-moxibustion combined with western medicine versus western medicine alone for childhood malaria.
comparator: western medication alone (Quinoline and expectant therapy)
population: children with malaria
primary_outcome: Total effective rate and clinical/lab improvement (fever reduction, malarial parasite density, duration of illness, RBC recovery time)
impact_summary: Acupuncture and moxibustion combined with western medicine showed better therapeutic effect than western medicine alone for treating malaria in children in Africa.

title: Antimalarial resistance and DHFR/DHPS genotypes of Plasmodium falciparum three years after introduction of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine in rural Tanzania.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP and AQ) in humans with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates at 14 and 28 days).
population: under five children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure (clinical and parasitological outcome) at day 14 and day 28
impact_summary: Both sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine showed unacceptably high total treatment failure rates three years after their introduction as first- and second-line malaria treatments in rural Tanzania.

title: Safety of the RTS,S/AS02A malaria vaccine in Mozambican children during a Phase IIb trial.
screening_reason: Published Phase IIb RCT of malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS02A) with reported safety and efficacy outcomes in humans.
comparator: control vaccines (Engerix-B or Prevnar and Hiberix)
population: children aged 1-4 years living in malaria-endemic areas
primary_outcome: Safety and reactogenicity of RTS,S/AS02A vaccine (unsolicited and solicited adverse events, serious adverse events)
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS02A vaccine demonstrated a good safety profile with lower serious adverse events than control vaccines, and most unsolicited adverse events were self-limited.
effect_metric: vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria (reported in prior efficacy analysis)
safety_summary: 1712 unsolicited adverse events recorded post-vaccination (53% intervention, 47% control); most were self-limited with full recovery; local reactogenicity increased with number of doses; fewer serious adverse events in RTS,S/AS02A recipients than controls.

title: Inferiority of single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine intermittent preventive therapy for malaria during pregnancy among HIV-positive Zambian women.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing SP IPTp dosing regimens for malaria prevention in pregnant women, a primary malaria intervention.
comparator: 2-dose SP IPTp regimen (standard) versus monthly SP IPTp
population: HIV-positive pregnant women
primary_outcome: Maternal and neonatal birth outcomes (anemia, parasitemia, prematurity, low birth weight) by number of SP doses received
impact_summary: Single-dose SP IPTp was associated with worse maternal and neonatal outcomes and was more common under the standard 2-dose regimen than under monthly dosing, suggesting monthly IPTp may reduce inadvertent underdosing.
effect_metric: relative risk of receiving only 1 dose (2-dose vs monthly regimen)
safety_summary: Single-dose SP was associated with higher maternal anemia, peripheral and cord blood parasitemia, infant prematurity, and low birth weight compared to higher-dose regimens.

title: Efficacy and safety of artemisinin-based antimalarial in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children in southern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemisinin-based antimalarials for uncomplicated malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine (AL) and artesunate plus amodiaquine (AS+AQ) were well tolerated and highly efficacious, with PCR-adjusted cure rates of 100% for AL and 93.8% for AS+AQ, supporting Tanzania's switch from SP monotherapy to AL.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
transmission_setting: high SP resistance area, malaria endemic southern Tanzania
safety_summary: Both combinations were well tolerated with rapid fever and parasite clearance; hemoglobin improved moderately in both groups (1 g/dl in AL, 0.4 g/dl in AS+AQ, p<0.001).

title: Randomized comparison of amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, artemether-lumefantrine, and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Burkina Faso.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three antimalarial treatment regimens in humans with reported efficacy outcomes for malaria treatment, meeting all inclusion criteria.
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, aged >=6 months
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent parasitemia by day 28 and day 42, unadjusted and PCR-adjusted for recrudescence vs new infection
impact_summary: Amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were more efficacious than artemether-lumefantrine in preventing recurrent parasitemia, though all regimens cleared infection well and had low recrudescence rates.
effect_metric: risk difference in day 28 recurrent parasitemia
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were noted.

title: Rectal versus intravenous quinine for the treatment of childhood cerebral malaria in Kampala, Uganda: a randomized, double-blind clinical trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two treatment modalities for severe malaria with fully reported outcome results including mortality, coma recovery time, and parasite clearance.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, coma recovery time, time to sit unsupported, time to begin oral intake, time until oral quinine tolerated, and death
impact_summary: Intrarectal quinine showed no significant difference in clinical and parasitological outcomes or mortality compared with intravenous quinine, suggesting it is an efficacious alternative when intravenous therapy is not feasible.
safety_summary: Intrarectal quinine was well tolerated, with no major immediate adverse events; mortality was similar between groups (4/56 vs 5/54 deaths).

title: Comparison of different artemisinin-based combinations for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Kigali, Rwanda, an area of resistance to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine: artesunate plus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine versus artesunate plus sulfamethoxypyrazine/pyrimethamine.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based combinations) in humans with reported outcome results (ACPR day 28).
comparator: active comparator (artesunate plus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine vs artesunate plus sulfamethoxypyrazine/pyrimethamine)
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) on day 28
impact_summary: Both artemisinin-based combinations were effective, with As + SP achieving ACPR ≥90% and As + SMP achieving ACPR ≥95%, and both were well tolerated.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) rate
safety_summary: No side effects observed with either combination.

title: Pharmacokinetics and efficacy of piperaquine and chloroquine in Melanesian children with uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (piperaquine-dihydroartemisinin vs chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in children with uncomplicated malaria that reports outcome results (parasitological and clinical responses).
population: Melanesian children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected 42-day adequate clinical and parasitological response and pharmacokinetic parameters of piperaquine and chloroquine
impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved high cure rates (100% and 94%, respectively) but piperaquine's pharmacokinetic profile, despite a longer elimination half-life, may offer limited post-treatment malaria-suppressive protection due to prompt distribution and lack of an active metabolite.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected 42-day adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
safety_summary: No significant differences in age, gender, body weight, or admission parasitemia between groups; no major safety issues reported.

title: Ibuprofen does not affect levels of tumor necrosis factor alpha and soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor types I and II in Gabonese children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine/sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (TNF-alpha and receptor levels); malaria is the primary focus.
population: pediatric patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Serum levels of TNF-alpha, sTNFR-I, and sTNFR-II during treatment of fever
impact_summary: Ibuprofen did not affect serum levels of TNF-alpha, sTNFR-I, or sTNFR-II compared to placebo, though TNF-alpha correlated with body temperature.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events described in abstract.

title: Immune responses after single-dose sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine indicate underestimation of protective efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment in infants.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants) with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, a malaria chemoprevention intervention in humans, with reported outcome results on immune responses and malaria infections.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Anti-P. falciparum IgG antibody levels
impact_summary: SP-treated infants had significantly lower anti-P. falciparum IgG levels, and placebo-treated children had a higher incidence of P. falciparum infections than clinically observed, suggesting IPTi's protective efficacy is underestimated, with no evidence of impaired immune responses after single-dose SP.
safety_summary: No evidence for impaired immune responses after a single dose of SP within the framework of IPTi.

title: Comparison of the therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyremethamine in children and pregnant women.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria treatment in children and pregnant women with reported parasitological failure outcomes.
population: children under 5 years and pregnant women with malaria parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure rate (recrudescence) by day 28 after start of treatment
impact_summary: Children were twice as likely to experience parasitological treatment failure (recrudescence) by day 28 compared with pregnant women, for both chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment.

title: Primaquine clears submicroscopic Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes that persist after treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and artesunate.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP+AS versus SP+AS+PQ) in children with P. falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results (gametocyte prevalence and density at follow-up).
population: Children aged 3-15 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, asexual parasite density 500-100,000 parasites/microL
primary_outcome: P. falciparum gametocyte prevalence and density during 42-day follow-up measured by QT-NASBA
impact_summary: Addition of a single dose of primaquine to SP+AS significantly reduced gametocyte prevalence and density, with only 3.9% of PQ-treated children harbouring gametocytes on day 14 compared to 62.7% in the SP+AS-only group.
safety_summary: Hb levels were reduced in the week following treatment with SP+AS+PQ, related to G6PD deficiency, but recovered to pre-treatment levels or greater within one month; considered a safe approach for individuals without severe anaemia.

title: Marked differences in the prevalence of chloroquine resistance between urban and rural communities in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: RCT comparing CQ-methylene blue to CQ alone in children with uncomplicated malaria that has reported clinical and parasitological outcome results.
population: young children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological failure rates of chloroquine treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine resistance and treatment failure rates were significantly higher in urban areas than rural areas, associated with higher prevalence of the pfcrt T76 mutation and greater drug pressure.
effect_metric: odds ratio for clinical failure with pfcrt T76
transmission_setting: urban vs rural areas in Burkina Faso

title: Varying efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in infants in two similar trials: public health implications.
screening_reason: This is a published comparative analysis of two completed randomized controlled trials of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on clinical malaria efficacy.
design: randomized, placebo-controlled, phase III, comparative analysis of two trials
population: infants receiving routine EPI vaccinations
primary_outcome: clinical malaria incidence
impact_summary: IPTi with SP significantly reduced clinical malaria in Ifakara (high ITN use) but had no effect in Manhiça (no ITN use), suggesting ITN coverage explains the difference in efficacy.
transmission_setting: endemic, varying ITN coverage (68% Ifakara, 0% Manhiça)

title: Mefloquine versus 3-day oral quinine-clindamycin in uncomplicated imported falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments with reported outcome results (discontinuation rates and adverse events); primary focus is malaria treatment in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated imported falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment discontinuation / tolerability
impact_summary: Mefloquine treatment was associated with a higher risk of treatment discontinuation compared to quinine-clindamycin, mainly due to mild gastrointestinal adverse events.
safety_summary: Mefloquine was poorly tolerated, with mainly mild gastrointestinal adverse drug events leading to higher discontinuation rates than quinine-clindamycin.

title: Clinical and pharmacological determinants of the therapeutic response to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for drug-resistant malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with reported outcome results on parasitological failure.
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria including children and adults
primary_outcome: Cumulative risk of parasitological failure (recurrence/recrudescence) at day 42
impact_summary: Plasma piperaquine concentration on day 7, particularly levels below 30 ng/ml, was the major determinant of parasitological failure with both P. falciparum and P. vivax after dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine treatment, with children more likely to have low concentrations despite receiving higher mg/kg doses.
age_range: children and adults (under 15 years and adults)

title: Electrocardiographic safety evaluation of dihydroartemisinin piperaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with reported safety outcome results (ECG findings).
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Change in QTc interval (Bazett's correction) after treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine caused only small changes in QTc interval consistent with recovery from malaria rather than drug-induced cardiotoxicity, indicating no clinically significant ECG effects at therapeutic doses.
effect_estimate: 2 ms (4h post first dose); 14 ms (4h post last dose)
follow_up: until 4 hours after last dose (day 3 of treatment)
safety_summary: No clinically significant effects of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine on the electrocardiogram; small QTc changes attributed to recovery from acute malaria rather than drug toxicity.

title: Comparison of artemether-lumefantrine with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in eastern Nepal.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two malaria treatments in humans; primary focus is malaria treatment intervention with efficacy data.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure assessed from clinical and microscopic evidence of recurrent parasitemia during 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was more effective than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nepal, with no recurrent parasitemia in the AL group compared to 12.1% in the SP group.
safety_summary: Efficacy/safety study conducted; specific adverse event details not reported in abstract.

title: Impact of intermittent preventive anti-malarial treatment on the growth and nutritional status of preschool children in rural Senegal (west Africa).
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (seasonal IPTp with artesunate and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results on growth and nutritional status in children.
population: preschool children
primary_outcome: growth and nutritional status (weight gain, skinfold thickness, height increments)
impact_summary: Seasonal intermittent preventive anti-malarial treatment with artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine significantly improved weight gain and reduced skinfold losses compared to placebo, and prevented an increase in wasting prevalence seen in the control group.

title: [Open radomized study comparing chloroquine and amodiaquine for treatment of uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Aboisso, Cote d' Ivoire].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in humans; primary malaria focus; phase not stated but acceptable.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment outcome/therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine versus amodiaquine
impact_summary: The study compared chloroquine and amodiaquine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children in Aboisso, Cote d'Ivoire.

title: Impact of Olyset nets on malaria transmission in India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticidal bed nets (vector control) for malaria with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and entomological endpoints.
population: rural village residents
primary_outcome: malaria incidence and entomological indices (indoor resting density, mosquito entry, parity rate)
impact_summary: Olyset nets reduced indoor resting density of An. culicifacies, mosquito entry, and parity rate, and only one malaria case occurred in the Olyset net village compared with continued cases in the untreated net and control villages.
effect_estimate: 1 case in Olyset village vs continued cases in other villages
transmission_setting: rural endemic area, vector An. culicifacies

title: A randomized and controlled comparison of the wash-resistances and insecticidal efficacies of four types of deltamethrin-treated nets, over a 6-month period of domestic use with washing every 2 weeks, in a rural area of Iran.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (vector control intervention for malaria prevention) with reported outcome results on wash-resistance and insecticidal efficacy over 6 months of domestic use.
comparator: conventionally treated nets (K-O Tab deltamethrin-treated) and other LLIN brands (Yorkool, A-Z) compared to PermaNet
population: households in a rural area using treated bed nets
primary_outcome: insecticidal efficacy and wash-resistance of treated nets after 6 months of domestic use with washing every 2 weeks
impact_summary: PermaNet nets retained insecticidal activity better than Yorkool and conventionally treated nets after 6 months of biweekly washing, though not significantly better than A-Z or conventionally treated nets in some comparisons, and were the only commercial nets tested that truly appeared to be long-lasting insecticidal nets.

title: Extended follow-up following a phase 2b randomized trial of the candidate malaria vaccines FP9 ME-TRAP and MVA ME-TRAP among children in Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria vaccine intervention in children with 18 months of outcome results (malaria incidence) reported.
population: children aged 1-6 years
primary_outcome: time to parasitaemia >2,500/microl (febrile malaria)
impact_summary: Vaccination with FFM ME-TRAP was not protective against malaria; malaria incidence during 18 months of surveillance was similar in both vaccine groups.
safety_summary: Extended follow-up monitored for serious adverse events; no specific safety concerns reported beyond incidence of malaria.

title: Therapeutic efficacy and effects of artemether-lumefantrine and amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine on gametocyte carriage in children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in southwestern Nigeria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results including cure rates, parasite clearance, and gametocyte carriage.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (parasite clearance and cure rate) and gametocyte carriage
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine cleared parasitemia faster than amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine, but amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine had higher PCR-corrected cure rates and better resolution of anemia, while gametocyte carriage rates were similar between the two treatments.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; all children recovered clinically.

title: Malaria mosquito control using edible fish in western Kenya: preliminary findings of a controlled study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (treated vs. control ponds) testing a malaria vector-control intervention (larvivorous fish) with reported outcome results (94% reduction in Anopheles larvae).
population: Mosquito larvae/immatures in fishponds (entomological study, not human participants)
primary_outcome: Reduction in mosquito larval/immature densities (Anopheles gambiae s.l., Anopheles funestus, and culicine mosquitoes) after introduction of O. niloticus
impact_summary: Introduction of the larvivorous fish Oreochromis niloticus into abandoned fishponds caused a more than 94% reduction in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus and more than 75% reduction in culicine mosquito larvae after 15 weeks compared to an untreated control pond.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in mosquito larvae (Mulla's formula)
safety_summary: Not applicable; fish already farmed and eaten locally, so acceptance not expected to be a problem

title: Age interactions in the development of naturally acquired immunity to Plasmodium falciparum and its clinical presentation.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (Deltaprim) in infants with reported outcome results on clinical malaria, severe malaria, and anaemia incidence.
population: infants aged 2-12 months at enrollment, followed to age 4 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria, severe malaria, and anaemia assessed through hospital-based passive surveillance
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis during infancy markedly reduced malaria and anaemia morbidity in the first year but was followed by a rebound increase in clinical malaria incidence after discontinuation, resulting in slightly higher cumulative clinical malaria but slightly lower severe malaria and anaemia by age 4 compared to placebo.
effect_metric: rate difference in cumulative episodes by age 4 years
effect_ci: clinical malaria: -0.21 to 0.59; severe malaria: -0.27 to 0.03; anaemia: -0.40 to 0.01

title: Clinical efficacy of high dose monotherapy of oral dihydroartemisinin in uncomplicated falciparum malaria in viet nam.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two malaria treatment regimens with reported efficacy outcomes (parasite clearance, fever clearance, recrudescence rates) in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite and fever clearance times (PCT and FCT) and recrudescence rates
impact_summary: High-dose dihydroartemisinin monotherapy for 5 days did not improve efficacy compared to DHA-mefloquine combination, and had a significantly lower radical cure rate.
safety_summary: No difference in clinical manifestations or laboratory tests between groups; no serious adverse events reported.

title: Intermittent preventive treatment in infants as a means of malaria control: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in northern Ghana.
