screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing IPTi (chemoprevention) for malaria prevention in infants; not early-phase.
population: infants
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria and severe anemia during the intervention period (3 to 18 months of age)
impact_summary: IPTi with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine administered at 3, 9, and 15 months of age reduced malaria and severe anemia in infants in northern Ghana, though a rebound of severe malaria occurred after the intervention ended.
safety_summary: Treatment was generally well tolerated; one case of moderately severe skin reaction followed sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment.

title: A comparative study on the efficacy of artesunate plus sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine versus artemether-lumefantrine in eastern Sudan.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (ACPR, treatment failures, PCR-corrected efficacy).
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected treatment outcome (adequate clinical and parasitological response) at day 28
impact_summary: Both AS/SP and AL were highly effective against uncomplicated falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan, with AS/SP showing slightly higher PCR-corrected efficacy than AL.

title: Levamisole inhibits sequestration of infected red blood cells in patients with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of levamisole as adjunctive treatment for falciparum malaria with reported outcome results on parasite sequestration.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: peripheral blood parasitemia and parasite stage distribution over time, and sequestration ratio of infected red blood cells
impact_summary: Levamisole given as an adjunct to quinine decreased sequestration of infected red blood cells, with near-complete prevention of early trophozoite sequestration and over 65% prevention of midtrophozoite sequestration compared with quinine alone.
effect_estimate: near complete prevention of early trophozoite sequestration; >65% prevention of midtrophozoite sequestration

title: Dramatically decreased therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, but not mefloquine, in southern Benin.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of malaria treatment interventions (chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, mefloquine) in children with uncomplicated malaria that has reported outcome results (therapeutic efficacy rates).
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs mefloquine)
population: children presenting with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: In vivo therapeutic efficacy at day 28 (WHO in vivo 28-day protocol), with PCR genotyping (msp1/msp2) to distinguish recrudescence from new infection
impact_summary: Chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed very high treatment failure rates (85.7% and 50%, respectively), while mefloquine remained highly effective (97.5% success).
safety_summary: Chloroquine use was intentionally restricted after 1 month as it was considered dangerous for children due to high failure rates; no other major safety issues reported.

title: Clinical efficacy of chloroquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for Plasmodium vivax treatment in Thailand.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (cure rates) for a malaria treatment intervention (artemether-lumefantrine vs chloroquine for vivax malaria) in humans.
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (clinical and parasitological outcomes)
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine plus primaquine was as effective as chloroquine plus primaquine for treating vivax malaria, with similar adverse events between groups.
transmission_setting: South-East Asia, mixed falciparum-vivax endemic area
safety_summary: Adverse events were similar between the artemether-lumefantrine and chloroquine treatment groups; both regimens were well tolerated.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of four antimalarial combinations in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Senegal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug combinations for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported efficacy and tolerability outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (four different antimalarial drug combinations compared against each other)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological response rate (efficacy) on day 28, corrected for PCR results
impact_summary: All four antimalarial drug combinations were highly effective and well tolerated, with day 28 cure rates of 100% except for the four-dose artemether-lumefantrine regimen which achieved 96.4%.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected clinical and parasitological response rate
safety_summary: All combinations were well tolerated clinically and biologically; no unexpected side-effects observed and all side-effects resolved by end of treatment; no serious side-effects requiring premature termination of treatment.

title: Effects of maternal vitamin supplements on malaria in children born to HIV-infected women.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (vitamin supplementation) in a human population, not early-phase.
population: Children born to HIV-infected women
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria in children up to 2 years of age
impact_summary: Maternal supplementation with multivitamins (B, C, E) excluding vitamin A/beta-carotene during pregnancy and lactation significantly reduced the incidence of clinical malaria in their children by 71% compared with placebo.
effect_metric: percent reduction in incidence of clinical malaria
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: A comparison of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with chloroquine and pyrimethamine for prevention of malaria in pregnant Nigerian women.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with chloroquine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention (IPTp) in pregnant women, with reported outcome results on malaria and anemia.
comparator: chloroquine followed by weekly pyrimethamine (CQ + P)
population: pregnant Nigerian women
primary_outcome: Febrile illness, peripheral parasitemia, anemia at delivery, and low birth weight
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was superior to chloroquine plus pyrimethamine for prevention of malaria and anemia in pregnant Nigerian women.
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported beyond the outcomes measured; low birth weight rates were similar between groups (P = 0.21).

title: A randomized controlled trial of extended intermittent preventive antimalarial treatment in infants.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants), a malaria chemoprevention intervention in humans, with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and anemia.
population: infants (children treated at 3, 9, and 15 months of age)
primary_outcome: malaria incidence
impact_summary: IPTi with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine reduced malaria episodes by 20% overall, but protection was age-dependent and the third dose at 15 months provided no additional benefit and increased anemia episodes.
age_range: 3-15 months at treatment, followed to 21 months post-recruitment
safety_summary: Number of anemia episodes increased after the last IPTi dose (protective efficacy, -24%; 95% CI, -50% to -2%), indicating a negative effect on anemia protection after the third treatment.

title: Efficacy of chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine mono- and combined therapy against falciparum malaria in Sudan.
journal: Eastern Mediterranean health journal = La revue de sante de la Mediterranee orientale = al-Majallah al-sihhiyah li-sharq al-mutawassit
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing malaria treatment efficacy (chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in humans with reported outcome results (failure rates); malaria is the primary focus.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria; children under 5 years assessed separately
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate (parasitological/clinical failure) after chloroquine, sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, or combined therapy
impact_summary: Chloroquine had high failure rates (43.4% in northern Sudan, 80.2% in southern Sudan), sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine had a low failure rate (4.4%), and combined therapy had intermediate failure rates (14.5% and 5.9% in two sites).
age_range: children and adults; children under 5 years in southern sites

title: Pharmacokinetics of mefloquine with dihydroartemisinin as 2-day regimens in patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine-dihydroartemisinin combination) with reported clinical outcome results (treatment response, recrudescence during 42-day follow-up).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics of mefloquine (MQ) in combination with dihydroartemisinin (DHA)
impact_summary: Both MQ-DHA regimens were well tolerated with similar mefloquine pharmacokinetics and no recrudescence at 42 days, with no pharmacokinetic drug interaction observed, favoring the regimen with MQ given 24 hours after initial DHA dose for compliance.
effect_metric: time period maintaining whole blood MQ concentration above 500 ng/ml
safety_summary: Both combination regimens were well tolerated.

title: Artemether-lumefantrine versus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for treatment of malaria: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments in children with uncomplicated malaria that has reported full outcome results including efficacy and safety endpoints.
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent parasitemia at 28 and 42 days, unadjusted and adjusted by genotyping to distinguish recrudescences and new infections
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was superior to artemether-lumefantrine, significantly reducing the risk of recurrent parasitemia and gametocytemia while improving hemoglobin recovery.
effect_metric: risk difference in recurrent parasitemia at 28 days (unadjusted)
transmission_setting: area of very high malaria transmission intensity
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; serious adverse events were uncommon and unrelated to study drugs.

title: Effect of artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine on haematological recovery and anaemia, in Kenyan children with uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of antimalarial treatment (artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in Kenyan children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that has reported full outcome results on haematological recovery and anaemia.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Haematological recovery, defined as a day-28 haemoglobin concentration of at least 11 g/dl
impact_summary: Neither artesunate regimen (AS1 or AS3) improved haematological recovery, day-28 haemoglobin, or reduction in anaemia prevalence compared with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.

title: Randomized clinical trial of artemisinin versus non-artemisinin combination therapy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Madagascar.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (parasitological failure, clinical cure rates) at days 14 and 28.
comparator: chloroquine (CQ), amodiaquine (AQ), sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP), and artesunate plus amodiaquine (AQ+AS) as active comparators
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day-14 and day-28 risk of parasitological treatment failure (unadjusted and PCR-adjusted)
impact_summary: All treatment regimens except chloroquine achieved clinical cure rates above 97% by day 14 and 92% by day 28 (PCR-corrected), with AQ+SP as effective as AQ+AS and associated with a lower risk of new infection.

title: Cotrimoxazole in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in nigerian children : a controlled clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in malaria treatment.
population: children with clinical and parasitological evidence of P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times and cure rates on days 14, 21 and 28
impact_summary: Cotrimoxazole showed similar efficacy to pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in treating acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
transmission_setting: area of high malaria transmission, endemic Southwest Nigeria
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated.

title: Efficacy of antimalarial treatment in Guinea: in vivo study of two artemisinin combination therapies in Dabola and molecular markers of resistance to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in N'Zérékoré.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin combination therapies for malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy outcomes.
population: children aged 6-59 months with falciparum malaria (Dabola); patients in refugee camp for molecular genotyping (Laine)
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted treatment failure rate at day 28 (Dabola); prevalence of dhfr/dhps resistance mutations (Laine)
impact_summary: Both AS/amodiaquine and AS/sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine were highly efficacious in Dabola, while molecular evidence in Laine showed established resistance to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, supporting Guinea's adoption of AS/AQ as first-line treatment.
transmission_setting: West Africa, endemic malaria region including refugee camp settings
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Comparative study of the effectiveness and pharmacokinetics of two rectal artesunate/oral mefloquine combination regimens for the treatment of uncomplicated childhood falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate/mefloquine combination) in children with reported efficacy outcomes (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates, recrudescence).
comparator: active comparator (higher dose rectal artesunate regimen vs lower dose regimen)
population: children aged 1-14 years with uncomplicated multi-drug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and proportion of patients with recrudescence
impact_summary: Both the 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day rectal artesunate regimens followed by oral mefloquine were safe and equally effective, achieving a 100% cure rate at 28-day follow-up, with no additional benefit from the higher dose.
safety_summary: Both regimens were reported as safe with no significant adverse events noted; safety was comparable between groups.

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine efficacy and selection of Plasmodium falciparum DHFR mutations in Burkina Faso before its introduction as intermittent preventive treatment for pregnant women.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (a malaria treatment) with reported efficacy outcomes in children; primary purpose is malaria intervention and results are published.
population: children between 6 months and 15 years of age
primary_outcome: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment efficacy (PCR-corrected and uncorrected treatment failure) and prevalence of DHFR/DHPS resistance mutations
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failure was high and associated with a high prevalence of DHFR resistance mutations, suggesting it should not be used as monotherapy.

title: Artesunate, artemether or quinine in severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria?
screening_reason: Published RCT of artesunate vs quinine for severe malaria treatment with reported mortality outcomes; not early-phase.
population: adults with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality
impact_summary: Artesunate reduced mortality in adults with severe falciparum malaria compared to quinine, with mortality of 15% versus 22%.
transmission_setting: severe malaria endemic areas in Asia

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artesunate-amodiaquine: superior efficacy and posttreatment prophylaxis against multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for malaria with reported outcome results (parasitological failure rates, recrudescence, safety); primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
population: Patients with malaria infection (P. falciparum, P. vivax, or mixed) in southern Papua
primary_outcome: Overall cumulative parasitological failure rate at day 42
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHP) was significantly more effective and better tolerated than artesunate-amodiaquine (AAQ) against multidrug-resistant P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria, with lower failure rates, less anemia, and reduced gametocyte carriage.
effect_metric: hazard ratio (parasitological failure rate at day 42, AAQ vs DHP)
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum and P. vivax co-endemic area
safety_summary: AAQ recipients were 2.95-fold (95% CI, 1.2- to 4.9-fold) more likely to be anemic and 14.5-fold (95% CI, 3.4- to 61-fold) more likely to carry P. vivax gametocytes compared with DHP recipients; DHP was better tolerated overall.

title: Low-level malaria infections detected by a sensitive polymerase chain reaction assay and use of this technique in the evaluation of malaria vaccines in an endemic area.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (FP9 ME-TRAP/MVA ME-TRAP) with reported outcome results on infection rates and immunogenicity in humans; Phase II vaccine evaluation study.
comparator: rabies vaccine (active comparator); sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs no SP
population: adult volunteers in a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Prevalence of low-level malaria infection (20 parasites/mL) detected by sensitive PCR assay
impact_summary: The FP9 ME-TRAP/MVA ME-TRAP vaccine regimen showed low T-cell immunogenicity and no protection against infection, and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine did not reduce very low-density infections but did reduce higher density infections.
effect_estimate: no significant difference between SP and no-SP groups
safety_summary: All volunteers received primaquine and Lapdap plus artesunate to clear parasites; no major safety concerns reported beyond reduced vaccine immunogenicity.

title: Artemisinin-based combination therapy for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Colombia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based combination therapy for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results including efficacy, gametocyte carriage, and safety.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic response (efficacy) based on per protocol analysis and PCR genotyping, and Kaplan-Meier survival estimates
impact_summary: Both amodiaquine/placebo and amodiaquine/artesunate regimens were highly effective and similarly efficacious, but adding artesunate significantly reduced gametocyte carriage without worsening tolerability.
safety_summary: Most subjects in both groups reported at least one drug-related adverse event (81% amodiaquine/placebo, 75.6% amodiaquine/artesunate); symptoms were generally mild and self-limiting with no serious adverse events; two patients on amodiaquine/artesunate withdrew due to intolerance.

title: Randomized controlled trial of fosmidomycin-clindamycin versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments in children with P. falciparum malaria, reporting outcome results (94% efficacy) with malaria treatment as primary purpose.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: efficacy of treatment (parasitological/clinical cure)
impact_summary: Fosmidomycin-clindamycin and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed comparably good tolerability and identical high efficacy of 94% in treating uncomplicated malaria.
safety_summary: Both treatments showed comparably good tolerability.

title: Activities of amodiaquine, artesunate, and artesunate-amodiaquine against asexual- and sexual-stage parasites in falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions (amodiaquine, artesunate, artesunate-amodiaquine) in children with P. falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results on parasite and gametocyte clearance.
comparator: active comparator (amodiaquine vs artesunate vs artesunate-amodiaquine)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and gametocyte carriage rate
impact_summary: Artesunate and artesunate-amodiaquine achieved faster parasite clearance and lower gametocyte carriage than amodiaquine alone, suggesting reduced transmissibility.
effect_metric: parasite clearance time and gametocyte carriage rate
effect_estimate: parasite clearance 1.4 days (artesunate) or 1.4 days (artesunate-amodiaquine) vs 3.2 days (amodiaquine); gametocyte carriage 3.3% or 1.7% vs 11.7%

title: Community-randomized trial of lambdacyhalothrin-treated hammock nets for malaria control in Yanomami communities in the Amazon region of Venezuela.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results demonstrating malaria intervention (treated hammock nets) effectiveness in humans; vector-control trials are not early-phase.
population: Yanomami indigenous ethnic group
primary_outcome: malaria incidence rate per thousand person-years at risk
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated hammock nets reduced malaria incidence by 56% and parasitaemia prevalence by 83% compared to placebo-treated hammock nets among the Yanomami.
transmission_setting: moderate malaria transmission, forested Amazon region, Anopheles darlingi vector
safety_summary: Prevalence of splenomegaly and anaemia was too low to detect any possible reduction as a result of ITHN; no other safety issues reported.

title: A randomized open study to assess the efficacy and tolerability of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Cambodia.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans with malaria.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR genotyping-adjusted cure rate on day 63
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was as efficacious as mefloquine-artesunate but was better tolerated, with fewer adverse effects such as vomiting, dizziness, palpitations, and sleep disorders.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events occurred; MAS3 group had significantly more vomiting (P=0.03), dizziness (P=0.002), palpitations (P=0.04), and sleep disorders (P=0.03), consistent with mefloquine's known side-effect profile.

title: Revaccination with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine does not reduce morbidity from malaria in African children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria prevention intervention (BCG revaccination) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria morbidity.
population: children previously vaccinated with BCG at birth, without strong tuberculin reaction
primary_outcome: Incidence of first episodes of malaria (any level of parasitaemia) during the 2003 malaria transmission season
impact_summary: BCG revaccination at 19 months did not reduce malaria morbidity and was associated with a higher incidence of all-cause hospitalisation compared to controls.
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, capital of Guinea-Bissau
safety_summary: Incidence of all-cause hospitalisation was higher among BCG-revaccinated children than controls (IRR = 2.13; 95% CI: 1.10-4.13).

title: Molecular genotyping in a malaria treatment trial in Uganda - unexpected high rate of new infections within 2 weeks after treatment.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate plus SP vs SP alone) with reported outcome results on parasite genotyping and recrudescence/reinfection rates.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Differentiation of recrudescent from new Plasmodium falciparum infections by PCR genotyping following antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: PCR genotyping revealed an unexpectedly high proportion of new infections (as opposed to recrudescences) occurring as early as day 7 and 14 post-treatment, with the ratio of new to recrudescent infections increasing significantly over follow-up.
effect_metric: ratio of new to recrudescent infections

title: Chloroquine prophylaxis against vivax malaria in pregnancy: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine prophylaxis) in pregnancy with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety.
population: pregnant women (Karen)
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. vivax malaria episodes during pregnancy
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis completely prevented P. vivax episodes in pregnant women, while placebo group had 10.1% experiencing at least one episode; there was no significant difference in P. falciparum episodes between groups.
effect_metric: proportion with at least one P. vivax episode
age_range: pregnant women; infants followed to 12 months
safety_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis was well tolerated with no significant difference in overall reported side effects compared to placebo, except for longer duration of palpitations and sleeping disorders in the CQ group; no impact on maternal anaemia, birth weight, gestational age, or infant growth, neurological development, or visual acuity.

title: Pharmacokinetic study of artemether-lumefantrine given once daily for the treatment of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcomes comparing two dosing regimens of artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment.
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Comparison of the areas under the plasma lumefantrine concentration-time curves (AUC) between once-daily and twice-daily dosing regimens
impact_summary: Once-daily dosing of artemether-lumefantrine resulted in 30% lower lumefantrine drug exposure (AUC) compared with the conventional twice-daily regimen, with a trend toward lower cure rates.
effect_estimate: 30% lower in once-daily vs twice-daily regimen
safety_summary: Tolerability profiles were assessed as a secondary endpoint; no significant differences in peak plasma concentrations were reported, and no major safety concerns were highlighted.

title: Artemether-lumefantrine versus amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Burkina Faso: a randomised non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans; meets all inclusion criteria.
population: patients aged 6 months or older with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: risk of treatment failure within 28 days, either unadjusted or adjusted by genotyping to distinguish recrudescence from new infection
impact_summary: Amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was more effective than artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with lower rates of recurrent symptomatic malaria and recurrent parasitaemia.
safety_summary: Both regimens were safe and well tolerated; pruritus was more common with amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine than with artemether-lumefantrine.

title: Dihydroartemisinin suppository in moderately severe malaria: comparative efficacy of dihydroartemisinin suppository versus intramuscular artemeter followed by oral sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the management of moderately severe malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin derivatives for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at 14 and 28 days.
comparator: intramuscular artemether followed by oral sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
population: children with moderately severe malaria for whom oral therapy was not appropriate
primary_outcome: Parasitologic cure rate at day 14 and day 28, and parasite/fever clearance times
impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin suppository and intramuscular artemether regimens (each followed by oral sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) were efficacious and well tolerated, with similar cure rates and clearance times.
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated.

title: Influence of consecutive-day blood sampling on polymerase chain reaction-adjusted parasitological cure rates in an antimalarial-drug trial conducted in Tanzania.
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial drugs (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs artemether-lumefantrine) in children with malaria, with reported outcome results on parasitological cure rates.
comparator: single-day blood sampling vs consecutive-day blood sampling
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted parasitological cure rate (recrudescence classification) via msp2 and msp1 genotyping comparing single- vs consecutive-day sampling
impact_summary: Consecutive-day blood sampling identified more recrudescences than single-day sampling, but the sensitivity of msp1 genotyping relative to msp2 genotyping was similar between the two sampling methods (82% vs 81%), indicating that PCR-adjusted results depend significantly on sampling methodology.
effect_metric: sensitivity of single-day PCR protocol in msp1 genotyping

title: Amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine select distinct alleles of the Plasmodium falciparum mdr1 gene in Tanzanian children treated for uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment interventions (artemether-lumefantrine and amodiaquine) in humans with reported outcome results on treatment efficacy and parasite genetics.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pfmdr1 allele selection (86Y, 184Y, 1246Y) in pretreatment vs treatment-failure isolates
impact_summary: Amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine selected for opposite Pfmdr1 alleles among treatment failures, with children retaining the 86Y/184Y/1246Y haplotype significantly more likely after AQ treatment than AL treatment.

title: Rifampicin/Cotrimoxazole/Isoniazid versus mefloquine or quinine + sulfadoxine- pyrimethamine for malaria: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three treatment arms for drug-resistant malaria with reported outcome results on safety and efficacy.
design: open-label, block-randomised, comparative, multicentric, noninferiority trial, phase 3
population: patients of all ages with recurrent uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Rate of clinical and/or parasitological failure at day 14 and incidence of clinical and laboratory adverse events
impact_summary: Cotrifazid showed short-term clinical equivalence to mefloquine and quinine+SP but had a significantly higher parasitological failure rate at day 14, making it a poor alternative therapy for malaria.
effect_estimate: 9% (PCR corrected 8%) for Cotrifazid vs 0% for mefloquine and 3% for quinine+SP
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region of Madang and East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea
safety_summary: Cotrifazid group experienced lower overall incidence of adverse events than the mefloquine and quinine+SP groups.

title: [Plasmodium vivax malaria: treatment of primary attacks with primaquine, in three different doses, and a fixed dose of chloroquine, Antioquia, Colombia, 2003-2004].
journal: Biomedica : revista del Instituto Nacional de Salud
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine and primaquine regimens) in humans with reported outcome results on treatment efficacy.
comparator: active comparator (different primaquine doses with fixed chloroquine dose)
population: adult patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: antimalarial treatment response (early failure, late failure, adequate response per WHO-2001 protocol)
impact_summary: All 210 evaluated patients showed adequate treatment response to chloroquine-primaquine regardless of the primaquine dose used.
effect_metric: proportion with adequate clinical and parasitological response
transmission_setting: endemic region of Colombia (Turbo and El Bagre)
safety_summary: Adverse effects of CQ-PQ treatment were assessed; clinical findings similar to those described by other authors, specific adverse event rates not detailed in abstract.

title: Over-diagnosis of malaria is not a lost cause.
screening_reason: Published RCT of IPTi (malaria chemoprevention intervention in infants) with reported outcome results on diagnostic behavior and malaria case confirmation.
population: infants; hospital patients diagnosed with malaria
primary_outcome: Proportion of outpatient and inpatient cases diagnosed as malaria and proportion of blood slides positive for malaria parasites
impact_summary: Introduction of a training programme with laboratory quality assurance and supervision reduced over-diagnosis of malaria, with clinical diagnoses of malaria decreasing from 28-34% to 17% and slide positivity decreasing from 21% to 7% after 2005.

title: Efficacy of three artemisinin combination therapies for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Republic of Congo.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin combinations) in humans with reported 28-day efficacy outcomes; phase not stated but treatment trial is not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (three artemisinin combination therapies compared to each other)
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Proportion of cases of true (PCR-corrected) treatment success at day 28
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine achieved a higher PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 than artesunate+SP and artesunate+amodiaquine, making it the more clinically effective treatment in this area.
transmission_setting: Republic of Congo, Pool Province, malaria-endemic area
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported.

title: Estimating true antimalarial efficacy by heteroduplex tracking assay in patients with complex Plasmodium falciparum infections.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment in humans with reported outcome results (treatment efficacy and treatment failure classification).
comparator: three antimalarial treatments compared to each other
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Treatment efficacy assessed by heteroduplex tracking assay classification of recurrent episodes as treatment failure or reinfection
impact_summary: An elevated complexity of infection was strongly associated with treatment failure, and using HTA-based methods, 66% of recurrent episodes could be definitively classified as treatment failures or reinfections, allowing estimation of true antimalarial efficacy.
effect_metric: association between complexity of infection and treatment failure

title: Improved efficacy with amodiaquine instead of chloroquine in sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination treatment of falciparum malaria in Uganda: experience with fixed-dose formulation.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes comparing two malaria treatment regimens (amodiaquine+sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine vs chloroquine+sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria aged 6 months to 5 years
primary_outcome: Day 14 per protocol clinical and parasitological response according to WHO criteria
impact_summary: Amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (AQ+SP) was significantly more efficacious than the fixed-dose chloroquine plus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (CQ+SP, Homapak) for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Ugandan children, especially the youngest.
effect_metric: Day 14 adequate clinical and parasitological response rate

title: Combined chloroquine, sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and primaquine against Plasmodium falciparum in Central Java, Indonesia.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drug combinations (CQ+SP vs CQ) with reported clinical and parasitological outcome results for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment.
comparator: chloroquine monotherapy vs chloroquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with or without primaquine
population: subjects with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological cure of uncomplicated falciparum malaria at day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine combined with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved significantly higher cure rates than chloroquine alone, and primaquine accelerated gametocyte clearance without affecting asexual parasite cure.
transmission_setting: Menoreh Hills region, southern Central Java, Indonesia
safety_summary: CQ combined with SP was safe and well-tolerated

title: An open label randomized comparison of mefloquine-artesunate as separate tablets vs. a new co-formulated combination for the treatment of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (day 63 cure rates) testing a malaria treatment intervention (artemisinin-based combination therapy) in humans; not early-phase.
population: adults and children with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 63 PCR-adjusted cure rate
impact_summary: The new fixed-dose combination of mefloquine-artesunate had similar efficacy to the separate tablet regimen, with lower incidence of early vomiting and good tolerability.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, north-western border of Thailand
safety_summary: Lower incidence of early vomiting in the fixed combination group; treatment was well tolerated overall.

title: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of atovaquone-proguanil vs. sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of malarial anaemia in Zambian children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments with reported outcome results in malaria-infected children; primary purpose is malaria treatment.
population: children with moderately severe malarial anaemia and P. falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Treatment failure defined as need for blood transfusion or treatment with quinine, persistent anaemia, or death within 14 days from start of treatment
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil was more effective than sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in treating malarial anaemia, with lower treatment failure and reduced need for blood transfusion.
transmission_setting: area with a modest level of SP resistance
safety_summary: Six children died (five in the AP group), none considered directly related to treatment; ten children required blood transfusion, all in the SP group.

title: The pharmacokinetics of artemether and lumefantrine in pregnant women with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting pharmacokinetic outcome results for artemether-lumefantrine treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in pregnant women; phase not explicitly stated but treatment efficacy study consistent with Phase 3.
population: pregnant women with recrudescent uncomplicated multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic parameters of artemether and lumefantrine (plasma concentrations, elimination) in pregnant women
impact_summary: Pregnant women had lower plasma concentrations of artemether, dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine, and more rapid elimination of lumefantrine compared to non-pregnant adults, which may compromise cure rates.

title: A phase 2b randomised trial of the candidate malaria vaccines FP9 ME-TRAP and MVA ME-TRAP among children in Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention in children with reported outcome results on clinical malaria efficacy.
population: healthy 1- to 6-year-old children
primary_outcome: Time to a parasitaemia of over 2,500 parasites/µl (time to first episode of clinical malaria)
impact_summary: The FFM ME-TRAP vaccination regimen did not protect against febrile malaria in children and was associated with a shorter time to first malaria episode than control.
transmission_setting: rural, malaria-endemic area of coastal Kenya
safety_summary: The regimen was moderately immunogenic; no specific safety concerns reported beyond lower than expected T cell responses.

title: A randomized controlled trial of folate supplementation when treating malaria in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported efficacy outcomes (treatment failure rate and haemoglobin change at day 14).
population: pregnant women with uncomplicated malaria at first antenatal visit
primary_outcome: SP treatment failure rate and change in haemoglobin at day 14
impact_summary: Concomitant use of 5 mg folic acid supplementation compromised the efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treating uncomplicated malaria in pregnant women, while 0.4 mg folic acid did not significantly affect efficacy.
effect_metric: adjusted hazard ratio for treatment failure
effect_estimate: 2.19 (FA 5 mg vs placebo); 1.07 (FA 0.4 mg vs placebo)
age_range: pregnant women, gestational age 17 to 34 weeks
safety_summary: No specific adverse event data reported beyond haemoglobin outcomes; haemoglobin levels at day 14 were not significantly different between arms.

title: Azithromycin combination therapy with artesunate or quinine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults: a randomized, phase 2 clinical trial in Thailand.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of azithromycin combinations for P. falciparum malaria treatment in adults with reported outcome results (28-day cure rates and safety data).
comparator: azithromycin-quinine combinations compared to azithromycin-artesunate combinations (active comparator, no placebo)
population: adults with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Azithromycin combined with artesunate or standard-dose quinine achieved similarly high 28-day cure rates (~89-92%), while azithromycin plus low-dose quinine had a lower cure rate (73.3%) with early treatment failures, and artesunate combinations led to faster clinical and parasitological improvement than quinine combinations.
safety_summary: No deaths or drug-related serious adverse events were observed; treatment-related adverse events were significantly more common in the quinine cohorts (P<.001).

title: Efficacy, safety, and tolerability of amodiaquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine used alone or in combination for malaria treatment in pregnancy: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (amodiaquine ± sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.
population: pregnant women with gestational age 16 weeks or more, positive malaria test with P falciparum asexual parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure by day 28 of treatment
impact_summary: Amodiaquine alone or combined with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine resulted in significantly lower parasitological failure rates by day 28 than chloroquine or sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone, though with more minor side-effects.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected parasitological failure rate by day 28
safety_summary: No serious liver toxic effects or white-blood-cell dyscrasias were noted; minor side-effects reported more often on day 3 in amodiaquine (86%) and amodiaquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (90%) groups than sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (48%) or no antimalarial drugs (34%), p<0.0001 for every comparison.

title: A randomized trial of artesunate-sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mali.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarials for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in humans; not early-phase.
population: Patients at least 6 months of age with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28 using WHO 28-day protocol
impact_summary: Artesunate-sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine achieved a significantly higher cure rate than artemether-lumefantrine and was well tolerated with no serious adverse events.
transmission_setting: Seasonal transmission (studied during two transmission seasons, 2003 and 2004) in Sotuba, Mali
safety_summary: No serious adverse events occurred; artesunate-sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine was well tolerated.

title: Efficacy of three chloroquine-primaquine regimens for treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria in Colombia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (chloroquine-primaquine regimens) for P. vivax malaria in humans with reported efficacy outcomes at 6-month follow-up.
comparator: active comparator (different primaquine dose regimens: 45 mg vs 105 mg vs 210 mg total dose)
population: adults with P. vivax malaria infection
primary_outcome: Cure rate for blood-stage P. vivax malaria by day 28 and post-treatment reappearance of parasitemia during six months of follow-up
impact_summary: A total primaquine dose of 210 mg was significantly more protective against recurrence of P. vivax parasitemia than lower doses (45 mg and 105 mg), while all regimens achieved 100% cure of blood-stage infection by day 28.

title: Cost-effectiveness study of three antimalarial drug combinations in Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized effectiveness trial of antimalarial drug combinations in Tanzanian children with malaria that has reported outcome results (parasitological failure rates and cost-effectiveness).
design: randomised effectiveness trial with embedded economic evaluation, phase 3
population: children with non-severe slide-proven malaria
primary_outcome: cost-effectiveness measured as resource savings and cases of malaria averted based on parasitological failure rates at days 14 and 28
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine and AQ+artesunate were the most cost-effective drug combinations, dominating monotherapy despite being more expensive, due to significantly greater effectiveness in an area of high drug resistance.
effect_metric: net cost savings per case averted
effect_estimate: approximately US$22.40 net saving (US$1.70 gross saving) per case averted for AL and AQ+AS at day 28
transmission_setting: area of high drug resistance, malaria endemic

title: The effects of artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine on the hepatomegaly associated with Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine) for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results on hepatomegaly resolution.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and hepatomegaly
primary_outcome: Hepatomegaly reduction ratio (HRR) and hepatomegaly resolution rate (HRSR)
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine and amodiaquine-sulfalene-pyrimethamine showed similar effects on hepatomegaly reduction and resolution rates in children with falciparum malaria, with recurrence of parasitaemia associated with reoccurrence of hepatomegaly.

title: Gametocytaemia after drug treatment of asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (SP and SP+AS) versus placebo in P. falciparum-infected humans with reported outcome results on gametocyte prevalence and carriage.
design: three-arm, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, phase 3
population: asymptomatic carriers of P. falciparum, adults and children over 6 months old
primary_outcome: presence of gametocytes 7 and 56 days after treatment, and duration and density of gametocytaemia over 2 months
impact_summary: Treatment of asymptomatic P. falciparum carriers with SP or SP plus artesunate did not increase gametocyte carriage and substantially reduced gametocyte carriage compared to placebo over 2 months.
effect_metric: percent reduction in gametocyte carriage (area under curve) vs placebo
p_value: 0.87 (day 7 SP vs placebo); 0.28 (day 7 SP+AS vs placebo)
transmission_setting: dry season, low malaria transmission, rural villages

title: Long-term impact of malaria chemoprophylaxis on cognitive abilities and educational attainment: follow-up of a controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (cluster-randomized) of malaria chemoprophylaxis intervention with reported long-term outcome results on cognitive and educational measures; not early-phase.
design: household-based cluster-controlled intervention trial, follow-up study
population: children aged 3-59 months at enrollment, followed up as adolescents/young adults
primary_outcome: cognitive abilities, school enrolment, and educational attainment (highest grade reached at school)
impact_summary: No significant overall effect of childhood malaria chemoprophylaxis on cognitive abilities was found, but there were suggestive long-term benefits on cognitive function among those with limited post-trial prophylaxis and on educational attainment.
effect_metric: treatment effect (standard deviations) and grade difference
effect_estimate: 0.2 SD (no post-trial prophylaxis), 0.4 SD (<1 y post-trial prophylaxis); 0.52 grades higher educational attainment
age_range: 3-59 months at enrollment; 14 y 9 mo to 19 y 6 mo at follow-up
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: A randomised trial to assess the safety and efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Rwanda.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
population: children aged 12-59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted 28-day adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Coartem was more efficacious than AQ+SP, achieving significantly higher 28-day cure rates and faster parasite clearance, with a good safety profile.
transmission_setting: highly endemic and multidrug-resistant malaria area
safety_summary: Coartem had a good safety and tolerability profile; adverse events were recorded with no significant differences in packed cell volume changes between treatments.

title: Artesunate + amodiaquine and artesunate + sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Democratic Republic of Congo: a clinical trial with determination of sulphadoxine and pyrimethamine-resistant haplotypes.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate combinations) in humans with reported primary efficacy outcomes (28-day parasite recurrence and recrudescence rates).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day parasite recurrence rate (PCR-corrected recrudescence rate)
impact_summary: AS + AQ had significantly higher efficacy than AS + SP, with lower day 28 parasite recurrence and recrudescence rates.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region of Democratic Republic of Congo

title: Volume expansion with albumin compared to gelofusine in children with severe malaria: results of a controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (fluid resuscitation in severe malaria) with reported outcome results.
comparator: Gelofusine (succinylated modified fluid gelatin 4% intravenous infusion)
population: children with severe falciparum malaria with impaired consciousness or deep breathing, metabolic acidosis, and clinical features of shock
primary_outcome: resolution of shock and acidosis
impact_summary: Albumin infusion was associated with lower mortality than Gelofusine, despite similar effects on resolution of shock and acidosis.
safety_summary: No participant developed pulmonary oedema or fluid overload; fatal neurological events were more common in the Gelofusine group.

title: Safety and tolerability of elubaquine (bulaquine, CDRI 80/53) for treatment of Plasmidium vivax malaria in Thailand.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported safety and efficacy outcomes comparing anti-relapse drugs for P. vivax malaria treatment in humans.
population: Patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria infection, including some with G6PD deficiency
primary_outcome: Safety and tolerability of anti-relapse treatment (hematologic effects, adverse events, relapse rate)
impact_summary: Elubaquine was as safe and well tolerated as primaquine, causing no significant hemolysis even in G6PD-deficient patients, unlike primaquine.
p_value: 0.015, 0.027, 0.048 (hematocrit changes on days 7, 8, 9 in primaquine G6PD-deficient patients)
follow_up: Not clearly stated (relapse monitored at least to day 26)
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; adverse effects (significant hematocrit drop) occurred only in G6PD-deficient patients treated with primaquine, not elubaquine.

title: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of Malarone for malaria prophylaxis in non-immune Colombian soldiers.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (Malarone) with reported efficacy outcome results in a non-immune population in an endemic area.
population: non-immune Colombian soldiers, male
primary_outcome: Incidence of parasitemia (malaria infection) during prophylaxis
impact_summary: Malarone provided 100% protective efficacy against malaria (including P. vivax) compared to placebo among non-immune Colombian soldiers.
effect_estimate: 100% (96% including one case with undetectable drug levels)
effect_ci: LL 95% CI = 63% (all malaria); LL 95% CI = 58% (P. vivax)
follow_up: 1 day before entering endemic area to 7 days after leaving, duration not specified in weeks
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area of Colombia, predominately P. vivax
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond compliance issues; no specific adverse events reported in abstract.

title: A fixed-dose 24-hour regimen of artesunate plus sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.
journal: Annals of clinical microbiology and antimicrobials
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatment regimens with reported efficacy outcomes (PCR-adjusted cure rates) in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
comparator: active comparator (loose combination of AS+SMP dosed over 3 days)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR genotyping-adjusted cure rate on day 28
impact_summary: Both the fixed-dose 24-hour regimen and the loose 3-day regimen of artesunate plus sulfamethoxypyrazine-pyrimethamine were effective and safe, with no significant difference in cure rates.
safety_summary: Three (4.1%) patients experienced drug-related adverse effects (one in the fixed group, two in the loose group); no gametocytaemia detected during follow-up.

title: Safety and efficacy of lumefantrine-artemether (Coartem) for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Zambian adults.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing artemether-lumefantrine to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
population: adult patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure (early treatment failure, late clinical failure, late parasitological failure) per WHO classification
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was significantly more efficacious than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Zambian adults, with lower treatment failure and faster clinical and parasitological clearance.
effect_metric: odds ratio for total treatment failure (SP vs AL)
safety_summary: AL was well tolerated with faster clearance of clinical symptoms; fever at day 3 was significantly lower and haemoglobin at day 45 significantly higher with AL compared to SP; no major safety concerns reported, though data on AL safety in pregnant women were noted as needed.

title: Different doses of amodiaquine and chloroquine for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children in Guinea-Bissau: implications for future treatment recommendations.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing chloroquine and amodiaquine doses for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (ACPR rates).
comparator: active comparator (different doses of chloroquine vs amodiaquine)
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum monoinfection
primary_outcome: cumulative adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate on Day 28 and number of true recrudescences determined by PCR
impact_summary: Amodiaquine at 30 mg/kg or 15 mg/kg had high cure rates similar to chloroquine 50 mg/kg, while chloroquine 25 mg/kg was less effective, suggesting chloroquine 50 mg/kg could be an interim first-line treatment.
safety_summary: No differences in adverse effects were observed between treatment groups.

title: Insecticide-treated bednets for the prevention of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Cambodia: a cluster-randomized trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of ITN (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (P. falciparum incidence and prevalence).
population: residents of villages in Rattanakiri, North East Cambodia, including under 5-year-olds and older individuals
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum incidence and prevalence measured via cross-sectional surveys and passive surveillance
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednets showed a non-significant reduction in P. falciparum incidence and prevalence overall, with a more pronounced but still non-significant protective effect among children under 5 years of age.
effect_metric: protective efficacy (adjusted rate ratio for incidence)
p_value: not significant (interaction P = 0.042 for age effect)
transmission_setting: rural forested area of North East Cambodia, low to moderate endemicity
age_range: all ages, with subgroup analysis in under 5-year-olds

title: An open, randomized comparison of artesunate plus mefloquine vs. dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Laos).
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing two malaria treatments in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria; phase not stated but treatment trials do not require explicit phase designation.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day cure rate (adjusted for reinfection, by survival analysis)
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was not superior in efficacy to artesunate-mefloquine but caused fewer adverse effects.
p_value: 0.031 (for adverse effects); 0.4 and 0.17 (fever and parasite clearance times)
safety_summary: More patients experienced at least one potential side effect in the AM group (58%) compared to the DP group (44%), P=0.031.

title: Use of insecticide-treated clothes for personal protection against malaria: a community trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated clothes for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on infection rates and mosquito density.
comparator: placebo (clothes and bedding treated with plain water)
population: Somali refugees in Dadaab refugee camps
primary_outcome: Rate of malaria parasite infection
impact_summary: Use of insecticide-treated clothes significantly reduced malaria infection rates and indoor mosquito density, with odds of infection reduced by about 70 percent.
safety_summary: No side effects related to use of the ITCs were observed from the participants.

title: Artemisinin combination therapies for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing artemisinin combination therapies for uncomplicated malaria treatment in humans.
population: Children with confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent symptomatic malaria and recurrent parasitemia at 28 days, unadjusted and adjusted by genotyping to distinguish recrudescences and new infections
impact_summary: Both amodiaquine + artesunate and artemether-lumefantrine were highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated malaria, but artemether-lumefantrine was superior to amodiaquine + artesunate in preventing recurrent malaria due to new infections.
effect_metric: risk difference in recurrent symptomatic malaria
safety_summary: Both regimens were well-tolerated; serious adverse events were uncommon with both regimens.

title: Randomised trial of chloroquine/sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in Gambian children with malaria: impact against multidrug-resistant P. falciparum.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatments (CQ, SP, CQ/SP) in Gambian children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with reported efficacy outcomes at 28 days; phase not stated but appropriate for inclusion.
comparator: SP alone and CQ alone (active comparators)
population: children aged 12 months to 10 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitaemia at any time during 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: CQ/SP combination was more efficacious than CQ alone and similarly efficacious to SP alone for treating uncomplicated malaria, though high prevalence of multidrug-resistant parasites suggests this efficacy is unlikely to be sustained.
transmission_setting: Gambia, area with malaria endemicity (rural/town setting, Farafenni)

title: Chloroquine/sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for gambian children with malaria: transmission to mosquitoes of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results including gametocyte prevalence, infectiousness, and transmission endpoints.
comparator: active comparator (CQ vs SP vs CQ/SP)
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: posttreatment gametocyte prevalence and density, and infectiousness to mosquitoes
impact_summary: Parasites carrying the multidrug-resistant TYRG haplotype had a significant transmission advantage after CQ/SP treatment, though this genotype did not significantly affect in vivo therapeutic efficacy.
effect_estimate: significantly higher oocyst burdens with TYRG haplotype after CQ/SP treatment
transmission_setting: endemic, rural Gambia (Farafenni and surrounding villages)

title: [Coartem and fansimef in the treatment of falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two malaria treatments (Coartem and Fansimef) with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates) in Mali.
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, asexual parasite clearance time, and cure rate at 28 days
impact_summary: Coartem and fansimef showed similar efficacy in treating falciparum malaria with no significant difference in fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, or cure rate at 28 days.

title: Supervised versus unsupervised antimalarial treatment with six-dose artemether-lumefantrine: pharmacokinetic and dosage-related findings from a clinical trial in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of supervised versus unsupervised antimalarial treatment (artemether-lumefantrine) with reported outcome results (lumefantrine concentrations, recrudescence, re-infection risks) in humans with malaria in Uganda.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria treated with six-dose artemether-lumefantrine, subset analyzed pharmacokinetically
primary_outcome: 28-day recrudescence and re-infection risk in relation to lumefantrine plasma concentrations and dose
impact_summary: Unsupervised treatment and lower weight-adjusted lumefantrine dose were associated with lower day 3 and day 7 lumefantrine plasma concentrations, and decreasing lumefantrine dose per kg resulted in up to 13-fold higher adjusted risk of re-infection, with re-infections occurring only in patients with day 7 lumefantrine concentrations below 400 ng/mL.
effect_estimate: up to 13-fold higher risk with decreasing lumefantrine dose per kg
transmission_setting: stable Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum transmission setting
safety_summary: No safety outcomes reported; no recrudescences occurred in either treatment arm.

title: High efficacy of two artemisinin-based combinations (artesunate + amodiaquine and artemether + lumefantrine) in Caala, Central Angola.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based antimalarial combinations in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that has reported efficacy outcomes.
population: children 6-59 months of age with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate + amodiaquine showed high efficacy, with a 100% PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 in both treatment groups.
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; anemia significantly improved in both groups after 28 days (Coartem: 54.1% to 13.4%; ASAQ: 53.1% to 15.9%).

title: Efficacy and safety of beta-arteether and alpha/beta-arteether for treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments (beta-arteether vs alpha/beta-arteether) with reported outcome results (cure rates, fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, safety).
population: adult patients with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate, fever clearance time, and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Both beta-arteether and alpha/beta-arteether were equally safe and efficacious in treating acute falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in cure rates or clearance times.
follow_up: 4 weeks (1 week hospitalization plus 3 weeks post-discharge)
safety_summary: No statistically significant difference in occurrence of side effects between groups; both formulations were considered safe.

title: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial of intermittent preventive treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in Gambian multigravidae.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported outcome results (anaemia, birthweight).
population: multigravidae (pregnant women, multigravida) in a rural area of The Gambia
primary_outcome: Severe anaemia (Hb < 7 g/dl) after delivery and infant birthweight
impact_summary: IPTp with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine did not significantly reduce severe anaemia or increase birthweight overall in Gambian multigravidae, but among women not using bednets, SP was associated with higher infant birthweight.
transmission_setting: rural, malaria-endemic area of The Gambia
safety_summary: No major safety concerns reported; anaemia rates were similar between SP and placebo groups (10.7% vs 8.8% severe anaemia)

title: Intermittent preventive treatment for malaria control administered at the time of routine vaccinations in Mozambican infants: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTi (intermittent preventive treatment in infants) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention in humans that has reported outcome results including clinical malaria incidence and hospital admissions.
population: infants receiving routine EPI vaccinations
primary_outcome: incidence of clinical malaria during the first year of life
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine given alongside routine vaccinations moderately reduced the incidence of clinical malaria and hospital admissions in Mozambican infants without safety concerns.
effect_metric: reduction in incidence of clinical malaria
safety_summary: IPTi was well tolerated, with no adverse events associated with SP documented; serological responses to EPI vaccines were not modified.

title: Efficacy and effectiveness of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artesunate-mefloquine in falciparum malaria: an open-label randomised comparison.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans; primary endpoint (PCR-confirmed parasitological failure rate) is clearly stated and analyzed.
population: children aged 1 year or older and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-confirmed parasitological failure rate by day 42
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was as efficacious as artesunate-mefloquine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with very low failure rates in both groups and good effectiveness even without supervision.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, southeast Asia
safety_summary: One death 22 days after receiving dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; gametocytaemia developed more frequently with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine than artesunate-mefloquine (relative risk 4.2, 95% CI 1.6-11.0, p=0.011); otherwise well tolerated by all age groups.

title: Safety and efficacy of dihydroartemisinin/piperaquine (Artekin) for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Rwandan children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (DHA-PQP) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; not early-phase.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response) by Day 28
impact_summary: DHA-PQP and AQ+AS achieved significantly higher cure rates and faster parasite clearance than AQ+SP, with DHA-PQP showing fewer adverse events.
safety_summary: Adverse events were significantly less frequent with DHA-PQP than with amodiaquine-containing combinations; DHA-PQP showed a good safety and tolerability profile.

title: Folic acid treatment of Zambian children with moderate to severe malaria anemia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing folic acid supplementation in children with malaria anemia, a malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: children with moderate to severe malaria anemia
primary_outcome: parasitemia and packed cell volume after treatment with folic acid or placebo
impact_summary: Folic acid supplementation increased parasitemia and worsened treatment outcomes in children treated with sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, but had no effect in those treated with atovaquone/proguanil, while leading to a small increase in packed cell volume compared to placebo.
effect_estimate: higher parasitemia in folic acid group vs placebo (SP arm)
safety_summary: Folic acid was associated with increased parasitemia in children treated with SP; no major adverse events reported beyond this interaction.

title: Lack of inhibition of the anti-malarial action of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine by folic acid supplementation when used for intermittent preventive treatment in Gambian primigravidae.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp with SP (malaria prevention in pregnant women) that reported outcome results (parasitemia prevalence and parasitologic cure).
population: primigravidae (pregnant women, first pregnancy)
primary_outcome: Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia on day 14 after treatment
impact_summary: Folic acid supplementation (500-1,500 microg/day) given alongside iron did not interfere with the anti-malarial efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine used for IPTp, as parasitemia prevalence and cure rates at day 14 were similar between groups.
effect_metric: risk difference in day 14 parasitemia prevalence
transmission_setting: low SP resistance area, malaria endemic
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; folic acid plus iron group had slightly higher mean hemoglobin concentration at day 14 than iron alone (difference 0.14 g/dL, 95% CI 0.01-0.27 g/dL).

title: Artemether-lumefantrine versus artesunate plus amodiaquine for treating uncomplicated childhood malaria in Nigeria: randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions in children with reported efficacy outcomes (ACPR, treatment failure rates).
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum infection
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) by day 14
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate plus amodiaquine both showed high and comparable cure rates and tolerability among under-five children in Calabar, Nigeria.
effect_metric: Odds ratio for ACPR (AL vs AAMQ)
transmission_setting: area with high levels of P. falciparum resistance to chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported in either treatment group.

title: Safety and efficacy of rectal compared with intramuscular quinine for the early treatment of moderately severe malaria in children: randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria treatment routes in children with moderately severe P. falciparum malaria.
population: children with moderately severe P falciparum malaria unable to take oral treatment
primary_outcome: Primary safety outcome: presence of blood in stools (and diarrhoea as secondary safety outcome); primary efficacy outcome: early treatment failure
impact_summary: Rectal quinine was associated with more blood in stools, diarrhoea, and early treatment failure than intramuscular quinine, but had a rare and transitory side-effect profile and was considered an acceptable option for early management of moderately severe malaria in children.
effect_metric: absolute difference in early treatment failure rate
safety_summary: Blood in stools and diarrhoea were more common with rectal quinine (5% vs 1% for both); anoscopy showed inflammatory lesions in 3% associated with bloody stool striations; rectal side effects were rare and transitory. Intramuscular quinine caused local pain (90%), inflammation (79%), and transient impaired mobility (15%).

title: Effect of the malaria vaccine Combination B on merozoite surface antigen 2 diversity.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
screening_reason: This is a published Phase 2b randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (Combination B) in humans that reports outcome results (MSP2 genetic diversity and parasite prevalence/morbidity).
population: study participants in a malaria-endemic area of Papua New Guinea
primary_outcome: Genetic diversity of MSP2 alleles (breakthrough genotypes) in vaccine versus placebo recipients
impact_summary: Vaccination with Combination B lowered prevalence of 3D7-type parasites but selected for FC27-type parasites, with no evidence that the vaccine altered the hypervariable MSP2 allele diversity itself.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area of Papua New Guinea

title: Effectiveness of mosquito nets treated with a tablet formulation of deltamethrin for malaria control in a hyperendemic tribal area of Sundargarh District, Orissa, India.
journal: Journal of the American Mosquito Control Association
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, prevalence, splenomegaly).
population: residents of tribal villages in a hyperendemic malaria area, including children aged 2-9 years
