primary_outcome: malaria incidence, prevalence, and splenomegaly
impact_summary: Malaria incidence was reduced by 64.3% in the village using deltamethrin-treated nets, compared to 45.2% in the village with untreated nets and 21.4% in the village without nets, with treated nets showing significantly greater reduction than untreated nets or no nets.
p_value: P < 0.05 (treated vs untreated); P < 0.005 (treated vs no net)
age_range: 2-9 years (subgroup for spleen/parasite rate); general population for incidence

title: Tolerability of amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, alone or in combination for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Rwandan adults.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported outcome results on tolerability and efficacy.
comparator: AQ alone and SP alone (active comparators)
population: adult patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Tolerability (adverse events) and efficacy of AQ+SP versus AQ or SP alone
impact_summary: AQ+SP was associated with significantly more adverse events, particularly pruritus and fatigue, than SP alone, making AQ-containing regimens poorly tolerated.
effect_metric: Risk Ratio for at least one adverse event
effect_estimate: approximately fourfold higher in AQ and AQ+SP groups vs SP
safety_summary: 40% of AQ group, 39% of AQ+SP group, and 21% of SP group reported at least one adverse event; pruritus and fatigue were more common with AQ-containing regimens; severe AEs (fatigue, nausea, dizziness, vomiting) occurred in 4 AQ, 10 AQ+SP, and 1 SP patient.

title: Mefloquine is highly efficacious against chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium vivax malaria and Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Papua, Indonesia.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine vs chloroquine) with reported outcome results (28-day cure rates).
population: Javanese adults and children living in a malaria-endemic transmigration area
primary_outcome: 28-day cumulative curative efficacy against P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria
impact_summary: Mefloquine achieved far higher cure rates than chloroquine against both P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria in Papua, Indonesia.
effect_estimate: Mefloquine 96% (P. falciparum), 99.6% (P. vivax) vs chloroquine 26% (P. falciparum), 82% (P. vivax)
follow_up: 28 days per treatment course, 1996-1999 overall surveillance
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area of Papua, Indonesia with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum and P. vivax
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: Complexity of Plasmodium falciparum infections and antimalarial drug efficacy at 7 sites in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drug efficacy (combination therapies) in humans with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates).
comparator: active comparator (comparison between 3 different combination antimalarial therapies)
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure/response to antimalarial combination therapy in relation to complexity of P. falciparum infection
impact_summary: Patients infected with 3 or more Plasmodium falciparum strains had almost 3 times the odds of antimalarial treatment failure compared with those infected with 1 or 2 strains.

title: Moderate effect of artemisinin-based combination therapy on transmission of Plasmodium falciparum.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results on malaria treatment (ACT) interventions with outcome measures (gametocytemia, transmission).
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) monotherapy vs SP plus amodiaquine vs SP plus artesunate vs artemether-lumefantrine
population: Kenyan children with P. falciparum infection
primary_outcome: Gametocyte prevalence and infectiousness to mosquitoes after treatment, measured by microscopy and Pfs25 QT-NASBA and membrane-feeding assays
impact_summary: ACT reduced the proportion of infected mosquitoes but did not significantly reduce the proportion of infectious children, indicating a moderate effect on malaria transmission due to common submicroscopic gametocytemia after treatment.

title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial of the impact of malaria prevention on the educational attainment of school children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria prevention (chloroquine chemoprevention) in humans with reported outcome results including malaria incidence, absenteeism, and educational attainment.
population: school children in grades 1-5
primary_outcome: educational attainment (language and mathematics examination scores)
impact_summary: Chloroquine chemoprophylaxis reduced malaria incidence and malaria-related absenteeism and led to significantly higher post-intervention language and mathematics scores compared with placebo.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Geographic differences in antimalarial drug efficacy in Uganda are explained by differences in endemicity and not by known molecular markers of drug resistance.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (CQ+SP and AQ+SP) in malaria patients with reported treatment failure outcomes across geographic sites.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: malaria patients treated with antimalarial therapy across 6 sites in Uganda
primary_outcome: Risk of antimalarial treatment failure (CQ+SP and AQ+SP) across sites, and prevalence of molecular markers of drug resistance
impact_summary: Geographic differences in antimalarial treatment failure risk in Uganda were explained by differences in transmission intensity (acquired immunity) rather than by known molecular markers of drug resistance.
effect_estimate: CQ+SP: 73% to 19%; AQ+SP: 38% to 2% across sites with increasing transmission intensity
transmission_setting: varying transmission intensity across 6 sites in Uganda

title: Predictors of the failure of treatment with pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine) with reported outcome results on treatment failure in children with P. falciparum malaria.
population: children with acute, symptomatic, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment failure by day 7 or 14 following pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine treatment
impact_summary: Age ≤1.5 years, presence of fever at presentation, and delayed parasite clearance >3 days were independent predictors of pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine treatment failure in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
effect_estimate: 2.9 (age ≤1.5 years); 3.3 (fever at presentation); 2.56 (delayed parasite clearance >3 days)

title: Effects of insecticide-treated bednets during early infancy in an African area of intense malaria transmission: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control) for malaria prevention in infants with reported outcome results (mortality, malaria incidence, anaemia).
comparator: delayed bednet protection (from age 6 months) versus bednet protection from birth
population: neonates followed through early infancy
primary_outcome: All-cause mortality in all study children and incidence of falciparum malaria in a representative subsample
impact_summary: Bednet protection from birth reduced falciparum malaria incidence and moderate-to-severe anaemia during infancy compared to delayed protection, but did not reduce overall mortality.
effect_estimate: RR 1.0 for mortality; RR 3.1 (early infancy) and RR 1.3 (late infancy) for malaria incidence
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no evidence of increased mortality or morbidity with early bednet use

title: (Sub)microscopic Plasmodium falciparum gametocytaemia in Kenyan children after treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine monotherapy or in combination with artesunate.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drug regimens (SP vs SP+AS) in Kenyan children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, reporting outcome results on gametocyte prevalence and density.
comparator: sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine monotherapy vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine plus artesunate
population: Kenyan children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte prevalence and density measured by QT-NASBA and microscopy over 28 days
impact_summary: Gametocyte carriage risk and density were considerably higher after treatment with SP alone compared with SP+artesunate, and gametocyte prevalence and density decreased over time in the SP+AS group but not in the SP-only group.
effect_metric: gametocyte prevalence by QT-NASBA vs microscopy
effect_estimate: 2.8-fold higher prevalence by QT-NASBA; 86% vs 22% at enrolment

title: Clinical-parasitological response and in-vitro sensitivity of Plasmodium vivax to chloroquine and quinine on the western border of Thailand.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing chloroquine vs quinine for P. vivax malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance); malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
comparator: active comparator (quinine vs chloroquine, both with primaquine)
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: clinical-parasitological response (cure rate) and in-vitro sensitivity (IC50) of P. vivax to chloroquine and quinine
impact_summary: Both chloroquine and quinine, each combined with primaquine, achieved nearly 100% cure rates within 28 days and were well tolerated for treating P. vivax malaria on the Thai-Myanmar border.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with no significant adverse effects reported.

title: Artesunate suppositories versus intramuscular artemether for treatment of severe malaria in children in Papua New Guinea.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two treatment formulations for severe malaria in children with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and clinical efficacy.
population: children with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time to 50% and 90% parasite clearance (PCT50 and PCT90) and time to per os status
impact_summary: Artesunate suppositories cleared parasites significantly faster than intramuscular artemether and were at least as effective overall.
safety_summary: One suppository-treated patient with multiple complications died within 2 h of admission; the remaining 78 patients recovered uneventfully.

title: A randomized, parallel study of the safety and efficacy of 45 mg primaquine versus 75 mg bulaquine as gametocytocidal agents in adults with blood schizonticide-responsive uncomplicated falciparum malaria [ISCRTN50134587].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two gametocytocidal agents for malaria treatment with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance.
comparator: active comparator (primaquine 45 mg vs bulaquine 75 mg)
population: hospitalized adults with blood schizonticide-responsive uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria and gametocytemia >55/microl
primary_outcome: Persistence of gametocytemia on day 8
impact_summary: Bulaquine cleared gametocytemia faster than primaquine, with fewer bulaquine recipients showing persistent gametocytes and viable gametocytes on day 8, suggesting it is a safe alternative gametocytocidal agent.
effect_metric: proportion with persistent gametocytemia on day 8
safety_summary: Bulaquine was found to be safe as a gametocytocidal agent, comparable to primaquine.

title: An open randomized clinical trial of Artekin vs artesunate-mefloquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based combination therapies) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, clearance times, safety).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate, fever clearance time, parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artekin (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) was as effective and well-tolerated as artesunate-mefloquine for treating acute uncomplicated multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria region, Southeast Asia
safety_summary: Artekin was well-tolerated with no significant differences in safety compared to artesunate-mefloquine.

title: Successful treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria with a six-dose regimen of artemether-lumefantrine versus quinine-doxycycline in the Western Amazon region of Brazil.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing artemether-lumefantrine to quinine-doxycycline for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported clinical outcome results (parasite clearance, efficacy, safety).
population: hospitalized patients with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time / percentage of infected patients by day 3
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine cleared parasitemia faster than quinine-doxycycline, with 0% of patients still infected by day 3 versus 48.8% in the quinine-doxycycline group.
transmission_setting: highly drug-resistant region of South America (Western Amazon)
safety_summary: Adverse events reported by 91.5% of participants, mostly mild and/or unrelated to treatment; two patients in the quinine-doxycycline group discontinued early due to ineffectiveness or adverse event.

title: Maternal vitamin A supplementation and immunity to malaria in pregnancy in Ghanaian primigravids.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vitamin A supplementation in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria immunity and placental infection; malaria is the primary focus.
population: primigravid pregnant women
primary_outcome: Levels of IgG antibodies binding to variant surface antigens (VSA) of P. falciparum placental and other isolates, and placental malarial infection status at delivery
impact_summary: Vitamin A supplementation was associated with significantly lower levels of antibodies to a placental CSA-adherent malaria isolate and a non-significant reduction in risk of active placental malaria infection compared to placebo.

title: A double-blind, randomized study of azithromycin compared to chloroquine for the treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria in India.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with randomized allocation to two treatment arms, malaria treatment as primary purpose, and outcome results reported (clinical cure, parasitologic success at Days 7 and 28).
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitologic cure at Day 7 and Day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine achieved significantly higher clinical and parasitologic cure rates and faster parasite clearance than azithromycin, though azithromycin was better tolerated.
p_value: P < 0.001 for parasite clearance time; P = 0.062 for adverse events
safety_summary: Drug-related adverse events occurred in 13% (13/98) of azithromycin recipients versus 24% (24/102) of chloroquine recipients (P = 0.062), indicating azithromycin was better tolerated.

title: Low-dose quinine for treatment of chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria in Sudanese pregnant women.
journal: Eastern Mediterranean health journal = La revue de sante de la Mediterranee orientale = al-Majallah al-sihhiyah li-sharq al-mutawassit
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (low-dose quinine) in humans with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety.
population: pregnant women with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time from admission to remission of fever and parasite clearance
impact_summary: Low-dose quinine (2 times/day) caused significantly fewer side effects such as vomiting and abdominal pain than standard-dose quinine (3 times/day), with no significant differences in fever remission time, parasite clearance, hypoglycaemia, preterm labour, or recrudescence.
effect_metric: proportion reporting vomiting and abdominal pain
p_value: significant for vomiting and abdominal pain (exact value not reported)
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, eastern Sudan
safety_summary: Low-dose group had significantly fewer reports of vomiting and abdominal pain; hypoglycaemia, preterm labour, and recrudescence were slightly but not significantly higher in the standard-dose group.

title: Effect of HIV-1 infection on antimalarial treatment outcomes in Uganda: a population-based study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial regimens in humans with reported outcome results (clinical treatment failure at 28 days), with malaria treatment as primary purpose.
comparator: active comparator (3 antimalarial regimens compared to each other)
population: patients aged 18 months or older with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, including adults and children
primary_outcome: Clinical treatment failure at 28 days after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: HIV-1 infection was associated with a more than 3-fold increased risk of clinical treatment failure in adults (mainly due to new infections rather than recrudescence), but no increased risk was found in HIV-1-infected children.

title: A randomized trial comparing the efficacy of four treatment regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Assam state, India.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (treatment success/parasitologic cure at 14 and 42 days) comparing malaria treatment regimens in humans.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs mefloquine vs mefloquine-artesunate)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical treatment success and parasitologic cure at day 14 and day 42
impact_summary: Chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine had high failure rates while mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate showed sustained responses of about 94% at 42 days, supporting mefloquine-artesunate as an effective alternative.
effect_metric: sustained parasitologic response rate at 42 days

title: Protective efficacy of lambda-cyhalothrin treated nets in Anopheles gambiae pyrethroid resistance areas of Côte d'Ivoire.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of lambda-cyhalothrin-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention that has reported outcome results (infection prevalence and disease protective efficacy).
population: children aged 0-59 months
primary_outcome: malaria infection prevalence and malaria disease incidence
impact_summary: Lambda-cyhalothrin treated nets reduced asymptomatic malaria infection prevalence by 12% and provided an estimated protective efficacy against malaria disease of 56% in an area of pyrethroid (kdr) resistance.
transmission_setting: Anopheles gambiae pyrethroid (kdr) resistance area, northern Côte d'Ivoire

title: Randomized, controlled, double-blind trial of daily oral azithromycin in adults for the prophylaxis of Plasmodium vivax malaria in Western Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of azithromycin for malaria prevention (chemoprevention) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia endpoints and protective efficacy); phase not stated but chemoprevention trials are exempt from phase restrictions.
population: adults
primary_outcome: prophylactic efficacy of azithromycin against malaria (endpoint parasitemia)
impact_summary: Daily oral azithromycin was safe, well-tolerated, and highly effective in preventing P. vivax malaria in adults.
safety_summary: Adverse events, compliance, and withdrawal rates were similar between azithromycin and placebo groups; azithromycin was safe and well-tolerated.

title: Amodiaquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and combination therapy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria: a randomized controlled trial from Burkina Faso.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes meeting all inclusion criteria.
comparator: active comparator (amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs combination)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, 6 months of age or older (53% under 5 years)
primary_outcome: 28-day treatment failure (based on WHO criteria)
impact_summary: AQ + SP combination therapy was the most efficacious regimen for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with lower treatment failure, recrudescence, and new infection rates than AQ or SP alone.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were seen.

title: [Evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy of amodiaquine versus chloroquine in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Abie, Côte-d'Ivoire].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results (clinical success/failure rates); not early-phase.
population: children under 15 years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (clinical success/failure rates) using WHO 14-day test
impact_summary: Amodiaquine achieved higher clinical success (95%) with fewer early and late clinical failures compared to chloroquine (79% success) in treating uncomplicated malaria.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; some patients had persistent asymptomatic parasitemia resistant in vitro to both drugs.

title: Parasitological rebound effect and emergence of pyrimethamine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum after single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprevention (IPTi with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in infants with reported parasitological outcome results.
population: infants who were aparasitemic at enrollment
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum infection rates and emergence of pyrimethamine resistance-associated mutations after single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine caused a parasitological rebound effect with selection of drug-resistant P. falciparum parasites shortly after drug clearance compared to placebo.
effect_metric: proportion of infants with drug resistance-associated mutations

title: Sublingual sugar administration as an alternative to intravenous dextrose administration to correct hypoglycemia among children in the tropics.
screening_reason: Randomized trial with reported outcome results (glucose kinetics, treatment failures) testing a malaria-relevant intervention (hypoglycemia management in children with severe malaria) in humans; phase designation not applicable to this clinical intervention study.
comparator: oral water, oral sugar, and dextrose infusion administrations
population: moderately hypoglycemic children
primary_outcome: Treatment failures, peak glucose concentrations, times to glucose concentration normalization, and kinetic profiles
impact_summary: Sublingual sugar administration was as effective as intravenous dextrose in correcting hypoglycemia, with no treatment failures compared to high failure rates with oral sugar or water administration.
effect_estimate: 0% in SG and IG vs 53% in OG and 81.8% in water group
safety_summary: No treatment failures observed in sublingual and intravenous groups; sublingual administration was well tolerated with children over 7 years requiring repeated doses to maintain normoglycemia.

title: Open randomized study of artesunate-amodiaquine vs. chloroquine-pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine vs. chloroquine-pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine) in children with reported outcome results including efficacy, safety, and gametocyte carriage.
population: children aged 12 years or younger with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Proportions of children with adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR), late parasitological failure, late clinical failure, early treatment failure, and parasitological cure rates on days 14-28
impact_summary: Artesunate plus amodiaquine was more effective than chloroquine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine, achieving 100% adequate clinical and parasitological response, faster parasite clearance, higher cure rates on days 21 and 28, and significantly reduced gametocyte carriage.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; no child was withdrawn because of drug intolerance.

title: Evaluation of long-lasting insecticidal nets after 2 years of household use.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized trial comparing long-lasting insecticidal nets for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on net durability and insecticidal efficacy.
comparator: conventional polyester bednets treated with deltamethrin
population: households in western Kenya
primary_outcome: Time to net failure (insecticidal activity by WHO cone bioassay mortality, first of two consecutive mortality rates <50%)
impact_summary: PermaNet 1.0 had a significantly lower risk of insecticidal failure than conventional nets over 2 years, while Insector had a significantly higher risk of failure; other net types did not differ significantly from conventional nets.
effect_estimate: PermaNet 1.0: HR 0.14; Insector: HR 2.57; Olyset: HR 1.29; Dawa: HR 0.58; cyclodextrin: HR 0.65
safety_summary: Households were monitored monthly for reported side effects in inhabitants; no significant adverse effects reported in abstract.

title: Impact of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis on falciparum malaria infection and disease.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing TS prophylaxis for malaria prevention in humans, with primary focus on malaria intervention.
population: children 5-15 years old
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria and SP efficacy for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: TS prophylaxis was highly effective in preventing falciparum malaria infection and disease and did not select for SP-resistant parasites.
safety_summary: No evidence of selection for antifolate resistance-conferring mutations in dihydrofolate reductase or dihydropteroate synthase during subclinical infections; no adverse events reported.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine among children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Zanzibar, Tanzania.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments for P. falciparum malaria in children; primary focus is malaria treatment efficacy.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, 6-59 months
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical response (ACR) and parasitological resistance to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine
impact_summary: Both sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine showed high overall adequate clinical response rates (>90%), with lower efficacy for SP at Kivunge, and overall treatment failure was 9.2% with SP and 5.5% with AQ.

title: Improving access to early treatment of malaria: a trial with primary school teachers as care providers.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting malaria treatment outcomes with school teachers as intervention providers; phase not early; malaria is primary focus.
population: schoolchildren with fever/presumptive malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of presumptive malaria cases correctly diagnosed and adequately treated
impact_summary: Pre-packaging of chloroquine by trained primary school teachers improved adequate treatment of presumptive malaria cases from 75% to 97% and ensured high patient compliance (96.6%).
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; pre-packaged chloroquine use associated with high compliance and no adverse events mentioned.

title: A randomized trial of artemether-lumefantrine versus mefloquine-artesunate for the treatment of uncomplicated multi-drug resistant Plasmodium falciparum on the western border of Thailand.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of two antimalarial drug combinations for treating uncomplicated malaria with reported 42-day PCR-adjusted cure rate outcomes in humans.
population: patients with slide-confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted cure rate at day 42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-mefloquine achieved high, equivalent PCR-adjusted cure rates for uncomplicated multi-drug resistant P. falciparum malaria, with no serious adverse events.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant P. falciparum area, Thai-Myanmar border
safety_summary: Both regimens were very well tolerated with no serious adverse events attributable to either combination.

title: Safety of the methylene blue plus chloroquine combination in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in young children of Burkina Faso [ISRCTN27290841].
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported safety and efficacy outcomes for a malaria treatment intervention in children; early-phase designation based on primary focus on safety evaluation with secondary efficacy assessment.
population: young children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: incidence of severe haemolysis or other serious adverse events (SAEs)
impact_summary: CQ-MB was safe, including in G6PD deficient children, with no significant difference in adverse events or haemoglobin compared to CQ alone, but efficacy was insufficient at the MB dose used, with treatment failure rates of 44.0% in the CQ-MB group versus 53.7% in the CQ group.
safety_summary: No differences in incidence of SAEs and other adverse events between CQ-MB and CQ groups; no cases of severe haemolysis; no significant difference in mean haemoglobin between groups, including in 24 children with G6PD deficiency.

title: Efficacy of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole compared with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus erythromycin for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children with integrated management of childhood illness dual classifications of malaria and pneumonia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatments; primary focus is malaria treatment efficacy in children.
population: children with IMCI dual classifications of malaria and pneumonia with P. falciparum parasitemia
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitologic response (ACPR) at day 14
impact_summary: TS and SP plus E were both efficacious treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in ACPR rates between groups.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; severely malnourished children were less likely to achieve ACPRs (relative risk = 3.34, P = 0.03)

title: [Blood levels of sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine, according to the malaria-treatment response, in two municipalities of Antioquia, Colombia].
journal: Revista panamericana de salud publica = Pan American journal of public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results on clinical response and drug levels.
design: experimental study, non-blinded, randomized to treatment group
comparator: none (single-arm drug level comparison between good clinical response and treatment failure groups)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Blood levels of sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine according to clinical-parasitological treatment response
impact_summary: Blood levels of sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine did not significantly differ between patients with good clinical response and those with treatment failure, indicating that drug levels do not explain the lack of response.
effect_metric: median blood level (sulfadoxine, micromol/L; pyrimethamine, nmol/L)
effect_estimate: Sulfadoxine: 136.6 (good response) vs 103.4 (failure); Pyrimethamine: 848.4 (good response) vs 786.1 (failure)

title: Artesunate versus quinine for treatment of severe falciparum malaria: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Open-label RCT of artesunate versus quinine for severe falciparum malaria treatment with reported mortality outcomes; malaria is the primary focus and intervention is a validated treatment.
population: patients admitted to hospital with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: death from severe malaria
impact_summary: Intravenous artesunate significantly reduced mortality compared with intravenous quinine in adults with severe falciparum malaria.
follow_up: until death or recovery during hospitalisation
safety_summary: Artesunate was well tolerated; quinine was associated with hypoglycaemia (relative risk 3.2, 95% CI 1.3-7.8; p=0.009).

title: An open, randomized trial of three-day treatment with artesunate combined with a standard dose of mefloquine divided over either two or three days, for acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate + mefloquine) with reported outcome results (cure rates, fever/parasite clearance times).
comparator: active comparator (2-day mefloquine regimen vs 3-day mefloquine regimen, both with artesunate)
population: adult patients with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure) with secondary endpoints of fever clearance time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Both the 3-day and 2-day mefloquine regimens combined with artesunate achieved high cure rates (100% and 99%, respectively) with similarly rapid fever and parasite clearance, and the 3-day regimen was effective and well tolerated.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; nausea or vomiting occurred in 3.8% of patients in both groups, transient dizziness occurred in 4% of group 1 and 9% of group 2 patients, with no significant differences in adverse effect incidence between groups.

title: Efficacy of artesunate plus chloroquine for uncomplicated malaria in children in Sao Tome and Principe: a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate + chloroquine vs chloroquine) in children with reported efficacy outcomes; phase III intervention trial.
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 14 parasitological failure rate
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus artesunate combination therapy significantly reduced parasitological and clinical treatment failure rates compared with chloroquine monotherapy, and was well tolerated.
effect_metric: odds ratio for day 14 parasitological failure
safety_summary: Combined treatment was well tolerated with no serious drug-related adverse events.

title: Short report: no evidence of cardiotoxicity of atovaquone-proguanil alone or in combination with artesunate.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (atovaquone-proguanil ± artesunate) with reported outcome results (QTc interval cardiotoxicity findings).
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Change in QTc interval on electrocardiogram from baseline to post-dose readings
impact_summary: There was no statistically significant change in QTc interval between baseline and subsequent readings in either treatment group, indicating no evidence of cardiotoxicity for atovaquone-proguanil alone or combined with artesunate.
safety_summary: No evidence of cardiotoxicity; no statistically significant QTc prolongation observed in either treatment group.

title: Efficacy of chloroquine + sulfadoxine--pyrimethamine, mefloquine + artesunate and artemether + lumefantrine combination therapies to treat Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, Bangladesh.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments (artemisinin-based and non-artemisinin combinations) for P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (three antimalarial combination regimens compared to each other)
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 42 PCR-corrected therapeutic efficacy (cure rate)
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was substantially less effective than mefloquine plus artesunate or artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) in curing P. falciparum malaria in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
transmission_setting: Chittagong Hill Tracts, Bangladesh, area with chloroquine and SP resistance
safety_summary: All three therapies were well tolerated; mild complaints during treatment appeared more frequent with mefloquine plus artesunate.

title: A randomized comparison of artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil versus quinine in treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria during pregnancy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil vs quinine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results including treatment failure, parasite clearance, and safety endpoints.
population: pregnant women (Karen ethnicity) in second or third trimester with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil (AAP) had a significantly lower treatment failure rate than 7-day supervised quinine, with better fever clearance, parasite clearance, and duration of anemia, and no adverse effects on birth outcomes or infant development.
safety_summary: No significant differences in birth weight, duration of gestation, or congenital abnormality rates in newborns; no adverse effects on growth and developmental parameters of infants monitored for 1 year; AAP was well tolerated.

title: Comparative efficacy of antimalarial drugs including ACTs in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria among children under 5 years in Ghana.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based and other antimalarials) in children with reported efficacy outcome results (PCR-corrected cure rates at day 28).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate on day 28
impact_summary: Artemisinin-based combinations (amodiaquine+artesunate and artemether+lumefantrine) had markedly higher cure rates than chloroquine and sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine, supporting their use in areas of high chloroquine failure like Ghana.
transmission_setting: high chloroquine failure area, sub-Saharan Africa
safety_summary: CHQ group showed no significant changes in haemoglobin levels during follow-up; SP group had highest prevalence of gametocytaemia; no other major safety issues reported.

title: Artemisinin versus nonartemisinin combination therapy for uncomplicated malaria: randomized clinical trials from four sites in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial combination therapies in humans with reported outcome results on parasitological failure and efficacy in uncomplicated malaria treatment.
comparator: chloroquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (CQ+SP) and amodiaquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (AQ+SP) as comparators to amodiaquine + artesunate (AQ+AS)
population: patients aged 6 months or older with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, majority under 5 years
primary_outcome: 28-day risk of parasitological failure (recrudescence), unadjusted and adjusted by genotyping to distinguish recrudescence from new infection
impact_summary: AQ+AS had the lowest risk of recrudescence but a higher risk of new infection than AQ+SP, and considering all recurrent infections AQ+SP was as good or better, especially at higher transmission sites.
p_value: p < 0.01 for AQ+SP or AQ+AS vs CQ+SP; p < 0.003 for risk differences of 15% and 16% at highest transmission sites
transmission_setting: four districts in Uganda with varying malaria transmission intensity, including highly endemic areas

title: A randomized, controlled study of a simple, once-daily regimen of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated, multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatment regimens with reported outcome results (cure rates at day 63); primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated, multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR genotyping-adjusted cure rate at day 63
impact_summary: A once-daily, 3-dose regimen of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP3) achieved a cure rate similar to the standard 4-dose regimen (DP4) and significantly higher than mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3), with good tolerability.
effect_metric: PCR genotyping-adjusted cure rate at day 63
p_value: P=.008 (DP4 vs MAS3); P=.03 (DP3 vs MAS3)
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria along the Thailand-Myanmar border
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated; 3 deaths occurred (1 in MAS3, 2 in DP3), considered unrelated to treatment; adverse event rates were comparable except diarrhea, more common in the DP4 group (P=.05 vs MAS3).

title: Reduction of the efficacy of antifolate antimalarial therapy by folic acid supplementation.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT comparing SP+iron with or without folic acid in malaria patients; reports outcome results (parasite clearance rates) on a malaria treatment intervention.
comparator: SP and iron without folic acid (placebo/no folic acid arm)
population: patients of all ages with anemia and uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria attending an outpatient clinic
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rates (parasitologic and clinical failure) measured by survival analysis
impact_summary: Folic acid supplementation significantly reduced the efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine antimalarial therapy in terms of parasitologic failure, though it did not affect clinical failure or improve anemia recovery.

title: A comparison of the efficacy of artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with that of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone, in the treatment of uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: RCT comparing artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results at 28-day follow-up.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure by day 28 (parasitological and clinical cure), fever- and parasite-clearance times
impact_summary: Artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved 100% cure by day 28 compared with 86.7% for sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone, with faster fever and parasite clearance and lower post-treatment gametocytaemia.
safety_summary: Adverse effects (nausea, itching, giddiness) occurred at similar frequencies in both arms (10.0% ASP vs 13.3% SP alone; P>0.05).

title: Quinine for the treatment of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in pregnant and non-pregnant Sudanese women.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with published outcome results testing quinine treatment for chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria in human participants.
population: pregnant and non-pregnant Sudanese women with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment response/parasite clearance
impact_summary: Quinine was effective for treating chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria in both pregnant and non-pregnant Sudanese women.

title: Efficacy of combination therapy with artesunate plus amodiaquine compared to monotherapy with chloroquine, amodiaquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum in Afghanistan.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-amodiaquine vs comparators) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; Phase III design using WHO procedures.
comparator: chloroquine monotherapy, amodiaquine monotherapy, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine monotherapy
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (cure rate) by day 42
impact_summary: Artesunate plus amodiaquine combination therapy substantially reduced treatment failure compared to amodiaquine monotherapy, but cure rates with AS/AQ remained inadequate and lower than with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, indicating AS/AQ is not a suitable ACT option for Afghanistan.
effect_metric: odds ratio for treatment failure by day 42 (AS/AQ vs AQ monotherapy)
transmission_setting: high chloroquine and emerging sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance region, South/Central Asia

title: A randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial on sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone or combined with artesunate or amodiaquine in uncomplicated malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions with reported outcome results (ACPR rates, parasite clearance, adverse events) in humans.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) alone vs SP+amodiaquine vs SP+artesunate (placebo-controlled)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: SP alone had a substantially higher treatment failure rate than SP combined with amodiaquine or artesunate, both of which achieved similarly high cure rates around 94%.
p_value: <0.0001 for both SP+AQ and SP+AS vs SP
safety_summary: No severe adverse events attributable to study medication were observed.

title: A sensitivity analysis of a randomized controlled trial of zinc in treatment of falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: This is a published sensitivity analysis of a completed RCT testing zinc as adjuvant therapy for falciparum malaria in children, with reported outcome results on time to parasite clearance.
population: children with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: time to total parasite clearance
impact_summary: After correcting for identified sources of bias, the effect estimate comparing placebo to zinc changed only slightly but the confidence interval widened by 22%, indicating that conventional analysis underestimated total error.

title: Artesunate-clindamycin versus quinine-clindamycin in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate-clindamycin vs quinine-clindamycin) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, adverse events, parasite clearance).
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 in the per-protocol population
impact_summary: Artesunate-clindamycin had comparable cure rates to quinine-clindamycin (87% vs 94%) and led to faster clearance of fever and parasites.
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission region of sub-Saharan Africa
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported; tolerability was good and similar in both groups.

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus chloroquine or amodiaquine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria: a randomized, multisite trial to guide national policy in Uganda.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes over 28 days; primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention.
comparator: chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
population: patients aged 6 months or greater with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Genotyping-adjusted risk of clinical treatment failure at 28 days
impact_summary: Amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was significantly more efficacious than chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, though treatment failure with the latter was unacceptably high.
age_range: 6 months and older (subgroup analysis in children under 5 years)
safety_summary: Serious adverse events were uncommon with both regimens.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Peru.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes over 28-day follow-up.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: recurrence of parasitemia and clinical symptoms over 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Combination therapy with artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resulted in faster resolution of fever and parasitemia, lower gametocytemia, and fewer recurrences of parasitemia than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone, though with more mild adverse effects.
transmission_setting: north Pacific coastal region of Peru, endemic for P. falciparum malaria
safety_summary: No severe adverse drug reactions observed; self-limited rash and pruritus, and exacerbation of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain were significantly more common with SP-AS.

title: Antimalarial efficacy of chloroquine, amodiaquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and the combinations of amodiaquine + artesunate and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine + artesunate in Huambo and Bie provinces, central Angola.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatments (chloroquine, amodiaquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and artemisinin combinations) in children with malaria that reports PCR-corrected efficacy outcomes at day 28.
comparator: chloroquine, amodiaquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as monotherapies compared to amodiaquine+artesunate and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine+artesunate combinations
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected treatment failure proportion at day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed high failure rates, amodiaquine moderate efficacy, while artemisinin-based combinations (amodiaquine+artesunate and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine+artesunate) had very low failure rates and were highly efficacious.
effect_estimate: CQ 83.5%; SP Caala 25.3%, SP Kuito 38.8%; AQ Caala 17.3%, AQ Kuito 21.6%; AQ+AS 1.2%; SP+AS 1.2%
effect_ci: CQ 74.1-90.5; SP Caala 16.7-35.8; SP Kuito 28.4-50.0; AQ Caala 10.0-27.2; AQ Kuito 14.3-30.6; AQ+AS and SP+AS 0.0-6.4

title: Malaria in the Nuba Mountains of Sudan: baseline genotypic resistance and efficacy of the artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and artesunate plus amodiaquine combinations.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results for artemisinin-based combination treatments (AS+SP and AS+AQ) for P. falciparum malaria in humans.
population: children under 5 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at 28 days
impact_summary: Both artesunate combinations achieved high PCR-corrected cure rates at 28 days, but high prevalence of Pfcrt K76T mutation suggests chloroquine would work poorly and AS+AQ is likely a better long-term option than AS+SP.

title: Intermittent preventive antimalarial treatment for Tanzanian infants: follow-up to age 2 years of a randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of antimalarial chemoprevention (IPTi) in infants with reported outcome results (clinical malaria rates) demonstrating efficacy.
design: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with extended follow-up
population: infants followed up to age 2 years
primary_outcome: rate of clinical malaria (events per person-year at risk)
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in infancy produced a sustained 36% reduction in clinical malaria risk up to age 2 years compared to placebo, without evidence of a rebound effect.

title: Amodiaquine alone, amodiaquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine+artesunate, and artemether-lumefantrine for outpatient treatment of malaria in Tanzanian children: a four-arm randomised effectiveness trial.
screening_reason: Four-arm RCT with reported efficacy outcomes (parasitological failure rates) for malaria treatment in children; pragmatic effectiveness trial, not early-phase.
comparator: amodiaquine monotherapy (active comparator) versus combination therapies
population: children aged 4-59 months with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure by day 14, assessed blind to treatment allocation
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine had the lowest parasitological failure and recrudescence rates by day 28, followed by amodiaquine+artesunate, amodiaquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and amodiaquine alone, which had the highest failure rate and was stopped early due to poor efficacy.
effect_metric: day 28 parasitological failure rate (PCR-corrected recrudescence rate)
effect_estimate: Amodiaquine 76% (48.4% corrected), amodiaquine+SP 61% (34.5% corrected), amodiaquine+artesunate 40% (11.2% corrected), artemether-lumefantrine 21% (2.8% corrected)
transmission_setting: High malaria transmission area with high prevalence of resistance to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and chloroquine (Muheza, Tanzania)
safety_summary: The amodiaquine monotherapy arm was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board due to high failure rates; no other specific safety/adverse event details reported.

title: Supervised versus unsupervised intake of six-dose artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mbarara, Uganda: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine treatment for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (28-day parasitological cure rates).
comparator: unsupervised (outpatient) intake versus supervised (inpatient, observed) intake
population: patients of all ages (weight >10 kg) with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28 day, PCR-adjusted, parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine achieved similarly high cure rates whether administered under supervision with food or under routine, unsupervised outpatient conditions.
safety_summary: 15 non-severe, drug-related adverse events were recorded, all of which resolved.

title: Reduction of malaria transmission to Anopheles mosquitoes with a six-dose regimen of co-artemether.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine combination) in children with falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results on gametocyte carriage and mosquito infectiousness.
comparator: chloroquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (three doses and one dose respectively)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Carriage rates of Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes and trophozoites measured 7, 14, and 28 days after treatment; infectiousness to Anopheles mosquitoes via membrane-feeding
impact_summary: Six-dose co-artemether was significantly more effective than chloroquine plus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine at preventing post-treatment gametocyte carriage, reducing gametocyte density and duration, and reducing infectiousness to mosquitoes.
effect_metric: proportion of children carrying gametocytes within 4 weeks post-treatment

title: Efficacies of mefloquine alone and of artesunate followed by mefloquine, for the treatment of uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing malaria treatment interventions (mefloquine monotherapy vs. artesunate-mefloquine combination) with reported outcome results on efficacy and adverse effects.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological clearance) and adverse effects at 28 days follow-up
impact_summary: Mefloquine alone and artesunate followed by mefloquine were equally effective at clearing parasitaemia, but the combination cleared gametocytaemia better and caused fewer adverse effects.
safety_summary: Mefloquine alone caused more nausea, vomiting and dizziness (25.0% vs 2.6%, P=0.005) and more gametocytaemia (12.5% vs 0%, P=0.02) than the combination; almost 10-fold higher rate of adverse effects than the combination therapy.

title: Curdlan sulphate in human severe/cerebral Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes testing curdlan sulphate as adjunct treatment for severe/cerebral malaria in humans.
population: patients with severe and severe/cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: efficacy and safety of curdlan sulphate as adjunct medication (e.g. fever clearance time, mortality)
impact_summary: Curdlan sulphate as adjunct therapy appeared to reduce disease severity, shortening fever clearance time, though no difference in mortality was observed due to small patient numbers.
safety_summary: The only adverse event was an increase in activated partial thromboplastin time, which could be monitored easily; no other differences in laboratory parameters between arms.

title: Comparison of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with and without chloroquine for uncomplicated malaria in Nigeria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in humans.
population: outpatients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (fever and parasitemia > 2,000/microL)
primary_outcome: Parasitologic and clinical response (parasite clearance and symptom resolution) by day 14
impact_summary: Combined sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus chloroquine was superior to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Nigerian patients, with higher rates of parasite clearance and symptom resolution and lower resistance rates.
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; study focused on efficacy outcomes

title: A randomized comparison of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and combination of sulphadoxine pyrimethamine with chloroquine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Eastern Sudan.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans.
comparator: sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine plus chloroquine
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment outcome (parasitological/clinical cure) of uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: The trial compared sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone versus sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine combined with chloroquine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Eastern Sudan.

title: Efficacy of two artemisinin combination therapies for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children under 5 years, Malakal, Upper Nile, Sudan.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin combination therapies for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy outcomes over 42 days.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy of antimalarial therapy in curing malaria infection and preventing recrudescence over 42 days
impact_summary: Both AS+SP and AS+AQ were efficacious in treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with AS+SP appearing slightly more effective than AS+AQ, leading to recommendation of AS+SP for this area of Sudan.
effect_metric: relative risk of returning with malaria within 42 days

title: A randomized comparative study of chloroquine, amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Ghana.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported outcome results (14-day efficacy); phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 14-day adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Chloroquine had significantly lower efficacy than amodiaquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, suggesting it should be replaced as first-line treatment in Ghana, preferably with amodiaquine-based combination therapy.
effect_metric: 14-day adequate clinical and parasitological response rate

title: Randomized trial of volume expansion with albumin or saline in children with severe malaria: preliminary evidence of albumin benefit.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention (fluid resuscitation) in humans with reported outcome results (mortality and other clinical outcomes); not early-phase.
comparator: normal saline (with a maintenance-only control group)
population: children with severe falciparum malaria and metabolic acidosis
primary_outcome: percentage reduction in base deficit at 8 hours
impact_summary: Mortality was significantly lower in children who received albumin (3.6%) compared to those who received saline (18%), though there was no significant difference in resolution of acidosis between groups.
effect_metric: relative risk of death (saline vs albumin)
safety_summary: No significant difference in resolution of acidosis; albumin group had lower mortality than saline group; safety of albumin vs saline vs fluid restriction not fully determined by study design.

title: Rectal artemether versus intravenous quinine for the treatment of cerebral malaria in children in Uganda: randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments (artemether vs quinine) in children with cerebral malaria, with outcome results reported.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Time to clearance of parasites and fever; time to regaining consciousness, starting oral intake, and sitting unaided; and adverse effects
impact_summary: Rectal artemether showed similar parasitological and clinical outcomes to intravenous quinine for cerebral malaria in children, with lower mortality in the artemether group though the difference in mortality was not statistically significant.
effect_metric: relative risk of mortality (quinine vs artemether)
safety_summary: No serious immediate adverse effects occurred; mortality was 10/52 in the quinine group versus 6/51 in the artemether group.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of artesunate in Plasmodium vivax malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate (artemisinin derivative) for treatment of P. vivax malaria in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance, fever clearance, cure rates).
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria aged 12-56 years admitted to Bangkok Hospital for Tropical Diseases
primary_outcome: Parasitological and clinical efficacy of artesunate (fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and 14-day cure rate)
impact_summary: Artesunate followed by primaquine rapidly resolved fever and parasitemia in vivax malaria patients, achieving a 100% 14-day cure rate, though two relapses occurred by day 21-25.
safety_summary: No adverse events reported; two cases of parasitemia reappearance considered true relapse rather than recrudescence or treatment failure.

title: Evidence basis for antimalarial policy change in Sierra Leone: five in vivo efficacy studies of chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Five-site randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy outcomes comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Sierra Leone.
design: multi-site, open-label, non-comparator arms, in vivo efficacy studies (WHO standard methodology)
comparator: active comparator (three drugs compared against each other: CQ, SP, AQ)
population: children 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic (treatment) failure proportions at day 28 following treatment with chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine or amodiaquine, with PCR genotyping to distinguish recrudescence from re-infection
impact_summary: Chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine showed very high treatment failure rates across sites, while amodiaquine had more moderate failure rates and faster fever/parasite clearance, supporting a policy shift to artesunate plus amodiaquine.
safety_summary: No specific safety outcomes reported; artemether-lumefantrine was not chosen partly due to absence of safety data in pregnancy

title: Efficacy and effectiveness of the combination of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and a 3-day course of artesunate for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in a refugee settlement in Zambia.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP/artesunate combination) in humans with reported outcome results (efficacy and effectiveness at 28 days); not early-phase.
population: children aged up to 5 years with confirmed uncomplicated falciparum malaria in a refugee settlement
primary_outcome: Therapeutic response (adequate clinical and parasitological response) at day 28, PCR-adjusted for recrudescence vs re-infection
impact_summary: Supervised treatment with SP plus 3-day artesunate achieved significantly higher efficacy (83.5%) than unsupervised treatment (63.4%), indicating poor adherence reduces effectiveness.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted cure rate (efficacy vs effectiveness) at day 28

title: Intrarectal quinine for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
screening_reason: This is a published systematic review and meta-analysis of 8 randomized controlled trials comparing intrarectal quinine with other routes for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria, with reported outcome results on efficacy and adverse effects.
design: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized and quasi-randomized controlled trials
population: children with uncomplicated and severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Death, parasite clearance by 48 hours and 7 days, parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, coma recovery time, duration of hospitalization, and time to drinking
impact_summary: No statistically significant difference was found between intrarectal and intravenous or intramuscular quinine for efficacy outcomes, though pain may be reduced with the intrarectal route.
safety_summary: Intrarectal quinine appeared less painful than intramuscular administration in one large trial; no other significant differences in adverse events reported.

title: Mefloquine versus quinine plus sulphalene-pyrimethamine (metakelfin) for treatment of uncomplicated imported falciparum malaria acquired in Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: patients with imported uncomplicated falciparum malaria acquired in Africa, mainly immigrants and visiting relatives and friends from western African countries
primary_outcome: Efficacy (cure rate), tolerability, and length of hospital stay
impact_summary: Mefloquine and quinine plus sulphalene-pyrimethamine had similar cure rates, but mefloquine was associated with shorter fever clearance time and shorter hospital stay, though with a higher rate of CNS side effects.
p_value: 0.05 for fever clearance time; 0.007 for hospital stay; <0.001 for CNS disturbances
follow_up: extended follow-up completed by 72.2% of subjects (duration not specified)
transmission_setting: imported malaria acquired in Africa, treated in non-endemic Italy
safety_summary: Overall side effect rates were similar between groups, but the mefloquine group had a significantly higher rate of central nervous system disturbances (29.0% vs 9.6%, P<0.001).

title: Control of vectors and incidence of malaria in an irrigated settlement scheme in Sri Lanka by using the insect growth regulator pyriproxyfen.
journal: Journal of the American Mosquito Control Association
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector control (larvicide pyriproxyfen) for malaria with reported outcome results on malaria incidence; phase not early-phase.
comparator: untreated control villages (with residual house spraying only)
population: residents of villages in an irrigated settlement scheme in the dry zone of Sri Lanka
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria in treatment versus control villages
impact_summary: Larviciding with pyriproxyfen reduced adult malaria vector populations by 72-78% and reduced malaria incidence by about 70% in treated villages compared to controls.
transmission_setting: dry zone, seasonal breeding in riverbed pools and irrigation ditches

title: Pre-transfusion management of children with severe malarial anaemia: a randomised controlled trial of intravascular volume expansion.
screening_reason: Published RCT of a malaria treatment intervention (pre-transfusion management for severe malarial anaemia) with reported outcome results; phase not early-phase.
population: children with severe falciparum anaemia (haemoglobin <5 g/dl) and respiratory distress
primary_outcome: mean percentage reduction in base excess between admission and 8 h
impact_summary: Pre-transfusion volume expansion with albumin or saline was safe and did not cause pulmonary oedema, but did not significantly improve base excess reduction compared to control, although fewer children in the saline group required emergency interventions.
effect_metric: mean percentage reduction in base excess
safety_summary: Pre-transfusion management with albumin or saline was apparently safe, with no development of pulmonary oedema or other adverse events.

title: Efficacy and safety of artemether in the treatment of severe end complicated malaria in mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether versus quinine for severe malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (efficacy, safety, mortality).
population: children with severe and complicated malaria, hospitalised in pediatric service
primary_outcome: Efficacy and safety measures including parasitic clearance, thermal clearance, delay of exit of coma, tolerance, and mortality
impact_summary: Artemether was as efficacious and safe as quinine for the treatment of severe and complicated malaria in children.
safety_summary: No statistical difference in tolerance or mortality between artemether and quinine groups.

title: Malaria Vaccine Trial: Modest Protection, Good Progress.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting malaria vaccine outcome results with a primary focus on a malaria prevention intervention in humans.
impact_summary: The malaria vaccine trial showed modest protection against malaria along with progress in vaccine development.

title: A randomized open label clinical trial to compare the efficacy and safety of intravenous quinine followed by oral malarone vs. intravenous quinine followed by oral quinine in the treatment of severe malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (severe P. falciparum) with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety; not early-phase.
population: patients with severe P. falciparum malaria admitted to hospital
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, efficacy, and adverse events profile
impact_summary: Truncated therapy with intravenous quinine followed by oral Malarone was safer and as effective as intravenous quinine followed by oral quinine in treating severe malaria, with lower recrudescence rate in the Malarone arm.
safety_summary: Adverse reaction frequency was higher in the quinine group (31.6%) than in the Malarone group (25.7%); 5 deaths occurred (1.4%), 3 in the quinine arm.

title: Comparison of intermittent preventive treatment with chemoprophylaxis for the prevention of malaria during pregnancy in Mali.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing IPT/SP and IPT/CQ chemoprevention strategies for malaria in pregnancy, a core malaria prevention intervention in humans.
comparator: weekly chloroquine chemoprophylaxis and 2-dose IPT with chloroquine
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Third-trimester anemia, placental parasitemia, and low birth weight (<2500 g)
impact_summary: IPT with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was more efficacious than weekly chloroquine chemoprophylaxis in reducing third-trimester anemia, placental parasitemia, and low birth weight during pregnancy in Mali.
safety_summary: No significant differences in stillbirths, spontaneous abortions, or neonatal deaths among the 3 groups.

title: Comparison of the parasitologic efficacy of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Bungoma District of western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported parasitologic efficacy outcomes.
population: symptomatic children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitologic response to treatment (sensitive vs RI/RII/RIII resistance) at day 14
impact_summary: Amodiaquine achieved a significantly higher rate of parasitologic sensitivity (89.2%) than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (62.7%), with resistance rates consistently higher in SP-treated patients.

title: Endogenous opioids, mu-opiate receptors and chloroquine-induced pruritus: a double-blind comparison of naltrexone and promethazine in patients with malaria fever who have an established history of generalized chloroquine-induced itching.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (pruritus severity) in malaria-fever patients; primary purpose is malaria treatment (chloroquine side-effect management in malaria); not early-phase.
population: patients with parasitologically proven malaria fever and an established history of severe chloroquine-induced generalized pruritus
primary_outcome: Pruritus intensity (self-assessed itching severity score) over time, quantified as area under the pruritus-intensity time curve (AUCP0-72h) after chloroquine dosing
impact_summary: Naltrexone reduced chloroquine-induced pruritus to a similar extent as promethazine, with no statistically significant difference in antipruritic effect between the two treatments, though the relationship between parasite density and pruritus differed significantly between groups.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported; both treatments were subjectively tolerated, with reduction in itching severity compared to prior historical experience.

title: Malaria vaccine trial shows promising results.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria vaccine intervention in humans.

title: Combination treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Kampala, Uganda: randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment interventions with reported 28-day clinical outcome results; phase not explicitly stated but treatment efficacy comparison indicates Phase 3.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine+artesunate)
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day clinical treatment failure risk (adjusted and unadjusted by genotyping) and incidence of serious adverse events
impact_summary: Chloroquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine had unacceptably high treatment failure risk compared with amodiaquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine or amodiaquine+artesunate, which were significantly more efficacious and similarly effective to each other.
effect_metric: risk difference in 28-day clinical treatment failure
p_value: p<0.0001 for both comparisons; p=0.854 for retreatment comparison between amodiaquine+SP and amodiaquine+artesunate
safety_summary: Serious adverse events were uncommon across all treatment regimens.

title: Comparison of chloroquine, sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate for the treatment of falciparum malaria in Kachin State, North Myanmar.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment interventions (chloroquine, sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, mefloquine, mefloquine-artesunate) in patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with primary endpoint of treatment failure rates.
comparator: chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, mefloquine alone vs mefloquine-artesunate combination
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, stratified into three age-groups
