primary_outcome: Early and day 42 treatment failure rates
impact_summary: Chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine were highly ineffective against falciparum malaria in northern Myanmar, whereas mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate were much more effective though still associated with substantial day 42 failure rates.
p_value: P > 0.2 (ETF comparison between M and MA)
age_range: children and adults (stratified into three age-groups)
safety_summary: Four children (two CQ, two SP) developed symptoms of cerebral malaria within 3 days after treatment; no other adverse events reported.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-mefloquine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Luang Namtha Province, Lao People's Democratic Republic.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-mefloquine) with reported outcome results (42-day cure rates).
place: Luang Namtha Province, Lao People's Democratic Republic
population: patients of all age groups with acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day cure rate (adequate clinical and parasitological response)
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-mefloquine showed excellent efficacy and tolerability, with high cure rates and no significant difference in initial therapeutic response.
transmission_setting: low transmission, forested/border area of Northern Laos
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with no significant safety concerns reported.

title: A randomised, double-blind, controlled vaccine efficacy trial of DNA/MVA ME-TRAP against malaria infection in Gambian adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (DNA/MVA ME-TRAP) with reported efficacy outcome results in human participants.
population: adult men aged 15-45 years, semi-immune to malaria
primary_outcome: time to first infection with asexual P. falciparum
impact_summary: The DNA/MVA ME-TRAP prime-boost vaccine was safe and highly immunogenic but did not significantly reduce the incidence of natural P. falciparum infection compared to rabies vaccine control in semi-immune Gambian adults.
safety_summary: DNA ME-TRAP and MVA ME-TRAP vaccines were safe and well-tolerated

title: Randomised trial of artemether versus artemether and mefloquine for the treatment of chloroquine/sufadoxine-pyrimethamine-resistant falciparum malaria during pregnancy.
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether versus artemether+mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety.
population: pregnant women with chloroquine/sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine-resistant falciparum malaria in second and third trimesters
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times and cure rate
impact_summary: Both artemether alone and artemether followed by mefloquine were effective and well tolerated, with similar clearance times and cure rates and no adverse effects on newborns.
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated; all newborn babies were normal at birth with normal physical and neurodevelopmental assessments during follow-up.

title: Efficacies of chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and quinine in the treatment of uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug efficacies for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates and parasitological outcomes).
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs quinine)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment response (adequate clinical response vs early/late treatment failure) at 28 days
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was fully effective, quinine was mostly effective (90.6% adequate response), while chloroquine had a high failure rate (only 23.1% adequate response), indicating worsening chloroquine resistance in eastern Sudan.

title: Clinical and parasitological response of Plasmodium falciparum to chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in rural Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in humans with reported clinical and parasitological outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine vs combined chloroquine+sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine)
population: infants and young children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, median age 15 months
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological response classified as adequate clinical response, early treatment failure, or late clinical failure
impact_summary: Combined chloroquine plus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine treatment achieved the highest cure rate and fastest clinical and parasitological response compared to either drug alone.
age_range: infants and young children (median age 15 months)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; post-therapeutic increase in haematocrit observed in patients with adequate clinical response, particularly those clearing parasitaemia.

title: Randomized, controlled dose-optimization studies of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates); primary intervention is antimalarial therapy; not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine plus artesunate; higher-dose DP+)
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day-28 (hospital study) and PCR-genotyping-adjusted day-63 (community study) cure rates
impact_summary: The standard dose of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was highly effective, safe, and well tolerated for treating multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, with efficacy not improved by adding more dihydroartemisinin.
effect_estimate: 98.3% (DP) vs 100% (MAS3/DP+) at day 28; 96.1% (DP) vs 98.3% (DP+) vs 94.9% (MAS3) at day 63
safety_summary: Adverse events were few, with an excess of mild abdominal pain in the DP group.

title: Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia in children. Risk factors, treatment outcomes, and gametocytaemia following treatment.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing multiple antimalarial drug regimens for malaria treatment in children; primary focus is malaria intervention (treatment outcomes and drug efficacy).
comparator: active comparator (multiple antimalarial drug regimens compared to each other)
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Risk factors for hyperparasitaemia at enrolment and treatment outcomes (cure rate, resistance response) and gametocyte carriage following treatment
impact_summary: Age ≤5 years and high core temperature (≥39.5°C) were independent risk factors for hyperparasitaemia at enrolment, cure rate on day 14 was significantly lower with chloroquine than other treatments, and severe resistance occurred more often in hyperparasitaemic children, while gametocyte carriage was not significantly different between hyperparasitaemic and non-hyperparasitaemic children.
effect_estimate: significantly lower in chloroquine group compared to other treatment groups
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on treatment outcomes and resistance patterns rather than adverse events

title: Efficacy of the RTS,S/AS02A vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum infection and disease in young African children: randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported efficacy outcomes in young African children; Phase IIb is not early-phase.
population: young African children aged 1-4 years
primary_outcome: Time to first clinical episode of P falciparum malaria (axillary temperature >=37.5°C and P falciparum asexual parasitaemia >2500 per microL) over a 6-month surveillance period
impact_summary: The RTS,S/AS02A vaccine significantly reduced clinical malaria episodes, infection prevalence, and severe malaria in young African children.
effect_metric: vaccine efficacy for first clinical episode
safety_summary: The RTS,S/AS02A vaccine was safe, well tolerated, and immunogenic.

title: Randomized comparison of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus artesunate plus mefloquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in the Lao People's Democratic Republic.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (42-day cure rates) comparing three antimalarial treatment regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans.
comparator: chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (standard care) vs artesunate plus mefloquine vs artemether-lumefantrine
population: patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day cure rate (intention-to-treat, PCR-adjusted for reinfection)
impact_summary: Artesunate plus mefloquine and artemether-lumefantrine achieved high 42-day cure rates (100% and 97%) and faster parasite clearance than chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (93% cure rate), which showed higher treatment failure.
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond treatment failure rates; no major adverse events reported in abstract.

title: Randomized trial of 3-dose regimens of tafenoquine (WR238605) versus low-dose primaquine for preventing Plasmodium vivax malaria relapse.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing tafenoquine regimens versus primaquine for preventing P. vivax malaria relapse with reported outcome results (relapse rates).
comparator: low-dose primaquine and no further treatment (chloroquine alone)
population: patients with P. vivax infection
primary_outcome: Relapse of P. vivax malaria within follow-up period
impact_summary: Tafenoquine, including doses as low as a single 600-mg dose, was significantly more effective than low-dose primaquine at preventing P. vivax relapse after chloroquine treatment.

title: Is amodiaquine failing in Rwanda? Efficacy of amodiaquine alone and combined with artesunate in children with uncomplicated malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatment regimens in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with reported efficacy outcomes at day 28.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment failure at day 28
impact_summary: Combining amodiaquine with artesunate significantly reduced clinical and total treatment failure compared to amodiaquine alone, though rising amodiaquine resistance raises concerns for its use as first-line therapy in Rwanda.
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated with no serious adverse events recorded.

title: Impact of a double dose of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine to reduce prevalence of pregnancy malaria in southern Mozambique.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine chemoprevention (IPTp) for pregnancy malaria with reported outcome results on parasitaemia, birthweight, and gestational duration.
population: adolescent nulliparous and primiparous pregnant women attending antenatal clinic
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria parasitaemia (peripheral and placental) at delivery
impact_summary: Two doses of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine significantly reduced the prevalence of peripheral and placental malaria parasitaemia and improved birthweight compared to placebo among adolescent pregnant women in Mozambique.
follow_up: from enrollment through delivery and 7 days postpartum
age_range: adolescent, nulliparous and primiparous pregnant women
safety_summary: Minor adverse events reported: two cases of urticaria and one case of nausea in the placebo group, one case of vomiting in the SP group; no serious SP-related side effects observed in newborns.

title: Efficacy of monthly tafenoquine for prophylaxis of Plasmodium vivax and multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (protective efficacy against P. vivax and P. falciparum) testing a malaria chemoprevention intervention in humans; not early-phase.
population: Thai soldiers
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria infections during prophylaxis
impact_summary: Monthly tafenoquine was highly effective and safe for preventing P. vivax and multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in Thai soldiers.
safety_summary: Monthly tafenoquine was safe and well tolerated.

title: Efficacy of chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kajo Keji county, Sudan.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasitological failure rates at day 28) testing antimalarial drug treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in humans.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure rate at day 28 (PCR-corrected)
impact_summary: Amodiaquine had the lowest failure rate (25.2%), while chloroquine (93.9%) and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (69.9%) showed very high failure rates, indicating none were suitable as monotherapy.

title: Intermittent preventive sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment of primigravidae reduces levels of plasma immunoglobulin G, which protects against pregnancy-associated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of IPTp (intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with malaria outcome results reported.
population: primigravidae (pregnant women, first pregnancy)
primary_outcome: Levels of VSA(PAM)-specific immunoglobulin G (IgG)
impact_summary: Kenyan primigravidae receiving sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine IPTp had significantly lower levels of VSA(PAM)-specific IgG, which mediates protection against pregnancy-associated malaria, than women receiving placebo, with levels declining further with more IPTp doses.
effect_estimate: lower in SP-IPTp group vs placebo, dose-dependent decrease

title: Artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated malaria in Kenyan children: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans; not early-phase.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure by days 14 and 28 (PCR-corrected for new infections)
impact_summary: Adding 3 days of artesunate to SP significantly reduced treatment failure rates compared with SP alone, while 1 day of artesunate reduced failure only by day 14, and overall SP resistance remained high enough to question the combination's suitability for widespread use in Kenya.
effect_metric: risk difference in treatment failure rate (day 28)
safety_summary: The artesunate and SP combination was well tolerated with no serious drug-related adverse events.

title: Increases in correct administration of chloroquine in the home and referral of sick children to health facilities through a community-based intervention in Bougouni District, Mali.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment (chloroquine) administration and referral intervention in Mali.
comparator: standard care (comparison group without enhanced intervention)
population: sick children in the community and their carers
primary_outcome: correct administration of chloroquine in the home and referral of sick children to health facilities
impact_summary: The intervention significantly increased knowledge of danger signs, quality of counselling, correct home administration of chloroquine, and referral of sick children to community health centres compared to the comparison group.
effect_metric: odds ratio for referral to CHC
transmission_setting: southern Mali, community-based malaria endemic setting
age_range: children (sick children, exact age range not specified)

title: Artesunate with mefloquine at various intervals for non-severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes for a malaria treatment intervention (artesunate plus mefloquine) in humans; Phase III or equivalent.
comparator: active comparator (different timing intervals of artesunate and mefloquine administration, with placebo used to blind timing)
population: patients with non-severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite recurrence/recrudescence and efficacy of artesunate-mefloquine combination at different dosing intervals
impact_summary: Artesunate and mefloquine given simultaneously or at 8 or 24 hour intervals showed similar efficacy and pharmacokinetics with no drug interaction, but parasite recurrence occurred in 26-33% of patients, indicating single-dose combination therapy does not fully prevent recurrence or mefloquine resistance.
effect_estimate: 26%, 26%, and 33% in groups A, B, and C respectively
safety_summary: All patients recovered rapidly except one case of treatment failure within the first 24 hours; no significant interaction between artesunate and mefloquine in terms of tolerance.

title: Efficacy of a 14-day primaquine regimen in preventing relapses in patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria in Mumbai, India.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine for malaria treatment (P. vivax relapse prevention) with reported outcome results comparing intervention to control.
population: patients with confirmed Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Recurrence/relapse of parasitaemia after primaquine antirelapse therapy
impact_summary: A 14-day supervised primaquine regimen reduced recurrences compared to no antirelapse therapy, but PCR-SSCP genotyping revealed a true relapse rate suggesting probable primaquine resistance in some cases.
effect_estimate: 4.6% (primaquine) vs 9.2% (no therapy); true relapse rate 2.29% by PCR-SSCP

title: No benefits from combining chloroquine with artesunate for three days for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum in Guinea-Bissau.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment interventions (chloroquine and artesunate combinations) in children with Plasmodium falciparum infection; primary focus is malaria treatment; not early-phase.
comparator: chloroquine monotherapy and artesunate monotherapy (active comparators)
population: children with symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: presence of parasites on day 28 (and day 35) after treatment
impact_summary: Combining chloroquine with artesunate, either concomitantly or sequentially, did not improve outcomes compared with chloroquine monotherapy, showing no antagonistic, additive, or synergistic effect.

title: Preliminary report of the evaluation of the gametocytocidal action of bulaquine, in adult patients with acute, Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (bulaquine for gametocytocidal action in P. falciparum) with reported outcome results; phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
population: adult patients with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: gametocytocidal action of bulaquine
impact_summary: Bulaquine was evaluated for its gametocytocidal effect in adult patients with acute P. falciparum malaria, but specific quantitative results are not detailed in the available information.

title: A prospective study evaluating the efficacy of a single, 45-mg dose of primaquine, as a gametocytocidal agent, in patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mumbai, India.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine (malaria treatment intervention) with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance; not early-phase.
population: adults with uncomplicated or severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria who were gametocytaemic
primary_outcome: Persistence of gametocytaemia and gametocyte viability (exflagellation) following treatment
impact_summary: A single 45-mg dose of primaquine significantly reduced the proportion of patients remaining gametocytaemic compared to those not receiving primaquine, in both uncomplicated and severe malaria groups.
effect_estimate: Uncomplicated: 4.2% (primaquine) vs 27.3% (no primaquine); Severe: 9.5% (primaquine) vs 31.8% (no primaquine)
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; no adverse events mentioned

title: Low-dose quinine is effective in the treatment of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in eastern Sudan.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (quinine for chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum) with reported outcome results on parasitaemias and recrudescence.
population: Patients with chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria presenting at a health centre
primary_outcome: Parasite-clearance time and recurrence of parasitaemia by day 28
impact_summary: Once-daily low-dose quinine (15 mg/kg/day) was as effective as thrice-daily quinine (30 mg/kg/day) in treating chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in parasite clearance or recrudescence rates among the three dosing regimens.
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; treatment administered orally and sometimes intravenously without reported major adverse events

title: A randomized, comparative study of two regimens of beta-artemether for the treatment of uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria, in northern Ghana.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (beta-artemether for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitological clearance).
comparator: active comparator (80 mg vs 160 mg loading dose of beta-artemether)
population: adults aged >=15 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological cure rate by day 14
impact_summary: Both the 80 mg and 160 mg loading dose regimens of beta-artemether were similarly safe and effective, with the higher loading dose regimen offering shorter treatment duration and potentially better compliance.
safety_summary: The 160-mg loading dose regimen appeared as safe as the 80-mg regimen, with adverse events monitored on days 1,2,3,4/5,7 and 14; no major safety differences reported.

title: Efficacy of artesunate plus chloroquine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children in Burkina Faso: a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of artesunate plus chloroquine for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy outcomes at days 14 and 28.
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological clearance/cure rate at day 14 and day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus artesunate cleared parasites significantly faster and more effectively than chloroquine alone by day 14 and day 28, though overall day 28 cure rates remained low.
safety_summary: No adverse drug reactions were recorded.

title: A randomized comparison of oral chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Laos.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (treatment failure rates) in humans.
population: patients over 5 years old with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of patients with treatment failure
impact_summary: Chloroquine had a much higher treatment failure rate than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Laos, prompting a call to review treatment policy.

title: Artesunate and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combinations for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Uganda: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (day 14 and 28 cure rates) testing malaria treatment combinations in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological/clinical response) at day 14 and day 28
impact_summary: Adding 3 days of artesunate to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine significantly improved cure rates compared with SP alone, while adding only 1 day of artesunate did not provide as strong a benefit and SP alone was ineffective.
safety_summary: All drug regimens were well tolerated; the combinations were well tolerated and safe.

title: Prevention of anaemia in pregnancy using insecticide-treated bednets and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in a highly malarious area of Kenya: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria interventions (ITNs and IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on hemoglobin levels and anemia prevention.
population: pregnant women (primigravidae and secundigravidae)
primary_outcome: Haemoglobin (Hb) levels during pregnancy / prevention of anaemia
impact_summary: Combination of insecticide-treated nets and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was most protective against anaemia in primigravidae, with SP alone and ITNs alone also showing protective efficacy, while secundigravidae showed little benefit.
p_value: P < 0.006 (Hb improvement in primigravidae); P = 0.03 (Hb decline in secundigravidae)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Atovaquone-proguanil versus chloroquine-proguanil for malaria prophylaxis in nonimmune pediatric travelers: results of an international, randomized, open-label study.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention in nonimmune pediatric travelers with reported safety and efficacy outcome results.
population: nonimmune pediatric travelers, age 2-17 years
primary_outcome: Safety and clinical outcome (adverse events) evaluated at 7, 28, and 60 days after travel
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil was as effective as chloroquine-proguanil for malaria prophylaxis in children, with fewer treatment-related adverse events and no cases of malaria in either group.
safety_summary: By day 7 posttravel, 35% of atovaquone-proguanil and 37% of chloroquine-proguanil recipients reported at least one adverse event; treatment-related adverse events occurred in 8% vs 14%, including gastrointestinal complaints (5% vs 10%); two subjects discontinued prophylaxis due to drug-related adverse events, both in the chloroquine-proguanil group.

title: Comparison of chlorproguanil-dapsone with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in young African children: double-blind randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (efficacy, safety, adverse events).
population: young African children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Acceptable clinical and parasitological response by day 14
impact_summary: Chlorproguanil-dapsone was more efficacious than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in African children, though it caused more reversible haematological adverse effects.
safety_summary: Adverse events occurred in 46% (CD) and 50% (SP) of patients; haemoglobin was significantly lower in the CD group at day 7 (difference -4 g/L, 95% CI -6 to -2), with reversible haematological effects; methaemoglobinaemia occurred in CD group (mean 4.2% at day 3, declining by day 7); G6PD-deficient patients on CD had greater odds of haemoglobin decline with high baseline temperature.

title: Sustainability of reductions in malaria transmission and infant mortality in western Kenya with use of insecticide-treated bednets: 4 to 6 years of follow-up.
screening_reason: Community randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on mortality and transmission over 4-6 years of follow-up.
population: residents of villages including infants and children under 5 years in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission
primary_outcome: Proportion of children younger than 5 years using insecticide-treated bednets, mean number of Anopheles mosquitoes per house, and all-cause mortality rates
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednets sustained reductions in mosquito density and infant mortality over up to 6 years without evidence of increased mortality in older children who used bednets from birth.
age_range: infants (1-11 months) and children under 5 years
safety_summary: No evidence that bednet use from birth increases all-cause mortality in older children in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission.

title: Efficacy of rectal artesunate compared with parenteral quinine in initial treatment of moderately severe malaria in African children and adults: a randomised study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasitaemia reduction at 12 and 24 h) comparing rectal artesunate versus parenteral quinine for moderately severe malaria treatment in African children and adults.
population: children and adults with moderately severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of patients with peripheral asexual parasitaemia of less than 60% of that at baseline after 12 h
impact_summary: A single rectal dose of artesunate produced a significantly greater reduction in parasite density at 12 and 24 hours than parenteral quinine in both children and adults, with equivalent clinical response.
safety_summary: Clinical response was equivalent with rectal artesunate and parenteral quinine; specific adverse event data not detailed.

title: Cost-effectiveness of malaria control interventions when malaria mortality is low: insecticide-treated nets versus in-house residual spraying in India.
screening_reason: Community randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria vector-control interventions (ITNs vs IRS) with reported outcome results (cost-effectiveness and malaria prevention effectiveness) in a low-mortality malaria endemic setting.
population: general population in a low mortality malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: cost-effectiveness (cost per malaria case averted) of ITNs versus IRS
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated nets were more cost-effective than in-house residual spraying for preventing malaria, with significantly lower mean cost per case averted.
effect_estimate: ITNs Rs. 1848 (US$52) vs IRS Rs. 3121 (US$87); incremental cost-effectiveness ratio Rs. 799 (US$22)

title: Open randomized study of pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine vs. pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine plus probenecid for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine ± probenecid) in children with P. falciparum malaria that has reported primary outcome results (parasitological cure rates on days 14 and 28).
population: children aged 12 years or younger with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological cure rates on days 14 and 28
impact_summary: Adding probenecid to pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine significantly improved fever and parasite clearance times and day 14 cure rate, but did not significantly improve day 28 cure rate or gametocyte carriage.
p_value: 0.02 (day 14 cure rate); 0.4 (day 28 cure rate); 0.02 (fever duration); 0.04 (parasite clearance)
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; no child was withdrawn because of drug intolerance.

title: Randomized controlled trial of a traditional preparation of Artemisia annua L. (Annual Wormwood) in the treatment of malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention with reported outcome results (cure and recrudescence rates); not early-phase; malaria is the primary focus.
population: patients with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate after 7 days of treatment
impact_summary: Traditional Artemisia annua tea preparations achieved lower cure rates (74%) than quinine (91%) and had high recrudescence rates, so monotherapy with Artemisia annua cannot be recommended as an alternative to modern antimalarials.
safety_summary: Treatment resulted in quick resolution of parasitaemia and clinical symptoms; specific adverse events not detailed, but high recrudescence rates were noted with Artemisia treatment.

title: Randomized control trial of quinine and artesunate in complicated malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial drugs (artesunate vs quinine) in children with complicated malaria, with outcome results reported (coma resolution time, fever clearance time, parasite clearance time).
population: children with complicated malaria
primary_outcome: Comparative efficacy of quinine versus artesunate assessed via coma resolution time (CRT), fever clearance time (FCT) and parasite clearance time (PCT)
impact_summary: Artesunate resulted in significantly faster coma resolution, fever clearance and parasite clearance than quinine, with no observed side effects, in children with complicated malaria.
effect_estimate: CRT 50.4 vs 70.15 hrs; FCT 43.55 vs 62.23 hrs; PCT 41.67 vs 52.24 hrs (artesunate vs quinine)
safety_summary: No side effects were observed in the artesunate treated group.

title: Patterns of resistance and DHFR/DHPS genotypes of Plasmodium falciparum in rural Tanzania prior to the adoption of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as first-line treatment.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP vs CQ) in children with uncomplicated malaria that reported clinical and parasitological outcome results.
population: Children under five years with clinical, uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical recovery and parasitological resistance (RII/RIII) to treatment at day 28
impact_summary: SP produced better clinical recovery (98%) than CQ (90%), but pre-existing parasitological resistance (RII/RIII) was found in 14% of SP-treated and 51% of CQ-treated patients prior to SP's adoption as first-line treatment.
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; overall significant increase in haemoglobin levels from day 0 to day 28 in both groups.

title: Antimalarial efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine and a combination of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in Bundi Bugyo, western Uganda.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatments in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria reporting 28-day PCR-adjusted efficacy outcomes; phase not stated but treatment efficacy study (not early-phase).
design: randomized, open-label, in vivo antimalarial efficacy study
comparator: active comparator (three regimens compared to each other: SP vs AQ vs CQ+SP)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted treatment failure proportion at day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (Uganda's first-line regimen) and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed high PCR-adjusted failure rates, with amodiaquine performing best, suggesting the need to replace CQ+SP with a more efficacious regimen such as artesunate plus amodiaquine.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted treatment failure proportion at day 28
transmission_setting: district with large displaced population, endemic malaria area

title: A randomized trial of amodiaquine and artesunate alone and in combination for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children from Burkina Faso.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (artesunate and amodiaquine) for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite and fever clearance times, cure rates).
comparator: active comparator (amodiaquine alone vs artesunate alone vs amodiaquine+artesunate combination)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, aged 1-15 years
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Artesunate alone and artesunate plus amodiaquine combination therapy resulted in faster parasite and fever clearance than amodiaquine alone, with all treatments highly efficacious and well tolerated.
effect_estimate: AR 1.13 days, AQAR 1.13 days vs AQ 1.6 days
p_value: P = 0.008 (AR vs AQ); P < 0.01 (AQAR vs AQ)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region with established chloroquine resistance
safety_summary: No adverse reactions were observed in any group during follow-up.

title: Activities of artesunate and primaquine against asexual- and sexual-stage parasites in falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, gametocyte carriage, clinical recovery) in malaria treatment intervention (artesunate and primaquine combinations).
comparator: quinine (with or without tetracycline or primaquine) versus artesunate (with or without primaquine)
population: adult patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time, gametocyte carriage and clearance, fever clearance time, and rates of P. falciparum reappearance
impact_summary: Artesunate reduced the appearance of gametocytemia and shortened parasite clearance times compared to quinine, while primaquine accelerated gametocyte clearance without affecting therapeutic response.
p_value: P <= 0.007 (parasite/gametocyte clearance comparisons); P <= 0.038 (gametocyte clearance time); P > 0.2 (primaquine effect on therapeutic response)
safety_summary: Clinical recovery occurred in all patients; no significant differences in fever clearance times or recurrence rates between treatment groups; no severe adverse events reported.

title: Efficacy of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone or combined with amodiaquine or chloroquine for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Ugandan children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (SP alone vs. combinations) in Ugandan children with reported efficacy outcomes at day 14 and day 28.
comparator: SP alone and CQ/SP compared with AQ/SP
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure (RI-RIII) at day 28 and adequate clinical response at day 14
impact_summary: AQ/SP combination was significantly more efficacious than CQ/SP or SP alone, with lower parasitological failure rates at day 28.
effect_metric: odds ratio for parasitological failure at day 28 (vs AQ/SP)
transmission_setting: high chloroquine resistance area, East/Central Africa

title: Efficacy of mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Amazon region of Bolivia.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate) with reported efficacy outcomes in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine monotherapy vs mefloquine-artesunate combination)
population: Patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, aged 5 to 60 years
primary_outcome: Recurrence of parasitaemia during 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Both mefloquine monotherapy and mefloquine-artesunate combination therapy were fully effective with no recurrences of parasitaemia at 28 days, though the combination therapy cleared parasites faster and reduced gametocyte carriage more than monotherapy.
safety_summary: All patients tolerated the medications well.

title: CV8, a new combination of dihydroartemisinin, piperaquine, trimethoprim and primaquine, compared with atovaquone-proguanil against falciparum malaria in Vietnam.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial drug combinations for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcomes over 28 days.
population: Vietnamese adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate / parasite elimination half-life and clearance time
impact_summary: CV8 was as effective as atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone) for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with similar parasite clearance times and 28-day cure rates.
safety_summary: No significant side-effects were found with either treatment.

title: Efficacy of chloroquine, amodiaquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and combination therapy with artesunate in Mozambican children with non-complicated malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment interventions in children with reported efficacy outcomes; malaria is the primary focus; not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine monotherapies and combinations)
population: children with non-complicated (uncomplicated) malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological response/efficacy to antimalarial treatment at day 14 and follow-up
impact_summary: Amodiaquine was more efficacious than sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and chloroquine, and combination therapies (AQ+SP, AR+SP, AQ+AR) were safe with 100% clinical efficacy at 14-day follow-up.
safety_summary: Combination therapies (AQ+SP, AR+SP, AQ+AR) were reported as safe

title: Optimising operational use of artesunate-mefloquine: a randomised comparison of four treatment regimens.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: RCT comparing malaria treatment regimens (artesunate-mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results on recrudescence, P vivax infections, and anaemia.
comparator: active comparator (four different artesunate-mefloquine dosing regimens compared against each other)
population: adults and children (>1 year old) with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR genotyping-confirmed recrudescence within 42 days follow-up
impact_summary: The 3-day directly observed artesunate-mefloquine regimen resulted in no recrudescence and fewer P. vivax infections and less post-treatment anaemia compared with single-dose regimens, making it the most effective treatment despite single-dose observed regimens also being highly effective.
transmission_setting: Western Myanmar, endemic falciparum malaria region
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated; post-treatment anaemia (haemoglobin <10 g/dL) was reduced by the 3-day regimens; gametocyte appearance was low with all four regimens.

title: Compliance with 14-day primaquine therapy for radical cure of vivax malaria--a randomized placebo-controlled trial comparing unsupervised with supervised treatment.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: RCT comparing supervised vs unsupervised primaquine treatment for vivax malaria radical cure with reported relapse outcome results at 9 months follow-up.
population: Clinical cases of P. vivax malaria in an Afghan refugee camp, excluding individuals with G6PD deficiency
primary_outcome: Relapse rate (recurrence of P. vivax episodes) after primaquine treatment, compared between supervised, unsupervised, and placebo groups
impact_summary: Both supervised and unsupervised 14-day primaquine treatment were equally effective at reducing P. vivax relapse compared to placebo, showing that unsupervised treatment with simple instructions can achieve compliance similar to supervised treatment.
transmission_setting: Afghan refugee camp, endemic vivax malaria area
age_range: all age groups (including children and adults)
safety_summary: Individuals with G6PD deficiency were excluded from the trial to avoid hemolysis risk from primaquine; no other major safety issues reported.

title: DEET mosquito repellent provides personal protection against malaria: a household randomized trial in an Afghan refugee camp in Pakistan.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Household randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria cases detected) evaluating DEET repellent for malaria prevention in humans.
population: residents of an Afghan refugee village (all ages/families)
primary_outcome: Incidence of falciparum and vivax malaria detected by passive case detection at the camp clinic
impact_summary: DEET-permethrin repellent soap significantly reduced falciparum malaria incidence compared to placebo, but showed no protective effect against vivax malaria.
transmission_setting: refugee camp setting with both P. falciparum and P. vivax transmission
safety_summary: The repellent was popularly received and very few side-effects were reported.

title: Efficacy of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Republic of Congo.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (SP vs CQ) in malaria-infected children with reported efficacy outcome results.
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, 6-59 months old (mean 33 months)
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment failure rate at day 14
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine showed a much lower treatment failure rate than chloroquine, with no clinical or parasitologic failure in 75 of 80 children followed to day 14, supporting SP as an alternative first-line treatment.
safety_summary: No serious adverse reactions were observed with SP treatment.

title: Fosmidomycin-clindamycin for Plasmodium falciparum Infections in African children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (fosmidomycin-clindamycin combination) in humans with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and cure rates.
population: schoolchildren with asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum infections
primary_outcome: day 14 and day 28 cure rates (radical clearance of asexual parasites)
impact_summary: Fosmidomycin-clindamycin combination therapy achieved 100% cure rates at day 14 and 28 and cleared parasites faster than either drug alone, outperforming fosmidomycin monotherapy which had a 42% day 28 cure rate.
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated with no serious adverse events.

title: Assessment of chloroquine single dose treatment of malaria due to Plasmodium vivax in Brazilian Amazon.
journal: Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de Sao Paulo
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine for P. vivax) with reported outcome results (parasitological cure and efficacy).
comparator: standard 3-day chloroquine regimen (450 mg on days 2-3) with placebo on days 2-3 in single-dose group
population: outpatients with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological cure
impact_summary: Single-dose chloroquine (600 mg) showed similar parasitological cure rates and parasite density decline compared to the standard 3-day chloroquine regimen, though three patients had inadequate response.
transmission_setting: Brazilian Amazon Region, remote/difficult-access malaria endemic area
safety_summary: Inadequate response observed in three patients, indicating need for further studies; no other adverse effects specified.

title: Addition of artesunate to chloroquine for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Gambian children causes a significant but short-lived reduction in infectiousness for mosquitoes.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial combination therapy for P. falciparum treatment in humans with reported outcome results on gametocyte prevalence, mosquito infectivity, and treatment efficacy.
population: children with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Post-treatment sexual-stage (gametocyte) parasitaemia and infectiousness to mosquitoes over 4-week follow-up
impact_summary: Adding artesunate to chloroquine significantly reduced gametocyte prevalence, density, and mosquito infectivity in the short term, but the benefit was largely lost by day 28 due to recrudescence of chloroquine-resistant parasites.
p_value: P<0.001 (gametocyte carriage rate association); P=0.002 and P=0.30 (intensity of infection by group)
transmission_setting: endemic, area of increasing chloroquine resistance
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; focus was on transmissibility outcomes rather than adverse events

title: The efficacy of chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and a combination of both for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in an area of low transmission in western Uganda.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (fever clearance, clinical success, parasitological resistance).
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment outcome (fever clearance, clinical success/failure, parasitological resistance) by day 14
impact_summary: Chloroquine remains effective for uncomplicated malaria in this low-transmission area, though combination therapy with SP+CQ is recommended to delay resistance development.

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine against multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Vietnam: randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) for malaria in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: non-immune patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: reappearance of P. falciparum malaria within 56 days of treatment
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine achieved high cure rates (97.4-98.7%) similar to artesunate-mefloquine but with significantly fewer treatment-related side effects, supporting its use as an effective, safe, and inexpensive treatment for multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria region, Southeast Asia
safety_summary: DHA-TP and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were well tolerated with fewer than 3% of patients experiencing treatment-related side-effects, compared with 16% in the A3M group (p<0.001); no patients lost to follow-up.

title: Primaquine for prevention of malaria in travelers.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trials of primaquine chemoprevention in travelers with reported efficacy and safety outcomes against malaria parasites.
population: nonpregnant children (>8 years) and adults with normal G6PD levels
primary_outcome: protective efficacy against malaria (P. falciparum and P. vivax) and adverse events including methemoglobinemia
impact_summary: Primaquine base at 30 mg/day (0.5 mg/kg/day) provided 85%-93% protective efficacy against malaria with no greater risk of adverse events than placebo and only mild, transient methemoglobinemia.
safety_summary: No greater risk of adverse symptomatic events than placebo; methemoglobinemia was mild (<13%, typically <6%) and transient (<2 weeks duration) among 151 subjects evaluated after 20 or 52 weeks of therapy.

title: [Clinical efficacy of four schemes for vivax malaria treatment in children].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing four malaria treatment schemes in children with vivax malaria that has reported outcome results (parasite clearance and treatment efficacy).
comparator: active comparator (four different chloroquine+primaquine dosing schedules)
population: outpatient children with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and complete cure (absence of relapse) with four therapeutic schedules of chloroquine plus primaquine
impact_summary: A doubled dose of primaquine achieved better complete cure of vivax malaria than the standard dose, regardless of treatment duration, while schedule D (standard dose, shorter duration) was not recommended.
effect_metric: comparison of cure rates between schedules (Fisher's Exact test)
effect_estimate: doubled primaquine dose significantly more effective than standard dose
p_value: 0.0042 (dose comparison); 0.022 (A vs D); 0.005 (C vs D); 0.6104 (duration comparison)

title: Malaria parasitaemia in relation to HIV status and vitamin A supplementation among pre-school children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported results examining vitamin A supplementation effects on malaria parasitaemia in children; malaria is the primary focus.
population: pre-school children 6-60 months of age
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria parasitaemia and high parasite density at 4-8 months after first dose of vitamin A supplementation
impact_summary: HIV infection was associated with lower prevalence of malaria parasitaemia, and vitamin A supplementation had no significant effect on malaria parasitaemia.

title: Antipyretic, parasitologic, and immunologic effects of combining sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine with chloroquine or paracetamol for treating uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing malaria treatments (SP-based combinations) in humans with parasitologic and immunologic results; not early-phase.
comparator: chloroquine alone, SP alone, SP plus paracetamol
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Axillary temperature reduction, daily parasitemia, and serum IgG antibody levels to P. falciparum
impact_summary: Adding chloroquine or paracetamol to sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine improved fever control compared to SP alone or chloroquine alone, but did not affect parasitologic clearance or antibody response.
effect_estimate: lower mean temperatures with SP plus chloroquine or paracetamol vs SP alone or chloroquine alone
p_value: P < 0.001 (SP+chloroquine/paracetamol vs SP alone); P < 0.05 (vs chloroquine alone)

title: Randomised efficacy and safety study of two 3-day artesunate rectal capsule/mefloquine regimens versus artesunate alone for uncomplicated malaria in Ecuadorian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment regimens with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitemia clearance, safety) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
comparator: artesunate monotherapy (rectal capsules) versus artesunate rectal capsules combined with mefloquine (two regimens)
population: children aged 2-12 years with confirmed uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure) at day 28 and clearance of parasitaemia
impact_summary: Combining artesunate rectal capsules with mefloquine significantly improved cure rates and reduced recrudescence compared with artesunate monotherapy, and was safe and well tolerated.
safety_summary: No adverse events were reported; vital signs and laboratory examinations showed no clinically relevant changes.

title: Field efficacy of thermally expelled or live potted repellent plants against African malaria vectors in western Kenya.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial (latin square design with random assignment) testing malaria vector control intervention (spatial repellents via potted plants and thermal expulsion) with reported efficacy results.
design: Latin square design, randomized, field trial
population: residents of traditional houses in western Kenya
primary_outcome: Repellency of malaria vector mosquitoes (Anopheles gambiae s.l. and An. funestus) measured by mosquito entry into experimental houses
impact_summary: Live potted plants and thermally expelled plant materials significantly repelled Anopheles gambiae sensu lato, with Corymbia citriodora showing the highest repellency, offering potential low-cost household protection against malaria vectors.
effect_estimate: 48.71% (C. citriodora, thermal expulsion); 44.54% (O. kilimandscharicum and O. suave); 37.91% (O. americanum potted); 27.22% (L. camara potted); 36-44% residual repellency
p_value: P < 0.0001 (C. citriodora); P = 0.001 (O. kilimandscharicum/O. suave); P = 0.004 (O. americanum); P = 0.05 (L. camara)

title: Treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in southern Vietnam: can chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine be reintroduced in combination with artesunate?
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: RCT comparing artesunate-chloroquine and artesunate-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates and parasitological response).
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, including semi-immune residents in Dac Lac and nonimmune workers and relatives in Binh Phuoc
primary_outcome: In vivo and PCR-confirmed treatment response (cure rate) by day 28 following treatment with artesunate combined with chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Artesunate combined with chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved high cure rates (>96%) in semi-immune patients in Dac Lac but poor efficacy (<52%) in nonimmune patients in Binh Phuoc, with pfcrt K76T mutation predicting recrudescence in the chloroquine arm.
transmission_setting: varying transmission intensity: high exposure since birth in Dac Lac vs low/nonimmune exposure in Binh Phuoc
age_range: mean age 9.6 years (Dac Lac); mean age 24.2 years (Binh Phuoc)

title: Atovaquone and proguanil versus amodiaquine for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in African infants and young children.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (atovaquone/proguanil vs amodiaquine) in African children with reported outcome results (day-28 cure rates).
population: African infants and young children weighing >=5 and <11 kg with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate on day 28
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil resulted in a significantly higher cure rate (95%) than amodiaquine (53%) for treating P. falciparum malaria in young children.
safety_summary: Incidence of adverse events was similar in both groups; no serious adverse events attributed to atovaquone/proguanil.

title: Chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine efficacy for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Upper Nile, south Sudan.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment drugs with reported outcome results (clinical response rates); primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (active comparators) vs amodiaquine
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and fever, stratified by age group
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical response (treatment success) at day 14 after treatment
impact_summary: SP was the most effective treatment (100% adequate clinical response), followed by amodiaquine (94.1%) and chloroquine (88.5%), with lower efficacy of chloroquine and amodiaquine in children under 5 years.
transmission_setting: South Sudan, malaria-endemic region (eastern Upper Nile)
age_range: children under 5 years, children 5-15 years, and adults

title: The effect of mass administration of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combined with artesunate on malaria incidence: a double-blind, community-randomized, placebo-controlled trial in The Gambia.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind community-randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (SP+AS mass drug administration) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence.
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years, surveilled following mass drug administration to the general community
primary_outcome: incidence of clinical malaria episodes during 20-week surveillance period
impact_summary: Mass drug administration with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus artesunate did not significantly reduce malaria incidence compared to placebo.

title: A comparative clinical trial of artemether and quinine in children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether vs quinine for severe malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, fever clearance, coma recovery).
population: hospitalized children with severe malaria (WHO criteria)
primary_outcome: Death in hospital and residual organ damage
impact_summary: Artemether and quinine had similar mortality but artemether resulted in significantly faster parasite clearance and faster recovery from coma than quinine.
follow_up: Until two successive negative blood films / hospital discharge
safety_summary: Overall mortality rate was 23.9% with no significant difference between artemether and quinine groups; mortality was directly proportional to number of coexisting severe malaria manifestations, reaching 100% with four coexisting manifestations.

title: Comparative efficacy of chloroquine and cotrimoxazole in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: The Central African journal of medicine
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing drug treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children; phase not stated but treatment trial is not early-phase.
population: children with acute symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever and other symptoms clearance times, parasite clearance times, and cure rates
impact_summary: Cotrimoxazole (three-day and five-day regimens) was as effective as chloroquine for treating acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children, with comparable clearance times and cure rates.
safety_summary: All three treatment regimens were well tolerated.

title: Chloroquine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Savannakhet Province, Lao People's Democratic Republic: an assessment of national antimalarial drug recommendations.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized comparative trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported outcome results (treatment efficacy/failure rates); not early-phase.
place: Savannakhet Province, Lao People's Democratic Republic
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate at day 42
impact_summary: Chloroquine cleared fever faster but had double the treatment failure rate compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, indicating both drugs have unsatisfactory efficacy in Laos.
safety_summary: Gametocytemia after treatment was associated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine receipt and with treatment failure (P=.009); no other adverse events reported.

title: N'Dribala (Cochlospermum planchonii) versus chloroquine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing N'Dribala versus chloroquine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance at day 5).
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure (no detectable parasitemia) at day 5
impact_summary: N'Dribala was statistically as efficient as chloroquine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with similar cure rates and no significant side effects.
safety_summary: N'Dribala appeared safe with no significant side effects observed.

title: [A randomized comparative study of naphtoquine, mefloquine and artsunate in the treatment of falciparum malaria].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (naphtoquine vs mefloquine vs artesunate) with reported outcome results (fever-subsidence time, parasite-clearance time, 28-day cure rates).
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day curative ratio, fever-subsidence time, parasite-clearance time
impact_summary: Naphtoquine had a slower fever-subsidence and parasite-clearance time but a higher 28-day cure rate than mefloquine and artesunate.
p_value: P<0.05 (naphtoquine vs mefloquine and artesunate); P<0.01 (parasite-clearance and fever-subsidence time comparisons)
safety_summary: Slight nausea and vomiting observed in a few patients in all three groups; no serious adverse events reported.

title: Assessing the efficacy of chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcomes (treatment failure rates and parasitemia clearance).
population: children under 5 with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate at day 14 (in vivo response to CQ and SP)
impact_summary: Chloroquine had a much higher treatment failure rate (45.4%) than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (7.5%), indicating CQ is no longer effective in DRC and SP may be a suitable replacement first-line therapy.
transmission_setting: endemic, rural and other sites in DRC

title: Comparative clinical trial of two-fixed combinations dihydroartemisinin-napthoquine-trimethoprim (DNP) and artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem/Riamet) in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (DNP vs artemether-lumefantrine) in adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at 28 days.
population: adults with acute uncomplicated multidrug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Both DNP and artemether-lumefantrine were safe, well tolerated and highly efficacious, with cure rates of 99% and 97% respectively at 28 days.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria endemic area
safety_summary: No serious adverse events occurred; both regimens were safe and well tolerated.

title: N-acetylcysteine in severe falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing an adjunctive treatment (N-acetylcysteine) for severe falciparum malaria in humans.
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety and efficacy of NAC as adjunctive therapy in severe falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Adjunctive N-acetylcysteine with artesunate showed excellent results with no attributable adverse reactions other than vomiting, supporting further large-scale trials.
safety_summary: No patient sustained an adverse reaction to NAC other than vomiting; two critically ill patients in Group 1 died, attributed to severe disease with multiple organ involvement rather than NAC.

title: Plasmodium falciparum gametocytaemia in Nigerian children: before, during and after treatment with antimalarial drugs.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug regimens in children with P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results on gametocyte carriage and treatment efficacy.
comparator: active comparator (various antimalarial drug regimens compared with each other)
population: children with acute, symptomatic, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: gametocyte carriage and intensity of gametocytaemia before, during and after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine-resistant infections and pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine monotherapy were associated with significantly higher and more prolonged gametocyte carriage and density, potentially increasing transmission of drug-resistant parasites, while combining amodiaquine with pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine significantly reduced gametocyte carriage.
effect_estimate: higher gametocyte carriage and density in CQ-resistant vs CQ-sensitive and PS-treated groups
p_value: 0.04 and 0.01 (RI vs RII resistance comparison on days 5 and 7)

title: Effects of pyrimethamine versus proguanil in malarial chemoprophylaxis in children with sickle cell disease: a randomized, placebo-controlled, open-label study.
journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental
screening_reason: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (pyrimethamine vs proguanil) in children with sickle cell disease that has reported outcome results on parasitemia, parasite density, and malaria complications.
population: children with homozygous sickle cell disease
primary_outcome: Prevention of malaria and complications of P. falciparum infection (hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, bone pain crisis, hemolytic crisis)
impact_summary: Proguanil significantly decreased mean parasite density more effectively than pyrimethamine, and both pyrimethamine and proguanil appeared to protect against complications of P. falciparum infection compared with placebo, with proguanil showing an advantage in preventing bone pain crises.
effect_estimate: lower with proguanil vs pyrimethamine and placebo
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region, February to December including rainy season, period of greatest transmission
safety_summary: One patient in the placebo group died of septicemia; hospitalizations and episodes of bone pain and hemolytic crisis occurred most frequently with placebo.

title: The addition of artesunate to chloroquine for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Gambian children delays, but does not prevent treatment failure.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatments in humans with reported outcome results (clinical failure rates, parasitemia); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention.
population: Gambian children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day clinical treatment failure rate
impact_summary: Combination therapy of artesunate plus chloroquine delayed but did not prevent treatment failure, showing only a non-significant reduction in clinical failure and a significant reduction in parasitemia compared with chloroquine alone.

title: Clinical trial of oral artesunate with or without high-dose primaquine for the treatment of vivax malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate and primaquine for P. vivax) with reported outcome results comparing efficacy and safety across randomized treatment groups.
population: patients with acute, symptomatic Plasmodium vivax malaria admitted to Bangkok Hospital for Tropical Diseases
primary_outcome: Recurrence/reappearance of P. vivax parasitemia in the blood during 28 days of observation
impact_summary: None of the patients who received high-dose primaquine relapsed within 28 days, compared with 50% relapse among those who received artesunate alone.
safety_summary: Adverse effects were confined to 13 patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; high-dose primaquine had to be stopped in 4 (31%) of these patients due to a significant decrease in hematocrit.

title: Pentoxifylline adjunct improves prognosis of human cerebral malaria in adults.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (coma resolution time, mortality, TNF-alpha levels) evaluating adjunctive pentoxifylline for cerebral malaria treatment in adults.
population: adult patients with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Coma resolution time
impact_summary: Adding pentoxifylline to quinine therapy significantly shortened coma resolution time and reduced serum TNF-alpha levels compared with quinine alone, with a non-significant reduction in mortality.
safety_summary: No serious side-effects necessitating withdrawal of patients receiving pentoxifylline therapy.

title: The impact of Malarone and primaquine on psychomotor performance.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (double-blind crossover design) testing malaria chemoprophylaxis drugs (Malarone and primaquine) with reported outcome results on psychomotor performance and safety endpoints.
population: Canadian Forces aircrews (healthy adults)
primary_outcome: Impact of Malarone and primaquine on psychomotor performance (serial reaction time, logical reasoning, serial subtraction, multitask performance)
impact_summary: Neither Malarone nor primaquine significantly impacted psychomotor performance, mood, sleepiness, or fatigue compared to placebo.
follow_up: 3-wk washout intervals after each 7-d dosing protocol
transmission_setting: chemoprophylaxis for travel to malaria endemic areas
safety_summary: No significant main effects or interactions for documented adverse effects (abdominal cramps, epigastric distress, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, headache, coughing, dizziness).

title: Rectal dihydroartemisinin versus intravenous quinine in the treatment of severe malaria: a randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two treatments for severe malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates, adverse effects).
population: children and adults with severe malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, efficacy and side effect profile
impact_summary: Rectal dihydroartemisinin cleared parasites faster than intravenous quinine, with similar fever clearance and cure rates but a better adverse reaction profile.
effect_estimate: shorter in rectal DATM group than quinine group
safety_summary: Adverse reaction profile was better with rectal DATM than with quinine; tinnitus was observed more frequently in the quinine group.

title: Effect of insecticide-treated bednets for malaria control in Southeast Anatolia-Turkey.
journal: Journal of vector ecology : journal of the Society for Vector Ecology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results showing significant reduction in malaria incidence.
design: cluster field trial, non-randomized, controlled, intervention vs control villages
comparator: non-impregnated bednets (NIB) and untreated control area
population: rural inhabitants of villages in an endemic malaria area of Sanliurfa, SE Anatolia
primary_outcome: malaria incidence rate (pre- vs post-intervention) in intervention and control villages
impact_summary: Deltamethrin-impregnated bednets significantly reduced malaria incidence in the intervention village, whereas incidence increased in the control village and in villages using non-impregnated bednets.
transmission_setting: endemic rural area, Anopheles sacharovi vector

title: Randomized comparison of artesunate and quinine in the treatment of severe falciparum malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artesunate and quinine for severe malaria treatment in adults with reported outcome results including mortality and parasite clearance.
population: adults with clinically severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality
impact_summary: Artesunate treatment resulted in lower mortality (12%) compared to quinine (22%), though the difference was not statistically significant, and was associated with shorter parasite clearance time and less hypoglycemia.
safety_summary: Fewer patients became hypoglycemic during artesunate therapy (10%) than during quinine therapy (28%) (P=.03); coma recovery and lactate normalization times were similar between groups.

title: Tolerability of azithromycin as malaria prophylaxis in adults in northeast papua, indonesia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of azithromycin prophylaxis against malaria in humans with reported tolerability and safety outcomes over 20 weeks.
population: adults
primary_outcome: Tolerability (frequency of self-reported and elicited symptoms) of azithromycin as malaria prophylaxis
