impact_summary: Daily azithromycin prophylaxis was generally well tolerated by Indonesian adults over 20 weeks, with more heartburn, paresthesia, and itching but less fever and tinnitus compared to placebo, and no evidence of hearing, hematologic, hepatic, or renal toxicity.
effect_estimate: heartburn 10.5, paresthesia 2.03, mild itching 1.55, severe itching 11.2, fever 0.21, tinnitus 0.09
effect_ci: heartburn 2.8-88.1; paresthesia 1.08-4.24; mild itching 1.01-2.48; severe itching 1.34-infinity; fever 0.09-0.49; tinnitus 0.04-0.21
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region of northeast Papua, Indonesia
safety_summary: Azithromycin was well tolerated overall; more heartburn, paresthesia, and itching reported versus placebo; no clinical hearing loss or hematologic, hepatic, or renal toxicity; one participant developed an erythematous rash.

title: The efficacy of combined mefloquine-artesunate versus mefloquine-primaquine on subsequent development of Plasmodium falciparum gametocytemia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine-artesunate vs mefloquine-primaquine) with reported outcome results on gametocytemia development.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: gametocyte carriage rate / subsequent development of gametocytemia
impact_summary: Complete eradication of P. falciparum asexual forms by effective antimalarial treatment, rather than addition of primaquine, was the most effective means to prevent subsequent gametocytemia.
transmission_setting: western Thailand, Kanchanaburi Saiyok District (malaria-endemic border area)

title: Efficacy of mefloquine and a mefloquine-artesunate combination therapy for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Amazon Basin of Peru.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing mefloquine monotherapy vs. mefloquine-artesunate combination for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitemia recurrence, parasite density, gametocyte prevalence); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria aged 5-50 years
primary_outcome: Recurrence of parasitemia during 28-day follow-up (efficacy) and safety/tolerability
impact_summary: Both mefloquine alone and mefloquine-artesunate combination therapy achieved 100% cure with no recurrences by day 28, but the combination therapy cleared parasites faster and reduced gametocyte carriage.
transmission_setting: Amazon Basin endemic region with high chloroquine/sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance
safety_summary: All patients tolerated the medication well.

title: [Short course schemes for vivax malaria treatment].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vivax malaria treatment (artemisinin and chloroquine regimens) with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance and cure rates).
population: patients with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: parasitaemia clearance and cure rate
impact_summary: Arthemisin cleared parasitaemia faster than chloroquine, and a seven-day course of primaquine achieved a higher cure rate (92.3%) than a five-day course (80.2%).

title: A randomized comparison of chloroquine and chloroquine plus ketotifen in the treatment of acute, uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing malaria treatments (chloroquine vs chloroquine plus ketotifen) in children with P. falciparum malaria, with reported outcome results on fever clearance, parasitaemia clearance, and clinical cure.
population: children with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever-clearance time and parasitological/clinical cure rates
impact_summary: Adding ketotifen to chloroquine shortened fever-clearance time but did not significantly enhance overall antimalarial efficacy compared with chloroquine alone.
effect_estimate: significantly shorter with CQK than CQ alone
safety_summary: Adverse reactions were tolerable and included pruritus, gastro-intestinal disturbances, drowsiness and weight gain; drowsiness and weight gain were more frequent with CQK; haematological and biochemical parameters were unaffected by either treatment.

title: Changes in house design reduce exposure to malaria mosquitoes.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (house design modifications) with reported outcome results on mosquito entry reduction.
population: experimental huts used by human volunteer sleepers in a rural Gambian village
primary_outcome: House entry rates of Anopheles gambiae (and Mansonia spp.) mosquitoes
impact_summary: Installing ceilings (plywood, synthetic-netting, insecticide-treated synthetic-netting, or plastic insect-screen) substantially reduced house entry by malaria mosquitoes compared to control huts, while closing the eaves had a smaller, non-significant effect.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in house entry by Anopheles gambiae
effect_estimate: 37-80% (plywood 59%, synthetic-netting 79%, insecticide-treated synthetic-netting 78%, plastic insect-screen 80%, closed eaves 37%)
p_value: P < 0.001 (for ceiling interventions); ns (for closed eaves)
species: Anopheles gambiae (malaria vector); also Mansonia spp.
transmission_setting: low to moderate malaria transmission, rural Gambia

title: Effect of intermittent treatment with amodiaquine on anaemia and malarial fevers in infants in Tanzania: a randomised placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (amodiaquine) in infants with reported outcome results (malarial fevers and anaemia).
population: infants aged 12-16 weeks
primary_outcome: Malarial fevers and anaemia monitored at bimonthly treatment visits and by self-reporting to health centres
impact_summary: Presumptive intermittent treatment with amodiaquine significantly reduced malarial fevers and anaemia in infants in an area with high resistance to other antimalarials.
transmission_setting: holoendemic, chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine resistant area
safety_summary: No haematological or clinical adverse effects noted; no rebound morbidity during 4 months follow-up.

title: [In vivo evaluation of chloroquine therapeutic efficacy in uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Central African Republic ine 1997 and 1998].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine treatment for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (efficacy, parasitaemia clearance, relapse rates) following WHO protocol.
design: multicenter, single-arm, in vivo efficacy study
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with uncomplicated malaria attending pediatric services
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine (parasitological and clinical response) assessed by in vivo test at days 0, 3, 7 and 14
impact_summary: Chloroquine remained effective in most provincial towns but showed strong resistance in Bangui, where the success rate was only 36% and early relapse reached 40%, suggesting chloroquine should be replaced as first-line treatment there.
transmission_setting: endemic, five sanitary regions of Central African Republic
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy and relapse rates rather than adverse events

title: Implications of the western Kenya permethrin-treated bed net study for policy, program implementation, and future research.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published group-randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria with reported efficacy outcomes; phase not applicable for cluster-randomized trials.
population: pregnant women and infants; general population in high malaria transmission area
primary_outcome: all-cause post-neonatal mortality
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bed nets were efficacious in reducing all-cause post-neonatal mortality in an area of intense, perennial malaria transmission.

title: The cost-effectiveness of permethrin-treated bed nets in an area of intense malaria transmission in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Group-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in children with reported outcome results (cost-effectiveness based on clinical endpoints).
comparator: no ITN (untreated nets or no nets)
population: children less than five years of age
primary_outcome: cost per life-year gained and cost per all-cause sick child clinic visit averted
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bed nets were found to be a highly cost-effective intervention for reducing child mortality and morbidity from malaria in an area of intense transmission in western Kenya.

title: Community-wide effects of permethrin-treated bed nets on child mortality and malaria morbidity in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Group-randomized controlled trial of ITN vector control intervention with reported outcome results (child mortality, malaria morbidity, anemia, parasitemia).
population: children living in villages with and without insecticide-treated bed nets
primary_outcome: child mortality
impact_summary: ITNs provided a protective community-wide effect on nearby compounds without nets, reducing child mortality, moderate anemia, and high-density parasitemia, comparable to the effect within ITN villages, depending on the proportion of nearby compounds with treated nets.
transmission_setting: area of intense malaria transmission, western Kenya

title: Effect of permethrin-treated bed nets on the spatial distribution of malaria vectors in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of ITN intervention (vector control) with reported outcome results on malaria vector abundance and sporozoite infection rates.
population: residents of villages in western Kenya, including those in intervention and neighboring non-intervention villages
primary_outcome: spatial distribution and abundance of malaria vectors (Anopheles gambiae and An. funestus) and sporozoite infection rates in relation to distance from ITN intervention villages
impact_summary: High coverage of permethrin-treated bed nets was associated with community-wide suppression of malaria vector populations detectable in neighboring villages lacking ITNs, particularly within 600 meters of intervention villages, providing some protective benefit to residents of those non-ITN villages.
effect_estimate: reduction in mosquito abundance most apparent within 600 meters of intervention villages
p_value: P=0.027 (pre-intervention An. gambiae), P=0.002 (post-intervention An. gambiae), P=0.05 (change in trend strength), P=0.373 (pre-intervention An. funestus), P=0.027 (post-intervention An. funestus), P<0.001 (sporozoite rate decrease)

title: Effects of permethrin-treated bed nets on immunity to malaria in western Kenya II. Antibody responses in young children in an area of intense malaria transmission.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ITNs (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results on antibody responses; phase not applicable for community-based cluster trial.
population: children less than three years old
primary_outcome: IgG antibody responses to P. falciparum antigens (CSP, LSA-1, MSP-1(19) kD)
impact_summary: ITNs reduced IgG responses to pre-erythrocytic antigens (CSP and LSA-1) but did not compromise IgG responses to the blood stage antigen MSP-1 in young children over two years.
effect_estimate: lower IgG to CSP and LSA-1 in ITN villages; higher IgG to MSP-1 at 14 months in ITN villages

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bed nets on malaria and all-cause morbidity in young children in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission in western Kenya: cross-sectional survey.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Group-randomized controlled trial of ITNs (vector control) with reported malaria morbidity outcomes in an area of intense transmission; cluster-randomized design and vector-control intervention are 'not applicable' phase.
population: children less than three years old
primary_outcome: Malaria and all-cause morbidity indicators including illness requiring treatment, splenomegaly, parasitemia, clinical malaria, anemia, and body rash
impact_summary: ITNs substantially reduced malaria-associated morbidity and improved weight gain in young children in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission.
effect_estimate: 15% (illness requiring treatment); 32% (enlarged spleen); 19% (parasitemia); 44% (clinical malaria); 39% (moderate anemia); 38% (pruritic rash)

title: Permethrin-treated bed nets in the prevention of malaria and anemia in adolescent schoolgirls in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control, malaria prevention) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria and anemia.
comparator: no ITNs (untreated bed nets or no nets)
population: adolescent schoolgirls aged 12-18 years, non-pregnant, school-attending
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria and anemia
impact_summary: ITNs reduced the prevalence of mild anemia and increased hemoglobin concentrations in younger schoolgirls (12-13 years) but had no effect on anemia, malaria parasitemia, clinical malaria, or nutritional status in older girls or overall.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio for all-cause anemia
transmission_setting: rural area with intense perennial malaria transmission

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bed nets on growth, nutritional status, and body composition of primary school children in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ITN vector-control intervention for malaria with reported outcome results (growth, nutritional status, body composition).
population: primary school children under 13 years
primary_outcome: linear growth and nutritional status (protein-energy malnutrition measures)
impact_summary: ITNs did not significantly improve linear growth or overall nutritional status in primary school children but were associated with a small increase in percent lean body mass.
effect_metric: change in percent lean body mass
transmission_setting: area of intense perennial malaria transmission

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bed nets on malaria, anemia, and growth in infants in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-based group-randomized controlled trial of ITNs (a vector-control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence, parasitemia, anemia, and growth in infants.
population: infants and children under 24 months of age, including birth cohort followed from birth
primary_outcome: malaria attack rates (force of infection), clinical malaria incidence, moderate-severe anemia incidence, and growth (height/weight gain)
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bed nets substantially reduced malaria attack rates, clinical malaria, and moderate-severe anemia, and improved growth in infants and young children in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission.
effect_metric: reduction in malaria attack rate / clinical malaria and anemia incidence
effect_estimate: 74% reduction in attack rate; 60% reduction in clinical malaria and moderate-severe anemia
p_value: P < 0.0001 for time-to-first parasitemia; P < 0.001 for clinical malaria and anemia
safety_summary: No increased malaria morbidity observed in one-year-old children despite reduced malaria exposure during infancy with continued ITN use

title: Effects of permethrin-treated bed nets on immunity to malaria in western Kenya I. Antibody responses in pregnant women and cord blood in an area of intense malaria transmission.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published group-randomized controlled trial of an insecticide-treated bed net intervention (vector control) with reported immunological outcome results in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: pregnant women and their newborns (cord blood)
primary_outcome: Antibody responses (total IgG and IgG subclasses) to P. falciparum CSP, LSA-1, and MSP-1(19 kD) antigens in maternal and cord plasma
impact_summary: ITN use in pregnant women was associated with decreased antibody responses to LSA-1 and MSP-1 antigens (with corresponding reductions in cord blood antibodies) but increased antibody responses to CSP in mothers, with no effect on CSP antibodies in cord blood.
effect_metric: antibody levels (total IgG and IgG subclasses)

title: Reduction of malaria during pregnancy by permethrin-treated bed nets in an area of intense perennial malaria transmission in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing insecticide-treated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in pregnant women in a high-transmission setting.
comparator: no ITNs (control villages, ITNs distributed two years later)
population: pregnant women (gravidae 1-4 and higher)
outcome_family: pregnancy/birth; clinical incidence; infection prevalence; anaemia
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria parasitemia and severe malarial anemia during pregnancy; birth outcomes including low birth weight and placental/maternal malaria
impact_summary: In gravidae 1-4, permethrin-treated bed nets reduced malaria parasitemia, severe anemia, placental/maternal malaria, and low birth weight during pregnancy, with no benefit observed in gravidae five or higher.
effect_estimate: 38% reduction in malaria parasitemia; 47% reduction in severe malarial anemia; 35% reduction in placental/maternal malaria; 28% reduction in low birth weight
effect_ci: parasitemia 17-54%; anemia 6-71%; placental/maternal malaria 20-47%; low birth weight 2-47%
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bed nets on the incidence of sick child visits to peripheral health facilities.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (vector control intervention for malaria prevention) with reported outcome results showing reduction in malaria-related sick child visits.
population: children less than five years of age visiting peripheral health facilities
primary_outcome: Incidence of sick child visits (SCVs) to peripheral health facilities
impact_summary: Compared with baseline, ITN villages showed a significantly greater reduction in sick child visits, including those diagnosed as malaria, than control villages, though no effect was seen on other illnesses.
effect_metric: reduction in incidence of sick child visits
transmission_setting: area with intense malaria transmission, western Kenya
safety_summary: No specific safety concerns reported; severe anemia was rarely diagnosed (<2%) due to lack of laboratory facilities, regardless of intervention status.

title: Efficacy of permethrin-treated bed nets in the prevention of mortality in young children in an area of high perennial malaria transmission in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Group-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in children with reported mortality outcomes over two years in Kenya.
population: children 1-59 months of age
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality in children 1-59 months of age
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated bed nets reduced all-cause mortality in children 1-59 months by 16%, with greater efficacy (23%) in infants 1-11 months, but efficacy was reduced when re-treatment was delayed beyond six months.

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bed nets on entomologic indices in an area of intense year-round malaria transmission.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ITN (vector control/malaria prevention intervention) with reported outcome results on entomologic indices and transmission; phase not applicable for vector-control cluster trials.
comparator: untreated bed nets/control houses without ITNs
population: residents of study area (households/villages) in an area of intense year-round malaria transmission
primary_outcome: Indoor resting densities of fed Anopheles gambiae s.l. and An. funestus, and sporozoite infection rates
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated bed nets reduced indoor resting mosquito densities and sporozoite infection rates, resulting in an estimated 90% reduction in overall malaria transmission compared to control areas.
safety_summary: Permethrin resistance was not detected during the study period.

title: Population kinetics, efficacy, and safety of dichloroacetate for lactic acidosis due to severe malaria in children.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (efficacy and safety data) testing a malaria treatment intervention (adjunctive therapy for severe malaria) in humans.
population: children with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria and lactic acidosis
primary_outcome: Change in blood lactate levels following DCA administration
impact_summary: A single infusion of DCA was well tolerated and significantly increased the initial rate and magnitude of fall in blood lactate levels when given with intravenous quinine, without interfering with quinine kinetics.
safety_summary: A single 50 mg/kg infusion of DCA was well tolerated with no notable adverse effects reported.

title: Can mothers be trusted to give malaria treatment to their children at home?
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment intervention in children with reported outcome results; not early-phase.
population: children with symptomatic malaria
primary_outcome: outcome of treatment and blood drug concentrations on day 7
impact_summary: No differences were found in treatment outcome or blood drug concentrations between children treated at home by mothers versus supervised at a health centre, indicating mothers can be trusted to give adequate treatment at home.
safety_summary: No adverse safety issues reported; no differences in outcomes between groups.

title: Adverse effect of rifampin on quinine efficacy in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine ± rifampin) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, recrudescence rates, cure rates).
population: adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Adding rifampin to quinine shortened parasite clearance time but significantly increased recrudescence rates due to increased metabolic clearance of quinine, indicating rifampin should not be combined with quinine for malaria treatment.
safety_summary: Rifampin co-administration increased quinine metabolism to 3-hydroxyquinine, lowering plasma quinine concentrations and reducing treatment efficacy; specific adverse events not detailed.

title: [Efficacy of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in the treatment of malaria not complicated by Plasmodium falciparum in Nariño, Colombia, 1999-2002].
journal: Biomedica : revista del Instituto Nacional de Salud
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic failure (treatment failure) at 14 and 28 days follow-up
impact_summary: In El Charco no treatment failures occurred, but in Tumaco amodiaquine had a much higher treatment failure rate (12/24) than sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (4/26) after 28 days.
transmission_setting: low to moderate malaria transmission, Pacific Coast region

title: A comparative clinical trial of combinations of dihydroartemisinin plus azithromycin and dihydroartemisinin plus mefloquine for treatment of multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial drug combinations with reported outcome results (cure rates at day 28), directly addressing malaria treatment in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: The combination of dihydroartemisinin plus mefloquine achieved a 100% cure rate at day 28 compared to 69.7% with dihydroartemisinin plus azithromycin, a statistically significant difference.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria; patients stayed in non-malaria endemic area during study
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported; both regimens were considered safe.

title: An open randomized clinical trial of Artecom vs artesunate-mefloquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (Artecom vs artesunate-mefloquine) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans.
population: adults with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Artecom achieved a 97% 28-day cure rate, equivalent to artesunate-mefloquine, with no significant differences in fever or parasite clearance times.
safety_summary: Artecom was well-tolerated, with safety comparable to artesunate-mefloquine.

title: A new tool for malaria prevention?: Results of a trial of permethrin-impregnated bedsheets (shukas) in an area of unstable transmission.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (permethrin-impregnated bedsheets) with reported outcome results (malaria incidence/prevalence).
population: individuals residing in hamlets (manyattas), including children and adults
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria cases (clinical and laboratory-confirmed) per person-days at risk
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bedsheets (shukas) were associated with a significantly lower rate of malaria among individuals aged 6 and over, though results were inconclusive for children under 5.
age_range: all ages, with subgroup analysis for children ≤5 years and individuals aged 6 and over

title: Comparison of intramuscular artemether and intravenous quinine in the treatment of Sudanese children with severe falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and quinine for severe falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, coma resolution times); malaria is the primary focus.
population: children with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, coma resolution time and side effects
impact_summary: Artemether resulted in faster parasite and coma clearance than quinine, but quinine reduced fever more quickly than artemether; both drugs were effective with quinine showing one death and one case of hypoglycaemia.
safety_summary: In the quinine group, one patient died and one developed hypoglycaemia; recrudescence occurred in one of fifteen quinine patients by day 28, treated successfully with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine.

title: Comparative efficacy of aminoquinoline-antifolate combinations for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Kampala, Uganda.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported efficacy results; primary purpose is antimalarial intervention in humans; Phase III appropriate for treatment efficacy study.
comparator: active comparator (SP monotherapy vs SP/CQ vs SP/AQ)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria over 6 months of age
primary_outcome: Clinical treatment failure after 14 days
impact_summary: Combination therapies (SP/CQ and especially SP/AQ) were safe and more efficacious than SP monotherapy for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with SP/AQ showing 0% treatment failure.
effect_metric: clinical treatment failure rate at day 14
safety_summary: Combination therapies were safe.

title: Therapeutic equivalence of a low dose artemisinin formulation in falciparum malaria patients.
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (therapeutic equivalence and parasite clearance) for a malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: uncomplicated falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: Therapeutic equivalence assessed via parasite clearance and cure rate
impact_summary: The 150 mg beta-cyclodextrin-artemisinin complex was therapeutically equivalent to 250 mg Artemisinin 250, with all patients in both groups cured and similar parasite clearance times of approximately three days.
safety_summary: All patients in both treatment groups were cured with no reported adverse events; both regimens were well tolerated.

title: A randomized, double-blind study on the efficacy and safety of a practical three-day regimen with artesunate and mefloquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Africa.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-mefloquine) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
comparator: active comparator (sequential dosing regimen of artesunate plus mefloquine)
population: hospitalized patients with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 14-day cure rate
impact_summary: A 3-day once-daily co-administered artesunate-mefloquine regimen achieved a 100% 14-day cure rate versus 98% with a sequential dosing regimen, with no recrudescence by day 28 and fewer episodes of vomiting.
safety_summary: Tolerability was good in both groups; vomiting was significantly less frequent in the investigational (simultaneous dosing) group compared to the reference (sequential dosing) group (3.8% vs. 19.2%, P = 0.014).

title: Mortality in a seven-and-a-half-year follow-up of a trial of insecticide-treated mosquito nets in Ghana.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated nets (a vector-control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results (mortality follow-up data).
comparator: no ITN / standard care (untreated nets or no nets)
population: children aged 6-59 months at trial start, followed into other age groups over time
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality
impact_summary: ITNs reduced all-cause mortality by 17% during the original trial period, and no increased mortality was observed in the ITN group after the intervention ended, over a 7.5-year follow-up.
age_range: 6-59 months (at enrollment), followed across age groups over 7.5 years
safety_summary: No evidence of increased mortality in the ITN group after the end of the randomized intervention period, in any age group.

title: Intrarectal pharmacokinetics of two formulations of quinine in children with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two quinine formulations in children with acute falciparum malaria, with reported outcome results (parasitaemia and pyrexia at 72h); primary purpose is malaria treatment.
population: children with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics/bioavailability of quinine (Cmax, tmax, relative bioavailability) after intrarectal vs intravenous administration
impact_summary: Intrarectal administration of quinine hydrochloride salt or Cinchona alkaloid mixture achieved similar blood concentration-time profiles and moderate relative bioavailability (57% and 62% respectively) compared to intravenous infusion, suggesting intrarectal quinine hydrochloride is a feasible delivery route in remote areas.
safety_summary: All children were aparasitaemic and apyretic at 72 h; no adverse events specifically reported.

title: House-scale evaluation of bifenthrin indoor residual spraying for malaria vector control in India.
screening_reason: Randomized house-scale trial of bifenthrin IRS for malaria vector control with reported entomological outcomes on mosquito mortality and density.
population: rural households in villages with malaria vector Anopheles culicifacies resistant to DDT, HCH, and malathion
primary_outcome: 24-hour mortality of Anopheles culicifacies in contact bioassays on sprayed surfaces over 24 weeks
impact_summary: Bifenthrin indoor residual spraying, particularly at the 25-mg/m2 dose, was superior to malathion in residual insecticidal efficacy and mosquito density reduction with least excito-repellency, making it the most favorable of the doses tested.
effect_metric: mortality (%) and duration of >=80% mortality persistence
effect_estimate: 25-mg dose maintained >=80% mortality for 24 wk on tin, 20 wk on mud, 16 wk on brick, 8 wk on wood surfaces; 100- and 200-mg doses maintained >=80% mortality for 24 wk on all surfaces
p_value: P < 0.05 (difference between 25- and 50-mg doses on wood surface)
transmission_setting: rural, DDT/HCH/malathion-resistant Anopheles culicifacies malaria vector area in India

title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial of tafenoquine for weekly prophylaxis against Plasmodium falciparum.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (tafenoquine) with reported outcome results on P. falciparum infection prevention in humans.
population: adult residents of northern Ghana
primary_outcome: positive malaria blood smear result during the 13 weeks of study drug coverage
impact_summary: All tafenoquine dosages (25-200 mg/week) and mefloquine significantly protected against P. falciparum infection compared to placebo, with 50, 100, and 200 mg/week doses being safe, well tolerated, and effective.
effect_estimate: 32% (25 mg), 84% (50 mg), 87% (100 mg), 86% (200 mg) tafenoquine; 86% mefloquine
safety_summary: There was little difference between study groups in adverse events reported, and no evidence of a relationship between tafenoquine dosage and physical complaints or abnormal laboratory parameters; doses of 50, 100, and 200 mg/week were safe and well tolerated.

title: [A study of artemether combined with primaquine in the treatment of falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemether+primaquine versus single artemether for falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (fever clearance, cure rates, relapse rates).
population: falciparum malaria cases
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time, clinical cure rate, and relapse rate
impact_summary: Artemether combined with primaquine reduced relapse rate of falciparum malaria more effectively than single artemether alone, with both regimens showing good therapeutic effects.
safety_summary: Side effects in cases of all groups were mild.

title: [Study on treatment of multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria by using a combination of dihydroartemisinin and pyronaridine].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing dihydroartemisinin/pyronaridine combination versus single agents for treatment of drug-resistant falciparum malaria in humans.
population: patients with multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate, fever subsidence time, asexual form clearance time, recrudescence rate, and gametocyte carriage rate
impact_summary: Combined dihydroartemisinin and pyronaridine treatment cleared parasites faster than pyronaridine alone and reduced fever faster than dihydroartemisinin alone, with lower gametocyte carriage than pyronaridine alone, supporting its use as an ideal regimen for multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Rate of side-effects was assessed among groups; specific rates not detailed in abstract.

title: [Clinical comparative trial of co-artemether and benflumetol (two formulations) in the treatment of falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment interventions (artemether-based drugs) in humans with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates).
comparator: active comparator (benflumetol tablet and benflumetol capsule)
population: hospitalized patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Co-artemether was more effective than benflumetol (both formulations) in clearing fever and parasites and achieved a higher 28-day cure rate, with no apparent side effects.
safety_summary: No apparent side-effect was observed in any treatment group.

title: Effects of chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine on gametocytes in patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Colombia.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in malaria patients with reported outcome results on gametocyte carriers.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: proportion of gametocyte carriers over time post-treatment
impact_summary: Gametocyte carriage was common overall (85%) and did not differ significantly between chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine groups, but patients with chloroquine treatment failure had an increased risk of carrying gametocytes on day 14 compared to those with adequate response.

title: Efficacy of chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and mefloquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria on the north coast of Peru.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (chloroquine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, mefloquine) for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs mefloquine)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum infections
primary_outcome: In vivo treatment response (RI/RII/RIII classification) and early/late treatment failure rates over 14 days
impact_summary: Chloroquine showed high failure rates while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and mefloquine were largely effective, with mefloquine showing no failures and SP showing few late failures.
transmission_setting: north coast of Peru, endemic region

title: Lack of prediction of mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate treatment outcome by mutations in the Plasmodium falciparum multidrug resistance 1 (pfmdr1) gene for P. falciparum malaria in Peru.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate for malaria treatment in humans with reported 28-day outcome results showing 100% clinical efficacy.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria in the Peruvian Amazon
primary_outcome: 28-day clinical treatment efficacy (parasite clearance) and correlation with pfmdr1 mutations
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and mefloquine-artesunate achieved 100% clinical efficacy over 28 days, and pfmdr1 mutations (C1034S, D1042N, Y1246D) did not predict treatment outcome.

title: Protective efficacy of the RTS,S/AS02 Plasmodium falciparum malaria vaccine is not strain specific.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS02) in humans with reported efficacy outcome results against natural P. falciparum infection.
population: semi-immune adults
primary_outcome: vaccine efficacy against natural P. falciparum infection during the malaria season following vaccination
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS02 vaccine efficacy against natural infection was 34%, and breakthrough infections showed no evidence of strain-specific selection based on csp genotyping.

title: Impact of preseason treatment on incidence of falciparum malaria and parasite density at a site for testing malaria vaccines in Bandiagara, Mali.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing malaria intervention (preseason chemoprevention with SP) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and parasite density.
population: residents of Bandiagara at a malaria vaccine testing site
primary_outcome: Cumulative and age-specific incidence of clinical malaria episodes
impact_summary: Preseason SP treatment delayed the median time to first clinical malaria episode from 38.5 to 68 days but did not reduce overall cumulative incidence, and after the initial protection period disease incidence in the treated group surpassed that of the untreated group; parasite densities during disease episodes were lower in the SP group.
effect_metric: median time to first clinical episode
transmission_setting: seasonal, high transmission area in Mali

title: Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine alone or with amodiaquine or artesunate for treatment of uncomplicated malaria: a longitudinal randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results; randomized allocation to three antimalarial regimens with clinical endpoints measured over 1-year follow-up.
comparator: sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine plus placebo (active comparator arms: amodiaquine or artesunate)
population: healthy children aged 6 months to 5 years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: total number of treatments for malaria per time at risk
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine reduced treatment failure and the rate of subsequent malaria episodes compared with sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine alone or with artesunate.
effect_metric: rate reduction in subsequent treatments for malaria
safety_summary: All regimens were safe and well tolerated.

title: Artesunate and mefloquine given simultaneously for three days via a prepacked blister is equally effective and tolerated as a standard sequential treatment of uncomplicated acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria: randomized, double-blind study in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment (artesunate + mefloquine combination) in humans with primary efficacy endpoint (day 28 cure rate) achieved.
population: adults and children with acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: Simultaneous three-day co-administration of artesunate and mefloquine via a prepacked blister was equally effective and well tolerated compared with the standard sequential regimen for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Tolerability was good in both groups with no difference in overall adverse event incidence; low incidence of nausea/vomiting (4.9% both groups) and CNS side effects (4.9% Group A vs 8.8% Group B), generally mild.

title: Treatment of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria with artesunate-atovaquone-proguanil.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-based regimens) in humans with reported outcome results; not early-phase.
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure/recrudescence confirmed by PCR genotyping
impact_summary: Adding artesunate to atovaquone-proguanil significantly reduced treatment failure and gametocyte carriage compared to atovaquone-proguanil alone, and all three regimens were highly effective and well tolerated.
p_value: P<.001 for fever/parasite clearance; P<=.014 for adverse events
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area on Thailand-Myanmar border
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated; gastrointestinal complaints more common with artesunate in first 48h, while dizziness, sleep disturbance, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia were more common with mefloquine after day 2.

title: Intramuscular bioavailability and clinical efficacy of artesunate in gabonese children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate (antimalarial drug) for treatment of severe malaria in children with reported clinical efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcomes.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics and bioavailability of intramuscular artesunate (DHA levels) and parasite clearance kinetics
impact_summary: Intramuscular artesunate was rapidly absorbed with good bioavailability and comparable parasite clearance to intravenous artesunate, with no major adverse events, supporting its use in severe childhood malaria.
safety_summary: No major adverse events attributable to artesunate were observed.

title: Radical curative efficacy of five-day regimen of primaquine for treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria in India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (primaquine regimen for P. vivax) with reported outcome results (recurrence rates).
population: cases of P. vivax malaria infection
primary_outcome: recurrence of parasitaemia with fever during 1 year follow-up
impact_summary: Adding a 5-day primaquine regimen to chloroquine did not significantly reduce recurrence of P. vivax infection compared to chloroquine alone.
transmission_setting: malaria endemic forested area with high prevalence of P. falciparum

title: Deferiprone (L1) as an adjuvant therapy for Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (deferiprone as adjuvant therapy for P. falciparum) with reported outcome results; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
comparator: placebo (added to standard quinine and doxycycline therapy)
population: patients with P. falciparum infection (severe malaria)
primary_outcome: time taken for resolution of parasitaemia, fever and coma, and final outcome (death or severe complications)
impact_summary: Deferiprone as adjuvant therapy significantly speeded resolution of fever, coma and parasitaemia clearance compared to placebo, though mortality difference was not statistically significant.
effect_estimate: faster resolution in deferiprone group; parasitaemia cleared 24 h earlier
p_value: P < 0.05 for fever/coma resolution; P > 0.05 for mortality
safety_summary: Deferiprone was well tolerated with no reported side effects.

title: Efficacy of atovaquone/proguanil for malaria prophylaxis in children and its effect on the immunogenicity of live oral typhoid and cholera vaccines.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (atovaquone/proguanil) with reported outcome results (97% efficacy against P. falciparum); not early-phase.
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against P. falciparum malaria and immunogenicity of typhoid and cholera vaccines (antibody titer changes)
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was highly effective for malaria prophylaxis (97% efficacy) and did not significantly interfere with the immunogenicity of oral typhoid and cholera vaccines.
p_value: P=.96 (anti-S. Typhi IgG), P=.07 (anti-S. Typhi IgA), P=.64 (vibriocidal antibodies)

title: Evidence for the efficacy of artesunate in asymptomatic Plasmodium malariae infections.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate (malaria treatment) with reported efficacy outcomes; phase unstated but post-Phase I.
population: asymptomatic Plasmodium malariae infected individuals
primary_outcome: parasitological cure rate on day 7 and day 56
impact_summary: A 3-day course of artesunate achieved 100% cure at day 7 and 83% at day 56, compared with no cure in the placebo group.
safety_summary: Artesunate was evaluated for safety; no adverse events specifically detailed in abstract.

title: The effects of chloroquine, amodiaquine and chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine on the disposition kinetics of the hepatomegaly associated with acute, uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine-based regimens) in children with P. falciparum malaria that reports outcome results on hepatomegaly resolution.
population: children with acute, symptomatic, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and hepatomegaly
primary_outcome: Resolution of hepatomegaly (liver enlargement) over time, including AUC of hepatomegaly vs time and half-life of hepatomegaly resolution
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine led to significantly faster and greater resolution of malaria-associated hepatomegaly compared to chloroquine alone or amodiaquine alone.

title: Malarial anemia leads to adequately increased erythropoiesis in asymptomatic Kenyan children.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria intervention (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, a malaria treatment/chemoprevention) in humans with primary focus on malaria and erythropoiesis.
population: anemic Kenyan children with asymptomatic malaria
primary_outcome: Erythropoiesis evaluated by serum concentrations of erythropoietin and soluble transferrin receptor relative to degree of anemia
impact_summary: Malarial infection increased erythropoietin and transferrin receptor levels while decreasing hemoglobin, indicating an adequate erythropoietic response to malarial anemia rather than one impaired by inflammation.

title: Chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine efficacy for uncomplicated malaria treatment and haematological recovery in children in Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso during a 3-year period 1998-2000.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (alternate allocation) of malaria treatment drugs (CQ vs SP) with reported outcome results (parasitological resistance, clinical failure, haematological recovery).
design: randomized, alternating allocation, in vivo test (WHO 14-day protocol), multi-year cohort
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological resistance and clinical failure to chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine at day 14, and haematological recovery (PCV)
impact_summary: Both chloroquine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine remained efficacious for treating uncomplicated malaria, though chloroquine showed higher parasitological resistance (18%) than SP (<1%), and SP-treated children had significantly lower anaemia prevalence at day 14 compared to CQ-treated children.
effect_metric: Relative risk (anaemia prevalence at day 14, CQ vs SP)
transmission_setting: endemic, seasonal malaria area in Burkina Faso
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy and haematological recovery rather than adverse events

title: Tolerability of doxycycline monohydrate salt vs. chloroquine-proguanil in malaria chemoprophylaxis.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria chemoprophylaxis interventions with reported outcome results (tolerability, compliance, adverse effects, malaria incidence); phase not applicable for preventive intervention in non-endemic population.
population: French soldiers deployed to Gabon and Chad
primary_outcome: Tolerability and compliance with malaria chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Doxycycline monohydrate was better tolerated and had higher compliance than chloroquine-proguanil, with fewer adverse effects and no significant difference in malaria incidence.
safety_summary: No major adverse events (evacuation or hospitalization) related to medications; epigastralgia, diarrhoea, urticaria, mouth ulcers, sun sensitization and desquamation significantly more frequent in the chloroquine-proguanil group (P < 0.05); no difference in vertigo, nausea, or hair loss.

title: Chlorproguanil-dapsone versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for sequential episodes of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Kenya and Malawi: a randomised clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chlorproguanil-dapsone versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and treatment failure.
population: paediatric outpatients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: annual malaria incidence
impact_summary: Children treated with chlorproguanil-dapsone did not have a higher incidence of malaria episodes than those treated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, despite its rapid elimination; treatment failure was more common with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
effect_metric: relative risk of annual malaria incidence
follow_up: up to 1 year (median 338 days Kenya CD, 120 days Malawi CD)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic areas in Kenya and Malawi
safety_summary: In Kenya, haemoglobin concentration of 50 g/L or less caused exit in 6.9% of chlorproguanil-dapsone patients versus 1.5% of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine patients, though most anaemia occurred before re-treatment; in Malawi only one patient exited due to anaemia; anaemia in Kenya was probably not an adverse reaction to chlorproguanil-dapsone.

title: Atovaquone/proguanil therapy for Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax malaria in Indonesians who lack clinical immunity.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of atovaquone/proguanil for malaria treatment with reported outcome results in humans; malaria prevention/treatment is the primary purpose.
population: Indonesians lacking clinical immunity to malaria who developed malaria during a chemoprophylaxis trial
primary_outcome: Efficacy and tolerability of atovaquone/proguanil therapy for uncomplicated P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was a safe, well-tolerated, and effective therapy for uncomplicated malaria in nonimmune Indonesians.
safety_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was safe and well-tolerated as therapy for uncomplicated malaria.

title: Prime-boost malaria vaccine in field trial.
screening_reason: Published field trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported outcome results in humans, phase not explicitly stated but consistent with advanced development.

title: Treatment of children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria with chloroquine in Guinea-Bissau.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine treatment for P. falciparum malaria in children with reported efficacy outcomes; phase not stated but malaria treatment trials are typically Phase III or later.
population: children with symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Recrudescence/parasitemia during 5-week follow-up
impact_summary: Treatment with chloroquine at a higher dose (50 mg/kg) was significantly more effective than the standard 25 mg/kg dose in preventing recrudescence of P. falciparum malaria.
effect_metric: relative risk of parasitemia (low-dose vs high-dose)
effect_estimate: 0.20 on day 21; 0.38 on day 28; 0.48 on day 35
safety_summary: Few adverse events reported overall; more vomiting and diarrhea on day 2 in the high-dose group compared with low-dose group, but difference not statistically significant.

title: The safety and efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine, and their combination in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (clinical and parasitological cure rates, safety endpoints) evaluating malaria treatment interventions (SP, AQ, AQ+SP) in humans.
comparator: active comparator (AQ vs SP vs AQ+SP arms)
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological cure rates at Day 28 (following WHO 28-day protocol)
impact_summary: Coadministered amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was safe and combined the greater efficacy of SP with the faster symptom resolution of AQ, while reducing gametocytemia compared to SP alone.
effect_estimate: AQ+SP: 96.2% clinical cure, 64.2% parasitological cure; SP alone: 93.7% clinical cure, 75% parasitological cure; AQ alone: 72.5% clinical cure, 55% parasitological cure
p_value: 0.03 (vomiting SP vs AQ); 0.001 (gametocytemia AQ+SP vs SP)
safety_summary: SP was associated with more vomiting during follow-up (32% vs 17%, P=0.03) and prolonged fever clearance times; coadministered AQ+SP was found to be safe.

title: Artemisinin or chloroquine for blood stage Plasmodium vivax malaria in Vietnam.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of antimalarial treatments (artemisinin vs chloroquine) for P. vivax blood-stage malaria with reported efficacy outcomes over 28-day follow-up.
population: inpatients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and rate of parasite reappearance (recrudescence) within 28 days
impact_summary: Artemisinin and chloroquine were equally effective in clearing P. vivax parasitemia, but parasite reappearance before day 16 in 7% of cases suggests emerging chloroquine resistance and 3 days of artemisinin monotherapy did not prevent recrudescence.
effect_metric: parasite reappearance rate at end of 4-week follow-up
safety_summary: All patients recovered rapidly; no chloroquine-resistant P. vivax reported prior to study; specific adverse events not detailed.

title: Effect of zinc on the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (zinc supplementation as adjunct to chloroquine) in humans; phase is appropriate (not early-phase).
population: children with fever and acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time to reduction of fever and reduction in parasitemia (>=75% reduction from baseline within first 72 h)
impact_summary: Zinc supplementation as an adjunct to chloroquine treatment showed no beneficial effect on time to fever reduction, parasitemia clearance, or hemoglobin concentration in children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
effect_metric: proportion with >=75% reduction in parasitemia at 72h
transmission_setting: multiple endemic settings across Africa and South America
safety_summary: No significant adverse safety issues reported; zinc supplementation increased plasma zinc concentrations at 72 h compared with placebo (P < 0.001).

title: Atovaquone plus chloroguanide versus mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis: a focus on neuropsychiatric adverse events.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results comparing malaria prophylaxis regimens (mefloquine vs atovaquone-proguanil) in travelers; primary purpose is malaria prevention intervention; outcome results on adverse events are clearly reported.
population: travelers to malaria-endemic areas attending the Travel Clinic, Rotterdam
primary_outcome: occurrence of neuropsychiatric adverse events (mood disturbance) and concentration impairment during malaria prophylaxis
impact_summary: Mefloquine prophylaxis was associated with significantly greater deterioration in mood (depression, anger, fatigue, vigor) compared to atovaquone plus chloroguanide, though sustained attention declined in both groups.
effect_estimate: higher depression, anger, and fatigue scores and lower vigor scores with mefloquine vs atovaquone plus chloroguanide
follow_up: from baseline to 7 days after leaving malaria-endemic area
safety_summary: Mefloquine use was associated with significantly worse neuropsychiatric adverse events including depression, anger, fatigue, and reduced vigor compared to atovaquone plus chloroguanide, particularly in female patients; sustained attention deteriorated in both groups after travel.

title: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of atovaquone/proguanil for the prevention of Plasmodium falciparum or Plasmodium vivax malaria among migrants to Papua, Indonesia.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (atovaquone/proguanil) in humans; efficacy primary endpoint measured for P. vivax and P. falciparum prevention.
population: non-immune migrants from areas of malaria non-endemicity in Indonesia who moved to Papua within 26 months before the study
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. falciparum or P. vivax malaria during prophylaxis period
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was significantly more effective than placebo in preventing both P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria among non-immune migrants to Papua, Indonesia.
effect_estimate: 93% overall (84% for P. vivax, 96% for P. falciparum)
effect_ci: 95% CI 77%-98% overall; 44%-95% for P. vivax; 72%-99% for P. falciparum
safety_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was well tolerated and safe; hematologic and clinical chemistry values did not change significantly.

title: Short report: therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine combined with primaquine against Plasmodium falciparum in northeastern Papua, Indonesia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine + primaquine vs placebo) with reported outcome results on therapeutic efficacy.
population: nonimmune Javanese migrants with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 14-day cumulative incidence of therapeutic failure
impact_summary: Adding daily primaquine to chloroquine marginally improved therapeutic efficacy at day 14 but showed no significant benefit at day 7 or day 28, indicating primaquine has little discernible effect on P. falciparum parasitemia.
effect_metric: odds ratio for therapeutic failure at day 14
transmission_setting: northeastern Papua, Indonesia, area with malaria transmission among nonimmune migrants

title: The efficacy of artemether versus quinine in the treatment of cerebral malaria.
journal: Journal of the Egyptian Society of Parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether vs quinine) in humans with reported outcome results (fever clearance time, consciousness recovery, parasite clearance, cure rate, sequelae, mortality).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Response to therapy evaluated using fever clearance time (FCT), time of regaining consciousness (TRC) and parasite clearance time (PCT)
impact_summary: Artemether showed slightly better fever clearance, time to regain consciousness, and parasite clearance than quinine, but differences were not statistically significant, with comparable cure rate, neurological sequelae, and case fatality.
effect_metric: mean difference in fever clearance time, time to regain consciousness, and parasite clearance time
effect_estimate: FCT 32 vs 36 hrs; TRC 21 vs 26 hrs; PCT 36 vs 41 hrs (artemether vs quinine)
follow_up: until resolution of illness (approx. 7 days treatment course)
safety_summary: Cure rate, neurological sequelae, and case fatality were comparable between artemether and quinine groups.

title: [Diluted injectable quinine in the intramuscular and intrarectal route: comparative efficacity and tolerance in malaria treatment for children ].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two routes of injectable quinine for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results on efficacy and tolerance.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria presenting with vomiting, single seizure with postictal coma, or prostration
primary_outcome: Clinical efficacy (temperature curve) and tolerance of diluted injectable quinine by intramuscular versus intrarectal route
impact_summary: No significant difference was found between intramuscular and intrarectal diluted quinine in clinical effectiveness or parasite clearance, and the intrarectal route was well tolerated, supporting its use as an alternative administration route in outlying health care settings.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic outlying health care units in Togo
safety_summary: 25% of intrarectal group required re-administration due to insufficient retention; 12.5% of intramuscular group had residual injection site pain; endoscopic exam showed no anorectal ulceration or necrosis.

title: Population pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling of artemisinin and mefloquine enantiomers in patients with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin and mefloquine combination for malaria treatment with reported pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic outcome results.
population: male and female patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling of artemisinin and mefloquine enantiomers, and parasite clearance
impact_summary: All patients were successfully treated regardless of regimen, with no significant pharmacokinetic interactions between artemisinin and mefloquine, though the fastest parasite clearance occurred when both drugs were given together on day 1.
effect_estimate: RS-mefloquine 3.51 l/h; SR-mefloquine 0.602 l/h; artemisinin oral clearance 6.9-fold higher on last day vs first day
safety_summary: All patients were successfully treated regardless of treatment; no adverse events specifically reported.

title: Treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children in Guinea-Bissau with chloroquine, quinine, and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug regimens in children with uncomplicated malaria; reports efficacy outcomes at day 28 follow-up.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine, quinine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine regimens compared against each other)
population: children with symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: Presence of parasitaemia on day 28 after treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine at an increased dose of 50 mg/kg was as effective as sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, while quinine-based regimens had significantly higher treatment failure rates by day 28.
effect_estimate: 2.9 (group 1 vs group 4); 2.1 (group 2 vs group 4); 1.3 (group 3 vs group 4)
safety_summary: No severe adverse reaction was observed in any of the treatment groups.

title: Artemether vs quinine therapy in Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Manipur--a preliminary report.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether vs quinine for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, fever resolution, coma recovery, adverse effects).
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and clinical outcomes (fever resolution, coma recovery, mortality)
impact_summary: Artemether cleared parasites faster and was associated with fewer deaths and fewer serious adverse effects than quinine in the treatment of P. falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Artemether was associated only with gastrointestinal intolerance; quinine was associated with myocarditis, hypotension, hypoglycemia, and GI intolerance.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine and the sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine-amodiaquine combination against uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in young children in Cameroon.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, amodiaquine, and their combination) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results through day 28 follow-up.
comparator: active comparator (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine vs combination)
population: young children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological and clinical response (therapeutic efficacy) at day 28 according to modified 1996 WHO protocol
impact_summary: The sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine-amodiaquine combination had 0% therapeutic failure by day 28, outperforming sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (13.6% failure) and amodiaquine alone (10.2% failure), though with increased minor side-effects.
safety_summary: AQ associated with more transient minor side-effects than SP; SP+AQ increased incidence of minor side-effects but was generally well tolerated; anaemia improved in all three regimens.

title: [Treatment of cerebral malaria in African children by intravenous quinine: comparison of a loading dose regimen to a regimen without a loading dose].
journal: Archives de pediatrie : organe officiel de la Societe francaise de pediatrie
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing intravenous quinine regimens for cerebral malaria treatment in African children.
comparator: active comparator (quinine regimen without loading dose)
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy and toxicity (coma duration, parasitemia clearance, case-fatality, cardiovascular tolerance) of loading dose vs non-loading dose intravenous quinine regimens
impact_summary: Both quinine regimens (with and without a loading dose) showed similar coma duration, parasitemia clearance, and case-fatality rates, but the loading dose regimen was better tolerated in terms of temperature control and was less costly, suggesting it is slightly more effective.
safety_summary: No significant cardiovascular toxicity observed via ECG monitoring in either group; a significant increase in body temperature was noted between 51st and 63rd hour in the group without loading dose.

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine monotherapy in Tanzanian children gives rapid parasite clearance but slow fever clearance that is improved by chloroquine in combination therapy.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes testing malaria treatment (SP±CQ±paracetamol) in children with uncomplicated malaria; results on parasite and fever clearance reported.
comparator: chloroquine alone, SP plus chloroquine, SP plus paracetamol
population: children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: time to fever clearance and time to parasite clearance
impact_summary: SP plus CQ combination therapy resulted in significantly faster fever clearance than SP alone, while SP alone produced rapid parasite clearance comparable to CQ alone.
effect_metric: median survival time to fever clearance
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; treatment failures occurred in 20.5% of the CQ alone group within 72 h, none in other groups.

title: Pharmacokinetics of sequential and simultaneous treatment with the combination chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Philippines.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (chloroquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcome results in 32 acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria patients.
design: randomized (two-group comparison, sequential vs simultaneous regimen)
comparator: active comparator (sequential CQ+SP vs simultaneous CQ+SP)
population: patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times, parasite elimination half-life, and treatment outcome (efficacy) of sequential vs simultaneous CQ+SP treatment
impact_summary: Simultaneous administration of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine on Day 0 was more efficacious (faster parasite and fever clearance) than sequential administration, with both regimens well tolerated.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with minimal side-effects, mainly nausea and vomiting.

title: Sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine: an appropriate first-line alternative for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Ghanaian children under 5 years of age.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (CQ vs SP) in children with reported outcome results (parasitological, clinical, and haematological responses).
population: children under 5 years of age with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological, clinical and haematological response to treatment assessed via modified WHO 28-day in vivo protocol (treatment failure and resistance classification)
impact_summary: Sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine showed markedly lower early and late clinical treatment failure and resistance rates compared with chloroquine in Ghanaian children under 5 years old.
safety_summary: No difference in haematological response between the two treatment groups; no other adverse events reported.

title: A randomized comparison of chloroquine, amodiaquine and their combination with pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in the treatment of acute, uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug treatments (chloroquine, amodiaquine, and combinations) for P. falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, cure rates, adverse events).
population: children with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite-clearance time and cure rate on days 14, 21, and 28
impact_summary: Combination treatments (chloroquine or amodiaquine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine) resulted in significantly higher cure rates and faster parasite clearance than monotherapy, particularly chloroquine alone.
safety_summary: Adverse reactions were tolerable and similar across groups except pruritus, which was significantly more common with chloroquine alone; haematological and biochemical parameters were not adversely affected.

title: Clinical efficacy of chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children under five from south-western Uganda with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results (treatment failure rates).
population: children under five with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate at day 14
impact_summary: Chloroquine had a much higher treatment failure rate (81.1%) than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (25.0%) for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children under five.

title: Dose-finding and efficacy study for i.m. artemotil (beta-arteether) and comparison with i.m. artemether in acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy outcomes (parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, recrudescence) comparing artemotil and artemether doses for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time (and fever clearance time)
impact_summary: Both artemotil dose regimens tested achieved full parasite clearance but had significantly longer parasite clearance times than the standard artemether regimen, though safety was comparable.
effect_metric: mean difference in parasite clearance time (hours)
effect_estimate: A vs R: 52h vs 43h; C vs R: 55h vs 43h
effect_ci: A vs R: 0-16 h; C vs R: 2-19 h
safety_summary: No clinically relevant neurological or audiometric findings; adverse events (headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain) were characteristic of malaria and resolved during treatment.

title: A pilot study of N-acetylcysteine as adjunctive therapy for severe malaria.
journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing NAC as adjunctive therapy for severe malaria; phase not stated but pilot design with objective outcome measures reported.
population: adult males with severe, quinine-treated malaria
primary_outcome: serum lactate level (time to normalization)
impact_summary: N-acetylcysteine adjunctive therapy normalized serum lactate levels twice as fast as placebo in patients with severe malaria.
safety_summary: NAC did not markedly alter plasma cytokine profiles; described as a safe compound with no major adverse effects reported.

title: Amodiaquine-artesunate versus amodiaquine for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in African children: a randomised, multicentre trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (amodiaquine-artesunate combination) in children with reported outcome results (parasitological cure rates at days 14 and 28).
population: children with uncomplicated P falciparum malaria, 10 years or older (age noted as inclusion criterion)
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure rates at days 14 and 28
impact_summary: Amodiaquine-artesunate improved treatment efficacy compared to amodiaquine alone in Kenya and Gabon, and was equivalent to amodiaquine in Sénégal.
p_value: Kenya p<0.0001; Sénégal p=0.5; Gabon p=0.02 (day 28)
