safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; six patients in the amodiaquine-artesunate group and five in the amodiaquine group developed early drug-induced vomiting requiring alternative treatment.

title: A randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and quinine in the treatment of cerebral malaria in Bangladesh.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (case fatality, fever clearance, parasite clearance, coma resolution) comparing artemether and quinine for cerebral malaria treatment in humans.
population: adults with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Case fatality, fever clearance time, and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether was as effective as parenteral quinine in treating cerebral malaria in adults, with no significant differences in case fatality, fever, or parasite clearance times, though coma resolution was significantly delayed with artemether.
safety_summary: Coma resolution time was significantly delayed in artemether recipients compared to quinine recipients; no other significant differences reported.

title: Malaria prevention in highland Kenya: indoor residual house-spraying vs. insecticide-treated bednets.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector-control interventions (IRS and ITNs) with reported outcome results on P. falciparum infection prevalence.
population: residents of homesteads in three age-groups: 6 months-4 years, 5-15 years, and >15 years
primary_outcome: Prevalence of P. falciparum infection (Pf HRP-2 antigenemia) detected by rapid immunochromatographic test
impact_summary: Both indoor residual spraying and insecticide-treated bednets reduced the risk of P. falciparum infection compared to no protection, with IRS showing a greater reduction and lower cost per case prevented than ITNs.
transmission_setting: low, seasonal transmission in highland Kenya

title: A recombinant blood-stage malaria vaccine reduces Plasmodium falciparum density and exerts selective pressure on parasite populations in a phase 1-2b trial in Papua New Guinea.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria vaccine (blood-stage) with reported outcome results showing parasite density reduction in a phase 1-2b trial.
population: children 5-9 years old with previous malaria exposure
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum parasite density
impact_summary: The Combination B vaccine reduced P. falciparum parasite density by 62% in children not pretreated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and exerted selective pressure on parasite populations based on MSP2 genotype.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area of Papua New Guinea

title: Artemisinin pharmacokinetics and efficacy in uncomplicated-malaria patients treated with two different dosage regimens.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin treatment for uncomplicated malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times and pharmacokinetic findings).
population: adult male and female uncomplicated falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and artemisinin pharmacokinetics
impact_summary: The escalating dose regimen resulted in longer parasite clearance time and altered pharmacokinetics but did not produce higher artemisinin concentrations at the end of treatment compared to the fixed-dose regimen.

title: Oral artesunate dose-response relationship in acute falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of oral artesunate for acute falciparum malaria treatment with reported pharmacodynamic outcome results (parasite clearance time).
comparator: different artesunate dose levels (0 to 250 mg) with mefloquine
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria and parasitemia >= 1%
primary_outcome: Acceleration of parasite clearance (shortening of parasite clearance time)
impact_summary: There was no additional reduction in parasite clearance time with single oral artesunate doses higher than 2 mg/kg, indicating this as the average lower limit of the maximally effective dose.
effect_metric: 50% effective dose (ED50) for shortening of parasite clearance time

title: Malaria control--two years' use of insecticide-treated bednets compared with insecticide house spraying in KwaZulu-Natal.
journal: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets versus house spraying (vector-control interventions) for malaria with reported outcome results (malaria incidence rate ratios).
population: communities in malaria high-risk areas (Ndumu and Makanis)
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence comparing insecticide-treated bednets versus insecticide house spraying
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednets significantly reduced malaria incidence compared with house spraying over 2 years, with a 16% reduction in bednet areas versus a 45% increase in sprayed areas.

title: A randomized controlled trial on the efficacy of alternative treatment regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in a multidrug-resistant falciparum area of Bangladesh--narrowing the options for the National Malaria Control Programme?
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment regimens with reported outcome results (treatment failures and clinical/parasitological outcomes).
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine, quinine+SP, quinine 7-day, mefloquine compared against each other)
population: symptomatic patients aged 12 years and older with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, parasite density 500-250,000/mm3, no antimalarial use in previous week
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment failure (early treatment failure and RII/RIII parasitological failure) by day 28
impact_summary: Chloroquine had significantly more clinical and parasitological treatment failures than the other regimens, leading the authors to recommend quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as a better, though still imperfect, first-line therapy.
effect_metric: RII and RIII parasitological failure rate
effect_estimate: 56% (Group I, chloroquine), 12% (Group II, Q3+SP), 8% (Group III, Q7), 14% (Group IV, mefloquine)
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria area of Bangladesh
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy outcomes with early treatment failures noted only in the chloroquine group

title: Co-trimoxazole compared with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Kenyan children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment interventions in children with reported 14-day parasitological and clinical outcome results.
population: children under 5 years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological and clinical treatment failure at 14 days
impact_summary: Co-trimoxazole and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine had similar efficacy and risk of treatment failure for uncomplicated malaria in Kenyan children.

title: Randomized comparison of quinine-clindamycin versus artesunate in the treatment of falciparum malaria in pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (day-42 cure rates) comparing two malaria treatments in pregnant women; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
population: pregnant women with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in 2nd or 3rd trimester
primary_outcome: Day-42 cure rate
impact_summary: Both quinine-clindamycin and artesunate regimens achieved 100% day-42 cure rates with no difference in efficacy, though artesunate resulted in less gametocyte carriage and less tinnitus.
p_value: P < 0.01 for gametocyte carriage; P < 0.001 for tinnitus
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum endemic area, western border of Thailand
safety_summary: No difference in gastrointestinal symptoms between groups; significantly more tinnitus in quinine-clindamycin group (44.9%) versus artesunate group (8.9%), RR 5.1 (95% CI 1.9-13.5).

title: Molecular markers for failure of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and chlorproguanil-dapsone treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of malaria treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and chlorproguanil-dapsone) that reports outcome results (treatment failure rates stratified by parasite genotypes).
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and chlorproguanil-dapsone associated with DHFR/DHPS genotypes
impact_summary: Parasites carrying the 'quintuple mutant' (3 DHFR mutations plus 2 DHPS mutations) were associated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failure but not chlorproguanil-dapsone failure, and a simpler two-mutation marker (DHFR Arg-59 plus DHPS Glu-540) accurately predicted the presence of the quintuple mutant.

title: Randomized trial of artesunate and mefloquine in comparison with quinine sulfate to treat P. falciparum malaria pregnant women.
journal: Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand = Chotmaihet thangphaet
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate/mefloquine vs quinine) in pregnant women with P. falciparum infection that has reported clinical outcome results including parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, and adverse effects.
population: second to third trimester pregnant women with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time (PCT) and fever clearance time (FCT), and maternal/fetal safety outcomes
impact_summary: Artesunate with mefloquine cleared parasites and fever faster than quinine sulfate, had fewer adverse effects, and was associated with better fetal outcomes, though no significant differences in placental calcification or IUGR were found between groups.
effect_metric: difference in parasite clearance time (PCT) and fever clearance time (FCT)
effect_estimate: PCT and FCT significantly shorter in artesunate+mefloquine group than quinine sulfate group
transmission_setting: Mae Hong Son, Thailand (malaria-endemic border region)
age_range: pregnant women, second to third trimester
safety_summary: Group I (quinine sulfate) had more adverse effects than group II (artesunate/mefloquine); no adverse neurological effects in pregnancy were found in either group; no congenital abnormalities in infants at 2, 4, 6, and 12 months follow-up.

title: Cardiac effects of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in malaria-infected African patients.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (parasitological and clinical responses).
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cardiac effects (electrocardiographic changes including bradycardia and interval prolongation) of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Amodiaquine caused significant but clinically asymptomatic bradycardia and prolongation of ECG intervals, while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine caused only minor and transient ECG changes, with no cardiovascular adverse effects reported by patients.
effect_estimate: 16 of 20 amodiaquine-treated patients on Day 2; 12 of 20 on Day 7
safety_summary: No patients complained of cardiovascular adverse effects; bradycardia and ECG interval prolongation observed with amodiaquine were not clinically symptomatic; sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine caused only minor, transient ECG changes.

title: Artemisinin for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria: is there a place for monotherapy?
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin monotherapy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times and recrudescence rates).
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, adults and children under 15 years
primary_outcome: recrudescence rate and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Extending artemisinin monotherapy from 5 to 7 days did not reduce recrudescence rates despite similar rapid parasite clearance.

title: Efficacy of mefloquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum infection in Machinga District, Malawi, 1998.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (SP vs mefloquine) in children with P. falciparum with reported parasitologic efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: Parasitologic treatment failure (RII/RIII) by day 14/28
impact_summary: Both sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and mefloquine showed high failure rates (20.0% and 22.0% respectively), with mefloquine failures strongly associated with low day 2 drug levels, suggesting neither drug is fully adequate as a first-line treatment.
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed beyond drug level and failure associations; no major safety signals reported.

title: Efficacy of RTS,S/AS02 malaria vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum infection in semi-immune adult men in The Gambia: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results for a malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS02) against P. falciparum infection in humans.
population: semi-immune adult men
primary_outcome: time to first infection with P. falciparum
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS02 significantly delayed and reduced natural P. falciparum infection compared with control, with efficacy waning over the transmission season and boosted by a fourth dose the following year.
safety_summary: RTS,S/AS02 was safe and well tolerated.

title: A comparison of oral artesunate and artemether antimalarial bioactivities in acute falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate vs artemether) in humans with reported outcome results (pharmacokinetics and antimalarial activity).
comparator: active comparator (oral artemether vs oral artesunate)
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: comparative oral antimalarial bioavailability and pharmacokinetics (area under plasma antimalarial activity time curve and maximum plasma antimalarial activity)
impact_summary: Oral artesunate produced significantly greater antimalarial bioactivity (AUC and Cmax) than oral artemether, with artemether's relative bioavailability being only about 58% of artesunate's despite a lower molar dose.
effect_metric: relative oral antimalarial bioavailability of artemether vs artesunate
p_value: P ≤ 0.02 (AUC/Cmax comparison); P = 0.018 (day 1 vs day 2 bioavailability)
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; no specific adverse events described.

title: Treatment of falciparum malaria in Vietnamese children: the need for combination therapy and optimized dosage regimens.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate vs mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results on parasitological recrudescence/re-infection over 28 days.
population: children and adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria without previous treatment
primary_outcome: Recrudescence/re-infection (parasitaemia) during 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Children had significantly higher rates of treatment failure than adults, especially with mefloquine, supporting combination therapy and higher pediatric dosing.

title: Randomized, parallel placebo-controlled trial of primaquine for malaria prophylaxis in Papua, Indonesia.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing primaquine for malaria prevention (chemoprophylaxis) in humans, not early-phase.
population: G6PD-normal Javanese transmigrants (nonpregnant adults)
primary_outcome: Incidence of parasitemia (malaria infection) over 20 weeks of prophylaxis
impact_summary: Daily primaquine prophylaxis was 93% effective at preventing malaria compared to placebo, with only 2 of 97 primaquine recipients becoming parasitemic versus 37 of 149 placebo recipients.
safety_summary: Primaquine was as well tolerated as placebo; mild methemoglobinemia (mean 3.4%) resolved within 2 weeks; no evidence of toxicity in blood chemistry or hematological parameters.

title: A comparison of artesunate alone with combined artesunate and quinine in the parenteral treatment of acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment interventions (artesunate vs. artesunate plus quinine) with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and adverse events in P. falciparum malaria patients.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate plus quinine vs artesunate alone)
population: patients with uncomplicated and severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Combining artesunate and quinine did not improve parasite clearance time compared to artesunate alone and was associated with more frequent adverse events, showing no benefit to combination parenteral therapy.
safety_summary: Adverse events were significantly more frequent in the artesunate plus quinine group (P = 0.05); quinine had no significant antipyretic effect; artesunate did not affect the QTc interval.

title: A new primaquine analogue, tafenoquine (WR 238605), for prophylaxis against Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Double-blinded randomized controlled trial of tafenoquine for malaria prevention with reported efficacy outcomes; primary purpose is malaria intervention (chemoprevention); not early-phase (dose-ranging Phase 2 acceptable).
population: adult volunteers
primary_outcome: protective efficacy against Plasmodium falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Weekly tafenoquine prophylaxis at 200 mg or 400 mg after a 3-day loading dose was highly effective and well tolerated in preventing falciparum malaria compared with placebo.
effect_estimate: 68% (400 mg 3-day only), 86% (200 mg loading + 200 mg weekly), 89% (400 mg loading + 400 mg weekly)
safety_summary: A similar number of volunteers in the 4 treatment groups reported adverse events; regimens were well tolerated.

title: Control of malaria vectors with the insect growth regulator pyriproxyfen in a gem-mining area in Sri Lanka.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector control (insect growth regulator) for malaria with reported outcome results (malaria incidence and prevalence).
population: residents of gem-mining villages, including symptomless individuals surveyed for parasitaemia
primary_outcome: incidence of malaria cases and prevalence of parasitaemia in intervention versus control villages
impact_summary: Treating gem pits and river pools with pyriproxyfen significantly reduced adult vector populations and cut malaria incidence to about 24% of that in control villages.
transmission_setting: gem-mining area with breeding sites in shallow pits and river bed pools; stratified into high and low transmission villages

title: Anemia of persistent malarial parasitemia in Nigerian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs. fansidar) in children with reported outcome results (parasite counts, PCV levels, treatment efficacy).
population: children aged 0-60 months with malaria parasitemia
primary_outcome: packed cell volume (PCV) levels and parasite clearance in relation to persistent malaria parasitemia
impact_summary: Fansidar produced faster parasite clearance and hematological recovery (7 days) than chloroquine (21 days), with high levels of drug resistance observed in both groups.
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; focus was on parasite resistance (RII resistance found in 81 of 100 patients) rather than adverse events.

title: Therapy of uncomplicated falciparum malaria: a randomized trial comparing artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone in Irian Jaya, Indonesia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results including treatment failure rates, fever clearance, and parasite clearance.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate at day 14 and day 28
impact_summary: Combined artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resulted in more rapid fever and parasite clearance, was well tolerated, reduced risk of treatment failure, and lowered gametocyte carriage compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.
effect_metric: relative risk of treatment failure at 28 days
safety_summary: Mild diarrhea, rash, and itching occurred and resolved without treatment.

title: Safety of the insect repellent N,N-diethyl-M-toluamide (DEET) in pregnancy.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of DEET insect repellent for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported safety outcomes; malaria prevention is the primary focus and results are published.
population: pregnant women in second and third trimesters
primary_outcome: Safety of DEET application (adverse neurologic, gastrointestinal, dermatologic effects; fetal/infant survival, growth, development)
impact_summary: Daily DEET application during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy showed no adverse neurologic, gastrointestinal, or dermatologic effects, and no adverse effects on survival, growth, or development at birth or one year, with low placental transfer detected in 8% of cord blood samples.
effect_metric: proportion of cord blood samples with detectable DEET
safety_summary: No adverse neurologic, gastrointestinal, or dermatologic effects observed; DEET crossed the placenta and was detected in 8% of cord blood samples; no adverse effects on survival, growth, or development at birth or at one year.

title: [Value of malaria prophylaxis in surgical intervention in a malaria endemic zone , Niamey, Niger].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prophylaxis (chloroquine) intervention in humans in an endemic setting.
population: surgical patients
primary_outcome: Presence of malaria parasitemia (thick smear positivity) postoperatively
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis significantly reduced malaria infection rates in surgical patients, especially those with surgery lasting more than 1 hour and general anaesthesia.
transmission_setting: malaria endemic zone with moderate chloroquine resistance

title: Randomized comparison of chloroquine and amodiaquine in the treatment of acute, uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) for Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results including cure rates, parasite-clearance times, and adverse events.
population: Children with acute, symptomatic, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure) at days 14, 21 and 28, along with fever- and parasite-clearance times
impact_summary: Amodiaquine produced significantly faster fever and parasite clearance and higher cure rates than chloroquine in Nigerian children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: Area with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum, endemic setting in Nigeria
safety_summary: Adverse reactions similar and tolerable in both groups; pruritus in 10 (AQ) and 11 (CQ) children, gastrointestinal disturbances in 3 children per group; haematological parameters unaffected by either drug.

title: [Intrarectal administration of quinine: an early treatment for severe malaria in children?].
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing intrarectal quinine with IV/IM routes for severe malaria treatment in children with reported mortality and clinical outcomes.
population: children with cerebral malaria or severe malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical efficacy and mortality of intrarectal quinine compared with intravenous or intramuscular quinine in severe/cerebral malaria
impact_summary: Intrarectal quinine showed similar clinical efficacy, parasite clearance and mortality compared with intravenous or intramuscular quinine, with good tolerance, in children with severe or cerebral malaria.
effect_estimate: 0% (QIR) vs 7.6% (IM) in severe malaria; 4/... vs 9/... deaths in cerebral malaria
safety_summary: QIR was well tolerated with no reported major adverse effects; associated symptomatic treatments given for hyperthermia, hypoglycemia, anemia and seizures.

title: Gametocytaemia in Senegalese children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria treated with chloroquine, amodiaquine or sulfadoxine + pyrimethamine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (three antimalarial drugs) in humans with reported outcome results (gametocytaemia measurements).
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte prevalence and density following treatment with chloroquine, amodiaquine, or sulfadoxine + pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Gametocyte prevalence and density were higher after treatment with sulfadoxine+pyrimethamine than chloroquine, and higher with chloroquine than amodiaquine, with higher gametocytaemia also seen in drug-resistant infections and with longer delay before treatment.
effect_metric: gametocyte prevalence and geometric mean density

title: Malaria prophylaxis/radical cure: recent experiences of the Australian Defence Force.
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (tafenoquine vs placebo/primaquine) with reported outcome results in humans.
population: soldiers (Thai soldiers for prophylaxis study; Australian Defence Force soldiers deployed to Bougainville for radical cure study)
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria (prophylaxis study: falciparum/vivax malaria infection; radical cure study: vivax malaria relapse after treatment)
impact_summary: Tafenoquine was highly effective for malaria prophylaxis compared to placebo, and for radical cure of vivax malaria it was found to be non-inferior but not superior to a 14-day course of primaquine, though better tolerated due to shorter course.
effect_estimate: Prophylaxis: 1/104 (tafenoquine) vs 28/101 (placebo); Radical cure: 7/201 (tafenoquine) vs 7/210 (primaquine) developed vivax malaria
follow_up: 6 months (prophylaxis study); until return to Australia and follow-up (radical cure study)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic areas including Cambodia, Somalia, Rwanda, Bougainville, and East Timor
safety_summary: Tafenoquine was well tolerated; participants preferred the shorter tafenoquine course over the 14-day primaquine regimen and it was operationally more suitable.

title: A trial of proguanil-dapsone in comparison with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the clearance of Plasmodium falciparum infections in Tanzania.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments (proguanil-dapsone vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in malaria-infected children with reported efficacy outcome results; phase not stated but treatment trial eligible.
population: children with asymptomatic falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Clearance of asexual parasites at day 7
impact_summary: Proguanil-dapsone achieved markedly higher day 7 parasite clearance (93.5%) than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (14.3%), and both regimens were well tolerated.
transmission_setting: north-eastern Tanzania, area with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well tolerated.

title: Causal prophylactic efficacy of atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone) in a human challenge model.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (atovaquone-proguanil) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia and clinical malaria); human challenge model is phase II appropriate.
population: healthy volunteers challenged with P. falciparum via infected mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Development of parasitaemia and malarial symptoms after mosquito challenge
impact_summary: All 4 placebo volunteers developed parasitaemia and malaria symptoms, while none of the 12 atovaquone-proguanil recipients acquired malaria, demonstrating causal prophylactic (liver-stage) efficacy allowing discontinuation 7 days after exposure.
transmission_setting: experimental human challenge model via infected mosquitoes
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond noting placebo group developed malaria symptoms; no adverse events specifically reported for atovaquone-proguanil group in abstract.

title: Insecticide-treated materials, mosquito adaptation and mass effect: entomological observations after five years of vector control in Burkina Faso.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results on insecticide-treated materials vector control for malaria prevention with 5 years of follow-up entomological data.
population: communities in villages with and without insecticide-treated curtains
primary_outcome: mosquito vector density, resistance/behavioural adaptation, sporozoite rates
impact_summary: After 5 years of insecticide-treated curtain use in Burkina Faso, vector densities remained low with no evidence of mosquito resistance selection or a shift to outdoor biting, though vector densities and sporozoite rates were higher at the periphery of the intervention zone.

title: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of vitamin A in severe malaria in hospitalised Mozambican children.
screening_reason: Randomised controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (vitamin A supplementation in severe malaria) in hospitalised children.
population: hospitalised children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: survival, recovery during hospitalisation and outcome 6 weeks after discharge
impact_summary: Vitamin A supplementation showed a non-statistically significant reduction in overall mortality among children with severe malaria, though a significant reduction was seen after the first 5 hours of admission.
safety_summary: Neurological sequelae occurred in 4/82 (4.9%) of the vitamin A group vs 2/78 (2.6%) in the placebo group (RR 1.90; 95% CI 0.36-10.09; p = 0.682); no other safety concerns reported.

title: Efficacy of Sulphadoxine and Pyrimethamine, Doxycycline and their combination in the treatment of chloroquine resistant Falciparum Malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum) with reported efficacy outcomes in human patients.
comparator: active comparator (doxycycline vs sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine vs combination)
population: Febrile patients with chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological and clinical response) after treatment, assessed daily for 6 days and weekly for 4 weeks
impact_summary: Combination therapy of sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine plus doxycycline achieved a 90-100% cure rate within 3-4 days, significantly higher than doxycycline alone (46%) or sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine alone (78%), with no relapses and good tolerability.
safety_summary: All treatments were well tolerated; a few cases reported nausea; no serious side effects observed.

title: [Assessment of the response to reduced treatment schemes for vivax malaria].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (vivax) in humans with reported outcome results (symptom clearance, parasitaemia clearance) comparing three therapeutic schemes.
comparator: active comparator (classical chloroquine/primaquine schedule vs two reduced-dose schedules)
population: outpatients with vivax malaria aged over 12 years
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological response (symptom resolution and parasitaemia clearance) to reduced treatment schedules compared with classical schedule
impact_summary: All three chloroquine-primaquine treatment schedules, including reduced-dose regimens, produced satisfactory clinical responses with symptom resolution within 96 hours and parasitaemia clearance within 72 hours.
safety_summary: Reduced schedules maintained similar tolerance and minimal adverse reactions compared to the classical schedule.

title: Clinical trial of halofantrine with modified doses for treatment of malaria in the hospital for tropical diseases.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of halofantrine (antimalarial drug) for malaria treatment with reported cure-rate outcomes; not early-phase.
population: falciparum malaria cases treated at hospital for tropical diseases
primary_outcome: cure rate
impact_summary: Halofantrine given as 500 mg three times on day one followed by 500 mg once daily for 7 days achieved the highest cure rate (97%) with no significant overt cardiac problems, and was significantly better than the 3000 mg regimen.
p_value: significant difference between HA3 and HA2 groups (exact p value not stated)
safety_summary: No overt cardiac problems were observed in this study.

title: The impact of insecticide-treated bednets on malaria and anaemia in pregnancy in Kassena-Nankana district, Ghana: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control) for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported outcome results.
population: pregnant women, primigravidae and secundigravidae
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia, anaemia, and low birthweight in the third trimester/at delivery
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednet use showed no significant benefit for reducing malaria parasitaemia, anaemia, or low birthweight in pregnant women.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; chloroquine use in pregnancy was low and comparable between groups.

title: Ketotifen in treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (ketotifen combinations vs. chloroquine) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, recrudescence); phase not stated but treatment trials are not excluded for unstated phase.
population: Sudanese patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Ketotifen combined with chloroquine and Fansidar resulted in faster parasite clearance and no recrudescence, whereas chloroquine alone or with ketotifen showed higher recrudescence rates.
effect_estimate: >39% in chloroquine alone/chloroquine+ketotifen groups vs 0% in triple combination group

title: Atovaquone-proguanil versus mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis in nonimmune travelers: results from a randomized, double-blind study.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (adverse events, malaria incidence) comparing two malaria prophylaxis interventions in humans; primary purpose is malaria prevention; not early-phase.
population: nonimmune travelers
primary_outcome: Adverse events and confirmed malaria episodes reported at 7, 28, and 60 days after travel
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil was better tolerated than mefloquine, with fewer neuropsychiatric adverse events, fewer moderate-to-severe adverse events, and fewer discontinuations, and was similarly effective for malaria prophylaxis, with no confirmed malaria cases in either group.
p_value: P=.001 for neuropsychiatric AEs, moderate/severe AEs, and discontinuations
safety_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil had fewer treatment-related neuropsychiatric AEs (14% vs 29%), fewer moderate/severe AEs (10% vs 19%), and fewer AEs causing discontinuation (1.2% vs 5.0%) compared to mefloquine; overall AE rates were similar (71.4% vs 67.3%).

title: Plasmodium vivax polymorphism in a clinical drug trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial drugs (bulaquine and primaquine) for malaria treatment, a primary malaria intervention.
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax infection
primary_outcome: Relapse rate of Plasmodium vivax infection after antirelapse treatment
impact_summary: Short-term relapse hypnozoites were not susceptible to either bulaquine or primaquine at the doses used, while long-term relapse hypnozoites were significantly susceptible, indicating polymorphic hypnozoite strains.
effect_estimate: significantly susceptible for long-term relapse hypnozoites; not susceptible for short-term relapse hypnozoites

title: Amodiaquine, sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine, and combination therapy for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Kampala, Uganda: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results on malaria treatment efficacy; meets all inclusion criteria.
comparator: sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine plus placebo vs amodiaquine plus placebo vs amodiaquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination
population: Patients with symptomatic, confirmed uncomplicated falciparum malaria (including children under 5 years)
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment failure at 14 days follow-up
impact_summary: Amodiaquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination therapy was more effective than sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine alone, particularly in children under 5 years, and was the most effective of the three regimens tested for uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
effect_metric: risk difference in clinical and parasitological failure (amodiaquine/SP vs SP alone) in children under 5
effect_estimate: clinical failure risk difference 10.4%; parasitological failure risk difference 13.6%
transmission_setting: Region of high chloroquine resistance in sub-Saharan Africa
age_range: Not specified overall; subgroup analysis in children younger than 5 years
safety_summary: Not specifically reported in abstract

title: The impact of indoor residual spraying with malathion on malaria in refugee camps in eastern Sudan.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (five camps randomly selected for malathion spraying, five controls) reporting outcome results (mortality and malaria incidence) for a malaria vector-control intervention.
population: refugees in camps in eastern Sudan
primary_outcome: morbidity and mortality rates in the camps from October to December
impact_summary: Mortality rates in the 3 months following indoor residual spraying with malathion were significantly lower in sprayed camps, but differences in clinical malaria incidence between sprayed and non-sprayed camps were not significant.
p_value: significant for mortality; not significant for clinical malaria incidence
transmission_setting: refugee camps, rainy season, eastern Sudan

title: Atovaquone and proguani hydrochloride compared with chloroquine or pyrimethamine/sulfodaxine for treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Peru.
journal: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments for acute P. falciparum malaria in humans.
population: patients with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure) of falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil achieved 100% cure rate and was significantly more effective than chloroquine, while being comparably effective to pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine.
transmission_setting: region with high prevalence of chloroquine resistance, northern Peru
safety_summary: Adverse events were typical of malarial symptoms and did not differ significantly between treatment groups.

title: Resistance of Plasmodium falciparum to antimalarial drugs in a highly endemic area of southern Viet Nam: a study in vivo and in vitro.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate vs mefloquine) with reported outcome results in humans.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria at a rubber plantation in Binh Phuoc Province
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and recurrence (re-infection or recrudescence) within 28 days of follow-up, and in vitro drug sensitivity (IC50) of P. falciparum isolates
impact_summary: Both artesunate and mefloquine cleared parasites within 5 days, mefloquine remained fully effective with a low re-infection rate, while artesunate had a recrudescence rate similar to other settings, and in vitro testing showed mefloquine, quinine, and chloroquine sensitivity remained largely preserved.
transmission_setting: highly endemic/hyperendemic area of southern Viet Nam
safety_summary: No major adverse events reported; treatments were well tolerated with both regimens clearing parasites within 5 days.

title: Improving adherence to malaria treatment for children: the use of pre-packed chloroquine tablets vs. chloroquine syrup.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (pre-packed tablets vs. syrup) in children with reported outcome results (adherence rates, cost, preference).
population: children aged 0-5 years diagnosed with malaria
primary_outcome: Adherence to recommended dosage of chloroquine at home, assessed on day 4 after clinic visit
impact_summary: Pre-packed chloroquine tablets resulted in much higher adherence (91%) compared to chloroquine syrup (42%), and were cheaper and preferred by most caregivers.

title: A clinical and pharmacokinetic trial of six doses of artemether-lumefantrine for multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, safety, pharmacokinetics).
population: patients aged >= 12 years with acute, uncomplicated multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: The six-dose artemether-lumefantrine regimen achieved a 95.5% 28-day cure rate compared with 100% for mefloquine-artesunate, and was well tolerated in multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Well tolerated with good compliance; most frequent adverse events were headache, dizziness, nausea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, vomiting, and skin rash; only 2% of patients in both groups showed QTc prolongation without cardiac complications.

title: Clinical trial of beta-arteether versus quinine for the treatment of cerebral malaria in children in Yaounde, Cameroon.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (arteether vs quinine for cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results including mortality, cure rates, and clinical endpoints.
population: children with cerebral malaria (Blantyre coma score of 2 or less)
primary_outcome: Mortality rate
impact_summary: Mortality was lower with arteether than quinine (15.7% vs 27.4%) but the difference was not statistically significant, and arteether was at least as effective and safe as quinine for treating cerebral malaria in children.
safety_summary: Arteether was reported to be safe, with similar fever clearance, coma resolution, and parasite clearance times compared to quinine.

title: Chloroquine/doxycycline combination versus chloroquine alone, and doxycycline alone for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax malaria in northeastern Irian Jaya, Indonesia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment interventions (chloroquine/doxycycline combinations) in P. falciparum and P. vivax; phase not stated but acceptable for this trial type.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum or P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite sensitivity (S) versus resistance (RI/RII/RIII) at 28 days
impact_summary: Chloroquine/doxycycline combination was highly effective against P. falciparum but only modestly effective against P. vivax, outperforming either drug alone.

title: Effect of zinc supplementation on malaria and other causes of morbidity in west African children: randomised double blind placebo controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on a malaria intervention (zinc supplementation) in children in a malaria-endemic area, with primary outcome of symptomatic malaria incidence measured and reported.
population: young children in a holoendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: Incidence of symptomatic falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Zinc supplementation had no effect on the incidence of falciparum malaria but reduced the prevalence of diarrhoea and non-significantly lowered all-cause mortality.
p_value: P=0.1 (mortality); not significant for malaria incidence
safety_summary: No adverse effects reported; all-cause mortality was non-significantly lower in the zinc group (5 vs 12 deaths, P=0.1).

title: Atovaquone plus proguanil versus halofantrine for the treatment of imported acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in non-immune adults: a randomized comparative trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (atovaquone-proguanil vs halofantrine) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance time, adverse events).
population: non-immune adults with imported uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate / parasite clearance time
impact_summary: All patients in both treatment groups were cured, though parasite clearance time was longer with atovaquone-proguanil than with halofantrine, and gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with atovaquone-proguanil.
safety_summary: No noteworthy electrocardiographic changes, particularly in QTc interval; gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent in the atovaquone-proguanil group.

title: Absence of significant pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions between artemether and quinoline antimalarials.
journal: European journal of drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic outcomes for antimalarial drug combinations in humans; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: healthy male Thai adults
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions between artemether and quinoline antimalarials (mefloquine, quinine, primaquine)
impact_summary: No significant pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interactions were found between artemether and mefloquine, quinine, or primaquine when co-administered.
safety_summary: All clinical and laboratory parameters were normal throughout; no adverse effects with ARTEM, QN, PQ alone or in combination with ARTEM, but mild transient weakness, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea and dizziness occurred in some subjects after mefloquine administration.

title: Comparison of chloroquine with artesunate in the treatment of cerebral malaria in Ghanaian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs artesunate) in humans with reported outcome results (mortality, neurological deficits, coma recovery).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality and neurological deficits; also parasite clearance, fever resolution, coma recovery time
impact_summary: Chloroquine and artesunate showed comparable clinical outcomes with no significant difference in mortality, neurological deficit, fever resolution, or coma recovery time in Ghanaian children with cerebral malaria.
transmission_setting: endemic, chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum reported in Ghana
safety_summary: No significant difference in mortality or neurological deficits between chloroquine and artesunate groups; specific adverse events not detailed.

title: A randomized clinical trial of combinations of artesunate and azithromycin for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT with outcome results (28-day cure rates) testing malaria treatment (artesunate combinations) as primary purpose in humans.
comparator: artesunate monotherapy and artesunate plus mefloquine (active comparators)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate plus mefloquine achieved a much higher 28-day cure rate (98%) than artesunate plus azithromycin (56%) or artesunate alone (44%), with azithromycin combination showing longer time to recrudescence than monotherapy.

title: Control of malaria in Pakistan by applying deltamethrin insecticide to cattle: a community-randomised trial.
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (deltamethrin application to livestock) with reported outcome results showing efficacy on malaria incidence and parasite prevalence.
population: Afghan refugee settlement residents in Pakistan
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria (P. falciparum and P. vivax) detected by passive case detection and parasite prevalence by cross-sectional surveillance
impact_summary: Treating livestock with deltamethrin insecticide reduced malaria incidence and vector density and life expectancy in treated villages compared with untreated villages.
transmission_setting: highly endemic, seasonal transmission in Afghan refugee settlements

title: Treatment of malaria in north-eastern and south-eastern Nigeria: a population study of mefloquine, sulphadoxine, pyrimethamine combination (MSP) vs chloroquine (CQ).
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (MSP vs chloroquine) with reported outcome results (clinical cure rates, adverse events) in a malaria population.
population: patients aged 6 months or more with clinical diagnosis of malaria (fever and axillary temperature >37.5°C)
primary_outcome: clinical cure rate assessed by disappearance of clinical signs and symptoms over 7-day period
impact_summary: MSP showed superior clinical cure rate (97.6%) compared to chloroquine (85.6%) with comparable fever clearance and safety.
safety_summary: Adverse event incidence was 9.5% with MSP and 9.2% with CQ; withdrawal rate was 2.0% with MSP and 5.0% with CQ, with 3.5% of CQ patients withdrawing due to adverse events compared to 0.47% with MSP.

title: Intermittent treatment for malaria and anaemia control at time of routine vaccinations in Tanzanian infants: a randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine chemoprevention (IPTi) for malaria in infants with reported efficacy outcomes (59% protective efficacy against clinical malaria).
population: infants
primary_outcome: First or only episode of clinical malaria and severe anaemia from recruitment to 1 year of age
impact_summary: Intermittent sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment given alongside routine vaccinations reduced the rate of clinical malaria by 59% and severe anaemia by 50% compared with placebo in infants.
follow_up: 12 months (with additional surveys at 12 and 18 months of age)
age_range: 2-12 months (treatment given at 2, 3, and 9 months of age)
safety_summary: Intermittent sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment was well tolerated with no drug-attributable adverse events recorded; serological responses to EPI vaccines were not affected.

title: A double-blind randomized therapeutic trial of insect repellents for the prevention of malaria in pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT testing a malaria prevention intervention (insect repellents) in humans with reported outcomes; vector-control trials are exempt from phase requirements.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria (Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax) infection during pregnancy
impact_summary: Use of the insect repellent was well tolerated and provided some protection against malaria in pregnant women, though details of statistical significance are not fully specified in the abstract.
transmission_setting: low, unstable transmission along Thai-Myanmar border
safety_summary: The repellent was well tolerated with no serious adverse effects reported; birth outcomes were similar between groups.

title: The influence of zinc supplementation on morbidity due to Plasmodium falciparum: a randomized trial in preschool children in Papua New Guinea.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of zinc supplementation in malaria-endemic children with reported outcome results (38% reduction in P. falciparum episodes); malaria morbidity is the primary focus.
population: preschool children aged 6 to 60 months
primary_outcome: Slide-confirmed Plasmodium falciparum health center-based episodes (parasitemia ≥9200 parasites/µl with axillary temperature ≥37.5°C or reported fever)
impact_summary: Daily zinc supplementation reduced Plasmodium falciparum health center-based malaria episodes by 38% compared to placebo in preschool children.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in P. falciparum health center-based episodes

title: Rapid therapeutic response onset of a new pharmaceutical form of chloroquine phosphate 300 mg: effervescent tablets.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (chloroquine phosphate formulation) with reported outcome results on fever clearance, symptom clearance, and parasitemia clearance.
population: adults with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time to fever, symptom and asexual parasite clearance
impact_summary: Effervescent chloroquine phosphate tablets produced significantly faster fever, symptom and parasite clearance than uncoated tablets, with similar safety and cure rates but better taste.
safety_summary: Adverse effects were similar between the two groups (P > 0.05), indicating comparable safety profiles.

title: Artesunate reduces but does not prevent posttreatment transmission of Plasmodium falciparum to Anopheles gambiae.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate combinations) in humans with reported outcome results on gametocyte infectivity and transmission.
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Infectivity of gametocytes in peripheral blood to Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes measured 4 or 7 days after treatment
impact_summary: Artesunate combined with pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine markedly reduced but did not completely eliminate posttreatment infectivity of P. falciparum gametocytes to mosquitoes compared to pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine alone.
effect_estimate: 8-fold higher in pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine alone group vs pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine plus 3 doses of artesunate

title: Effect of antipyretic drugs in children with malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing an antimalarial intervention (antipyretic treatment adjunctive to malaria management) in humans.
population: children with malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance and reduction of fever peaks
impact_summary: Naproxen showed a small effect in reducing fever peaks, but metamizol did not, and neither antipyretic improved fever clearance in children with malaria.
safety_summary: Antipyretic treatment should be used cautiously in malaria treatment.

title: A randomized controlled trial of artemotil (beta-arteether) in Zambian children with cerebral malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing artemotil to quinine for malaria treatment (cerebral malaria intervention) in humans.
population: children with cerebral malaria and Blantyre Coma Score of 2 or less
primary_outcome: Survival, coma resolution time, neurologic sequelae, parasite clearance time, and fever resolution time
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemotil showed no significant differences from intravenous quinine in survival, coma resolution, neurologic sequelae, parasite clearance, or fever resolution, and was well tolerated, suggesting it is therapeutically equivalent to quinine for pediatric cerebral malaria.
safety_summary: Artemotil was well-tolerated in the 48 patients who received it.

title: Chloroquine prophylaxis, iron/folic-acid supplementation or case management of malaria attacks in primigravidae in western Uganda: effects on congenital malaria and infant haemoglobin concentrations.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting results of malaria interventions (chloroquine prophylaxis, iron/folic-acid supplementation, case management) in pregnant women with congenital malaria as primary outcome.
comparator: placebo/case management of malaria attacks vs chloroquine prophylaxis vs iron/folic-acid supplementation
population: primigravidae and their infants
primary_outcome: congenital malaria (parasitaemia at birth) and infant haemoglobin concentrations
impact_summary: The maternal intervention had no significant effect on infant parasitaemia at birth or at 1 month, and congenital parasitaemia was not associated with birthweight but was related to anaemia at birth in infants born to mothers who received only case management.
effect_metric: association (p-value) between parasitaemia and infant anaemia
effect_estimate: not significant for birthweight; significant for anaemia at birth in case-management group
age_range: infants (birth to 1 month); primigravid mothers of reproductive age

title: Randomized comparison of mefloquine-artesunate versus quinine in the treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment regimens in pregnant women with reported outcome results (cure rates, gametocyte carriage) meeting primary inclusion criteria.
population: pregnant women (Karen) with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in second or third trimester
primary_outcome: Day 63 cure rate
impact_summary: Mefloquine-artesunate (MAS3) was significantly more effective and better tolerated than quinine (Q7) for treating multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in pregnancy, though mefloquine may carry a possible increased risk of stillbirth.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria area, western border of Thailand
safety_summary: MAS3 was significantly better tolerated than Q7, but there is a possible increased risk of stillbirth associated with mefloquine use in pregnancy.

title: Controlled trial of 3-day quinine-clindamycin treatment versus 7-day quinine treatment for adult travelers with uncomplicated falciparum malaria imported from the tropics.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine-clindamycin vs quinine) with reported outcome results (28-day cure rates and adverse effects).
population: adult travelers with uncomplicated falciparum malaria imported from the tropics
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: The 3-day quinine-clindamycin regimen was well tolerated and had a cure rate comparable to the 7-day quinine regimen, with no significant differences observed.
transmission_setting: imported malaria in travelers returning from the tropics
safety_summary: Adverse effects were similar in both groups; two patients in the quinine-only group had severe adverse reactions leading to cessation of treatment.

title: Efficacy of recombinant circumsporozoite protein vaccine regimens against experimental Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (RTS,S/SBAS2) with reported efficacy results against P. falciparum challenge; Phase 1/2a is acceptable as it reports outcomes beyond safety alone.
population: healthy adult volunteers undergoing experimental sporozoite challenge
primary_outcome: Development of malaria (parasitemia) after controlled human sporozoite challenge
impact_summary: RTS,S/SBAS2 vaccination reduced the incidence of malaria after sporozoite challenge compared with unvaccinated controls, with an overall protective efficacy of 41%.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental challenge, not field transmission)
safety_summary: RTS,S/SBAS2 was safe and immunogenic in all groups.
funder: SmithKline Beecham Biologicals and Walter Reed Army Institute of Research

title: Artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-lumefantrine for malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: children and adults with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: The 6-dose regimen of artemether-lumefantrine was better tolerated than, and as effective as, artesunate-mefloquine, achieving high cure rates comparable to the standard treatment.
safety_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine was better tolerated than artesunate-mefloquine.

title: Atovaquone-proguanil versus chloroquine-proguanil for malaria prophylaxis in non-immune travellers: a randomised, double-blind study. Malarone International Study Team.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (prevention) with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety in humans.
population: non-immune travellers to a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Safety and tolerability (adverse events) and prophylactic efficacy of atovaquone-proguanil versus chloroquine-proguanil
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil was as effective as and better tolerated than chloroquine-proguanil, with significantly fewer gastrointestinal adverse events and fewer discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events.
effect_metric: proportion with treatment-related gastrointestinal adverse events
safety_summary: At least one adverse event occurred in 61% of atovaquone-proguanil recipients vs 64% of chloroquine-proguanil recipients; atovaquone-proguanil had fewer gastrointestinal adverse events (12% vs 20%, p=0.001), fewer moderate/severe treatment-related adverse events (7% vs 11%, p=0.05), and fewer discontinuations due to adverse events (0.2% vs 2%, p=0.015); overall tolerability was similar between groups.

title: Chloroquine prophylaxis, iron-folic acid supplementation or case management of malaria attacks in primigravidae in western Uganda: effects on maternal parasitaemia and haemoglobin levels and on birthweight.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention (chloroquine prophylaxis) as a primary intervention in pregnant women in a malaria-endemic setting.
comparator: passive case management of malaria attacks
population: primigravidae (first-time pregnant women)
primary_outcome: Maternal parasitaemia, haemoglobin levels, and infant birthweight
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis and iron-folic acid supplementation improved maternal haemoglobin and reduced low birthweight compared to case management of malaria attacks.
effect_metric: relative risk of low birthweight (<2.5 kg)
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported in the abstract

title: A randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, comparative safety, and efficacy trial of oral co-artemether versus oral chloroquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults in India.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine vs chloroquine) with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance, fever resolution).
population: adults with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Co-artemether (CGP 56697) achieved a significantly higher 28-day cure rate than chloroquine, with faster parasite clearance and fever resolution, in patients with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in India.
safety_summary: CGP 56697 was safe and well tolerated; a death occurred in the chloroquine group leading to premature termination of recruitment due to declining chloroquine cure rate.

title: Humoral immune responses during a malaria vaccine trial in Tanzanian infants.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) in humans with reported immunogenicity and efficacy outcome results.
population: infants recruited alongside EPI vaccination
primary_outcome: safety, immunogenicity and efficacy of SPf66, and humoral response to SPf66 and EPI vaccines
impact_summary: SPf66 induced a humoral immune response in infants that declined by 2 years of age and was not associated with protection against clinical malaria, without interfering with seroconversion to EPI vaccines.
p_value: no statistically significant differences between SPf66 and placebo recipients in EPI seroconversion
safety_summary: SPf66 did not interfere with seroconversion to EPI vaccines; no statistically significant differences in prevalence or titres between SPf66 and placebo recipients

title: Indoor residual spraying with alphacypermethrin controls malaria in Pakistan: a community-randomized trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of indoor residual spraying (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (95% reduction in falciparum, 80% reduction in vivax malaria incidence).
population: residents of an irrigated rice-growing area, including schoolchildren for cross-sectional parasite surveys
primary_outcome: Incidence of falciparum and vivax malaria by fortnightly active case detection
impact_summary: Indoor residual spraying with alphacypermethrin (WP and SC formulations) greatly reduced malaria incidence and mosquito abundance compared to unsprayed control sectors over the 7 months following a single spray campaign.
effect_estimate: 95% lower falciparum incidence and 80% lower vivax incidence in WP-sprayed sectors
transmission_setting: seasonal transmission in an irrigated rice-growing area
safety_summary: Sprayed surfaces lacked odour, which contributed to the popularity of the campaign; no adverse events reported.

title: Therapeutic responses to quinine and clindamycin in multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (quinine and clindamycin combination) in humans with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates).
comparator: quinine alone and quinine plus tetracycline
population: adult Thai patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time and cure rate at 28 days
impact_summary: Quinine combined with clindamycin or tetracycline produced significantly faster fever clearance and higher cure rates than quinine alone, with clindamycin combination achieving 100% cure.
safety_summary: All patients had uncomplicated recoveries with no serious adverse effects.

title: Teaching mothers to provide home treatment of malaria in Tigray, Ethiopia: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (under-5 mortality reduction) for a malaria treatment/chemoprevention intervention in humans; phase not applicable for community-based cluster trial.
population: children under 5 years old
primary_outcome: under-5 mortality
impact_summary: Training mother coordinators to teach mothers to promptly give home-based chloroquine to sick children reduced under-5 mortality by 40% compared to the standard community health worker approach.

title: A randomized, parallel-group study in Mumbai (Bombay), comparing chloroquine with chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of adults with acute, uncomplicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine combination vs monotherapy) with reported outcome results (28- and 42-day cure rates).
population: adults with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28- or 42-day cure rate
impact_summary: The combination of chloroquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was significantly more effective and more cost-effective than chloroquine alone in curing adults with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Mumbai.

title: Halofantrine versus quinine-Fansidar combination in the treatment of post-chloroquine falciparum parasitaemia.
journal: Papua and New Guinea medical journal
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatments (halofantrine vs quinine-Fansidar) with reported outcome results on parasitaemia clearance and adverse effects.
population: adults with treatment-failure falciparum malaria after chloroquine
primary_outcome: Clearance of parasitaemia and recurrence during 21-day follow-up
impact_summary: Halofantrine cleared parasites faster than quinine-Fansidar (day 5 vs day 7) and showed similar efficacy with fewer severe adverse effects and no recurrence in either group over 21 days.
transmission_setting: endemic, Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
safety_summary: Nausea in 68% of halofantrine patients; in quinine-Fansidar group 79% had muffled deafness, 32% tinnitus, 26% dizziness, and 32% withdrew on day 2 due to intolerance to quinine.

title: In vivo efficacy study of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/ pyrimethamine in Kibwezi, Kenya and Kigoma, Tanzania.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) with reported efficacy outcomes in Plasmodium falciparum-infected children.
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: in vivo parasitological response (sensitivity/resistance) to amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Both amodiaquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine remained effective in clearing parasites at both sites, with no statistically significant difference between treatments except a slight difference favoring sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in R1 resistance in the best case scenario at Kibwezi.
p_value: not significant (except R1 resistance best case Kibwezi)
follow_up: not specified (short-term in vivo follow-up, likely 14-28 days)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic areas of Kenya and Tanzania

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis with tafenoquine: a randomised study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of tafenoquine (a malaria chemoprevention drug) with reported outcome results (blood smear positivity at days 56 and 77) in humans.
population: adolescents aged 12-20 years living in an endemic area, after curative treatment with halofantrine
primary_outcome: number of individuals with positive blood smears by day 56
impact_summary: Tafenoquine chemoprophylaxis, especially at higher doses (125 mg and 250 mg), was more effective than placebo at preventing malaria parasitemia and was well tolerated, with adverse events not differing significantly between groups.
effect_metric: number of positive blood smears by day 77
transmission_setting: endemic area for Plasmodium falciparum malaria
safety_summary: Numbers of adverse events did not differ significantly between treatment groups; tafenoquine was well tolerated.

title: Comparative efficacy of chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine alone and in a sequential combination with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated, falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment regimens in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: children with acute, symptomatic, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite-clearance time and cure rates (days 14, 21, 28)
impact_summary: Sequential treatment with chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine followed by a single dose of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was effective and well tolerated, with slightly higher cure rates than chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine alone, though parasite- and fever-clearance times were similar between groups.
safety_summary: Both regimens were relatively well tolerated; main adverse reactions (sleepiness on day 1, pruritus on days 1-3) were similar between groups; no adverse effect was attributable to SP.

title: Monitoring efficacy of commonly used antimalarials by a 14-day in-vivo test in a new settler's camp in endemic zone at Cox's Bazar.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial drug regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (3-day chloroquine plus single-dose sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine vs 3-day quinine plus single-dose sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine)
population: residents of a new settler's camp with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, all age groups
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (sensitive response vs early treatment failure) assessed by 14-day in-vivo test with blood slide examinations and clinical assessment on days 3, 7 and 14
impact_summary: Both chloroquine plus sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine and quinine plus sulphadoxine/pyrimethamine regimens showed less than 20% treatment failure, with quinine plus SP performing slightly better than chloroquine plus SP.
effect_metric: Sensitive response rate / early treatment failure rate
effect_estimate: CQ+SP: 79% sensitive, 16% early treatment failure; Q3+SP: 84% sensitive, 9% early treatment failure

title: Efficacy of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on malaria control in a hyperendemic area in Irian Jaya, Indonesia: differentiation between two age groups.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results in a hyperendemic area.
population: residents of a hyperendemic village, differentiated into children <10 years and children >10 years plus adults
primary_outcome: Malaria infection rates and density (P. falciparum and P. vivax) and spleen enlargement
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets reduced malaria parasite density and infection rates, particularly for P. falciparum, and reduced splenomegaly in younger children compared to placebo-treated nets in a control village.
effect_metric: relative risk of P. falciparum infection
effect_estimate: less than half that of control village
age_range: children <10 years and >10 years including adults

title: Efficacy of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on malaria control in a hyperendemic area in Irian Jaya, Indonesia: influence of seasonal rainfall fluctuations.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector control) for malaria with reported outcome results showing efficacy in parasite prevalence and spleen rates.
design: controlled intervention study, village-level comparison, placebo-controlled
population: residents of hyperendemic malaria villages
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax infection prevalence (parasite rates) and spleen rates
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets significantly reduced P. falciparum and P. vivax infection rates and spleen rates compared to a placebo-treated control village over two years.
transmission_setting: hyperendemic, perennial transmission with seasonal rainfall fluctuations

title: A clinical trial of combination of artesunate and mefloquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria: a short and practical regimen.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate-mefloquine combination) with reported outcome results (97% cure rate, parasite clearance time).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: A 2-day twice-daily combination of artesunate and mefloquine achieved a 97% cure rate and was well tolerated in patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: All patients tolerated the combination drugs well with no serious toxic adverse reactions.

title: Combinations of artemisinin and quinine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria: efficacy and pharmacodynamics.
screening_reason: RCT comparing artemisinin-quinine combinations versus quinine alone for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcomes (recrudescence rates).
comparator: quinine monotherapy (7 days) vs artemisinin plus 3 or 5 days of quinine
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Artemisinin followed by only 3 days of quinine resulted in a higher recrudescence rate (38%) than quinine alone (16%) or artemisinin followed by 5 days of quinine (15%), indicating that at least 5 days of quinine treatment (or 3 days after parasite clearance) is needed to prevent recrudescence.
transmission_setting: Vietnam, endemic falciparum malaria with reduced quinine sensitivity

title: Amodiaquine remains effective for treating uncomplicated malaria in west and central Africa.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
