screening_reason: Multicentre RCT of amodiaquine vs chloroquine for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported parasitological and clinical outcome results at 14 days.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological clearance on day 14 (parasitological success)
impact_summary: Amodiaquine was significantly more effective than chloroquine in treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in West and Central Africa.
transmission_setting: areas of West and Central Africa with prevalent chloroquine resistance

title: Randomized controlled trials of 5- and 14-days primaquine therapy against relapses of vivax malaria in an Afghan refugee settlement in Pakistan.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing primaquine regimens for vivax malaria relapse prevention in humans.
population: Afghan refugees with vivax malaria, passively detected at camp clinic
primary_outcome: Recurrence of clinical-parasitaemic episodes (relapse) of vivax malaria following treatment
impact_summary: The 14-day primaquine regimen substantially reduced relapse rates compared to chloroquine alone, while the 5-day primaquine regimen showed no meaningful benefit over chloroquine alone.
follow_up: 12 months (with additional 28-day recrudescence check in extended in vivo tests)
transmission_setting: Afghan refugee camp, endemic vivax malaria region of north-western Pakistan
safety_summary: No mention of G6PD testing being performed; drug appears generally tolerated as no adverse events reported, though safety was not a primary focus

title: Insecticide-treated materials for malaria control in Latin America: to use or not to use?
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (protective efficacy); vector-control intervention in humans.
population: general population in malaria-endemic communities on the Pacific Coast of Nicaragua
primary_outcome: protective efficacy of insecticide-treated materials against malaria according to coverage level
impact_summary: Protective efficacy of insecticide-treated bednets varied with coverage: 68% at ~50% coverage, 31% at 16-30% coverage, and no effect below 16% coverage.
transmission_setting: P. vivax endemic area with Anopheles albimanus as main vector, low parasite prevalence (8%) and low parasite densities

title: Efficacies of 5- and 14-day primaquine regimens in the prevention of relapses in Plasmodium vivax infections.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two primaquine regimens for P. vivax malaria treatment with reported relapse outcomes over 6-month follow-up.
comparator: 5-day primaquine regimen vs no primaquine treatment
population: Patients with Plasmodium vivax infection
primary_outcome: Relapse rate over 6-month follow-up
impact_summary: The 14-day primaquine regimen was more effective than the 5-day regimen in preventing relapses of vivax malaria in Mumbai.

title: Effect of phenobarbital on seizure frequency and mortality in childhood cerebral malaria: a randomised, controlled intervention study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria intervention (phenobarbital for seizure prevention in cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results including seizure frequency and mortality.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Seizure frequency (children with three or more seizures of any duration)
impact_summary: Phenobarbital significantly reduced seizure frequency compared to placebo but doubled mortality, making the 20 mg/kg dose unsafe for use.
safety_summary: Phenobarbital was associated with increased respiratory arrest and doubled mortality compared to placebo; mortality was greatly increased in children receiving phenobarbital plus three or more doses of diazepam (OR 31.7, 95% CI 1.2-814).

title: Effect of vaccination with 3 recombinant asexual-stage malaria antigens on initial growth rates of Plasmodium falciparum in non-immune volunteers.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine with reported outcome results (parasite growth rates); Phase 2 challenge study in non-immune volunteers is not early-phase (excludes only Phase 1 and dose-escalation/safety-only).
population: non-immune (malaria-naive) human volunteers
primary_outcome: Initial parasite growth rate following controlled challenge infection
impact_summary: Vaccination with the three recombinant P. falciparum blood-stage antigens did not reduce initial parasite growth rates compared to placebo after experimental challenge.
effect_metric: difference in parasite growth rate between vaccine and placebo groups
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental challenge, non-endemic setting)
safety_summary: Antibody responses were low and T cell responses were stronger; no significant safety concerns reported; all volunteers were treated on day 8 before developing symptoms.

title: A randomized safety and tolerability trial of artesunate plus sulfadoxine--pyrimethamine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention in humans with reported outcome results on safety, tolerability, and efficacy endpoints.
population: children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: safety and tolerability of artesunate plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: Both regimens were safe and well tolerated, and adding artesunate to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine increased the proportion of afebrile children and children with negative blood films on Day 2, and reduced gametocyte carriage, compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.
safety_summary: Both regimens were safe and well tolerated with no adverse experiences attributed to the combination.

title: Field trial of the direct acridine orange method and ParaSight-F test for the rapid diagnosis of malaria at district hospitals in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized comparison of two malaria diagnostic methods with reported outcome results (sensitivity/specificity data) in humans.
population: patients with suspected malaria presenting at district hospitals
primary_outcome: diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of the direct acridine orange method and ParaSight-F test compared with conventional microscopy for detection of malaria parasites
impact_summary: The acridine orange and ParaSight-F rapid diagnostic tests showed good sensitivity and specificity for detecting malaria parasites compared with conventional microscopy at district hospitals in Dar es Salaam.

title: Wide-scale installation of insecticide-treated curtains confers high levels of protection against malaria transmission in a hyperendemic area of Burkina Faso.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector-control intervention (insecticide-treated curtains) with reported entomological outcome results in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: residents of villages in a hyperendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: Indoor vector density and entomological inoculation rate
impact_summary: Wide-scale installation of insecticide-treated curtains substantially reduced indoor vector densities and entomological inoculation rates compared to control areas.

title: Permethrin-treated chaddars and top-sheets: appropriate technology for protection against malaria in Afghanistan and other complex emergencies.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported malaria outcome results testing permethrin-treated chaddars as a vector-control malaria prevention intervention.
population: Afghan refugees in a camp, including children and adults of all ages
primary_outcome: Malaria episodes recorded by passive case detection at the camp's health centre
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated chaddars and top-sheets reduced the odds of malaria episodes by 64% in children aged 0-10 years and by 38% in refugees aged under 20 years compared to placebo-treated chaddars, though no significant reduction was seen in those over 20.
transmission_setting: Afghan refugee camp in north-western Pakistan, seasonal transmission (August-November)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; permethrin treatment considered safe with no adverse events mentioned

title: Malaria control: bednets or spraying? Spray versus treated nets using deltamethrin--a community randomized trial in India.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two malaria vector-control interventions (insecticide-treated nets vs. indoor residual spraying) with reported outcomes in humans; cluster-randomized design appropriate for community-level vector control.
population: residents of study villages (community-wide)
primary_outcome: malaria incidence (Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax infection rates)
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednets and indoor residual spraying with deltamethrin were both effective in reducing malaria transmission, with treated nets performing at least as well as spraying.
effect_metric: incidence rate/comparative reduction in malaria cases

title: Malaria control: bednets or spraying? Trial in Kwazulu-Natal, South Africa.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing malaria vector-control interventions (bednets vs IRS spraying) with reported outcome results in humans.
population: residents of study villages
impact_summary: The trial compared bednets and indoor residual spraying for malaria control in Kwazulu-Natal, South Africa, but specific outcome data are not provided in the available text.

title: Dose findings of dihydroartemisinin in treatment of falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of dihydroartemisinin for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, recrudescence rates).
comparator: active comparator (dihydroartemisinin 480 mg over 5 days vs 640 mg over 7 days)
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and recrudescence rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: The 7-day dihydroartemisinin regimen (640 mg) resulted in a significantly lower recrudescence rate than the 5-day regimen (480 mg), while fever and parasite clearance times were similar between groups.
safety_summary: No clinical drug-related side effects were found in either treatment group during treatment.

title: Efficacy and effectiveness of five day treatment of uncomplicated falciparum with artemisinin or artesunate in Vietnam.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin/artesunate) with reported outcome results (cure rates at day 14); phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 14 follow-up
impact_summary: Both artemisinin and artesunate achieved 100% cure rate at day 14 in efficacy groups, while effectiveness groups showed 83% (artemisinin) and 93% (artesunate) cure rates.

title: A prospective study of combination antimalarial therapy and of anaemia in Zambian children with cerebral malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (combination antimalarial therapy) in humans with reported outcome results on cerebral malaria and anaemia.
population: children with cerebral malaria

title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of lumefantrine (benflumetol) in acute falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether-lumefantrine regimens in acute falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure rates and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic findings).
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, all ages (51 hospitalized adults and 215 community patients of all ages)
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic parameters of lumefantrine (e.g., absorption half-life, peak plasma concentration, AUC) and cure rates in relation to dosing regimen
impact_summary: Higher-dose six-dose lumefantrine regimens (B and C) produced greater drug exposure (AUC) and longer duration above the MIC, resulting in higher cure rates than the standard four-dose regimen (A), while oral bioavailability was strongly dependent on food intake and improved with clinical recovery.
effect_metric: increase in AUC relative to regimen A

title: Efficacy of primaquine regimens for primaquine-resistant Plasmodium vivax malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy outcome results for malaria treatment intervention (primaquine and artesunate regimens for P. vivax); not early-phase.
comparator: Fansidar alone vs Fansidar plus primaquine vs primaquine alone vs artesunate plus primaquine
population: patients aged 15-65 years with acute Plasmodium vivax malaria, mostly infected at Thailand-Myanmar border
primary_outcome: Cure rate on day 28 of follow-up
impact_summary: Fansidar alone had only a 40% cure rate while regimens including high-dose primaquine (with or without Fansidar or artesunate) achieved 100% cure rates by day 28, with artesunate plus primaquine clearing parasitemia fastest.
safety_summary: A high dose of primaquine (30 mg/day for 14 days) was found to be safe and effective during the 28-day follow-up period.

title: Assessment of therapeutic response of Plasmodium falciparum to chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in an area of low malaria transmission in Colombia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (therapeutic failure rates) in humans.
population: Patients aged >=1 year with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and parasite density >=1,000 asexual parasites/microliter
primary_outcome: Therapeutic response (early and late treatment failure) to chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine at day 14 follow-up
impact_summary: Chloroquine treatment failure occurred in 44% of patients while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failure occurred in only 6% of patients, indicating much higher chloroquine resistance in this low-transmission area of Colombia.
p_value: P < 0.01 (association of CQ failure with age <15 years)
transmission_setting: low-intensity malaria transmission area, Pacific Coast Region of Colombia

title: No evidence of cardiotoxicity during antimalarial treatment with artemether-lumefantrine.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-mefloquine) in 150 malaria patients with reported outcomes on cardiac safety.
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Electrocardiographic changes (QTc interval prolongation) during antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine showed no clinically significant electrocardiographic or cardiac effects compared with artesunate-mefloquine.
safety_summary: No clinically significant cardiotoxicity or QTc prolongation observed with artemether-lumefantrine; no relationship found between lumefantrine plasma concentrations and QTc prolongation.

title: Efficacy of artesunate plus pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine for uncomplicated malaria in Gambian children: a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (artesunate plus pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine) in children with uncomplicated malaria that has reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and treatment-failure rate at day 14
impact_summary: Adding artesunate to pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine cleared parasitaemia faster and reduced gametocyte carriage, with treatment being safe and well tolerated, though three doses of artesunate provided no additional benefit over one dose.
effect_metric: relative risk of parasitaemia clearance by day 1
safety_summary: The combined treatment was well tolerated with no adverse reactions attributable to treatment recorded.

title: Pharmacokinetics and bioequivalence evaluation of three commercial tablet formulations of mefloquine when given in combination with dihydroartemisinin in patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine formulations) in patients with acute falciparum malaria that reports pharmacokinetic and clinical outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (Lariam reference formulation vs Mephaquin 100 Lactab and Eloquin-250)
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics and relative bioavailability/bioequivalence of mefloquine (Cmax, AUC, tmax) among three formulations
impact_summary: The three mefloquine formulations showed significantly different pharmacokinetics, with Mephaquin 100 Lactab and Eloquin-250 found bioinequivalent to the reference Lariam formulation, and nine patients had recrudescent parasitaemia during follow-up.
safety_summary: The three combination regimens were well tolerated.

title: Chloroquine sensitivity of Plasmodium vivax in Thailand.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT of chloroquine treatment for vivax malaria in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance and recurrence rates).
comparator: no further treatment (chloroquine alone vs chloroquine plus primaquine)
population: patients with vivax malaria admitted to Bangkok Hospital for Tropical Diseases, mostly first malarial infection acquired on western border of Thailand
primary_outcome: Parasitological clearance and recurrence of P. vivax parasitaemia after chloroquine treatment
impact_summary: Virtually all patients responded to chloroquine with clearance of parasitaemia within 7 days, and only four patients had recurrence within 28 days, all of which were successfully retreated with chloroquine, indicating chloroquine remains effective against P. vivax in Thailand.
effect_metric: proportion with recurrent parasitaemia within 28 days
p_value: not significant (no significant difference between primaquine and no further treatment groups)
follow_up: 28 days after chloroquine treatment (with re-treatment follow-up of additional 28 days for relapsed cases)
transmission_setting: Western border of Thailand, malaria-endemic region
safety_summary: No significant adverse differences reported between primaquine and no further treatment groups; chloroquine treatment was well tolerated with successful parasite clearance.

title: In vivo efficacy of mefloquine for the treatment of Falciparum malaria in Brazil.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results for a malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine) in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.
design: single-arm, open-label, in vivo efficacy trial
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitologic cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: Mefloquine achieved a 99% cure rate for falciparum malaria with only one case of grade I resistance, associated with lower plasma mefloquine levels and higher parasite IC50.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area of Brazil (patients hospitalized in a malaria-free area for follow-up)
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; no adverse events described in the abstract.

title: Comparative efficacy of intramuscular artemether and intravenous quinine in Nigerian children with cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for cerebral malaria in children with reported outcome results (mortality, fever/parasite clearance, neurological sequelae).
population: children with cerebral malaria aged 12-60 months
primary_outcome: Efficacy (mortality and clinical recovery) comparing intramuscular artemether vs intravenous quinine
impact_summary: No statistically significant difference in efficacy was found between intramuscular artemether and intravenous quinine in treating cerebral malaria, with mortality of 20% in the artemether group versus 28% in the quinine group.
safety_summary: No adverse reactions to either drug were recorded; transient neurological sequelae including motor disabilities, cortical blindness, and afebrile seizures occurred similarly in both groups.

title: [Comparative study of artemether and quinine in severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults and older children in Cameroon].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and quinine for severe malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results on parasitemia clearance, fever control, and clinical recovery.
population: adults and older children/adolescents with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance (total and 90% clearance), fever control, and recovery of consciousness
impact_summary: Artemether was more effective than quinine in achieving total parasite clearance, 90% clearance, and fever control, and was equally effective for 50% clearance and recovery of consciousness.

title: Comparative clinical trial of four regimens of dihydroartemisinin-mefloquine in multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial comparing four dihydroartemisinin-mefloquine regimens for multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria treatment with reported clinical outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimens of mefloquine combined with dihydroartemisinin)
population: male patients with multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Recrudescent parasitaemia and clinical/parasitological therapeutic response
impact_summary: High-dose mefloquine combination regimens (III and IV) resulted in significantly lower recrudescence rates than low-dose regimens (I and II), with all regimens showing rapid clinical improvement and acceptable tolerability.
effect_estimate: regimens I/II: 8/23 and 9/16 vs regimens III/IV: 2/70 and 3/70
safety_summary: All combination regimens showed generally acceptable tolerability; vomiting within the first hour of mefloquine administration was associated with lower blood mefloquine concentrations; no serious adverse events reported.

title: Insecticide-treated curtains reduce the prevalence and intensity of malaria infection in Burkina Faso.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated curtains (vector control intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria infection prevalence and intensity in humans.
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: Prevalence and intensity of malaria infection (P. falciparum and P. malariae), fever prevalence, and haemoglobin levels
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated curtains led to a modest reduction in malaria infection prevalence and a more substantial reduction in infection intensity, along with increased haemoglobin levels, but showed no clear impact on fever-based malaria morbidity.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Low-dose treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combinations selects for drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results on drug-resistant parasite strains.
impact_summary: The parasite genes encoding dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) and dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) were assayed for point mutations that are associated with resistance against drugs.

title: A comparison of amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as first-line treatment of falciparum malaria in Kenya.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results in humans; not early-phase.
population: symptomatic outpatients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological, clinical and haematological response to treatment (resistance/treatment failure)
impact_summary: Amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed similar parasitological, clinical and haematological responses, with resistance rates of 18.5% vs 9.5% in the north and 35.1% vs 34.5% in the west, though amodiaquine produced faster fever resolution.
effect_estimate: 18.5% (amodiaquine) vs 9.5% (SP) in north; 35.1% (amodiaquine) vs 34.5% (SP) in west
transmission_setting: holoendemic in western site; lower transmission in north
safety_summary: No significant differences in haematological responses between drug groups; true clinical failure was unusual (9%).

title: Effect of insecticide-treated bed nets on the dynamics of multiple Plasmodium falciparum infections.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on infection dynamics; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: children aged 5 months to 2.5 years
primary_outcome: Rates of acquisition and loss of individual Plasmodium falciparum msp2 genotypes (infection dynamics)
impact_summary: ITNs reduced the incidence of new P. falciparum infections by 17% but had little effect on the establishment of chronic malaria infection or infection multiplicity in this high-endemicity area.
effect_metric: reduction in incidence of new infections

title: Effect of insecticide-treated bed nets on haemoglobin values, prevalence and multiplicity of infection with Plasmodium falciparum in a randomized controlled trial in Tanzania.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of insecticide-treated bed nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results (haemoglobin, P. falciparum prevalence, parasite density, multiplicity of infection) in humans.
population: children aged 5 to 24 months
primary_outcome: Haemoglobin values, P. falciparum prevalence and density, and multiplicity of infection (PCR-RFLP of msp2 locus)
impact_summary: ITN use significantly increased mean haemoglobin values and decreased P. falciparum prevalence by 16.4% after six months, with no significant effect on parasite density or multiplicity of infection.

title: Effect of iron supplementation and malaria prophylaxis in infants on Plasmodium falciparum genotypes and multiplicity of infection.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis in infants with reported outcome results on parasite genotypes and multiplicity of infection.
population: infants aged 5 and 8 months living under intense malaria transmission
primary_outcome: Multiplicity of Plasmodium falciparum infection (number of concurrent infections) determined by msp2 genotyping
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis significantly reduced the multiplicity of P. falciparum infection in infants, while iron supplementation had no effect on multiplicity, and FC27-like msp2 alleles were significantly associated with increased risk of clinical malaria.
effect_estimate: relative risk = 1.487 (prospective risk); odds ratio = 3.84 (present risk)
p_value: P=0.013 (prospective risk); P=0.026 (present risk); P=0.047 (association between infections and parasite densities)

title: Comparison of rectal artemisinin with intravenous quinine in the treatment of severe malaria in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (artemisinin vs quinine for severe malaria) with primary efficacy and safety endpoints.
population: adult patients with complicated severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic responses (parasite clearance time, fever subsidence time, coma resolution time) and adverse reactions
impact_summary: Rectal artemisinin achieved faster parasite, fever, and coma clearance than intravenous quinine, with similar cure and mortality rates but fewer adverse effects, suggesting it is more efficacious and safer.
effect_metric: parasite clearance time, fever subsidence time, coma resolution time
safety_summary: Quinine group had more vomiting, dizziness, hypoglycaemia and tinnitus; artemisinin group had tenesmus in some patients; mortality rates similar between groups.

title: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled assessment of chloroquine/primaquine prophylaxis for malaria in nonimmune Colombian soldiers.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine/primaquine) in humans, comparing treatment vs placebo with protective efficacy endpoints.
population: nonimmune Colombian soldiers on patrol duty
primary_outcome: occurrence of symptomatic parasitemia during 17 weeks of patrol/base camp plus 3 further weeks in base camp
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus primaquine provided 88% protective efficacy against malaria compared with placebo, but did not improve upon primaquine alone from a previous study.
safety_summary: Two chloroquine/primaquine recipients had severe gastrointestinal distress.

title: Effect of vitamin A supplementation on morbidity due to Plasmodium falciparum in young children in Papua New Guinea: a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vitamin A supplementation (malaria-related intervention) in humans with reported outcome results on P. falciparum morbidity; phase not stated but not early-phase.
population: young children aged 6-60 months in a P. falciparum endemic area
primary_outcome: P. falciparum febrile episodes (malaria morbidity) assessed through weekly community-based case detection and health centre surveillance
impact_summary: Vitamin A supplementation reduced P. falciparum febrile episodes by 30% compared with placebo, with the greatest benefit seen in children aged 12-36 months.

title: The comparative efficacy and tolerability of CGP 56697 (artemether + lumefantrine) versus halofantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in travellers returning from the Tropics to The Netherlands and France.
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of artemether-lumefantrine vs halofantrine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; Phase 3 therapeutic trial.
population: Travellers returning from the Tropics with acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, mostly non-immune
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: CGP 56697 (artemether-lumefantrine) cleared parasites faster than halofantrine but had a lower 28-day cure rate (82% vs 100%) due to high recrudescence, while halofantrine caused significant QTc prolongation not seen with CGP 56697.
p_value: P < 0.001 for parasite clearance time and parasite reduction at 24h
transmission_setting: Travellers returning from tropical endemic regions to non-endemic countries
safety_summary: Significant QTc prolongations (>30 ms) observed 6-12 h after halofantrine intake but not after CGP 56697; CGP 56697 was well-tolerated overall.

title: Efficacy of six doses of artemether-lumefantrine (benflumetol) in multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported efficacy outcomes (28-day cure rates) comparing artemether-lumefantrine doses for treatment of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: Two six-dose regimens of artemether-lumefantrine achieved significantly higher 28-day cure rates than the four-dose regimen in multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: No differences in reported adverse effects between the three treatment groups; six-dose regimens were very well-tolerated.

title: Evaluation of the SPf66 vaccine for malaria control when delivered through the EPI scheme in Tanzania.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Double-blind, individually randomized placebo-controlled trial of a malaria vaccine in infants with reported efficacy outcome results (2% VE against clinical malaria).
population: infants vaccinated through the EPI scheme
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical episodes of malaria detected through health facility-based passive case detection
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine given at 1, 2 and 7 months of age through the EPI scheme showed no efficacy in preventing clinical malaria episodes in young infants.
safety_summary: SPf66 was safe, immunogenic and did not interfere with humoral immune responses to EPI vaccines.

title: Atovaquone and proguanil versus pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine for the treatment of acute falciparum malaria in Zambia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment regimens with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance, fever clearance) over 28-day follow-up.
population: patients with acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (percentage of patients with parasitemia eliminated and no recurrence during 28 days follow-up), parasite clearance time, and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Atovaquone and proguanil was equally effective and as well tolerated as pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine for treating acute, uncomplicated, drug-resistant falciparum malaria, with cure rates of 100% versus 98.8%, though atovaquone/proguanil had a shorter fever clearance time but a longer parasite clearance time.
p_value: P < 0.05 for FCT and PCT differences; cure rate difference not significant
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated; adverse events and laboratory abnormalities were typical of those normally observed in patients with malaria.

title: Combination atovaquone and proguanil hydrochloride vs. halofantrine for treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment interventions with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance times, adverse events); primary focus is P. falciparum treatment in children; phase not stated but treatment trials are acceptable.
population: children with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at 28 days after treatment
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil hydrochloride had efficacy comparable to halofantrine for treatment of acute uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in Kenyan children, with fewer adverse events.
safety_summary: More adverse experiences were reported with halofantrine (119) than with atovaquone and proguanil hydrochloride (73).

title: Efficacy and safety of atovaquone/proguanil compared with mefloquine for treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial drug treatments for P. falciparum malaria in humans; primary malaria intervention focus; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: adult patients with acute P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate (percentage of patients in whom parasitemia was eliminated and did not recur during 28 days of follow-up)
impact_summary: Atovaquone/proguanil was significantly more effective than mefloquine, with a 100% cure rate compared to 86% for mefloquine.
safety_summary: Adverse events were generally typical of malaria symptoms, each occurring in <10% of patients in either group, except increased vomiting in the atovaquone/proguanil group; transient elevations of liver enzymes occurred more frequently with atovaquone/proguanil but were not significant and normalized by day 28.

title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled field trial to determine the efficacy and safety of Malarone (atovaquone/proguanil) for the prophylaxis of malaria in Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (atovaquone/proguanil) in humans with efficacy and safety endpoints.
population: adult volunteers
primary_outcome: failure of chemoprophylaxis, defined as a positive malaria blood smear or withdrawal due to a treatment-related adverse event
impact_summary: Malarone was significantly more effective than placebo at preventing malaria, with a prophylaxis success rate of 98% compared to 63% for placebo.
safety_summary: Headache and abdominal pain were the most commonly reported adverse events with possible causal relationship to study medication, occurring more frequently in the placebo group; no subjects withdrew due to treatment-related adverse events.

title: Atovaquone-proguanil compared with chloroquine and chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Philippines.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments for acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance time, adverse events).
population: Patients with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria (hospitalized)
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological/clinical response) at day 28
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil achieved a significantly higher cure rate (100%) than chloroquine (30.4%, P<.0001) or chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (87.5%, P<.05), and was well tolerated.
p_value: P<.0001 vs chloroquine; P<.05 vs chloroquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, Philippines
safety_summary: Adverse events were typical of malaria symptoms including vomiting, abdominal pain, anorexia, and headache; atovaquone-proguanil was well tolerated.

title: Response of falciparum malaria to different antimalarials in Myanmar.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Published RCT of antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results on treatment efficacy.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs mefloquine)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological treatment failure/success at day 14
impact_summary: Mefloquine was five times more likely to be effective than chloroquine or sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, which had nearly identical high failure rates exceeding 50% in some areas.
transmission_setting: endemic, township hospitals in Sagaing, northern and eastern Shan, Myanmar

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of artesunate and quinine + tetracycline for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Chanthaburi, Thailand.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment regimens (artesunate vs quinine+tetracycline) with reported outcome results (cure rates and cost-effectiveness).
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria attending a malaria clinic, aged 15-60 years
primary_outcome: Cure rate assessed on day 5 (artesunate) and day 7 (quinine + tetracycline) using intention-to-treat approach
impact_summary: Artesunate achieved a significantly higher cure rate (100%) than quinine + tetracycline (77.4%) and was more cost-effective within specified cost thresholds.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area, malaria-clinic-based setting in Thailand

title: A randomized, double-blind, comparative trial of a new oral combination of artemether and benflumetol (CGP 56697) with mefloquine in the treatment of acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether/benflumetol vs mefloquine) with reported outcome results in humans.
population: adult patients with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: CGP 56697 had a lower 28-day cure rate than mefloquine but was faster in clearing parasites, fever, and gametocytes.

title: Intermittent sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine to prevent severe anaemia secondary to malaria in pregnancy: a randomised placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasitaemia and anaemia at 34 weeks) testing intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria prevention in pregnancy, a primary malaria intervention in humans.
population: primigravid women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Severe anaemia (haemoglobin <8 g/dL) and malaria parasitaemia, assessed at 34 weeks of gestation
impact_summary: Intermittent sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment significantly reduced malaria parasitaemia and severe anaemia in primigravid women compared with placebo.
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; no major adverse events described in abstract.

title: Malaria prophylaxis using azithromycin: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Irian Jaya, Indonesia.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results (parasitemia failures) evaluating azithromycin for malaria chemoprevention in humans; not early-phase.
population: Indonesian adults with limited immunity to malaria, after radical cure therapy
primary_outcome: slide-proven parasitemia (prophylaxis failure)
impact_summary: Azithromycin provided excellent protection against P. vivax malaria but only modest protection against P. falciparum malaria compared with placebo.
effect_estimate: 71.6% vs P. falciparum; 98.9% vs P. vivax (azithromycin); doxycycline: 96.3% vs P. falciparum, 98% vs P. vivax
effect_ci: P. falciparum: 50.3-83.8; P. vivax: 93.1-99.9 (azithromycin); doxycycline: 85.4-99.6 and 88.0-99.9
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum and chloroquine-resistant P. vivax endemic area

title: Artesunate versus artemether for the treatment of recrudescent multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two artemisinin derivatives for malaria treatment in 443 patients with clear efficacy and safety endpoints.
population: patients with recrudescent multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times, and recurrence of infection by day 28
impact_summary: Artesunate and artemether showed equivalent therapeutic efficacy and safety in treating recrudescent multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, with no significant difference in recurrence rates by day 28.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, western border of Thailand
safety_summary: Both regimens were very well tolerated, with no significant adverse effects attributable to either derivative.

title: Treatment of malaria tropica with a fixed combination of rifampicin, co-trimoxazole and isoniazid: a clinical study.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (fixed combination vs chloroquine/pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine) in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: patients with malaria tropica, including infants and children between 2 months and 6 years of age
primary_outcome: Clearance of parasitemia (blood smear negativity) after treatment
impact_summary: Treatment with the fixed combination of rifampicin, co-trimoxazole and isoniazid (CF) cleared parasitemia in all 41 treated patients, with only 2 recurrences by day 14, compared to 7 failures (4 primary) in the control group treated with chloroquine or pyrimethamine/sulphadoxine.
effect_estimate: 41/41 (100%) initial clearance with CF vs 7 failures in control group
age_range: 2 months to adult (35 of 61 patients aged 2 months to 6 years)
safety_summary: CF was well tolerated, with excellent tolerance even in infants; no significant adverse events reported.

title: Population pharmacokinetics and therapeutic response of CGP 56697 (artemether + benflumetol) in malaria patients.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (artemether + benflumetol combination) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance time and 28-day cure rates).
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimens of CGP 56697: A, B, C)
population: malaria patients
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and 28-day cure rate correlated with pharmacokinetic parameters
impact_summary: Higher benflumetol AUC significantly increased the chance of cure, while higher artemether or dihydroartemisinin AUC decreased parasite clearance time, explaining the pharmacokinetic basis for the lower than expected cure rate seen in Thailand.
effect_metric: association between benflumetol AUC and cure

title: Early vomiting of mefloquine in children with malaria is not modified by the timing of antipyretic treatment.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (mefloquine) intervention in children with malaria.
population: children with malaria treated with mefloquine
primary_outcome: Early vomiting after mefloquine administration
impact_summary: The timing of antipyretic treatment did not affect the rate of early vomiting following mefloquine administration in children with malaria.

title: Chloroquine treatment for uncomplicated childhood malaria in an area with drug resistance: early treatment failure aggravates anaemia.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine antimalarial treatment in children with uncomplicated malaria reporting outcome results (treatment failure rates and haemoglobin changes).
comparator: pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine rescue treatment after chloroquine failure
population: children with clinical malaria episodes
primary_outcome: Early treatment failure (ETF) and late treatment failure (LTF) rates, and haemoglobin response after chloroquine treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine treatment failed in a large proportion of children (20% early treatment failure) and did not improve anaemia, whereas switching failures to pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine significantly improved haemoglobin levels.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported beyond haematological outcomes; no serious adverse events mentioned.

title: Cardiac effects of halofantrine in children suffering from acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (halofantrine) in humans with reported outcome results (cardiac ECG findings and clinical monitoring).
population: children with acute symptomatic uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cardiac effects (ECG changes including P-R interval and Q-Tc interval) after halofantrine treatment
impact_summary: Halofantrine at the recommended dose caused significant ECG abnormalities including AV block and Q-Tc interval prolongation in children with falciparum malaria, though without clinical symptoms.
safety_summary: First degree AV block occurred in 2 children, second degree AV block in 1 child; significant Q-Tc prolongation at multiple time points; rhythm disturbance rare; no clinical symptoms despite ECG abnormalities.

title: Comparative efficacy of chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine and halofantrine in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment regimens in children with reported efficacy outcomes (cure rates, parasite and fever clearance times).
population: children with acute symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times and cure rates
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine was as effective as halofantrine, with both regimens achieving similar 96% cure rates and being relatively well tolerated in children with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: area with chloroquine resistance rate of 35-45%
safety_summary: Both treatments were relatively well tolerated; pruritus was more common with chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine; intravascular haemolysis occurred in one patient and abdominal pain with or without diarrhoea in 4 patients treated with halofantrine.

title: An open randomized clinical study of intrarectal versus infused Quinimax for the treatment of childhood cerebral malaria in Niger.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results (mortality and coma recovery time); not early-phase.
population: children with cerebral falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fatal outcome and coma recovery time
impact_summary: Intrarectal Quinimax showed cure and mortality rates and coma recovery times similar to intravenous Quinimax, with no significant differences between groups, suggesting it is a viable alternative treatment route.
follow_up: until recovery/outcome (acute treatment course, 2 days plus follow-up)
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated; no anal irritation observed with intrarectal Quinimax.

title: A pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic study of artesunate for vivax malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate treatment for vivax malaria with reported pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic and parasite clearance outcome results.
population: male Vietnamese adults with slide-positive vivax malaria
primary_outcome: pharmacokinetic parameters of artesunate and dihydroartemisinin and time to 50% reduction in parasite count (PCT50)
impact_summary: Artesunate, given intravenously or orally, rapidly cleared both sexual and asexual forms of P. vivax and is confirmed as an effective and suitable initial treatment for vivax malaria.
effect_metric: mean time to 50% reduction in parasite count (PCT50)

title: Efficacy and safety of atovaquone/proguanil as suppressive prophylaxis for Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy outcomes for a malaria chemoprevention intervention (atovaquone/proguanil) in humans; not early-phase.
population: adult volunteers
primary_outcome: development of parasitemia, evident on blood smear, during prophylaxis
impact_summary: All subjects in both atovaquone/proguanil dose groups remained malaria-free during 10 weeks of prophylaxis, compared to only 48% of placebo recipients.
safety_summary: Both atovaquone/proguanil prophylactic regimens were as well tolerated as placebo.

title: Effect of iron chelation therapy on mortality in Zambian children with cerebral malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (iron chelation adjunctive therapy) in humans with reported mortality outcome results.
population: children with cerebral malaria under age 6 years
primary_outcome: Mortality
impact_summary: Adding deferoxamine to quinine therapy did not significantly reduce mortality in children with cerebral malaria compared to placebo.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (mortality, deferoxamine vs placebo)
transmission_setting: one rural and one urban site in Zambia
safety_summary: No beneficial effect on mortality was seen; hepatomegaly was associated with higher mortality and splenomegaly with lower mortality; deferoxamine was infused for 72 hours in addition to quinine.

title: Artesunate and mefloquine in the treatment of uncomplicated multidrug-resistant hyperparasitaemic falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate ± mefloquine) with reported outcome results (recrudescence/failure rates at day 42).
population: adults and children with uncomplicated hyperparasitaemic multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: recrudescence rate at day 42
impact_summary: Adding a single dose of mefloquine to a 5-day artesunate course markedly reduced recrudescence at day 42 compared to artesunate alone (6% vs 36%).
transmission_setting: area of high-level multidrug resistance, endemic for mefloquine-resistant P. falciparum
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with rapid clinical responses; no major adverse events reported.

title: Compliance with artesunate and quinine + tetracycline treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artesunate vs quinine+tetracycline for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (compliance and cure rates); primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: patients aged 15-60 years attending a malaria clinic with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Compliance with treatment regimen (and cure rate) assessed via patient interview/residual pill counts and peripheral blood smear
impact_summary: Compliance and cure rates were significantly higher with the 5-day artesunate regimen than with the 7-day quinine + tetracycline regimen.
safety_summary: Noncompliance was mostly due to adverse reactions and forgetting to take the drugs; specific adverse event rates not reported.

title: Influence of blister packaging on the efficacy of artesunate + mefloquine over artesunate alone in community-based treatment of non-severe falciparum malaria in Myanmar.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artesunate monotherapy vs. artesunate plus mefloquine for malaria treatment with reported parasitological outcomes (day 28 blood smear results).
population: patients with non-severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure assessed by blood smear on day 28
impact_summary: Blister packaging improved drug compliance to 99% in both arms, and the combination of artesunate plus mefloquine showed only marginally higher efficacy than artesunate alone, with one positive blood smear in the AD+mefloquine group versus seven in the AD-alone group.
effect_metric: number of positive blood smears on day 28
transmission_setting: community-based, endemic falciparum malaria in Myanmar
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; compliance was high (99%) with both regimens and no major adverse events described.

title: A comparison of use of a pyrethroid either for house spraying or for bednet treatment against malaria vectors.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector-control interventions (bednet treatment and house spraying) for malaria with reported outcome results on re-infection incidence and parasitemia.
population: children (cohorts monitored for re-infection), village populations
primary_outcome: probability of re-infection with malaria per child per week
impact_summary: Both insecticide-treated bednets and house spraying reduced malaria vector density, sporozoite rates, entomological inoculation rate by about 90%, and reduced probability of re-infection by 54-62% compared to untreated control villages, with no significant difference between the two methods.
effect_metric: reduction in probability of re-infection per child per week

title: Response of uncomplicated falciparum malaria to oral chloroquine and quinine in Burundi highlands.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing chloroquine and quinine treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (7-day treatment response); malaria treatment is the primary intervention.
population: children aged 0-14 with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment response evaluated by WHO 7-day in vivo test
impact_summary: Quinine was significantly more effective than chloroquine in both study periods, and chloroquine efficacy declined significantly over time, especially in children under 5 years old.
effect_metric: odds ratio for chloroquine treatment failure between study periods
transmission_setting: highlands of Northern Burundi, seasonal transmission

title: Primaquine prophylaxis against malaria in nonimmune Colombian soldiers: efficacy and toxicity. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of primaquine prophylaxis for malaria prevention in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; meets all inclusion criteria.
population: healthy, young, nonimmune adult male soldiers
primary_outcome: Symptomatic parasitemia determined over the 16-week intervention period and for 3 weeks in base camp
impact_summary: Primaquine prophylaxis provided high protective efficacy against malaria in nonimmune soldiers, with 89% efficacy against all malaria types, 94% against P. falciparum, and 85% against P. vivax, though some experienced gastrointestinal toxicity.
follow_up: 16 weeks intervention plus 3 weeks in base camp
safety_summary: Six primaquine recipients had mild to moderate gastrointestinal distress, and three had severe distress.

title: Comparative efficacy of chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine and pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments in children with reported efficacy outcomes (parasitaemia clearance, cure rates, fever/symptom resolution); malaria is the primary focus.
population: children with acute symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and cure rate following treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus chlorpheniramine combination therapy resulted in faster parasite, fever and symptom clearance and a higher cure rate than pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine, and cured all children who had failed PS treatment.
effect_estimate: significantly higher in CQ/CP group than PS group
safety_summary: Both treatments were well tolerated but adverse drug reactions were more common in children given pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine.

title: A trial of Fansidar plus chloroquine or Fansidar alone for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (Fansidar±chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite failure rates, clinical symptoms, safety).
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Persistent symptoms and clinic re-attendance within first 3 days after treatment; parasite failure rate at day 7 and day 28
impact_summary: Fansidar plus chloroquine was a more effective symptomatic treatment than Fansidar alone, reducing persistent symptoms, but did not improve parasite cure rate or packed cell volume compared to Fansidar alone.
safety_summary: Three children who received Fansidar alone had fits; none of the children treated with Fansidar plus chloroquine had fits.

title: Impact of spatial distribution of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on child mortality in rural northern Ghana.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-impregnated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (child mortality).
population: children 6-59 months of age
primary_outcome: child mortality
impact_summary: Insecticide-impregnated bed nets reduced child mortality, and their insecticidal effect also provided some protection to nearby non-users, with mortality among non-users increasing by 6.7% for each 100-m shift away from the nearest IIBN-using compound.
effect_metric: percent increase in mortality per 100m distance from nearest IIBN compound

title: Viability of Plasmodium falciparum ex vivo: comparison of the effects of artemether and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in severe malaria with reported outcome results on parasite viability and therapeutic response.
population: children with severe non-cerebral falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite viability ex vivo and conventional indices of therapeutic response (time to 50% or 90% reduction of parasitemia, parasite clearance time)
impact_summary: Artemether produced a significantly more rapid reduction of parasitemia and fever than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with faster and more complete loss of parasite viability ex vivo.

title: Efficacy and safety of CGP 56697 (artemether and benflumetol) compared with chloroquine to treat acute falciparum malaria in Tanzanian children aged 1-5 years.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemether-benflumetol to chloroquine for acute falciparum malaria treatment in children, with reported parasitological cure rates and safety outcomes.
population: children aged 1-5 years with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 14-day parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: CGP 56697 (artemether-benflumetol) achieved markedly higher 7-day and 14-day parasitological cure rates than chloroquine, which showed high levels of resistance.
transmission_setting: area of high malaria transmission and very high chloroquine resistance (Kilombero area)
safety_summary: No major adverse events observed with either CGP 56697 or chloroquine.

title: Distinction of recrudescences from new infections by PCR-RFLP analysis in a comparative trial of CGP 56 697 and chloroquine in Tanzanian children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (CGP 56697 vs chloroquine) in Tanzanian children with reported outcome results on parasitological clearance and recrudescence.
population: children with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological clearance/failure and distinction of recrudescence versus new infection by PCR-RFLP
impact_summary: CGP 56697 showed a superior clearance rate compared to chloroquine, clearing higher parasite densities and suppressing new infections over a longer period, with PCR-RFLP analysis confirming that many apparent treatment failures beyond day 7 were actually new infections rather than recrudescences.
effect_estimate: superior in CGP 56697 group vs chloroquine

title: A field trial with etofenprox (OMS 3002) as a residual insecticide against malaria vectors, in Tanjung Bunga district, east Flores, Indonesia.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of vector control (indoor residual spray and treated bednets with etofenprox) with reported outcome results (malaria positivity rates in successive surveys), and vector-control trials are correctly classified as 'not applicable' phase.
design: field trial, non-randomized (operational trial with treated and control areas)
population: general population, particularly children, in villages of Tanjung Bunga district
primary_outcome: malaria positivity rates measured by malariometric surveys
impact_summary: Indoor residual spraying and bednet impregnation with etofenprox led to steady declines in malaria positivity rates, particularly among children, compared to the untreated control area.
follow_up: 150-160 days (bioassay mortality); malariometric surveys over trial period

title: Two doses of artemether/mefloquine or artesunate/mefloquine combination for multidrug resistant falciparum Malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemether/mefloquine vs artesunate/mefloquine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance).
population: Thai male patients with multidrug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate / parasitological and fever clearance at day 42 follow-up
impact_summary: Both two-dose combination regimens (artemether/mefloquine and artesunate/mefloquine) achieved a 100% cure rate with rapid fever and parasite clearance and no serious adverse effects.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria, Southeast Asia
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects were found in either treatment group.

title: Intestinal parasite infections after extended use of chloroquine or primaquine for malaria prevention.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results comparing chloroquine and primaquine for malaria prevention (chemoprevention) in humans; not early-phase.
population: Javanese men enrolled in malaria prophylaxis trial
primary_outcome: Changes in intestinal parasite infection (species variety, egg counts, infection status) between baseline and endpoint after prolonged chloroquine or primaquine prophylaxis
impact_summary: Primaquine had little or no significant effect on intestinal parasite infections compared to placebo, while chloroquine was associated with a higher proportion of Entamoeba histolytica/dispar infections and lower hookworm egg counts.
effect_metric: proportion of new or increased infections
effect_estimate: lower in primaquine group than chloroquine group, comparable to placebo
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region of Irian Jaya, Indonesia
safety_summary: Primaquine showed little or no significant adverse effect on intestinal parasite prevalence, supporting its safety as a daily malaria prophylactic.

title: Randomized comparison of intramuscular artemether and intravenous quinine in adult, Melanesian patients with severe or complicated, Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Papua New Guinea.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for severe malaria with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, temperature defervescence, adverse effects).
population: Melanesian adults with severe or complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety and efficacy (including mortality, parasite clearance time, and temperature defervescence) of intramuscular artemether versus intravenous quinine
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether appeared safe and was probably as effective as intravenous quinine in treating severe or complicated falciparum malaria in Melanesian adults, with faster parasite and fever clearance and no hypoglycaemia compared to quinine.
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects attributable to artemether; hypoglycaemia occurred in 79% of quinine-treated patients without pre-treatment hypoglycaemia but in none of the artemether group; overall mortality was 12% (1/15 artemether vs 3/18 quinine).

title: Efficacy of oral pyronaridine for the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in African children.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (pyronaridine) in humans with reported clinical and parasitological outcome results.
population: children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological response (cure vs treatment failure) monitored over 14 days
impact_summary: All pyronaridine-treated children were cured, whereas 40% of chloroquine-treated children experienced treatment failure.
safety_summary: Side effects associated with pyronaridine were minor and transient; drug was safe and well tolerated.

title: Effect of chloroquine prophylaxis during pregnancy on maternal haematocrit.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT of chloroquine chemoprevention (IPTp) for malaria in pregnant women with reported outcome results (haematocrit, anaemia prevalence, birthweight).
population: pregnant women (Burkina Faso: all pregnant women; Cameroon: primigravidae only)
primary_outcome: Maternal haematocrit at delivery
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis during pregnancy was associated with significantly higher maternal haematocrit at delivery and a non-significant reduction in anaemia in both Burkina Faso and Cameroon.
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: An efficacy trial of the malaria vaccine SPf66 in Gambian infants--second year of follow-up.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine in humans with reported outcome results on protective efficacy.
design: randomized controlled trial, phase 3, second year follow-up
population: infants
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy of SPf66 against first and total attacks of malaria
impact_summary: SPf66 did not provide any significant degree of protection to Gambian infants during a second year of follow-up.
follow_up: second malaria transmission season (approximately 2 years total)

title: A randomized controlled trial of artemether/benflumetol, a new antimalarial and pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in African children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether/benflumetol versus pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results; phase unstated but appears Phase II/III therapeutic trial.
population: children 1-5 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and cure rate (day 3 and day 15 parasitological response)
impact_summary: Coartemether (artemether/benflumetol) cleared parasites faster and resulted in fewer gametocyte carriers than pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine, though more new infections occurred within 3-4 weeks post-treatment due to its shorter prophylactic effect.
safety_summary: CGP56697 was found to be safe in African children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.

title: Malaria chemotherapy trial at a minimal effective dose of mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine compared with equivalent doses of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine or mefloquine alone.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chemotherapy) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitological cure rates).
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine alone or sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine alone)
population: school children with mild P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: The triple combination (MSP) and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine alone (SP) achieved similarly high cure rates (67% and 69%), both significantly higher than mefloquine alone (13%).

title: A community randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets for the prevention of malaria and anaemia among primigravid women on the Kenyan coast.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on anaemia, malaria infection, and birth outcomes.
population: primigravid women with singleton pregnancies attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: malaria and anaemia among primigravidae (severe anaemia, placental malaria infection, birth weight, perinatal mortality)
impact_summary: ITBN had little impact on malaria-associated morbidity in primigravidae, with no significant differences in severe anaemia, placental malaria infection, birth weight, or perinatal mortality between intervention and control groups.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse effects mentioned.

title: Artemisinin kinetics and dynamics during oral and rectal treatment of uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin for uncomplicated malaria in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times and pharmacokinetic findings); not early-phase.
population: adult male patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time in relation to artemisinin pharmacokinetics
impact_summary: Oral and rectal artemisinin produced similar parasite clearance times despite lower drug exposure with rectal administration, suggesting oral doses may be unnecessarily high and that autoinduction of elimination could contribute to recrudescence and resistance risk.
p_value: p < 0.001 (for correlation between response onset index and unbound AUC)
follow_up: 5 days of treatment with pharmacokinetic sampling on first and last day

title: Allopurinol as an additive to quinine in the treatment of acute complicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine plus allopurinol vs quinine alone) with reported outcome results on parasite clearance, defervescence, and cure rates in humans with acute falciparum malaria.
population: Asian-Indian adults with acute complicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time, defervescence time, splenomegaly disappearance time, and cure rate
impact_summary: Allopurinol plus quinine significantly reduced parasite clearance, defervescence, and splenomegaly disappearance times compared to quinine alone, with a non-significantly higher cure rate.
p_value: 0.0214 (parasite clearance time); 0.0002 (defervescence time); 0.0002 (splenomegaly disappearance time); not significant (cure rate)

title: Immune responses to Plasmodium falciparum antigens during a malaria vaccine trial in Tanzanian children.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) in humans with reported immune response and clinical malaria outcome results.
population: children
primary_outcome: Immune response (IgG antibody titres) to malaria vaccine antigens and association with clinical malaria risk
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccination induced strong IgG antibody responses that persisted above placebo levels for 18 months, with a non-significant trend toward higher anti-SPf66 titres being associated with reduced risk of clinical malaria.
effect_metric: association between anti-SPf66 IgG titre and risk of clinical malaria
effect_estimate: trend toward decreasing risk with increasing titre

title: Effect of artemether on electrocardiogram in severe falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether vs quinine for severe falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (ECG findings and mortality); not early-phase, malaria is primary focus.
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria admitted to hospital
primary_outcome: Electrocardiographic changes (dysrhythmia, QTc prolongation, T-wave changes) associated with artemether or quinine treatment
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether did not cause significant dysrhythmia or adverse ECG changes, while quinine was associated with more hypotension and tachycardia, but neither drug caused significant dysrhythmia despite ECG abnormalities.
safety_summary: Hypotension was significantly more common with quinine (13 vs 2 cases); tachycardia, T-wave changes, and QTc prolongation occurred in some quinine patients; no significant dysrhythmia despite high plasma quinine levels; five deaths, ECGs not significantly different from survivors; in the artemether group, tachycardia occurred in 17 cases prior to treatment, QTc prolongation in 2, T-wave changes in 6, and one case of transient RBBB with second degree AV-block resolving by Day 2; no significant cardiovascular effect of artemether observed.

title: A comparative study of artesunate and artemether in combination with mefloquine on multidrug resistant falciparum malaria in eastern Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions (artesunate and artemether combinations) with reported outcome results (cure rates and safety).
comparator: quinine plus tetracycline and mefloquine alone (active comparators) across artesunate/artemether monotherapy and combination regimens
population: uncomplicated falciparum malaria cases at Trat and Chanthaburi malaria clinics
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological clearance/cure by Day 28)
impact_summary: Artesunate or artemether combined with mefloquine achieved high cure rates (96.7-98.7%) with no significant difference among the seven regimens, and all regimens were well tolerated.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, eastern Thailand
safety_summary: Patients tolerated all regimens very well; no serious side effects; adverse effects did not differ among the seven regimens.

title: Evaluation of SPf66 malaria vaccine efficacy in Brazil.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported efficacy outcome results in humans; phase not explicitly stated but field efficacy trial implies Phase 3; primary purpose is malaria prevention.
population: migrants from nonendemic areas, both sexes, ages 7 to 60 years
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria infections
impact_summary: SPf66 malaria vaccine showed no statistically significant overall protective efficacy against P. falciparum or P. vivax malaria in this trial.
