effect_estimate: -1.6% (P. falciparum overall), 14.1% (P. falciparum first episode), -19.7% (P. vivax overall), -10.8% (P. vivax first episode)
effect_ci: -32.9% to 22.4% (P. falciparum overall); -17.0% to 36.9% (P. falciparum first episode); -44.8% to 1.03% (P. vivax overall); -41.1% to 12.8% (P. vivax first episode)
transmission_setting: seasonal, area of recent migrant settlement

title: Pentoxifylline as an ancillary treatment for severe falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment (severe falciparum malaria) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, clinical recovery measures).
comparator: placebo (with low-dose and high-dose pentoxifylline as comparator arms, all combined with artesunate)
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria admitted to intensive care unit
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Addition of pentoxifylline to artesunate therapy for severe malaria produced no evident clinical benefit compared with placebo.
follow_up: 72 hours treatment period with outcomes assessed during hospitalization
safety_summary: No significant adverse effects reported; TNF concentrations reduced in all three groups at 48 hr after treatment.

title: Effect of pentoxifylline on cytokine patterns in the therapy of complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing pentoxifylline adjunctive therapy for severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria with reported cytokine outcome results; primary malaria focus; phase not stated but not early-phase safety-only.
population: adult patients with severe/complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Plasma levels of TNF, IL-6, and TNF-receptor after pentoxifylline therapy
impact_summary: High-dose pentoxifylline (40 mg/kg/day) reduced plasma TNF, IL-6, and TNF-receptor levels compared to low-dose pentoxifylline or placebo in adults with severe P. falciparum malaria, though clinical outcome benefit was not established.
effect_metric: change in cytokine plasma levels (TNF, IL-6, TNF-receptor)
effect_estimate: decreased TNF and IL-6 levels after 6 hr high-dose PTX; lower TNF-receptor at 12 and 24 hr
follow_up: first three days of antimalarial treatment
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported beyond cytokine and receptor measurements; no adverse events described.

title: Comparative efficacy of chloroquine/chlorpheniramine combination and mefloquine for the treatment of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates); not early-phase.
population: children with chloroquine-resistant uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasite clearance) at day 14/28
impact_summary: Mefloquine achieved a 100% cure rate at days 14 and 28, while the chloroquine/chlorpheniramine combination achieved an 81% cure rate at day 14, with mefloquine also producing faster parasite and fever clearance.
safety_summary: Adverse effects were minimal; drowsiness and pruritus occurred in the combination group, and abdominal discomfort occurred in the mefloquine group.

title: Randomised placebo-controlled study of atovaquone plus proguanil for malaria prophylaxis in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (blood smear positivity) evaluating atovaquone-proguanil for malaria chemoprevention in children.
population: children living in a hyperendemic area for P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: positive blood smear during chemosuppression
impact_summary: None of the 125 children given atovaquone plus proguanil developed positive blood smears compared with 25 of 140 children given placebo, demonstrating high prophylactic efficacy.
safety_summary: Adverse events during the chemosuppression phase did not differ between the atovaquone plus proguanil group and the placebo group; the combination was well tolerated.

title: A pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic study of intravenous vs oral artesunate in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate) in humans with reported pharmacokinetic and clinical outcome results (parasite and fever clearance).
population: patients with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic parameters of artesunate and dihydroartemisinin, including time to 50% parasite clearance (PCT50)
impact_summary: Both intravenous and oral artesunate produced rapid parasite and fever clearance with comparable clinical outcomes, and oral artesunate showed high relative bioavailability of dihydroartemisinin, supporting its use in primary care settings.
effect_metric: relative bioavailability of DHA (oral vs IV)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on pharmacokinetics with no mention of significant adverse events.

title: Intramuscular artemether vs intravenous quinine: an open, randomized trial in Malawian children with cerebral malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether vs quinine) in children with cerebral malaria that has reported outcome results including mortality and clinical endpoints.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: mortality rate
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether did not significantly reduce mortality compared with intravenous quinine in children with cerebral malaria, though parasite and fever clearance times were faster with artemether.
safety_summary: No significant difference in mortality or coma resolution times between groups; adjusted analyses did not alter findings.

title: Management of severe malarial anaemia in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (iron vs transfusion for malarial anaemia) with reported outcome results; phase not early-phase.
population: children with moderately severe malarial anaemia (PCV <15%)
primary_outcome: Haemoglobin/haematological restoration one month after presentation
impact_summary: Among less severely anaemic children randomized to treatment, oral iron therapy resulted in significantly better haematological restoration at 28 days than blood transfusion without iron, while children with severe anaemia and respiratory distress remained at high risk of death.
effect_estimate: iron group significantly better restored than transfusion group
transmission_setting: holoendemic, seasonal malaria transmission in Gambia
safety_summary: 24 children died overall (23 in the most severely anaemic group), most deaths occurred within 4 hours of admission before transfusion could be given; only 1 death occurred in the iron treatment group, and 10 of the iron group subsequently required transfusion.

title: Follow-up of Gambian children recruited to a pilot safety and immunogenicity study of the malaria vaccine SPf66.
screening_reason: Published pilot RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported safety and clinical malaria outcome results in human participants.
design: randomized, controlled, pilot safety and immunogenicity study, phase II
population: infants aged 6-11 months (followed up in 1995 as young children)
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria attacks
impact_summary: Children who received the SPf66 malaria vaccine had a higher incidence of clinical malaria attacks than controls, but by 1995 the differences between groups were no longer statistically significant.
effect_metric: incidence of clinical attacks per 1000 days at risk
p_value: not significant (>0.05) in 1995 follow-up; significant at 5% level in initial period for high dose Colombian vaccine group
follow_up: 18 weeks during 1995 malaria transmission season (approximately 2 years after initial immunization)
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission in The Gambia
safety_summary: Children who received SPf66 experienced more clinical attacks of malaria than controls; high dose Colombian vaccine group had statistically significant higher incidence initially, though this difference disappeared by 1995 follow-up.

title: Comparative clinical trial of artesunate suppositories and oral artesunate in combination with mefloquine in the treatment of children with acute falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate formulations) in children with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: children with acute uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times and cure rate by day 28
impact_summary: Artesunate suppositories combined with mefloquine were as safe and effective as oral artesunate combined with mefloquine, though parasite clearance was slower with suppositories.
p_value: P < 0.05 for time to 50% parasite reduction; P < 0.001 for time to 90% parasite reduction; not significant for cure rate difference
safety_summary: Both drug regimens were reported as safe and well tolerated, with no significant differences in adverse effects noted between groups.

title: A controlled trial of lambda-cyhalothrin-impregnated bed nets and/or dapsone/pyrimethamine for malaria control in Sierra Leone.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention interventions (insecticide-treated bed nets and chemoprevention) in children in an endemic setting.
population: children in malaria-endemic communities
primary_outcome: clinical malaria episodes due to P. falciparum detected via weekly morbidity surveillance
impact_summary: Combined use of insecticide-treated bed nets and dapsone/pyrimethamine prophylaxis reduced clinical malaria episodes by 72%, significantly more than either intervention alone (49% and 42% respectively).
safety_summary: Interventions were associated with reduced spleen rates, increased hematocrit values, and reduced duration of malaria episodes; no adverse safety issues reported.

title: Randomized comparison of artemether-benflumetol and artesunate-mefloquine in treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments in 617 patients with confirmed malaria, with reported outcome results (cure rates, safety) and clear treatment efficacy focus.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 63-day cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine had a significantly higher 63-day cure rate (94%) than artemether-benflumetol (81%), though artemether-benflumetol was better tolerated with fewer neurological side effects.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, western border of Thailand
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sleep disorders, and other neurological side effects were 2-4 times more common with artesunate-mefloquine than artemether-benflumetol (P < 0.001).

title: Chlorproguanil-dapsone: effective treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia rates at 28 days).
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence of parasitemia (reinfection/recrudescence) at day 28 compared with community surveillance group
impact_summary: Both pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine and triple-dose chlorproguanil-dapsone were effective treatments, while single-dose chlorproguanil-dapsone was associated with a significantly higher rate of parasitemia than the community surveillance group.
effect_metric: relative risk of parasitemia vs community surveillance group

title: Do insecticide-treated curtains reduce all-cause child mortality in Burkina Faso?
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated curtains (vector-control intervention) for malaria in humans with reported outcome results (all-cause child mortality).
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: all-cause child mortality among children aged 6-59 months
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated curtains were associated with a 15% reduction in all-cause child mortality over two years, with the benefit concentrated in the first year and no difference observed in the second year.
effect_estimate: 15% reduction overall (year 1 rate ratio 0.74; year 2 rate ratio 0.99)
transmission_setting: hyperendemic and markedly seasonal malaria transmission

title: A comparative clinical trial of sequential treatments of severe malaria with artesunate suppository followed by mefloquine in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate + mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, cure rates, safety).
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimen of artesunate suppository, higher total dose vs lower total dose)
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: A higher total dose regimen of artesunate suppository (1,600 mg, Group I) followed by mefloquine resulted in significantly faster parasite clearance than a lower dose regimen (1,200 mg, Group II), with no deaths and high cure rates in both groups.
safety_summary: No deaths occurred; no patients had major adverse drug effects; three patients (5%) required rescue treatment due to deteriorating conditions.

title: Monotherapy with sodium artesunate for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand: a comparison of 5- and 7-day regimens.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate monotherapy for uncomplicated malaria that has reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (5-day vs 7-day sodium artesunate regimen)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria acquired in Thailand
primary_outcome: cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Both 5-day (1200 mg) and 7-day (1600 mg) sodium artesunate regimens were safe and effective, with cure rates of 100% and 98% respectively and no significant difference in fever or parasite clearance between groups.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated with no significant adverse safety differences reported.

title: Effect of paracetamol on parasite clearance time in Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasite clearance time, fever clearance time) evaluating paracetamol as an adjunct in malaria treatment; malaria is the primary focus.
population: children with P falciparum malaria treated with intravenous quinine
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Paracetamol did not significantly reduce fever clearance time compared to mechanical antipyresis alone, but significantly prolonged parasite clearance time, likely via reduced TNF and oxygen radical production.
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; paracetamol associated with lower induced TNF and oxygen radical production and prolonged parasite clearance time.

title: The cost-effectiveness of permethrin impregnated bednets in preventing child mortality in Kassena-Nankana district of Northern Ghana.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bednets (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (child mortality, cost-effectiveness); phase not stated but vector-control trials are classified as 'Not applicable'.
population: children
primary_outcome: child mortality
impact_summary: Permethrin impregnated bednets were cost-effective in reducing child mortality, averting 74 child deaths at an estimated cost of US $2003 per death averted and US $73.5 per discounted healthy life-year gained.
effect_estimate: US $2003 per death averted; US $8.8 per child year protected; US $73.5 per discounted healthy life-year gained

title: Severe and complicated malaria treated with artemisinin, artesunate or artemether in Viet Nam.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin derivatives for severe malaria treatment with reported outcome results (defervescence, parasite clearance, consciousness recovery, mortality).
comparator: active comparator (artemisinin suppository vs intramuscular artemether vs intramuscular artesunate vs intravenous artesunate)
population: Vietnamese adults with severe and complicated malaria
primary_outcome: Time to defervescence, parasite clearance time, time to recovery of consciousness, and mortality
impact_summary: There was no significant difference in efficacy among the four artemisinin-based treatment regimens for severe malaria.
safety_summary: No significant differences in efficacy or mortality between treatments; specific adverse events not detailed.

title: Mefloquine compared with doxycycline for the prophylaxis of malaria in Indonesian soldiers. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria chemoprophylaxis interventions in humans with clear efficacy endpoints.
comparator: placebo and active comparator (doxycycline vs mefloquine)
population: Indonesian soldiers
primary_outcome: First occurrence of malaria as documented by a positive malaria smear
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and doxycycline were highly efficacious and well tolerated for malaria prophylaxis, with protective efficacies of 100% and 99% respectively compared to placebo.
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum endemic area, Irian Jaya
safety_summary: Both drugs were very well tolerated.

title: Open randomized trial of oral artemether alone and a sequential combination with mefloquine for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether and mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates and clearance times); not early-phase.
comparator: artemether alone (5-day vs 7-day regimens) compared to sequential artemether-mefloquine
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Sequential treatment with oral artemether followed by mefloquine and the 7-day artemether-alone regimen both achieved 98% cure rates, significantly higher than the 74% cure rate with the 5-day artemether-alone regimen.
safety_summary: No adverse effects were observed in any treatment group; treatments were well-tolerated.

title: Atovaquone and proguanil for the treatment of malaria in Brazil.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment regimens with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; malaria is the primary focus and purpose.
population: men with uncomplicated falciparum malaria and parasitemia 1000-100,000 ring forms/microL, hospitalized for 28 days
primary_outcome: cure rate for uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Atovaquone plus proguanil achieved a cure rate similar to quinine plus tetracycline (98.7% vs 100%), with faster parasite and fever clearance and fewer side effects.
safety_summary: Significantly fewer side effects were reported in the atovaquone plus proguanil group compared to quinine plus tetracycline.

title: Treatment of chloroquine-resistant malaria using pyrimethamine in combination with berberine, tetracycline or cotrimoxazole.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance rates); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
comparator: pyrimethamine plus tetracycline or pyrimethamine plus cotrimoxazole
population: patients with chloroquine-resistant malaria
primary_outcome: clearance rate of asexual parasitaemia after treatment
impact_summary: Pyrimethamine combined with berberine cleared asexual parasitaemia more effectively (74.4%) than pyrimethamine with tetracycline (67.2%) or pyrimethamine with cotrimoxazole (47.8%), indicating berberine combination is the most effective regimen for chloroquine-resistant malaria.

title: Chloroquine versus pyrimethamine/sulphadoxine in the treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in northern Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: symptomatic, parasitaemic patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, divided into children (<10 years) and adults (>10 years)
primary_outcome: Parasitological resistance/treatment failure to chloroquine versus pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine assessed at day 7 and day 14 follow-up
impact_summary: Chloroquine showed significantly higher parasitological resistance than pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine, which remained highly effective against P. falciparum in northern Kenya.
effect_metric: proportion resistant (treatment failure) to chloroquine vs pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine
age_range: children under 10 years and adults over 10 years

title: [The evaluation of the efficacy of artesunate combined with tetracycline in the therapy of falciparum malaria].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate for falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitaemia clearance); primary purpose is malaria intervention in humans; not early-phase.
population: hospitalized patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate and parasitaemia clearance time
impact_summary: Artesunate achieved a faster parasite clearance time than quinine, with similar cure rates among artesunate, mefloquine, and quinine.
safety_summary: No important side effects observed with any therapeutic regimen and no deaths registered.

title: Comparison of artemisinin suppositories, intramuscular artesunate and intravenous quinine for the treatment of severe childhood malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with published outcome results comparing artemisinin-based treatments for severe malaria in children; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans; not early-phase.
population: children with severe P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time (and fever clearance time, coma recovery, length of hospital stay)
impact_summary: Artemisinin suppositories and intramuscular artesunate cleared parasites significantly faster than intravenous quinine and were well tolerated, suggesting artemisinin suppositories are an effective and easy-to-administer treatment for severe childhood malaria in rural settings.
effect_estimate: faster in artemisinin and artesunate groups than quinine group
safety_summary: Both artemisinin and artesunate were well tolerated; lower peripheral reticulocyte counts by day 5 were noted versus quinine (P = 0.011), but no other adverse effects or toxicity were found; 9 deaths occurred overall (2 artemisinin, 4 artesunate, 5 quinine).

title: The effects of malaria control on nutritional status in infancy.
screening_reason: RCT of ITN vector control for malaria with reported outcome results on nutritional status; vector control is a primary malaria intervention.
population: infants aged 1 to 11 months
primary_outcome: Nutritional status markers (weight-for-age and mid-upper arm circumference)
impact_summary: Infants who slept under insecticide-treated bed nets had significantly better nutritional status, as measured by weight-for-age and mid-upper arm circumference, compared with infants not using nets.

title: Supportive pentoxifylline in falciparum malaria: no effect on tumor necrosis factor alpha levels or clinical outcome: a prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled study.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing a malaria treatment intervention (pentoxifylline as adjunct therapy) in humans with reported outcome results (TNF alpha levels, clinical course, laboratory parameters).
comparator: placebo (saline infusion) plus standard antimalarial therapy
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: TNF alpha serum levels and clinical outcome
impact_summary: Pentoxifylline did not reduce TNF alpha levels or improve clinical outcome compared to placebo, and was associated with more adverse effects, leading to early termination of the study.
p_value: P < 0.05 (for study medication discontinuation due to side effects)
safety_summary: Patients receiving pentoxifylline had more nausea and abdominal discomfort than the placebo group; 11 of 27 POF patients versus 3 of 24 placebo patients requested termination of study medication.

title: Analysis of multiple Plasmodium falciparum infections in Tanzanian children during the phase III trial of the malaria vaccine SPf66.
screening_reason: Published Phase III RCT of malaria vaccine SPf66 with reported outcome results on multiplicity of infection and clinical endpoints in Tanzanian children.
population: children
primary_outcome: Multiplicity of infection (MOI) as measured by PCR-RFLP of P. falciparum MSA2 in vaccine vs placebo recipients
impact_summary: MOIs were significantly reduced in asymptomatic SPf66 vaccine recipients compared with asymptomatic placebo recipients, and among placebo recipients higher MOI was associated with lower morbidity, suggesting premunition from concurrent infections protects against clinical malaria.
effect_estimate: 5 in asymptomatic vs 3.4 in symptomatic placebo recipients

title: [Comparison on treatment of falciparum malaria with different courses of artesunate tablet].
journal: Zhongguo Zhong xi yi jie he za zhi Zhongguo Zhongxiyi jiehe zazhi = Chinese journal of integrated traditional and Western medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing artesunate treatment efficacy for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in humans.
comparator: active comparator (different treatment durations of artesunate)
population: uncomplicated falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: Parasite recrudescence rate within 28 days
impact_summary: Prolonging the artesunate treatment course from 3 to 5 or 7 days significantly reduced parasite recrudescence rate within 28 days, while fever and parasite clearance times were similar across groups.
safety_summary: All patients were cured; no adverse events reported.

title: Side effects of mefloquine prophylaxis for malaria: an independent randomized controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (mefloquine vs. chloroquine-proguanil) with reported outcome results on side effects in humans.
comparator: chloroquine 300 mg weekly plus proguanil 200 mg daily
population: male soldiers (non-aviators) on military exercise
primary_outcome: Incidence and severity of side effects (neuropsychological, enteric, other) associated with chemoprophylaxis, assessed by questionnaire at 2 and 8 weeks
impact_summary: Mefloquine was not associated with a significantly different incidence of side effects compared with chloroquine-proguanil, and no serious neuropsychological reactions or malaria cases occurred.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region (military exercise in East Africa)
safety_summary: No serious neuropsychological reactions occurred in either group; side effect incidence did not differ significantly between mefloquine and chloroquine-proguanil groups; no malaria cases developed in 12 months post-return.

title: Single dose artemisinin-mefloquine versus mefloquine alone for uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (artemisinin-mefloquine combination) with reported outcome results on efficacy and recrudescence.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Radical cure rate / therapy failure
impact_summary: Adding a single dose of artemisinin to mefloquine increased the radical cure rate and reduced recrudescence compared to mefloquine alone, but efficacy remained inadequate.
safety_summary: No effect of artemisinin was noted on gametocytes present on admission, but new gametocytes developed less frequently in the AM group; no other safety issues reported.

title: Evidence for selection for the tyrosine-86 allele of the pfmdr 1 gene of Plasmodium falciparum by chloroquine and amodiaquine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine and amodiaquine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitological clearance and drug resistance markers at days 7 and 28).
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Prevalence of pfmdr1 tyr-86 allele in relation to treatment response over time
impact_summary: The tyr-86 allele of pfmdr1 was more prevalent in parasites from children who failed treatment early (day 7) and was selected for during the day 7-28 period, in both chloroquine and amodiaquine treatment groups.

title: Malaria in a nonimmune population after extended chloroquine or primaquine prophylaxis.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine and primaquine prophylaxis) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria infection rates and parasitemia.
population: nonimmune adult men
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria (attack rates, time to parasitemia, parasite density, symptoms) during 28 weeks after cessation of prophylaxis
impact_summary: After stopping one year of prophylaxis, the incidence of P. falciparum infection was significantly higher in the post-chloroquine group than the post-primaquine group during the first two months, with no evidence that primaquine increased risk of malaria compared to placebo or chloroquine.
effect_estimate: 6 of 10 primary P. falciparum and 3 of 10 P. vivax infections in former chloroquine group within one month vs 1 P. falciparum and 0 P. vivax in former primaquine group
safety_summary: No indication that daily primaquine use for one year placed subjects at greater risk of malaria infection or more severe clinical symptoms than placebo or chloroquine groups.

title: A preliminary evaluation of a recombinant circumsporozoite protein vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum malaria. RTS,S Malaria Vaccine Evaluation Group.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (RTS,S) with reported outcome results (infection rates post-challenge) in humans.
population: healthy adults never exposed to malaria
primary_outcome: Development of P. falciparum malaria infection after sporozoite challenge via infected mosquito bites
impact_summary: Vaccine formulation 3 (RTS,S/HBsAg with potent adjuvant) protected most vaccinated subjects against experimental P. falciparum challenge, with only 1 of 7 recipients becoming infected compared with all 6 controls.
safety_summary: Four subjects had adverse systemic reactions possibly related to intensity of immune response after the second dose, leading to reduction of the third dose.

title: [The impact of curtains impregnated with deltamethrin on the vectors and morbidity of malaria: results in Ankazobe, on the plateaus of Madagascar].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of deltamethrin-impregnated curtains (vector control intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on malaria morbidity.
population: volunteer families/villagers in Ankazobe, Madagascar Highlands
primary_outcome: Malaria morbidity, defined as patients having both temperatures greater than 37.5°C and Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia greater than 1500/microliter with clinical symptoms
impact_summary: Deltamethrin-impregnated curtains reduced mosquito bites and malaria morbidity compared to nonimpregnated curtains, with a significant reduction in malaria cases observed in 1994.
effect_estimate: 35 cases (I group) vs 65 cases (NI group) in 1994
transmission_setting: low transmission area, seasonal transmission with peak March to May

title: Maloprim malaria prophylaxis in children living in a holoendemic village in north-eastern Tanzania.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (Maloprim prophylaxis) in children with reported outcome results on clinical malaria incidence, parasitaemia, and secondary endpoints.
population: children aged 1-9 years in a holoendemic village
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria (malaria fever with fever and P. falciparum parasitaemia >=5000/microL)
impact_summary: Weekly Maloprim (dapsone-pyrimethamine) prophylaxis reduced clinical malaria episodes in children aged 1-4 years by 39%, with diminishing efficacy in older children and over time due to increased transmission and drug resistance.
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; trial noted D-P reduced parasite densities and splenomegaly and increased PCV, with no adverse events described.

title: Enhanced efficacy of chloroquine-chlorpheniramine combination in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine combination) in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, cure rates, resistance markers).
population: children with acute symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite and fever clearance times, and parasitological response to treatment
impact_summary: The chloroquine-chlorpheniramine combination showed enhanced efficacy over chloroquine alone, with a lower proportion of patients showing increased parasitaemia at 24 h and a higher cure rate on day 14.
safety_summary: Chloroquine and chloroquine-chlorpheniramine combination were well tolerated; the only prominent adverse effect was pruritus, with equal incidence in both groups.

title: Comparative efficacy of halofantrine, chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment drugs (halofantrine, sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results including cure rates and parasite clearance times.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs halofantrine)
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 7 and parasite/fever clearance times
impact_summary: Halofantrine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine were more effective than chloroquine, with cure rates of 92.3%, 72.7%, and 39.5% respectively, reflecting declining chloroquine sensitivity in the region.
safety_summary: All three drugs were well tolerated.

title: Halofantrine and primaquine for radical cure of malaria in Irian Jaya, Indonesia.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug regimens with reported outcome results (parasitemia recurrence, fever clearance, symptom resolution) for malaria treatment in humans.
population: Adult male Indonesian immigrants with no previous exposure to endemic malaria, normal G6PD activity, uncomplicated malaria illness
primary_outcome: Recurrent parasitaemia during 28 days of follow-up (radical cure failure)
impact_summary: Halofantrine-primaquine achieved 100% radical cure efficacy in both falciparum and vivax malaria, significantly outperforming chloroquine-primaquine against falciparum malaria (33% efficacy) but showing similar efficacy against vivax malaria (89% efficacy).
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported beyond noting faster fever clearance and decline in malaria-related physical complaints with halofantrine-primaquine; no significant difference in parasite-clearance times between regimens.

title: Effects of community-wide use of lambdacyhalothrin-impregnated bednets on malaria vectors in rural Sierra Leone.
screening_reason: Randomized trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (lambdacyhalothrin-treated bed nets) with reported outcome results on An. gambiae densities, parity, and sporozoite rates.
population: rural village residents in Sierra Leone (entomological outcomes, all inhabitants)
primary_outcome: Densities, parity and sporozoite rates of Anopheles gambiae, human blood index, and human biting rates
impact_summary: Community-wide use of lambdacyhalothrin-treated bednets provided personal protection but had little effect on An. gambiae biting density or human blood index, though parous rates were significantly reduced in all intervention villages and sporozoite rates fell in only some villages.
transmission_setting: rural, forest-form Anopheles gambiae malaria vector setting
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Modulatory potential of iron chelation therapy on nitric oxide formation in cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of iron chelation therapy (desferrioxamine) as adjunctive treatment for cerebral malaria in children with reported outcome results on immune markers and nitric oxide formation.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Serum concentrations of nitrite/nitrate (NO2-/NO3-), IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, and neopterin over 3 days
impact_summary: Desferrioxamine plus quinine significantly increased serum nitrite/nitrate levels over 3 days compared to placebo plus quinine, suggesting iron chelation enhances nitric oxide production and Th1-mediated immune function in cerebral malaria.
effect_estimate: significant increase in desferrioxamine group vs no change in placebo group
safety_summary: No adverse events specifically reported in abstract

title: Chemotherapy for cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results testing a malaria treatment intervention (chemotherapy for cerebral malaria) in humans.

title: Field trial of cyfluthrin as an effective and safe insecticide for control of malaria vectors in triple insecticide resistant areas.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector control (indoor residual spraying) for malaria with reported outcome results (vector densities, slide positivity rates) in humans; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
comparator: DDT and Malathion (standard insecticides), untreated controls
population: residents of predominantly tribal areas
primary_outcome: Vector density (per man hour density of An. culicifacies) and malaria slide positivity/slide falciparum rates
impact_summary: Cyfluthrin indoor residual spraying significantly reduced malaria vector densities and slide positivity/falciparum rates compared to controls, with higher community acceptance than DDT or Malathion and no reported adverse effects.
transmission_setting: triple insecticide resistant malaria endemic tribal areas
safety_summary: No reported ill-effects on humans or non-target organisms

title: The effect of oral iron therapy during treatment for Plasmodium falciparum malaria with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine on Malawian children under 5 years of age.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (haemoglobin gain); malaria is the primary focus.
population: children under 5 years of age with Plasmodium falciparum malaria and malaria-associated anaemia (>=500 parasites/microliter, hemoglobin >=5 g/dl)
primary_outcome: Hemoglobin (HB) gain from enrollment to day 28
impact_summary: Children with 5-8 g/dl hemoglobin at enrollment who received daily iron plus SP gained significantly more hemoglobin by days 21 and 28 than those receiving weekly iron plus SP or SP alone, but daily iron was associated with a higher rate of parasite clearance failure, suggesting iron may inhibit SP efficacy.
effect_estimate: SPD: 4.9 g/dl vs SPW: 3.7 g/dl vs SP: 3.5 g/dl by day 28
safety_summary: A larger proportion of iron-treated patients failed to clear parasitaemia compared to those given SP alone, suggesting oral iron may inhibit SP action; no other major safety issues reported.

title: Health education for community-based malaria control: an intervention study in Ecuador, Colombia and Nicaragua.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria prevention/control intervention (health education) with reported outcome results on knowledge and treatment practices.
population: residents of rural malaria-endemic communities on the Pacific coast
primary_outcome: knowledge of malaria aetiology, symptoms and chloroquine dosing, and correct self-treatment practices
impact_summary: Health education improved knowledge of malaria aetiology, symptoms and chloroquine dosing and increased correct chloroquine use in intervention communities compared with control communities, though effects were weaker in Nicaragua.
effect_estimate: 33-61% better knowledge; chloroquine dose knowledge increased 34% (Ecuador) and 93% (Colombia); correct chloroquine use improved 26% (Ecuador) and 85% (Colombia)

title: A comparative study of the efficacies of chloroquine and a pyrimethamine-dapsone combination in clearing Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia in school children in Tanzania.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance at days 2, 7, 14) in a malaria-endemic population.
population: asymptomatic semi-immune schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Clearance of P. falciparum parasitaemia (slide positivity rate at days 2, 7, and 14 after treatment)
impact_summary: The pyrimethamine-dapsone combination (Maloprim) showed lower parasite slide positivity rates than chloroquine at all follow-up points and no chloroquine-level resistance, though differences did not reach statistical significance.
effect_estimate: 23% vs 37% (day 2), 9% vs 20% (day 7), 21% vs 32% (day 14), Maloprim vs chloroquine
transmission_setting: Kilombero District, Tanzania (semi-immune population, endemic area)
safety_summary: No major side-effects were reported in either treatment group.

title: Field trial of permethrin impregnated sisal curtains in malaria control in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated sisal curtains (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results including malaria prevalence and entomological measures.
design: controlled field trial, intervention vs control village
population: children in intervention and control villages
primary_outcome: malaria prevalence in children over the trial period
impact_summary: Permethrin impregnated sisal eaves-curtains reduced indoor vector densities and EIR and were associated with significantly lower malaria prevalence and splenomegaly in children compared to controls.
safety_summary: No adverse events reported; no significant difference in mean change in haematocrit between groups.

title: The effect of a monoclonal antibody to tumor necrosis factor on survival from childhood cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (anti-TNF monoclonal antibody for cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results (mortality and neurologic sequelae).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: mortality and residual neurologic sequelae
impact_summary: The anti-TNF monoclonal antibody B-C7 did not improve survival in cerebral malaria and was associated with a significant increase in residual neurologic sequelae compared with placebo.
safety_summary: B-C7 was associated with a significant increase in neurologic sequelae among survivors (6.8% vs 2.2%; adjusted OR 3.35, 95% CI 1.08-10.4) without improving survival.

title: Evaluation of SPf66 malaria vaccine during a 22-month follow-up field trial in the Pacific coast of Colombia.
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with malaria vaccine intervention reporting outcome results (P. falciparum infection rates and vaccine efficacy) in endemic population.
population: residents of endemic villages who completed the three-dose vaccination schedule
primary_outcome: Incidence of Plasmodium falciparum malaria episodes detected by passive and active surveillance
impact_summary: The SPf66 malaria vaccine reduced the risk of P. falciparum malaria episodes compared to placebo, with an estimated protective efficacy of 35.2%.
transmission_setting: endemic rain forest area with exclusive fluvial access

title: Efficacy and tolerance of artemisinin in short combination regimens for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin-based regimens versus quinine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
comparator: standard seven-day course of oral quinine
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Artemisinin combined with quinine shortened treatment duration and produced faster parasite clearance with comparable efficacy and better tolerance than standard quinine, but artemisinin plus doxycycline was not effective in preventing recrudescence.
safety_summary: Adverse effects were mainly limited to cinchonism.

title: Co-administration of desferrioxamine B with artesunate in malaria: an assessment of safety and tolerance.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported safety and tolerance outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (artesunate co-administered with desferrioxamine B).
population: malaria patients
primary_outcome: safety and tolerance of desferrioxamine B co-administered with artesunate
impact_summary: Co-administration of desferrioxamine B with artesunate was assessed for safety and tolerance in malaria patients.
safety_summary: The combination was evaluated for adverse effects and tolerability; specific safety outcomes not detailed in available metadata.

title: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial of SPf66 malaria vaccine in children in northwestern Thailand. Shoklo SPf66 Malaria Vaccine Trial Group.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes in children; not early-phase.
population: Karen children aged 2-15 living in a malarious region
primary_outcome: Reduction in incidence of first cases of symptomatic falciparum malaria after three doses of vaccine
impact_summary: The SPf66 malaria vaccine showed no protective efficacy against clinical falciparum malaria in Karen children in northwestern Thailand.
safety_summary: Vaccine was well tolerated overall; 26 children had mild or moderately severe local or systemic allergic reactions compared with none in the comparator group; no deaths due to malaria occurred during the study.

title: Activity of artemether-azithromycin versus artemether-doxycycline in the treatment of multiple drug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether combinations) with reported outcome results (cure rates, PCT, FCT) in humans.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated multiple drug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at follow-up
impact_summary: The cure rate with artemether-azithromycin was significantly lower than with artemether-doxycycline (14.8% vs 53.3%), likely due to inadequate azithromycin dosage.
transmission_setting: Thai-Myanmar border, multidrug resistant falciparum malaria area
safety_summary: Low incidence of gastrointestinal adverse effects, especially with azithromycin regimen.

title: Safety evaluation of SPf66 malaria vaccine in Brazil.
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: This is a published RCT reporting safety/side-effect outcome results for a malaria vaccine intervention (SPf66) in humans; not early-phase first-in-human as it describes a vaccine efficacy trial with multiple doses and safety comparisons between vaccine and placebo groups.
population: participants of the SPf66 vaccine efficacy trial
primary_outcome: Frequency and description of side effects (local and systemic) after each dose of SPf66 vaccine or placebo
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine was associated with more frequent local side effects (especially after the 2nd dose) than placebo, but no severe adverse reactions were detected in either group.
safety_summary: Local reactions (mild inflammation, nodule, pain, erythema, pruritus) were more common in the SPf66 group than placebo, particularly after the 2nd dose and more frequent in females; systemic side effects (muscle aches, fever) were mild and similar between groups; no severe adverse reactions occurred.

title: Arteflene compared with mefloquine for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT comparing arteflene and mefloquine for P. falciparum malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance, resistance).
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: Single-dose arteflene was far less effective than mefloquine, with only 1 of 21 arteflene-treated patients cured by day 28 compared with all 21 mefloquine-treated patients.
safety_summary: Both treatment regimens were well-tolerated.

title: Evaluating the community education programme of an insecticide-treated bed net trial on the Kenyan coast.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (childhood malaria morbidity and community education impact).
population: mothers, household heads, and school children in communities on the Kenyan coast
primary_outcome: childhood malaria morbidity
impact_summary: The community education programme improved knowledge and awareness of ITBN use, with children's post-teaching test scores rising from 59% to 92% and 75% household awareness of the trial, though message transfer to homes and outreach coverage remained limited.

title: An efficacy trial of a malaria vaccine in Gambian infants and comparison with insecticide-treated bednets.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (SPf66) in humans with reported outcome results on clinical attacks and parasitaemia; primary purpose is malaria prevention and not early-phase.
comparator: inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) as placebo; comparison also made with insecticide-treated bednets
population: infants aged 6-11 months at first dose
primary_outcome: first or only clinical attack of malaria
impact_summary: The SPf66 malaria vaccine showed only 8% efficacy against the first or only clinical attack compared to placebo and had no significant effect on other malaria morbidity measures, performing worse than insecticide-treated bednets for malaria control.
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission in The Gambia

title: Infant parasite rates and immunoglobulin M seroprevalence as a measure of exposure to Plasmodium falciparum during a randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets on the Kenyan coast.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on parasite prevalence and force of infection.
population: infants on the Kenyan coast
primary_outcome: Parasite prevalence and IgM seropositivity as measures of P. falciparum exposure/force of infection
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bed net use reduced parasite prevalence, IgM seropositivity, and force of infection by approximately 50% compared to control infants.
effect_metric: reduction in force of infection/parasite prevalence/IgM seropositivity

title: Duration of protection and age-dependence of the effects of the SPf66 malaria vaccine in African children exposed to intense transmission of Plasmodium falciparum.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (SPf66) in children with reported efficacy outcomes over 18 months of follow-up.
population: children 1-5 years old
primary_outcome: clinical episodes of P. falciparum malaria over 18 months after third dose
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine showed 25% efficacy against clinical malaria episodes over 18 months and reduced parasite density by 21%, with no significant age-dependent variation in efficacy.
safety_summary: SPf66 vaccine was found to be safe

title: A controlled trial of artemether or quinine in Vietnamese adults with severe falciparum malaria.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether versus quinine for severe malaria treatment in adults with reported outcome results including mortality and clinical endpoints.
population: adults with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: mortality (death)
impact_summary: Artemether was associated with a non-significantly lower mortality rate than quinine and faster parasite clearance, but with slower fever resolution and coma recovery, in Vietnamese adults with severe falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: Vietnam, area with P. falciparum with reduced quinine sensitivity
safety_summary: Quinine treatment was associated with a higher risk of hypoglycemia (relative risk 2.7, 95% CI 1.7-4.4, P<0.001); no other serious side effects were reported in either group.

title: A trial of artemether or quinine in children with cerebral malaria.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether vs quinine for cerebral malaria in children) with reported outcome results (mortality and neurologic sequelae).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: mortality and residual neurologic sequelae
impact_summary: Artemether was as effective as quinine in treating cerebral malaria in children, with similar mortality and neurologic sequelae rates between groups.
safety_summary: Fewer local reactions at the injection site with artemether than with quinine (0.7% vs 5.9%, P=0.001).

title: The impact of permethrin-impregnated bednets on malaria vectors of the Kenyan coast.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednet vector-control intervention with reported outcome results on malaria vector populations.
population: households and residents in Kilifi study area on the Kenyan coast
primary_outcome: Indoor-resting densities and behaviour of malaria vector mosquitoes (An. gambiae s.l. and An. funestus), including engorgement, human blood index, sporozoite rate, parous rates and biting density
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bednets significantly reduced indoor-resting densities and proportion of engorged female mosquitoes in intervention zones, and reduced human-biting rates of An. gambiae s.l. by 8% compared to a 94% increase in control zones, but did not affect human blood index, sporozoite rate, or vector survival (parous rates), and were associated with increased early outdoor biting.
effect_metric: percent change in human-biting density of An. gambiae s.l.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; bioassay and susceptibility testing confirmed permethrin content maintained high mortality of susceptible vectors throughout the trial

title: Artemether or artesunate followed by mefloquine as a possible treatment for multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether or artesunate plus mefloquine for multidrug-resistant malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitemia clearance, safety).
comparator: active comparator (artemether vs artesunate, both followed by mefloquine)
population: male Thai patients with multidrug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 42 follow-up
impact_summary: Both artemether-mefloquine and artesunate-mefloquine regimens achieved high cure rates (98% and 97%, respectively) with rapid parasite and fever clearance and no significant difference between groups.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, eastern Thailand
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects observed; only mild and transient nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite, with no significant difference between the two groups.

title: Pyrethroid-impregnated bed nets for personal protection against malaria for Afghan refugees.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of pyrethroid-impregnated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results showing efficacy against P. vivax and P. falciparum.
design: field trial, non-randomized (families self-selected/issued nets), controlled
comparator: no bed nets (control families without nets)
population: Afghan refugees living in villages in Pakistan
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria infection (measured by microscopy) among intervention vs control groups
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets substantially reduced malaria incidence, with P. vivax infections reduced by about 42% and P. falciparum infections reduced by about 61% compared to controls.
effect_estimate: P. vivax RR 0.58; P. falciparum RR 0.39
effect_ci: P. vivax 95% CI 0.49-0.68; P. falciparum 95% CI 0.29-0.53
transmission_setting: seasonal transmission over a 6-month transmission season in Afghan refugee villages
safety_summary: No sex or age difference in net use or protective efficacy; headlouse infestation rates were reduced in PIB users; no adverse effects reported.

title: Effects of artemisinin derivatives on malaria transmissibility.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drugs (artemisinin derivatives vs mefloquine/halofantrine/quinine) with reported outcome results on gametocyte carriage and malaria transmissibility in humans with acute falciparum malaria.
population: adults and children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte carriage rate (person gametocyte week rate) after antimalarial treatment
impact_summary: Artemisinin derivatives markedly reduced Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte carriage and subsequent malaria incidence compared with mefloquine and quinine.
transmission_setting: malarious hill forest, area of multidrug resistance, western border of Thailand

title: Megatrials show impregnated mosquito nets could save 500,000 African children a year -- at very low cost.
screening_reason: Published results from randomized controlled trials of insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs), a malaria vector-control intervention, demonstrating outcome findings in a human population.
population: African children
impact_summary: Insecticide-impregnated mosquito nets could save 500,000 African children's lives per year at very low cost.

title: Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite vaccine immunogenicity and efficacy trial with natural challenge quantitation in an area of endemic human malaria of Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine with reported outcome results (efficacy, immunogenicity, and clinical endpoints); primary focus is malaria intervention in humans.
population: volunteers in a malaria endemic region, paired by adjacent sleeping arrangement
primary_outcome: Incidence of symptomatic P. falciparum parasitemia and malaria-free survival during post-vaccination observation periods
impact_summary: The circumsporozoite protein vaccine was safe and immunogenic but did not protect against natural P. falciparum challenge, with only 9% efficacy that was not statistically significant.
follow_up: three post-vaccination observation periods (duration not specified in days/months)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic region of Kenya with natural mosquito challenge (0.194 potentially infective Anopheles bites/volunteer/day)
safety_summary: Vaccine was safe, with side-effects similar in both vaccine and control groups.

title: Clinical efficacy and pharmacokinetics of artemisinin monotherapy and in combination with mefloquine in patients with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin-based interventions) with reported outcome results including parasite clearance, fever subsidence, and safety data.
population: adults with symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time (PCT) and fever subsidence time (FST)
impact_summary: Artemisinin combined with mefloquine produced faster parasite clearance and fever resolution, and prevented recrudescence, compared with artemisinin monotherapy.
safety_summary: One patient on combination therapy developed a psychiatric condition; two patients on monotherapy developed skin itch.

title: A comparative study of parenteral chloroquine, quinine and pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in the treatment of Gambian children with complicated, non-cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments in Gambian children with complicated malaria; reports outcome results including fever clearance times, parasite clearance times, clinical failures, and mortality.
comparator: active comparator (quinine vs chloroquine vs pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine)
population: children with complicated, non-cerebral Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Chloroquine and pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine were both effective and had shorter fever and parasite clearance times than quinine, and remain adequate treatments for complicated non-cerebral malaria in Gambian children under close observation.
p_value: 0.02 (chloroquine vs quinine), 0.06 (chloroquine vs P-S), 0.007 (chloroquine vs quinine parasite clearance), <0.001 (P-S vs quinine parasite clearance)
safety_summary: Four children died (one chloroquine, one quinine, two P-S); three chloroquine and three P-S recipients required change to quinine due to clinical failure.

title: Therapeutic effects of chloroquine in combination with quinine in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine with chloroquine vs quinine with tetracycline) in humans with reported outcome results (fever-clearance times, parasite-clearance times, recrudescence rates).
population: Thai men with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever-clearance time and parasite-clearance time; recrudescence (R1) rates
impact_summary: Chloroquine combined with quinine did not improve fever or parasite clearance compared with tetracycline plus quinine, and recrudescence rates were significantly higher in the chloroquine group.
follow_up: 2 months (up to 25 days for recrudescence detection)
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects were reported in either treatment group.

title: Atovaquone and proguanil for Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing atovaquone-proguanil versus amodiaquine for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: adults with acute uncomplicated P falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (clinical and parasitological cure) at day 28 or until recrudescence
impact_summary: Atovaquone plus proguanil achieved a significantly higher cure rate (87%) than amodiaquine (72%) in treating acute uncomplicated P falciparum malaria in Gabon.
safety_summary: Atovaquone plus proguanil group reported nausea (33%) and vomiting (29%); amodiaquine group reported pruritus (43%) and insomnia (27%); no serious adverse events noted.

title: Early clinical failures after pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of a malaria treatment intervention (pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine) in humans; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Early clinical failure after pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine treatment
impact_summary: Some patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria experienced early clinical failure following pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine treatment.

title: An open randomized trial of artemether versus quinine in the treatment of cerebral malaria in African children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing artemether versus quinine for treatment of cerebral malaria in children with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, sequelae), meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: children with coma and Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia (cerebral malaria)
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and mortality/neurological outcomes in cerebral malaria
impact_summary: Artemether cleared parasites faster than quinine but there was no significant overall difference in mortality between the two treatments, and mortality was higher with artemether in children with respiratory distress.
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated with no significant adverse effects observed.

title: Plasmodium falciparum: increased proportion of severe resistance (RII and RIII) to chloroquine and high rate of resistance to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in Peninsular Malaysia after two decades.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results on malaria drug treatment efficacy; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
population: uncomplicated falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: parasite response graded according to WHO criteria (drug resistance classification) over 28 days
impact_summary: Chloroquine resistance rates increased with more severe resistance (RII/RIII) and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance was also high in Peninsular Malaysia after two decades.
safety_summary: Plasma CHL and SDX/PYR levels were within reported ranges and not significantly different between sensitive and resistant responders; no other adverse events reported.

title: Efficacy and pharmacokinetics of a new intrarectal quinine formulation in children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine formulation) in children with P. falciparum malaria that has reported clinical and pharmacokinetic outcome results.
comparator: intramuscular Quinimax and intravenous Quinimax (active comparators)
population: children aged 2-14 years with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological and clinical response (parasite clearance, fever resolution) and pharmacokinetic parameters of quinine
impact_summary: Intrarectal quinine gluconate cream showed similar efficacy and tolerability to intramuscular and intravenous Quinimax in clearing parasitaemia and fever, despite lower bioavailability, suggesting it could be a safe alternative to intramuscular quinine injection in the field.
safety_summary: Tolerability of all three treatments was good; no rectal irritation reported with the intrarectal cream formulation.

title: [An efficacy and tolerance study of oral artesunate alone and in combination with mefloquine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in an endemic area of Pará, Brazil].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate ± mefloquine) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine alone vs artesunate-containing regimens)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time to parasitemia and fever disappearance, and cure/tolerance assessed by clinical, parasitological, biochemical and hematological evaluation over 35 days
impact_summary: Artesunate alone or combined with mefloquine led to faster clearance of parasitemia and fever than mefloquine alone, without significant differences in adverse clinical or biochemical effects among groups.
safety_summary: Clinical and biochemical alterations associated with drug administration did not show significant differences among groups; no important side effects observed.

title: In vivo efficacy of chloroquine, halofantrine, pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine and qinghaosu (artesunate) in the treatment of malaria in Calabar, Nigeria.
journal: The Central African journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (chloroquine, halofantrine, pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine, artesunate) in malaria treatment with reported parasitological and clinical outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs halofantrine vs pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine vs qinghaosu/artesunate)
population: patients with malaria screened from 1004 individuals, randomized to treatment groups
primary_outcome: Parasitological treatment failure rate and symptom clearance at 48 hours
impact_summary: Halofantrine and qinghaosu (artesunate) were significantly more efficacious than chloroquine and pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in clearing malaria parasitemia and symptoms, while chloroquine resistance was confirmed to be increasing in Calabar, Nigeria.
p_value: p < 0.003 (H vs CQ/P-S), p < 0.006 (Q vs CQ/P-S)

title: Impact of permethrin impregnated bednets on child mortality in Kassena-Nankana district, Ghana: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (child mortality reduction).
population: children aged 6 months to 4 years
primary_outcome: all-cause child mortality
impact_summary: Use of permethrin impregnated bednets was associated with a 17% reduction in all-cause mortality in children aged 6 months to 4 years.
transmission_setting: area of intense malaria transmission, seasonal (wet season peak)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Insecticide-treated bednets reduce mortality and severe morbidity from malaria among children on the Kenyan coast.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bednets (vector control) reporting mortality and severe morbidity outcomes in children with malaria in Kenya.
comparator: no ITBN (contemporaneous control communities without treated bednets)
population: children under 5 years of age
primary_outcome: childhood mortality and severe malaria morbidity
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bednets significantly reduced childhood mortality by 33% and severe, life-threatening malaria by 44% among children aged 1-59 months on the Kenyan coast.
transmission_setting: rural, endemic malaria transmission on Kenyan coast
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Artemether-pyrimethamine in the treatment of pyrimethamine-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-pyrimethamine for malaria treatment with reported clinical outcomes including cure rates and parasitemia clearance.
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimens of artemether-pyrimethamine)
population: patients with acute uncomplicated pyrimethamine-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and cure rate at 28 days follow-up
impact_summary: The 3-day artemether-pyrimethamine regimen achieved a significantly higher cure rate (75%) than the 2-day (27.8%) and 1-day (0%) regimens.
safety_summary: Transient mild nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite in a few patients during first 2 days; withdrawals not associated with drug-related adverse effects.

title: Quinine-tetracycline for multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (quinine-tetracycline vs alternatives) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (5-day vs 7-day quinine, both with 7-day tetracycline)
population: male Thai patients with uncomplicated multidrug resistant falciparum malaria admitted to hospital
primary_outcome: 28-day cure rate
impact_summary: The 7-day quinine plus 7-day tetracycline regimen achieved a 100% cure rate compared to 87% with the 5-day quinine plus 7-day tetracycline regimen, indicating the shorter quinine course significantly decreased cure rate.
transmission_setting: multidrug resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, Southeast Asia
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects were found in either group; transient nausea, vomiting and tinnitus (cinchonism) were common; incidence of adverse effects did not differ between groups.

title: Open comparison of artemether and mefloquine in uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether versus mefloquine for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia (>5% parasitized erythrocytes)
primary_outcome: Parasite reduction rate at 24 hours and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether produced significantly higher parasite reduction at 24 hours and shorter parasite clearance time than mefloquine, while both drugs achieved high cure rates and were well tolerated.
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; mefloquine produced more episodes of abdominal pain with or without diarrhoea and vomiting.

title: Reducing the oral quinine-quinidine-cinchonin (Quinimax) treatment of uncomplicated malaria to three days does not increase the recurrence of attacks among children living in a highly endemic area of Senegal.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (quinine-based regimen) in humans with reported outcome results (recurrence, clinical improvement).
population: children under the age of 10 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Recurrence of malaria attacks and clinical/parasitological improvement after treatment
impact_summary: Reducing oral Quinimax treatment from 7 to 3 days did not increase the recurrence of malaria attacks among children, even the youngest.
safety_summary: No adverse safety concerns reported; the shortened 3-day course was well tolerated with clinical improvement in 99.6% of patients.

title: A randomised controlled trial to assess the relative efficacy of chloroquine, amodiaquine, halofantrine and Fansidar in the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment drugs in children with reported efficacy and resistance outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs halofantrine vs Fansidar)
population: children aged three to twelve years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate / parasite clearance
impact_summary: Halofantrine had the highest cure rate (82%), followed by Fansidar (62%), amodiaquine (55%), and chloroquine (29%), with significant differences in cure rates and parasite clearance between groups.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region, Eldoret District Hospital, Kenya
safety_summary: Twelve patients discontinued due to poor clinical response, mostly in the chloroquine group; no other adverse events described.

title: A randomized trial of chloroquine, amodiaquine and pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine in Gambian children with uncomplicated malaria.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatments (chloroquine, amodiaquine, pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine) in children with uncomplicated malaria.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine)
population: rural Gambian children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological failure (parasitaemia) at day 7 and cumulative treatment failure by day 28
impact_summary: Amodiaquine and pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine were both more effective than chloroquine in clearing parasitaemia, with chloroquine having the highest cumulative parasitological failure rate by day 28, while pyrimethamine-sulphadoxine was associated with more early clinical complaints including convulsions.
effect_metric: cumulative parasitological failure rate by day 28
p_value: P = 0.0001 (CQ vs AQ); P = 0.001 (AQ vs PS)
transmission_setting: high chloroquine resistance area, rural sub-Saharan Africa
safety_summary: PS group had significantly more early clinical complaints (17% vs 7% CQ, 17% vs 3% AQ); five children had generalized convulsions (1 AQ, 4 PS), four of whom developed cerebral malaria.

title: Comparative clinical trial of artesunate followed by mefloquine in the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria: two- and three-day regimens.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate + mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance time).
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimen/duration of artesunate-mefloquine)
