population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at 28 days
impact_summary: The three-day artesunate-mefloquine regimen (Group II) achieved a 100% cure rate compared with 84% for the two-day regimen (Group I), with faster parasite and fever clearance.
safety_summary: No serious adverse reactions were reported in either treatment group.

title: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate plus tetracycline versus standard treatment (quinine plus tetracycline) for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Brazil.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT comparing malaria treatment regimens with reported outcome results (cure rates and parasite clearance); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rates (WHO criteria) and parasite clearance at day 2
impact_summary: Artesunate plus tetracycline had similar cure rates to quinine plus tetracycline but faster parasite clearance and fewer side effects.
safety_summary: Incidence of side effects was significantly higher in the QT group (82%) than in the AT group (50%), P < 0.001.

title: Serum neopterin, interleukin-4, and interleukin-6 concentrations in cerebral malaria patients and the effect of iron chelation therapy.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of iron chelation therapy (desferrioxamine B vs placebo) in cerebral malaria patients with reported outcome results on immune markers; malaria is the primary focus.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Serum levels of neopterin, IL-4, and IL-6 over four days
impact_summary: IL-4 levels increased significantly in the placebo group but remained stable in the desferrioxamine B group, while IL-6 decreased markedly in both groups.
effect_estimate: increase in placebo group, no change in desferrioxamine group
p_value: P = 0.04 (IL-4 placebo increase); P < 0.025 (IL-6 decrease in both groups)

title: Randomised trial of pyronaridine versus chloroquine for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance) comparing pyronaridine vs chloroquine for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance during 14-day follow-up
impact_summary: Pyronaridine achieved 100% parasite clearance versus 44% with chloroquine and was rapidly effective and well-tolerated in African patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: No serious drug-related side-effects were noted in pyronaridine-treated patients.

title: A clinical trial with halofantrine on patients with falciparum malaria in Colombia.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported treatment outcomes (cure rates, recrudescence, side effects) for a malaria intervention (halofantrine treatment) in humans; phase not stated but treatment trial is acceptable.
population: semi-immune adult male malaria patients
primary_outcome: cure rate of falciparum malaria following halofantrine treatment
impact_summary: Halofantrine schedule II (three doses of 500 mg) achieved the best cure rate (75%), though not significantly different from other dosing schedules, and 46 patients experienced recrudescent malaria.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum area; hospitalized in a non-endemic area (Medellin)
safety_summary: Side-effects were mainly gastrointestinal, uncommon and mild; cardiotoxicity assessed by ECG showed a mean Q-Tc prolongation of 28.5 ms (6.6 +/- 6.3% increase from baseline) on day 1.

title: The disposition and effects of two doses of dichloroacetate in adults with severe falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of dichloroacetate as adjunctive treatment for severe malaria with reported outcome results on lactate reduction and safety.
population: adults with severe falciparum malaria and lactic acidosis
primary_outcome: Reduction in venous plasma lactate concentration following dichloroacetate administration
impact_summary: Dichloroacetate rapidly and significantly reduced venous lactate concentrations compared with placebo in adults with severe falciparum malaria, without evidence of toxicity.
effect_metric: percent reduction in venous plasma lactate from baseline
safety_summary: No electrocardiographic or other evidence of toxicity associated with DCA administration.

title: Multiple dose pharmacokinetics of oral artemisinin and comparison of its efficacy with that of oral artesunate in falciparum malaria patients.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing oral artemisinin and artesunate for malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes (parasite clearance time, fever subsidence time); phase not stated but treatment trial is not early-phase.
population: adults with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: time to parasite clearance (PCT) and fever subsidence time (FST)
impact_summary: Oral artesunate cleared parasites and resolved fever faster than oral artemisinin, with both drugs showing similar recrudescence rates and no clinical abnormalities.
safety_summary: Standard haematology, blood biochemistry and urinalysis were normal on days 6 and 14; no clinical abnormality observed during the study.

title: Malaria parasite infection during pregnancy and at delivery in mother, placenta, and newborn: efficacy of chloroquine and mefloquine in rural Malawi.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial regimens (chloroquine vs mefloquine) for malaria treatment in pregnant women with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and infection rates.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Clearance of initial parasitemia, prevention of breakthrough infection, and parasitemia at delivery in maternal, placental, and cord blood
impact_summary: Women treated with chloroquine had significantly higher rates of persistent infection, breakthrough infection, and parasitemia at delivery than those treated with mefloquine, indicating chloroquine's reduced efficacy against resistant P. falciparum.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic rural Malawi with seasonal (rainy/postrainy) transmission and chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum

title: Comparability of treatment groups and risk factors for parasitemia at the first antenatal clinic visit in a study of malaria treatment and prevention in pregnancy in rural Malawi.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment and prophylaxis in pregnant women in Malawi with reported outcome results on parasitemia prevalence and risk factors.
design: prospective randomized trial, four treatment arms
comparator: chloroquine regimen (three groups) vs mefloquine regimen (one group)
population: pregnant women attending first antenatal clinic visit
primary_outcome: Parasitemia at first antenatal clinic visit and risk factors for infection
impact_summary: Parasitemia at first antenatal clinic visit was strongly associated with low gravidity, high transmission season, lack of prior prophylaxis, young age, HIV infection, low hematocrit, short stature, and second trimester, with HIV infection increasing risk of parasitemia by 55%; treatment groups were otherwise similar at baseline.
effect_metric: increased risk of parasitemia associated with HIV infection
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission, seasonal, rural Malawi
age_range: pregnant women, including those under 20 years

title: Clinical studies of iron chelators in malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of an iron chelator (desferrioxamine B) as an adjunctive malaria treatment intervention with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, coma recovery) in malaria-infected humans.
comparator: placebo (added to standard quinine-based therapy) for cerebral malaria cohort; single-agent open-label desferrioxamine in uncomplicated malaria cohort
population: Zambian and Thai patients with mild to moderate P. falciparum or P. vivax malaria, and Zambian children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Clearance of asexual peripheral blood parasites and recovery from coma (in cerebral malaria cohort)
impact_summary: Desferrioxamine B accelerated parasite clearance in mild to moderate malaria (though recrudescence was common) and, in cerebral malaria children, sped both parasite clearance and recovery from coma compared to placebo.
effect_metric: time to parasite clearance and coma recovery
age_range: children (cerebral malaria cohort); mixed ages (mild/moderate malaria cohort)
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond noting recrudescence occurred in most subjects with mild/moderate infection treated with desferrioxamine alone; no major adverse events reported in text.

title: Mefloquine in the Prophylaxis of P. Falciparum Malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine for malaria prophylaxis in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia incidence and side effects) across multiple drug arms including placebo.
population: semi-immune male volunteers living in an endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria breakthroughs (acute malaria attacks) and incidence of parasitemia
impact_summary: Mefloquine (Lariam), Fansidar, and Fansimef provided full protection against P. falciparum parasitemia, whereas chloroquine offered only partial protection, with comparable and mild side effects across all groups.
p_value: not significant (chi-square test for side effects)
safety_summary: Most frequent side effects were pruritus (5.6%), diarrhea (1.2%) and headache (0.06%); all transient and mild, with no significant differences between groups.

title: A comparative clinical trial of artemether and the sequential regimen of artemether-mefloquine in multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether vs artemether-mefloquine) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates).
population: Thai male patients with acute uncomplicated, multidrug resistant falciparum malaria admitted to hospital
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and cure rate following treatment
impact_summary: The sequential artemether-mefloquine regimen achieved a higher cure rate (94%) than artemether alone (88%), with rapid parasite and fever clearance in both groups and no serious adverse effects.
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects were observed in either treatment group.

title: Efficacy of halofantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: This is a published randomized controlled trial comparing halofantrine to metakelfin for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (fever resolution, parasitaemia, adverse effects).
population: patients with laboratory confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, mostly young children
primary_outcome: Resolution of fever and parasitaemia clearance
impact_summary: Halofantrine was comparable to metakelfin in resolving fever and clearing parasitaemia, with no major adverse effects observed.
age_range: 66% under 5 years; remainder unspecified older ages
safety_summary: No major adverse side effects were observed with halofantrine treatment.

title: Short report: pefloxacin does not potentiate quinine efficacy against Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine ± pefloxacin) with reported outcome results on parasite and fever clearance in humans.
population: patients with severe Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: speed of parasite or fever clearance
impact_summary: Pefloxacin combined with quinine did not improve antimalarial efficacy compared to quinine alone.

title: Efficacy of oral and intravenous artesunate in male Tanzanian adults with Plasmodium falciparum malaria and in vitro susceptibility to artemisinin, chloroquine, and mefloquine.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate (malaria treatment intervention) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times, fever subsidence times, recrudescence rates) in human participants.
comparator: active comparator (oral artesunate vs intravenous artesunate)
population: male adult patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time (PCT) and fever subsidence time (FST)
impact_summary: Oral and intravenous artesunate were equally efficacious and well tolerated, with similar parasite clearance and fever subsidence times and comparable recrudescence rates.
p_value: 0.006 (for weak correlation between artemisinin and chloroquine EC50 values)
safety_summary: No clinically significant changes in blood biochemistry, hematology, or electrocardiograms; erythrocyte count and hemoglobin slightly reduced after iv treatment but remained within normal range.

title: Increase of birth weight following chloroquine chemoprophylaxis during the first pregnancy: results of a randomized trial in Cameroon.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results (birth weight, placental infection).
population: primigravidae attending first prenatal visit at antenatal clinic
primary_outcome: birth weight and placental malaria infection at delivery
impact_summary: Chloroquine chemoprophylaxis during first pregnancy significantly increased mean birth weight and reduced low birth weight and placental infection despite moderate chloroquine resistance.
transmission_setting: hyperendemic, high transmission all year round
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Iron, but not folic acid, combined with effective antimalarial therapy promotes haematological recovery in African children after acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (antimalarial therapy with iron/folic acid supplementation) in children with acute falciparum malaria.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: haematological recovery (haemoglobin level) after antimalarial treatment with iron or folic acid supplementation
impact_summary: Iron supplementation significantly improved haematological recovery after malaria without increasing malaria prevalence, whereas folic acid did not improve recovery and increased treatment failure rates when combined with Fansidar.
safety_summary: Iron supplementation was not associated with increased prevalence of malaria; folic acid combined with Fansidar was associated with higher treatment failure rate.

title: Comparison of artemether and quinine in the treatment of severe falciparum malaria in south-east Thailand.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether versus quinine for severe falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, adverse effects).
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: survival rate and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether resulted in a higher survival rate and faster parasite clearance than quinine in patients with severe falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Quinine group had tinnitus, 2 cases of severe hearing impairment (resolved within 1 week), QTc prolongation without arrhythmia, 2 cases of facial palsy, 1 myasthenia gravis-like syndrome, and 7 deaths from pulmonary complications; artemether group had mild transient injection site pain with no abscesses, no neurological sequelae, and no deaths from complications.

title: A comparison of the efficacy of insecticide-treated and untreated bed nets in preventing malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria prevention in children.
comparator: untreated bed nets versus no bed net use
population: children 1-4 years old
primary_outcome: malariometric indices (parasitaemia, spleen rates) and packed cell volume
impact_summary: Both treated and untreated bed nets reduced malaria risk in children, with insecticide-treated nets providing greater protection, especially against infections with high parasitaemia.

title: Oral artesunate in the treatment of uncomplicated hyperparasitemic falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing oral artesunate versus quinine for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported clinical outcomes (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated hyperparasitemic falciparum malaria (>4% parasitemia, no vital organ dysfunction)
primary_outcome: Time to fever clearance, parasite clearance, and cure rate by day 28
impact_summary: Oral artesunate plus mefloquine resulted in faster fever and parasite clearance, quicker hospital discharge, and higher cure rates than intravenous quinine plus mefloquine.
effect_metric: relative risk of cure by day 28
p_value: <0.0001 for fever/parasite clearance and discharge times
safety_summary: No deaths, no progression to severe malaria, and no toxicity attributable to artesunate.

title: Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine or chloroquine/clindamycin treatment of Gabonese school children infected with chloroquine resistant malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (cure rates) for malaria treatment in humans; not early-phase.
population: school children infected with malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate
impact_summary: Combination regimens of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and chloroquine/clindamycin cured more than 90% of patients, while high-dose chloroquine monotherapy cured only 32%.

title: Deltamethrin impregnated bednets for the control of urban malaria in Kumba Town, South-West Province of Cameroon.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of deltamethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results (malaria prevalence, spleen rates, parasite density).
population: children aged ≤15 years in households
primary_outcome: malaria prevalence
impact_summary: Deltamethrin impregnated bednets significantly reduced overall malaria prevalence and enlarged spleen rates compared to no nets, though the effect was smaller than in rural settings.

title: Insecticide-impregnated bed nets for malaria control: varying experiences from Ecuador, Colombia, and Peru concerning acceptability and effectiveness.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-impregnated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (malaria incidence reduction).
comparator: control communities without impregnated bed nets (DDT spraying in one control area)
population: residents of endemic malarious communities
primary_outcome: reduction of malaria incidence in intervention versus control communities
impact_summary: Insecticide-impregnated bed nets reduced malaria incidence compared to control communities, with average protective efficacy of 40.8% for four-month clinical attack incidence and 28.3% for two-week incidence, though effectiveness varied widely (0%-70%) across study areas.
effect_estimate: 0%-70% (average 40.8% for four-month incidence, 28.3% for two-week incidence)

title: Effects of azithromycin on malariometric indices in The Gambia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing azithromycin (antimalarial intervention) in humans; malaria is the primary focus with parasitemia and spleen rates as main endpoints.
population: children aged 5-14 years in villages participating in a trachoma control trial
primary_outcome: Proportion of children with Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia at day 28
impact_summary: Azithromycin given for trachoma control significantly reduced malaria parasite rates, spleen rates, febrile parasitaemia, and P. malariae infection compared to tetracycline eye ointment.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events described.

title: Artesunate versus artemether in combination with mefloquine for the treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin-based treatment regimens for multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria in humans with reported outcome results (failure rates, parasite clearance times).
population: adults and children with multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment failure rate after adjusting for reinfections
impact_summary: Combination regimens of artesunate or artemether with mefloquine were significantly more effective and better tolerated than mefloquine alone, which had a much higher failure rate.
effect_metric: relative risk of treatment failure (mefloquine alone vs combination)
follow_up: not specified (fever/parasite clearance and failure rate after adjusting for reinfections)
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria area, Thai-Myanmar border
safety_summary: No significant adverse effects attributable to the artemisinin derivatives; both artesunate and artemether combinations were well tolerated.

title: The effect of plasma free fatty acids and long-chain triglycerides on glucose metabolism in uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a malaria treatment intervention (dextrose and lipid infusions in quinine-treated falciparum malaria patients) with reported outcome results on glucose metabolism.
comparator: dextrose infusion alone (without heparin/Intralipid) at two different rates
population: Untreated Thai adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria receiving quinine
primary_outcome: Change in plasma glucose concentration from beginning to end of dextrose infusion
impact_summary: Adding heparin and Intralipid to increase plasma free fatty acids and triglycerides enhanced the glycaemic response to lower-rate dextrose infusion but did not further augment the response to high-rate dextrose infusion, without causing rebound hypoglycaemia.
effect_metric: Mean change in plasma glucose concentration
effect_estimate: Group A: 0.1 mmol/L vs Group C: 1.0 mmol/L; Group B: 1.8 mmol/L vs Group D: 2.2 mmol/L
p_value: P = 0.015 (A vs C); P < 0.5 (B vs D)
safety_summary: No rebound hypoglycaemia observed in any patient during the 7 hours following infusion, despite significant increases in plasma insulin.

title: Fever in uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria: randomized double-'blind' comparison of ibuprofen and paracetamol treatment.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing antimalarial fever management in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria and fever >38.5°C
primary_outcome: Reduction in body temperature after treatment
impact_summary: Ibuprofen was significantly more effective than paracetamol at lowering fever during the first 4.5 hours after dosing in patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Ibuprofen should be considered an antipyretic providing there is no contraindication to its use; no specific adverse events reported.

title: A field trial with Lambda-cyhalothrin (ICON) for the intradomiciliary control of malaria transmitted by Anopheles darlingi root in Rondonia, Brazil.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of indoor residual spraying (IRS) with vector-control insecticide for malaria prevention that reported outcome results (malaria case incidence decline).
population: residents of households in Machadinho and Jaru districts, Rondonia
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence (reported Plasmodium falciparum cases) measured by passive case detection
impact_summary: Indoor residual spraying with Lambda-cyhalothrin (ICON) reduced reported P. falciparum cases by 76% in Machadinho and 28% in Jaru, outperforming DDT in vector control efficacy and duration.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in reported P. falciparum cases
transmission_setting: endemic, Amazon region, Anopheles darlingi as primary vector
safety_summary: Side effects of the insecticide were limited.

title: Chloroquine versus amodiaquine in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in northeast India.
journal: The Indian journal of medical research
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial drugs for P. falciparum treatment with reported efficacy outcomes; malaria treatment is the primary purpose; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria in chloroquine resistant areas
primary_outcome: cure rate, degree of resistance, mean parasite clearance time and mean parasite recrudescence time
impact_summary: Amodiaquine showed no advantage over chloroquine in treating P. falciparum malaria, with comparable cure rates and resistance patterns and evidence of complete cross-resistance between the two drugs.
effect_estimate: comparable between groups, not statistically significant
transmission_setting: chloroquine resistant areas of northeast India
safety_summary: Study notes toxicity concerns of amodiaquine but no specific adverse event data reported.

title: Efficacy of permethrin-impregnated uniforms in the prevention of malaria and leishmaniasis in Colombian soldiers.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of permethrin-impregnated uniforms (a vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results; phase not stated but vector-control trials are classified as 'not applicable' phase and are eligible.
population: Colombian soldiers on patrol in malaria- and leishmaniasis-endemic areas
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria and leishmaniasis infection among soldiers wearing permethrin-impregnated uniforms versus control uniforms
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated uniforms significantly reduced the incidence of both malaria and leishmaniasis among soldiers compared to control uniforms.
follow_up: Malaria: 4.2 weeks exposure plus 4 weeks observation; Leishmaniasis: 6.6 weeks exposure plus 12 weeks observation
transmission_setting: areas of endemicity for malaria and leishmaniasis in Colombia
safety_summary: Permethrin-treated uniforms were virtually nontoxic, with only two cases of mild skin irritation among 229 subjects.

title: Efficacy trial of malaria vaccine SPf66 in Gambian infants.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (SPf66) in human infants with reported outcome results (clinical malaria episodes, mortality, health centre admissions).
population: infants aged 6-11 months at first dose
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against clinical P. falciparum malaria (fever >=37.5°C with parasite density >=6000/microL)
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine did not provide significant protection against clinical malaria episodes in Gambian infants during the rainy season.
effect_metric: protective efficacy against first or only clinical episode
follow_up: three and a half months (one rainy season)
transmission_setting: seasonal, intensive malaria transmission during rainy season
safety_summary: No differences in mortality or health centre admissions were found between SPf66 and IPV groups.

title: Malaria prophylaxis. Toxicity of mefloquine is similar to that of other chemoprophylaxis.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results on malaria chemoprophylaxis (mefloquine vs other agents), a valid malaria prevention intervention in humans.
safety_summary: Toxicity of mefloquine was found to be similar to that of other chemoprophylaxis agents.

title: Quinine plus clindamycin improves chemotherapy of severe malaria in children.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, mortality) testing a malaria treatment intervention in children with severe P. falciparum malaria.
population: children with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: The 4-day quinine-clindamycin regimen resulted in significantly faster parasite and fever clearance and fewer recurring fever episodes compared to the standard 7-day quinine regimen.
safety_summary: One death occurred in each treatment group.

title: The impact of permethrin impregnated bednets on the malaria vector Anopheles maculatus (Diptera: Culicidae) in aboriginal villages of Pos Betau Pahang, Malaysia.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bednets (vector-control intervention for malaria) with reported outcome results on sporozoite rates and biting behavior.
population: aboriginal villagers
primary_outcome: Sporozoite rate, parous rate, and human biting rate (bites/man/night) of Anopheles maculatus
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bednets significantly reduced sporozoite and parous rates and human biting rates of An. maculatus compared to placebo bednets.
effect_metric: difference in bites/man/night pre vs post treatment
p_value: p < 0.05 for sporozoite/parous rates; p < 0.001 for bites/man/night in treated villages

title: Treatment of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium vivax with chloroquine and primaquine or halofantrine.
screening_reason: RCT comparing malaria treatments (chloroquine-resistant P. vivax) with reported outcome results on therapeutic failure; not early-phase.
population: Javanese residents of Irian Jaya infected by P. vivax
primary_outcome: Therapeutic failure within 14 and 28 days of starting therapy
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus primaquine and halofantrine were significantly more effective than chloroquine alone against chloroquine-resistant P. vivax infection.
effect_estimate: 44% (chloroquine) vs 5% (chloroquine+primaquine) vs 0% (halofantrine) at day 14; 78% vs 15% vs 6% at day 28
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant P. vivax endemic area, Irian Jaya
safety_summary: No difference in tolerance to or side effects among the three regimens.

title: Daily primaquine is effective for prophylaxis against falciparum malaria in Kenya: comparison with mefloquine, doxycycline, and chloroquine plus proguanil.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis in children with reported outcome results (efficacy against falciparum malaria infection).
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine, doxycycline, chloroquine plus proguanil, vitamin alone)
population: children 9-14 years old in a holoendemic malaria region
primary_outcome: Prevention of symptomatic and asymptomatic malarial infection
impact_summary: Daily primaquine was as effective as doxycycline and mefloquine in preventing malaria, while chloroquine plus proguanil was the least effective regimen, and primaquine showed no toxicity over the study period.
effect_metric: comparative efficacy in preventing malarial infection
safety_summary: No toxicity observed from daily primaquine during the 11-week study period.

title: Transferrin saturation and recovery from coma in cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: RCT of iron chelator (desferrioxamine B) versus placebo for cerebral malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (time to recovery from coma).
population: children with strictly defined cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: time to recover full consciousness in relation to transferrin saturation
impact_summary: Children with elevated transferrin saturations (>43%) had significantly delayed recovery of consciousness compared to those with lower saturations, and adding the iron chelator desferrioxamine to quinine therapy appeared to hasten recovery in children with high saturations.
effect_metric: median time to recover full consciousness (hours)
effect_estimate: 68.2 hours (high saturation) vs 25.4 hours (low saturation) among placebo group
transmission_setting: holoendemic malaria transmission area in Zambia
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond noting elevated transferrin saturations associated with delayed recovery; no specific adverse events reported in this analysis.

title: Primaquine for prophylaxis against malaria among nonimmune transmigrants in Irian Jaya, Indonesia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine versus chloroquine for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (infection rates and protective efficacy).
population: nonimmune transmigrant children and adults
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria infection (P. falciparum and P. vivax) during prophylaxis
impact_summary: Primaquine prophylaxis was significantly more protective than chloroquine against both P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria and was better tolerated.
effect_estimate: 74% against P. falciparum, 90% against P. vivax
safety_summary: Primaquine was better tolerated than chloroquine.

title: Efficacy and tolerance in adults of a short (3 days) course of quinine for uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Annales de la Societe belge de medecine tropicale
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting efficacy outcomes of quinine treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in adults.
population: adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological cure/efficacy of short-course quinine therapy
impact_summary: A shortened 3-day course of quinine was compared to a standard longer course for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in adults, assessing efficacy and tolerance.
safety_summary: Tolerance of the 3-day quinine regimen was assessed as part of the study outcomes.

title: Pentoxifylline as a supportive agent in the treatment of cerebral malaria in children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results (coma duration, mortality, TNF levels).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Coma duration and mortality
impact_summary: Children treated with pentoxifylline plus quinine had significantly shorter coma duration than those receiving quinine alone, with a trend toward lower mortality that did not reach statistical significance.
p_value: P < .001 for coma duration; P = .055 for mortality
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; pentoxifylline associated with decline in TNF serum levels on day 3 in some subjects, no adverse events reported in abstract.

title: Open comparison of mefloquine, mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and chloroquine in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatment interventions with reported outcome results (parasitaemia, fever reduction); primary focus is malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine vs mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine vs chloroquine)
population: children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological and clinical response to treatment (reduction of parasitaemia and fever)
impact_summary: Mefloquine alone and mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine had similar efficacy and reduced parasitaemia and fever faster than chloroquine, with no added benefit from combining mefloquine with sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine.
effect_estimate: 10% reduced susceptibility to mefloquine; 18% resistant to chloroquine

title: A comparative clinical trial of two different regimens of artemether plus mefloquine in multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemether/mefloquine combination) in humans with reported clinical outcomes (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates); not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (standard dose mefloquine vs high dose mefloquine)
population: male Thai patients with multidrug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at follow-up (parasite clearance and recrudescence)
impact_summary: The high-dose mefloquine combination with artemether achieved a significantly higher cure rate (96%) than the standard-dose regimen (75%).
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects; mild and transient dizziness, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea in about half of patients in each group.

title: Entomological evaluation of community-wide use of lambdacyhalothrin-impregnated bed nets against malaria in a border area of north-west Thailand.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (bed nets) with reported entomological outcome results; phase is not applicable for vector-control cluster trials.
population: Village residents in a malaria-endemic border area
primary_outcome: Mosquito biting density and parous rates of Anopheles species
impact_summary: Lambdacyhalothrin-treated bed nets showed no significant overall impact on mosquito biting density or parous rates compared to untreated/placebo nets, likely due to net washing and low reimpregnation rates.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic border area of north-west Thailand

title: Deltamethrin impregnated bednets against Anopheles minimus transmitted malaria in Assam, India.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of deltamethrin-impregnated bednets (vector control intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results showing significant decline in malaria parameters in treated villages.
comparator: untreated bednets and untreated no-net controls
population: tribal villagers in malaria-endemic villages
primary_outcome: slide positivity rate and monthly parasite index
impact_summary: Deltamethrin-impregnated bednets significantly reduced malaria slide positivity rate and monthly parasite index compared to untreated nets and no-net controls, where malaria indices remained unchanged or rose.
effect_metric: change in slide positivity rate/monthly parasite index
effect_estimate: significant decline in treated net villages vs rise in controls
transmission_setting: rural endemic, Anopheles minimus vector, biting peaks after midnight
safety_summary: Nets well received by local tribal population; no adverse events reported

title: Artemether-mefloquine combination in multidrug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether-mefloquine combination for malaria treatment with reported cure-rate outcomes in drug-resistant P. falciparum.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine 750 mg plus placebo vs mefloquine 750 mg plus 500 mg)
population: male Thai patients with multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at follow-up (day 28-42)
impact_summary: Adding a single oral dose of artemether (300 mg) to mefloquine 750 mg significantly improved the cure rate compared with mefloquine 750 mg plus placebo, with rapid clearance of parasitaemia and fever in both groups.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, eastern Thailand
safety_summary: No serious adverse effects; mild and transient nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite noted, not differing between groups.

title: The antipruritic effects of chlorpheniramine, cyproheptadine and sulphapyridine monitored with limb activity meters on chloroquine induced pruritus among patients with malaria.
journal: African journal of medicine and medical sciences
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing antipruritic interventions (chlorpheniramine, cyproheptadine, sulphapyridine) to manage chloroquine-induced pruritus in malaria patients; malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: active comparator (chlorpheniramine vs cyproheptadine vs sulphapyridine, with unmedicated healthy controls)
population: adult patients with chloroquine-induced pruritus during malarial febrile paroxysms
primary_outcome: Limb activity (scratch-related movement) measured by limb activity meters during nocturnal sleep
impact_summary: Sulphapyridine reduced upper limb scratching activity more than cyproheptadine and chlorpheniramine, though sulphapyridine-treated patients still itched more than unmedicated controls and had frequent gastrointestinal side effects.
effect_estimate: Sulphapyridine > cyproheptadine > chlorpheniramine in antipruritic effect
p_value: P < 0.0001 (right hand, sulphapyridine vs cyproheptadine); P < 0.01 (left hand); P < 0.05 (sulphapyridine vs controls, right hand)
safety_summary: 5 of 6 patients on sulphapyridine developed anorexia, fullness, or indigestion; no other major adverse effects reported.

title: Randomized trial of SPf 66 P. falciparum vaccine in children.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported outcome results in the target population (children).
population: children

title: [Rectal quinine, an alternative to parenteral injections for the treatment of childhood malaria. Clinical, parasitological and pharmacological study].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of quinine treatment (malaria intervention) in children with reported clinical and parasitological outcomes; phase and design appropriate; not early-phase.
population: children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria requiring parenteral therapy
primary_outcome: Clinical (temperature normalization) and parasitological (parasite clearance) response, and pharmacokinetics of quinine
impact_summary: Rectal administration of quinine (Quinimax or a new quinine gluconate formulation) achieved comparable temperature normalization and parasite clearance to intramuscular and intravenous quinine, with good tolerability, supporting its use as an alternative route for treating childhood malaria in Africa.
safety_summary: The new intrarectal quinine formulation was well tolerated with good efficacy, avoiding the frequent side effects associated with injectable quinine.

title: Randomised trial of SPf66 vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in southern Tanzania.
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (SPf66) in humans with reported outcome results (protective efficacy 31%) and primary malaria intervention focus.
population: children under 5 years old
primary_outcome: Incidence of febrile illness attributed to Plasmodium falciparum malaria
impact_summary: The SPf66 vaccine showed a protective efficacy of 31% against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Kilombero, southern Tanzania.
transmission_setting: perennial, intense transmission (parasite prevalence >=80% year-round, ~300 infectious bites per year)

title: Impregnated bednets trial in Kumba, Cameroon.
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Published RCT of an ITN (impregnated bednet) malaria prevention intervention with reported outcome results.

title: [Study of the impact of deltamethrin impregnated curtains on malaria morbidity in Ankazobe of the Madagascar highlands].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Published RCT of a vector-control intervention (deltamethrin-impregnated curtains) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results.
population: residents of villages in the Madagascar highlands, including children
primary_outcome: malaria morbidity (incidence of clinical malaria episodes)
impact_summary: Villages using deltamethrin-impregnated curtains showed reduced malaria morbidity compared to villages with unimpregnated curtains.

title: [NANP]19-5.1. A malaria vaccine field trial in Nigerian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (NANP/schizont export antigen 5.1) in humans with reported outcome results (clinical malaria incidence, antibody response).
population: schoolchildren with partial pre-existing immunity to malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria during 12 weeks of observation
impact_summary: During the 12-week observation period, no vaccinated or placebo child developed clinical malaria, likely because most children already had substantial antibody levels to both vaccine antigens, indicating the trial population was too immune to assess vaccine efficacy.
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; no adverse events described in abstract.

title: [Treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria attacks in children with artemether in Gabon].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (two artemether dose groups) reporting efficacy and safety outcomes in malaria treatment in children; primary focus is malaria intervention (treatment).
population: children with mild or severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria attacks
primary_outcome: Time to parasite clearance and resolution of severe symptoms
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether cleared parasites in all evaluable patients within a mean of 47.7 hours regardless of dose or severity, with excellent tolerance and no deaths.
safety_summary: No deaths; local and systemic tolerance was excellent; two cases of clinical and parasitological recrudescence on days 14 and 21; neurological symptoms resolved within 48 hours in most cases.

title: Specific and nonspecific responses to Plasmodium falciparum blood-stage parasites and observations on the gametocytemia in schoolchildren living in a malaria-endemic area of Mozambique.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs. pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine) in humans with reported outcome results on parasitemia and gametocytemia clearance.
population: schoolchildren with P. falciparum gametocytemia
primary_outcome: Dynamics of asexual parasitemia and gametocytemia over 28 days following treatment
impact_summary: Pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine cleared both asexual parasites and gametocytes far more effectively than chloroquine by day 28, suggesting high chloroquine resistance, with no evidence that either drug induced gametocytogenesis.
effect_estimate: chloroquine: 61.1% asexual, 5.6% gametocyte; pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine: 2.4% asexual, 2.4% gametocyte

title: Village trial of bednets impregnated with wash-resistant permethrin compared with other pyrethroid formulations.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (ITNs) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on mosquito catches and insecticidal efficacy.
comparator: placebo-treated bednets and other pyrethroid formulations
population: villagers using their own bednets in a Mandinka village
primary_outcome: Number of mosquitoes found under bednets during early morning searches and insecticidal efficacy measured by bioassay mortality
impact_summary: Pyrethroid-treated bednets, especially those with wash-resistant permethrin, showed significantly fewer mosquitoes and better retained insecticidal efficacy after washing compared with placebo-treated nets and standard formulations.
transmission_setting: rural West Africa, Anopheles gambiae main vector
safety_summary: Not reported

title: High efficacy of short-term quinine-antibiotic combinations for treating adult malaria patients in an area in which malaria is hyperendemic.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing malaria treatment regimens with reported outcome results (cure rates) in adults with P. falciparum malaria.
population: adult malaria patients
primary_outcome: Cure rate of P. falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Short-term quinine-antibiotic combination regimens (quinine-clindamycin and quinine-doxycycline) achieved cure rates of more than 90%, compared to only 38% with quinine monotherapy.

title: Evaluation of permethrin-treated military uniforms for personal protection against malaria in northeastern Thailand.
journal: Journal of the American Mosquito Control Association
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated clothing (a vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (malaria incidence).
population: Royal Thai Army troops
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria among troops
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated military uniforms did not reduce malaria incidence compared to placebo-treated uniforms in an operational setting.
transmission_setting: high transmission, operational/field setting in northeastern Thailand

title: Artemether 5 versus 7 day regimen for severe falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether treatment regimens for severe falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates, recrudescence).
population: male patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 28 (parasite and fever clearance, recrudescence)
impact_summary: The 7-day artemether regimen achieved a higher cure rate (73%) than the 5-day regimen (38%), though both had substantial recrudescence.
transmission_setting: endemic, severe malaria cases in Thailand
safety_summary: No deaths, no neurological sequelae, only transient injection site pain; no drug-related biochemical or ECG changes.

title: Safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of a malaria sporozoite vaccine administered with monophosphoryl lipid A, cell wall skeleton of mycobacteria, and squalane as adjuvant.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: RCT of malaria vaccine (PfCSP) with reported safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy outcomes including challenge-study parasite data; Phase 1 but includes efficacy results from controlled challenge infection.
population: healthy adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Safety, immunogenicity, and protection from P. falciparum parasitemia after sporozoite challenge
impact_summary: Two of the four volunteers with the highest antibody levels to the PfCSP repeat region were protected from parasitemia after sporozoite challenge, while all other vaccinees with lower antibody levels and all controls developed parasitemia.
effect_estimate: 2 of 4 high-responder vaccinees protected; 0 of 11 controls protected
safety_summary: Vaccine was generally well tolerated; most volunteers had sore arms, some with pain or malaise severe enough to interfere with work or sleep; one volunteer had malaise and painful induration after the second dose and withdrew.

title: The efficacy of antimalarial regimens containing sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and/or chloroquine in preventing peripheral and placental Plasmodium falciparum infection among pregnant women in Malawi.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial chemoprevention (SP/CQ regimens) in pregnant women with reported outcome results (placental malaria infection rates).
comparator: active comparator (CQ/CQ vs SP/CQ vs SP/SP regimens)
population: pregnant women in their first or second pregnancy
primary_outcome: Placental Plasmodium falciparum malaria infection at delivery
impact_summary: Two treatment doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP/SP) were highly effective in reducing placental malaria infection at delivery compared with chloroquine-based regimens.
transmission_setting: high transmission of chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum, seasonal peak April to July

title: Single dose artemisinin-mefloquine treatment for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing artemisinin-mefloquine combination for acute falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: artemisinin alone for 5 days, mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (MSP), quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP)
population: adults and children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, in-patient and rural out-patient settings
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate (RI) during 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Single-dose artemisinin plus mefloquine rapidly lowered parasitaemia and effectively prevented recrudescence in both in-patients and out-patients, outperforming artemisinin alone and artemisinin plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
effect_estimate: 15% (adult in-patients), 0% (adult and children out-patients) with artemisinin-mefloquine vs 33.3% (artemisinin alone), 47.3%/46.1% (artemisinin+SP)
transmission_setting: rural and hospital settings in Viet Nam

title: Can malaria chemoprophylaxis be restricted to first pregnancies?
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp with Maloprim vs placebo) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria infection and birth weight.
population: pregnant women (second pregnancies), primigravidae who received Maloprim or placebo during first pregnancy
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria infection of the blood and placenta during second pregnancies, and mean birth weight
impact_summary: Restricting malaria chemoprophylaxis to first pregnancies did not increase susceptibility to malaria or reduce birth weight in second pregnancies compared with women who had not received prophylaxis in their first pregnancy.
effect_metric: prevalence of malaria infection and mean birth weight
effect_estimate: similar between groups; birth weights almost identical
safety_summary: No adverse effects reported; outcomes in second pregnancy were comparable regardless of prior chemoprophylaxis exposure

title: Control of endophagic Anopheles mosquitoes and human malaria in Guinea Bissau, West Africa by permethrin-treated bed nets.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on mosquito densities and malaria parasite rates.
population: residents of six villages including children 2-9 years old and adults
primary_outcome: Reduction in Anopheles indoor resting densities and malaria parasite rates in humans
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated bed nets significantly reduced Anopheles mosquito indoor resting densities, malaria parasite rates, and infective mosquito bites compared to placebo-treated nets in control villages.
transmission_setting: high endemicity, seasonal (rainy season) transmission by Anopheles gambiae and A. melas
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Randomised trial of efficacy of SPf66 vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in southern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (SPf66) in children with reported efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
population: children aged 1-5 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria (measured fever ≥37.5°C and parasite density >20,000/microL) over 1 year follow-up after third dose
impact_summary: The SPf66 vaccine reduced the risk of clinical malaria by 31% compared to placebo among children in an area of intense P falciparum transmission, and was safe and immunogenic.
safety_summary: No severe side-effects were seen; frequency of mild side-effects after the third dose was less than 6%; 6 deaths occurred after the third dose (1 vaccine, 5 placebo).

title: Treatment of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria with 3-day artesunate-mefloquine combination.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing artesunate-mefloquine combination versus mefloquine monotherapy for treatment of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in humans.
population: adults and children with acute uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day treatment failure rate (parasitologic cure)
impact_summary: Three-day artesunate-mefloquine combination therapy was 98% effective compared to a 31% failure rate with high-dose mefloquine alone, and also reduced vomiting and reinfection-adjusted failure rates by day 63.
transmission_setting: area of increasing mefloquine resistance, multidrug-resistant malaria region
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; no adverse effects attributable to artesunate; vomiting significantly reduced by giving mefloquine on day 2 of treatment (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.20-0.79, P=.009).

title: The influence of Maloprim chemoprophylaxis on cellular and humoral immune responses to Plasmodium falciparum asexual blood stage antigens in schoolchildren living in a malaria endemic area of Mozambique.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (Maloprim) with reported outcome results on parasite rates and immune responses in schoolchildren.
population: schoolchildren aged 7-12 years
primary_outcome: Cellular and humoral immune responses to Plasmodium falciparum asexual blood stage antigens (GLURP and Pf155/RESA)
impact_summary: Weekly Maloprim chemoprophylaxis reduced parasite prevalence markedly but also lowered antibody response rates to GLURP compared to placebo, without significantly affecting lymphoproliferative responses.
effect_estimate: rainy season 43% to 4%; dry season 18% to 0%
follow_up: 2 years (1 year intervention plus 1 year follow-up without chemoprophylaxis)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic area, seasonal (rainy and dry seasons), suburban Maputo, Mozambique
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis, infection of the placenta and birth weight in Gambian primigravidae.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on placental infection and birth weight.
population: primigravid pregnant women
primary_outcome: Placental malaria infection and birth weight
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis with Maloprim reduced placental malaria infection and increased birth weight by an average of 153 g compared to placebo.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported

title: Chloroquine chemoprophylaxis in children during peak transmission period in Ethiopia.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (clinical malaria occurrence) testing malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine prophylaxis) in children; not early-phase.
population: children aged 1-14 years in the Awash Rift Valley
primary_outcome: occurrence of at least one episode of clinical malaria
impact_summary: Chloroquine chemoprophylaxis was no more effective than placebo in preventing clinical malaria, smear positivity, or splenomegaly among children during peak transmission season.
effect_metric: difference in occurrence of clinical malaria
transmission_setting: peak malaria transmission season, chloroquine resistance not yet reported in the area

title: A population-based clinical trial with the SPf66 synthetic Plasmodium falciparum malaria vaccine in Venezuela.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine with reported efficacy outcomes in an endemic population.
design: population-based, phase 3, non-randomized (vaccinated vs nonvaccinated) trial
population: residents of endemic villages in South Venezuela
primary_outcome: Incidence of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax infections
impact_summary: The SPf66 vaccine reduced the incidence of P. falciparum malaria by 55% and P. vivax malaria by 41% compared to nonvaccinated subjects.
safety_summary: Minor side effects requiring no treatment were reported by 12.6% of subjects, increasing in frequency from first to third dose; no autoimmune evidence observed in a sampled subset.

title: Rectal administration of chloroquine for treatment of children with malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of a malaria treatment intervention (chloroquine) in children with randomized allocation to compared groups.
population: children with malaria

title: Artemisinin: large community studies.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating artemisinin derivatives for malaria treatment in over 1000 patients across multiple clinical settings.
population: patients with multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria, including uncomplicated malaria, recrudescent infections, and high parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Treatment outcome (cure rate, recovery rate) of oral artemisinin derivatives in multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Oral artemisinin derivatives combined with mefloquine accelerated recovery, eliminated early treatment failures, and improved cure rates in multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria on the Thai-Burmese border.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria area, Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; rectal artemether formulation suggested as practical alternative for severe malaria treatment in rural areas.

title: Artemether in moderately severe and cerebral malaria in Nigerian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemether for moderately severe and cerebral malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, mortality, safety).
population: children with moderately severe or cerebral malaria requiring parenteral therapy
primary_outcome: parasite and fever clearance times, parasitological cure rate, recrudescence rate, and mortality
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether cleared parasites and fever faster than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine but had a higher recrudescence rate; in cerebral malaria, artemether was similarly effective to quinine with a lower mortality rate (12% vs 21%) and was well tolerated with no adverse clinical or laboratory effects.
safety_summary: Artemether was well tolerated with no abnormal haematological or biochemical changes and no adverse clinical reactions.

title: Comparison of micronized halofantrine with chloroquine-antibiotic combinations for treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria in adults from Gabon.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (halofantrine vs. chloroquine combinations) in adults with reported outcome results (cure rates by day 28).
comparator: chloroquine plus clindamycin; chloroquine plus doxycycline
population: adults with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate by day 28 of follow-up
impact_summary: Micronized halofantrine and chloroquine plus clindamycin achieved high cure rates (100% and 97%), while chloroquine plus doxycycline had a significantly lower cure rate of 75% with slower parasite clearance.
safety_summary: All treatment regimens were well-tolerated.

title: Randomized trial of mefloquine-doxycycline, and artesunate-doxycycline for treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artesunate and mefloquine combinations) with reported outcome results (cure rates, fever clearance, parasite clearance).
population: adult patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at 28 days
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus doxycycline achieved a higher cure rate (96%) than artesunate plus doxycycline (80%), though artesunate plus doxycycline resulted in faster fever and parasite clearance.
safety_summary: 12 patients left the study prior to completion of follow-up for reasons unrelated to treatment; no other major safety issues reported.

title: Randomised trial of mefloquine-tetracycline and quinine-tetracycline for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, safety, parasite clearance) in 102 patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at 28 days follow-up
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus tetracycline was equally effective and less toxic than quinine plus tetracycline for treating acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: area with highly drug-resistant P. falciparum strains
safety_summary: 94% of quinine-treated patients developed cinchonism compared with 12% of mefloquine-treated patients; 26% of quinine-treated patients developed delayed primary attacks of P. vivax versus none in the mefloquine group; other symptoms were similar between groups.

title: Daily chlorproguanil is an effective alternative to daily proguanil in the prevention of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kenya.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chlorproguanil) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia rates) in humans.
population: malaria-free schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Occurrence of Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia during follow-up
impact_summary: Daily chlorproguanil and daily proguanil significantly and equally reduced the risk of P. falciparum parasitaemia compared with placebo and weekly chlorproguanil, with no significant toxicity.
effect_estimate: 92% placebo, 31% daily proguanil, 38% daily chlorproguanil, 55% weekly chlorproguanil
safety_summary: No significant toxicity was reported or observed.

title: The distribution of birth weights in Gambian women who received malaria chemoprophylaxis during their first pregnancy and in control women.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp with Maloprim) in pregnancy with reported birth weight and perinatal mortality outcomes.
population: primigravid pregnant women
primary_outcome: Distribution of infant birth weights
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis with Maloprim during pregnancy reduced the prevalence of low birth weight babies and increased median birth weight compared with placebo, without a comparable increase in high birth weight babies or a significant reduction in perinatal mortality.
effect_metric: median birth weight and prevalence of low birth weight
effect_estimate: increase in median birth weight; reduction in low birth weight prevalence
safety_summary: No evidence found that chemoprophylaxis increased risk of cephalo/pelvic disproportion; perinatal mortality was lower but not significantly so in the chemoprophylaxis group.

title: Blood stage antimalarial efficacy of primaquine in Plasmodium vivax malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drugs (primaquine and chloroquine) for P. vivax malaria treatment with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and recurrence.
population: adult Thai men with acute Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and therapeutic response
impact_summary: Primaquine and chloroquine both produced satisfactory initial therapeutic responses in vivax malaria, though parasite clearance was slower with primaquine alone, and recurrence patterns differed between the two treatments, suggesting recrudescence after primaquine and relapse after chloroquine.
safety_summary: All patients had a satisfactory initial therapeutic response; no severe adverse events reported.

title: Randomized trial of mefloquine alone and artesunate followed by mefloquine for the treatment of acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate + mefloquine vs mefloquine alone) with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: Sequential artesunate followed by mefloquine achieved a higher cure rate (92%) than mefloquine alone (74%), with significantly faster parasite clearance.
p_value: P < 0.001 (parasite clearance time); P = 0.26 (fever clearance time)
safety_summary: Most patients responded well; none suffered serious toxic adverse reactions.

title: Safety, immunogenicity and protective effect of the SPf66 malaria synthetic vaccine against Plasmodium falciparum infection in a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled field trial in an endemic area of Ecuador.
screening_reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy) of a malaria vaccine intervention in humans.
population: residents of an endemic area (mixed age groups, exact ages not specified)
primary_outcome: Protective effect (vaccine efficacy) against Plasmodium falciparum malaria episodes
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine showed a protective effect against P. falciparum malaria episodes, though confidence intervals were wide and crossed zero.
effect_ci: -2.7 to 89.3% (any episode); -26 to 87.5% (one episode per individual)
safety_summary: Minor local side-effects occurred mainly after the second dose in about 19% of vaccinated subjects versus 3.7% of placebo recipients; no serious adverse events reported.

title: SPf66, a chemically synthesized subunit malaria vaccine, is safe and immunogenic in Tanzanians exposed to intense malaria transmission.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported immunogenicity and safety outcomes in exposed populations; phase appears early (safety/immunogenicity focus) but Phase 2 vaccine studies are eligible per inclusion criteria.
population: male adult expatriates, indigenous adults, and children aged 1-4 years
primary_outcome: Safety and immunogenicity of SPf66 vaccine (antibody titres) in individuals exposed to intense malaria transmission
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine was safe with no major side-effects and induced clear antibody responses after three doses in Tanzanian adults and children as well as expatriates.
safety_summary: No major side-effects observed in indigenous SPf66 recipients (adults and children).

title: Mefloquine prophylaxis prevents malaria during pregnancy: a double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
screening_reason: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of mefloquine prophylaxis (malaria prevention in humans) with reported outcome results on efficacy, safety, and adverse effects; not early-phase.
population: pregnant women (>20 weeks gestation), Karen ethnicity
primary_outcome: Prevention of malaria infection (Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax) during pregnancy
impact_summary: Mefloquine prophylaxis provided at least 86% protection against P. falciparum and complete protection against P. vivax in pregnant women, with good tolerability.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant malaria transmission area, Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Mefloquine prophylaxis was well tolerated; loading dose associated with transient dizziness; no other significant adverse effects on mother, pregnancy, or infant survival/development over 2 years follow-up.

title: High dose of primaquine in primaquine resistant vivax malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine dosing for vivax malaria treatment with reported relapse outcome results.
comparator: lower dose primaquine (15 mg) vs higher dose primaquine (22.5 mg); also low-dose (300 mg) vs (450 mg) chloroquine
population: Thai patients with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Relapse rate within 6 months after primaquine treatment
impact_summary: A higher daily dose of primaquine (22.5 mg for 14 days) resulted in a significantly lower relapse rate than the standard 15 mg dose in primaquine-resistant vivax malaria.
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; both chloroquine doses well tolerated with rapid fever and parasite clearance.

title: Single day mefloquine-artesunate combination in the treatment of multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatment regimens for falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; Phase III therapeutic efficacy study.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in a multi-drug resistant area
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate by day 28
impact_summary: Single-day mefloquine-artesunate combination reduced early treatment failures and was more effective than high-dose mefloquine alone, particularly in patients requiring re-treatment.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant, low transmission border area
safety_summary: Gastrointestinal side-effects and dizziness were more common with high-dose mefloquine; no evident adverse effects associated with artesunate.

title: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets for the prevention of malaria in schoolchildren on the Thai-Burmese border.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (malaria vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and prevalence in humans.
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria infections (confirmed by blood film) over 6 months
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated bed nets reduced parasitaemic P. falciparum infections by 38% and symptomatic episodes by 42%, with no significant effect on P. vivax malaria.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in P. falciparum parasitaemic infections
safety_summary: Compliance was high and no side-effects were reported.

title: A comparison of amodiaquine and chloroquine in the treatment therapy of falciparum malaria in Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results; not early-phase.
population: symptomatic outpatients with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance rate and clinical amelioration
impact_summary: Amodiaquine was significantly more effective than chloroquine in clearing parasites and achieving clinical amelioration, with better tolerance and no evidence of toxicity.
safety_summary: No evidence of granulocyte or gross hepatic toxicity; amodiaquine had fewer cutaneous side effects and better overall tolerance than chloroquine.

title: Failure of doxycycline as a causal prophylactic agent against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in healthy nonimmune volunteers.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing doxycycline prophylaxis against P. falciparum malaria in humans with reported outcome results (protection rates and parasitemia monitoring).
population: healthy nonimmune adult male volunteers experimentally challenged with P. falciparum-infected mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Protection from malaria (parasitemia) following experimental challenge with P. falciparum-infected mosquitoes while on doxycycline or placebo causal prophylaxis
impact_summary: Doxycycline 100 mg daily as causal prophylaxis had an unacceptably high failure rate, with only 8 of 12 (67%) doxycycline recipients protected from malaria after experimental mosquito challenge.
follow_up: through parasitemia monitoring after challenge (approximately days post-exposure)
transmission_setting: experimental sporozoite challenge (non-endemic, controlled laboratory setting)
safety_summary: No adverse pharmacokinetic differences noted between protected and nonprotected participants; specific adverse events not detailed in abstract.

title: Safety, immunogenicity and limited efficacy study of a recombinant Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite vaccine in Thai soldiers.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (P. falciparum circumsporozoite) with reported outcome results on safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy in humans.
population: soldiers (adult volunteers)
primary_outcome: Time to Plasmodium falciparum malaria infection (safety, immunogenicity and efficacy)
impact_summary: The recombinant R32Tox-A vaccine was safe and immunogenic, eliciting antibody responses in all vaccinees, but showed no protective efficacy against falciparum malaria compared to control vaccine.
effect_metric: log-rank comparison of time to falciparum malaria
effect_estimate: no significant difference between vaccinated and non-vaccinated subjects
p_value: p = 0.005 (antibody comparison); p = 0.06 and p = 0.014 (secondary analyses)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic border area (deployment after immunization in non-transmission area)
safety_summary: Vaccine was found to be safe with no major adverse events reported; elicited antibody responses in all vaccinees.

title: Efficacy and tolerance of extended-dose halofantrine for drug-resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and tolerance outcomes comparing halofantrine to quinine-tetracycline for drug-resistant P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
population: soldiers stationed along the Thai-Cambodian border with drug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate, parasite clearance time, and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Extended-dose halofantrine was as effective as quinine-tetracycline for multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria but was better tolerated with fewer side effects.
p_value: P > 0.1 for efficacy differences; P < 0.001 for side effects score and days with side effects; P < 0.01 for patients with adverse effects on every treatment day
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area (Thai-Cambodian border)
