safety_summary: Halofantrine was better tolerated than quinine-tetracycline, with lower side effects score (2 versus 11), fewer days with side effects (2.0 versus 5.5 days), and fewer patients with adverse effects on every treatment day (4% versus 42%).

title: Clindamycin in combination with chloroquine or quinine is an effective therapy for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children from Gabon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (clindamycin combinations vs standard antimalarials) in children with reported outcome results (cure rates and recrudescence by day 28).
comparator: chloroquine alone vs quinine alone (active comparator arms)
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate and recrudescence rate by day 28 (day 14 for quinine-clindamycin group)
impact_summary: Combination of clindamycin with chloroquine or quinine substantially increased cure rates and reduced recrudescence compared to chloroquine or quinine alone.
safety_summary: All treatment regimens were well tolerated.

title: SPf66 malaria vaccine trial: an update.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported outcome results.

title: Comparison of oral artesunate and quinine plus tetracycline in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments (oral artesunate vs quinine-tetracycline) for falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, cure rates, adverse effects).
population: male patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate (parasite and fever clearance, recrudescence)
impact_summary: Oral artesunate had faster parasite and fever clearance than quinine-tetracycline, with similar cure rates but better tolerability.
safety_summary: Tinnitus was significantly more common with quinine-tetracycline; nausea, dizziness, and possible neurotoxicity were noted with artesunate.

title: Chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine sensitivity in Burkina Faso. In vivo sensitivity of Plasmodium falciparum to chloroquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results showing drug sensitivity findings.
population: children with P. falciparum monospecific infection
primary_outcome: Parasitological response (clearance/recurrence of parasitaemia) on days 7 and 14 after treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine showed treatment failure (incomplete clearance by day 7 and recurrence by day 14) in a substantial proportion of children, whereas sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine achieved full parasitological sensitivity in all treated children by day 7 and day 14.
effect_estimate: chloroquine: 8.1% not cleared by day 7, 24.4% recurrence by day 14; sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine: 0% failure
transmission_setting: urban district of Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, endemic area with established chloroquine resistance
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; monitoring included urine tests (Bergqvist and Lignin) to confirm no prior drug exposure, but no adverse event data described.

title: Parenteral therapy of moderately severe malaria: comparison of intramuscular artemether and intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, recrudescence); primary focus is malaria treatment intervention in humans; phase not stated but acceptable.
population: children with severe but uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and parasitological clearance
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether cleared parasites and fever faster than intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with comparable parasitological clearance at day 14 but more recrudescences in the artemether group.
safety_summary: No toxic reaction of note in either group.

title: Pharmacokinetics of mefloquine alone or in combination with artesunate.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine ± artesunate) with reported outcome results (fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, cure rates).
comparator: mefloquine alone versus mefloquine combined with artesunate
population: Thai male patients with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of mefloquine (fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, cure rate) alone or combined with artesunate
impact_summary: Combination treatment with artesunate improved clinical response (shorter fever and parasite clearance times) but altered mefloquine pharmacokinetics, decreasing peak concentration and increasing clearance and volume of distribution, and did not improve cure rate compared to mefloquine alone.
safety_summary: No major safety concerns reported; one patient in the mefloquine-alone group developed P. vivax parasitemia on day 52; recrudescences occurred in both groups.

title: Falciparum malaria in eastern Thailand: a randomized trial of the efficacy of a single dose of mefloquine.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing mefloquine treatment efficacy for falciparum malaria in humans.
population: adult patients with uncomplicated multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological failure rate at day 28 and day 42
impact_summary: Both mefloquine dosing regimens resulted in high parasitological failure rates with no significant difference between 15 mg/kg and 25 mg/kg groups, indicating high-level multidrug resistance in the study area.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, eastern Thailand
safety_summary: Adverse effects were more common in the 25 mg/kg group but the difference was not statistically significant.

title: Pharmacokinetic study of mefloquine in Thai children aged 5-12 years suffering from uncomplicated falciparum malaria treated with MSP or MSP plus primaquine.
journal: European journal of drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (MSP with/without primaquine) in children with falciparum malaria that reports clinical and pharmacokinetic outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (MSP alone vs MSP plus primaquine)
population: children aged 5-12 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic parameters of mefloquine (Cmax, t1/2, Cl/f, Vd/f) and clinical/parasitological response
impact_summary: Adding primaquine to MSP did not alter mefloquine pharmacokinetics but significantly shortened gametocyte clearance time compared to MSP alone.
safety_summary: No serious side effects were recorded in either treatment group.

title: [Parasitological and clinical response to amodiaquine versus chloroquine in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in an endemic area].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) for P. falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever resolution, adverse effects, therapeutic failure rates).
population: children with symptomatic uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance and therapeutic response by day 7
impact_summary: Amodiaquine achieved faster parasite clearance and a 0% therapeutic failure rate compared to 16.3% failure with chloroquine, demonstrating superior efficacy over chloroquine.
safety_summary: Cutaneous adverse effects such as pruritus occurred in 3.2% of amodiaquine group and 6.8% of chloroquine group; amodiaquine had good safety profile.

title: Prevention of Plasmodium falciparum malaria by Fansimef and Lariam in the northeastern part of Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (Fansimef and Lariam) in humans with reported outcome results (malaria episodes and incidence rates).
population: soldiers
primary_outcome: Incidence of Plasmodium falciparum malaria episodes (cases per 100 person-months)
impact_summary: Fansimef (full or half dose) and Lariam (half dose) had significantly lower malaria incidence rates than chloroquine plus Fansidar, with no significant differences among the Fansimef/Lariam regimens themselves.
safety_summary: Adverse events in each group were mild.

title: The efficacy of artemether in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Sudan.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether to quinine for P. falciparum treatment with reported efficacy outcomes, parasitaemia clearance, and safety data.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether cleared parasitaemia as effectively as quinine, was well tolerated, and had no recrudescence in the artemether group versus 3 of 18 recrudescences in the quinine group.
safety_summary: No side effects reported by patients receiving artemether; drug was well tolerated.

title: Bed nets for the prevention of malaria and anaemia in pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of bed nets (a malaria prevention intervention) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria incidence and anaemia.
comparator: non-impregnated bed net and no net/own family net (control)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria in pregnancy and anaemia (haematocrit < 30%) at delivery
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets, along with family non-impregnated nets, reduced the incidence of malaria in pregnancy and were associated with significantly lower rates of maternal anaemia at delivery, though overall effect on patent parasitaemia was marginal.
follow_up: through delivery and infant outcome assessment
safety_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets were well tolerated with no apparent adverse effect on pregnancy or infant development.

title: Curing of chloroquine-resistant malaria with clindamycin.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing clindamycin versus chloroquine for treating P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure rates, recrudescence, parasitemia clearance); malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
population: semi-immune adult patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure/recrudescence by day 28 of follow-up)
impact_summary: Clindamycin cured 97% of patients compared to only 36% cured with chloroquine, demonstrating clindamycin's efficacy against chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria.
transmission_setting: Central Africa, chloroquine-resistant malaria endemic area
safety_summary: No severe side effects occurred in either treatment group.

title: Comparison of three regimens for malaria prophylaxis in travellers to east, central, and southern Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three malaria chemoprophylaxis regimens with reported outcome results (P. falciparum infection rates and prophylaxis failures) in humans.
comparator: active comparator (three different chemoprophylactic regimens compared to each other)
population: Dutch travellers to east, central, and southern Africa
primary_outcome: Confirmation of breakthroughs (prophylaxis failures) in malaria chemoprophylaxis regimens and assessment of compliance
impact_summary: No significant difference in prophylaxis failure rates was found between the three regimens, with prophylaxis failures occurring in less than 1% of participants; the chloroquine-proguanil combination can still be recommended for travellers.
effect_estimate: 5.4 (chloroquine 300mg weekly + proguanil 100mg daily); 2.8 (chloroquine 300mg weekly + proguanil 200mg daily); 6.0 (proguanil 200mg daily)
transmission_setting: travellers to east, central, and southern Africa (malaria-endemic regions)

title: [Randomised comparison on the treatment of falciparum malaria with dihydroartemisinin and piperaquine].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing dihydroartemisinin and piperaquine for falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
place: China, Dong Fang County, Hainan province
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance and treatment response (sensitivity/resistance grading)
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin was more effective than piperaquine phosphate against falciparum malaria in an area where the parasite showed high resistance to piperaquine.
transmission_setting: endemic area with piperaquine-resistant P. falciparum

title: Resistance of Plasmodium falciparum to antimalarial drugs in Equatorial Guinea.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drug treatments in children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria that reported outcome results (parasite clearance rates).
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs quinine vs sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: children under 10 years with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate by day 14
impact_summary: Parasite clearance rates by day 14 were 28% with chloroquine, 74% with amodiaquine, and 95% with quinine or sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, indicating high chloroquine resistance and good efficacy of quinine and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine.
safety_summary: Quinine recommended over sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine due to risk of serious reactions to sulpha drugs.

title: Postexposure administration of halofantrine for the prevention of malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (halofantrine vs. chloroquine) with reported outcome results in humans.
population: mine workers returning from endemic areas
primary_outcome: Development of falciparum malaria within 28 days after treatment
impact_summary: None of the men who received halofantrine developed falciparum malaria within 28 days, whereas three of those who received chloroquine did.

title: Response of falciparum malaria to chloroquine and three second line antimalarial drugs in a Kenyan coastal school age population.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment drugs with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance and reinfection rates) in a human population.
comparator: active comparator (three second-line antimalarials compared against each other; chloroquine assessed in vitro)
population: rural school age children with P. falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate and reinfection rate (day 28 parasitaemia) following treatment with amodiaquine, pyrimethamine/sulphadoxine, or pyrimethamine/sulfalene
impact_summary: All three second-line drugs (amodiaquine, pyrimethamine/sulphadoxine, pyrimethamine/sulfalene) effectively cleared parasitaemia with no significant difference in efficacy, but reinfection rates by day 28 differed, with chloroquine showing 60% in vitro resistance and no resistance detected to the second-line drugs.
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; all children treated successfully cleared their parasitaemia with no reported adverse events

title: Effectiveness of permethrin-impregnated bed nets and curtains for malaria control in a holoendemic area of western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on P. falciparum infection incidence.
population: children less than six years old in villages
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. falciparum infections and parasitemias in children under six years old
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets and curtains significantly reduced the incidence of P. falciparum infection, parasitemia, and fever compared with control villages, with bed nets offering greater protection than curtains.
effect_metric: percent reduction in incidence of P. falciparum infection

title: An open randomized comparative study of intramuscular artemether and intravenous quinine in cerebral malaria in children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments (artemether vs quinine) in children with cerebral malaria, with reported outcome results including mortality, parasite clearance, and adverse events.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, and time to recover from coma
impact_summary: Intramuscular artemether was similarly effective as intravenous quinine for cerebral malaria in children, with a lower but not statistically significant mortality rate and no notable toxicity.
effect_estimate: lower in artemether group (not statistically significant)
safety_summary: No toxic reaction of note in the artemether group; quinine considered potentially toxic.

title: Tolerability of prophylactic Lariam regimens.
journal: Tropical medicine and parasitology : official organ of Deutsche Tropenmedizinische Gesellschaft and of Deutsche Gesellschaft fur Technische Zusammenarbeit (GTZ)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing mefloquine prophylactic regimens with chloroquine in human participants that has reported tolerability and safety outcome results for malaria prevention.
population: US Marines (healthy adults)
primary_outcome: Tolerability of prophylactic mefloquine regimens (adverse effects, mood states, sleep disturbance)
impact_summary: Both weekly and loading-dose mefloquine regimens were well tolerated, though sleep disturbance, increased dream activity, and transient depressive feelings were more common than with chloroquine.
safety_summary: No compromise in function due to dizziness or incoordination in mefloquine groups; sleep disturbance and increased dream activity detected; depressive feelings occurred in two to three times more individuals in mefloquine groups than chloroquine group early on, resolving as tolerance developed.

title: Comparison of two mefloquine regimens for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria on the northeastern Thai-Cambodian border.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two mefloquine treatment regimens for P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine 15 mg/kg vs mefloquine 25 mg/kg)
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (children and adults)
primary_outcome: Treatment failure (recrudescence) by day 28 and day 42
impact_summary: High-dose mefloquine (25 mg/kg) resulted in significantly fewer early and late treatment failures than the conventional 15 mg/kg dose, though it was associated with more gastrointestinal side effects.
effect_metric: incidence of treatment failure by day 28
transmission_setting: multi-drug-resistant P. falciparum endemic area, Thai-Cambodian border
safety_summary: Upper gastrointestinal side effects and dizziness were significantly more common in the M25 group, but the high dose was relatively well tolerated overall, particularly in children.

title: Classification of clinical falciparum malaria and its use for the evaluation of chemosuppression in children under six years of age in Liberia, west Africa.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results on clinical malaria episodes.
population: children aged 6 months to 6 years
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria episodes classified as 'possible clinical malaria' or 'probable clinical malaria'
impact_summary: Children receiving regular chemosuppression with chloroquine had fewer clinical malaria attacks than those receiving presumptive treatment only, especially during the dry season.
transmission_setting: rural area with seasonal (dry and rainy season) transmission

title: Controlled trial of lambda-cyhalothrin impregnated bed nets and Maloprim chemosuppression to control malaria in children living in a holoendemic area of Sierra Leone, west Africa. Study design and preliminary results.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria interventions (ITNs and chemoprevention) in children with reported preliminary outcome results showing efficacy.
comparator: no bed nets / placebo (maloprim vs placebo)
population: children aged 3 months to 6 years living in a holoendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: malaria morbidity assessed by weekly active case detection (slide positivity rate, fever rate, temperature >=37.5C)
impact_summary: During the first 8 weeks of intervention, villages with lambda-cyhalothrin impregnated bed nets showed a significant reduction in slide positive rates, reported fever rates, and children with temperature >=37.5 degrees C.
effect_metric: reduction in slide positivity and fever rates

title: [Mefloquine chemoprophylaxis of malaria in the Brazilian Amazonia].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine chemoprophylaxis (malaria prevention intervention) in humans with reported outcome results (malaria attack rates); not early-phase.
population: volunteers living in an endemic malarious area
primary_outcome: Occurrence of acute malaria attacks
impact_summary: Mefloquine chemoprophylaxis (monthly or biweekly) significantly reduced acute malaria attacks compared with placebo in an area with drug multiresistant P. falciparum.
effect_estimate: 1/group I, 2/group II vs 6/group III and 6/group IV
transmission_setting: high prevalence of drug multiresistant P. falciparum transmission, endemic Amazonian region
safety_summary: Not detailed in abstract

title: Economic analysis of malaria control for migrant workers in eastern Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated nets (vector control/ITN intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (economic and effectiveness measures) in a malaria-endemic population.
population: long-term and seasonal agricultural migrant workers in malaria-endemic rural areas
primary_outcome: Economic impact (cost-effectiveness and cost-benefit) of permethrin-treated nets versus untreated nets for malaria control
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated nets were cost-saving and more effective than untreated nets, yielding net benefits of US$1.17 per worker from the Malaria Division's perspective and US$1.61 per worker from the worker's perspective.
transmission_setting: highly endemic for multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum

title: A malaria control trial using insecticide-treated bed nets and targeted chemoprophylaxis in a rural area of The Gambia, west Africa. 8. Cost-effectiveness of bed net impregnation alone or combined with chemoprophylaxis in preventing mortality and morbidity from malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets with or without chemoprophylaxis for malaria prevention in children with reported mortality and morbidity outcomes; vector-control cluster trials are classified as 'Not applicable' phase.
population: children between one and 4 years of age
primary_outcome: Cost-effectiveness (cost per death averted, per clinical episode averted, per healthy year of life saved) of insecticide-treated bed nets alone versus combined with chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Insecticide impregnation of bed nets, alone or combined with Maloprim chemoprophylaxis, reduced malaria morbidity and mortality in Gambian children and was highly cost-effective, with bed net impregnation alone being more cost-effective than the combined strategy.
effect_metric: cost per healthy year of life saved (discounted at 3%)
effect_estimate: US $7.90 (bed net impregnation alone) vs US $10.84 (combined with chemoprophylaxis)

title: A malaria control trial using insecticide-treated bed nets and targeted chemoprophylaxis in a rural area of The Gambia, west Africa. 6. The impact of the interventions on mortality and morbidity from malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria prevention interventions (insecticide-treated bed nets and chemoprophylaxis) in humans with reported outcome results on mortality and morbidity.
comparator: no impregnated bed nets / no chemoprophylaxis (untreated nets and placebo/no chemoprophylaxis groups)
population: rural Gambian children aged 6 months to 5 years
primary_outcome: Mortality and morbidity (clinical attacks of malaria, fever with parasitaemia) from malaria
impact_summary: Insecticide-impregnated bed nets reduced overall child mortality by about 60% and febrile malaria episodes by 45%, with chemoprophylaxis providing additional protection against clinical attacks and infection but not further reducing mortality.
transmission_setting: rural, seasonal malaria transmission in west Africa
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; chemoprophylaxis with Maloprim was administered weekly without reported adverse events described in abstract.

title: A malaria control trial using insecticide-treated bed nets and targeted chemoprophylaxis in a rural area of The Gambia, west Africa. 7. Impact of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on malaria vectors.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria with reported entomological outcome results; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: residents of rural villages
primary_outcome: Impact of permethrin-impregnated bed nets on malaria vector populations (mosquito density, survival, biting rates)
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets provided good individual protection against mosquito bites but did not significantly reduce village-wide mosquito survival or biting rates, likely due to mosquito circulation between treated and untreated villages.
transmission_setting: rural, seasonal, high transmission during rainy season

title: Spiramycin does not potentiate quinine treatment of falciparum malaria in pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (quinine ± spiramycin) in pregnant women with falciparum malaria.
population: pregnant women with falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Adding spiramycin to quinine did not improve treatment outcomes for falciparum malaria in pregnancy compared to quinine alone.

title: Comparison of intramuscular and intravenous quinine for the treatment of severe and complicated malaria in children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two treatment routes for severe malaria in children with reported outcome results (mortality, neurological sequelae, parasite/temperature/coma clearance times).
comparator: active comparator (intravenous quinine vs intramuscular quinine)
population: children with severe and complicated malaria, aged 6 months to 7 years
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and efficacy/side effects comparison between intramuscular and intravenous quinine
impact_summary: Intramuscular quinine was as effective as intravenous quinine for treating severe and complicated malaria in children, with no statistically significant differences in parasite, temperature, or coma clearance times.
safety_summary: 4 deaths and 3 neurological sequelae and 2 sterile intramuscular abscesses in the i.m. group (n=57); 6 deaths and 1 neurological sequela in the i.v. group (n=47); no significant difference in outcomes between groups.

title: Halofantrine versus mefloquine in treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments (halofantrine vs mefloquine) for treatment of multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (efficacy/failure rates at day 28).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cumulative treatment failure rate by day 28
impact_summary: High-dose halofantrine (72 mg/kg) was more effective and better tolerated than mefloquine for treating multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria, though the standard halofantrine dose (24 mg/kg) was less effective than mefloquine.
p_value: 0.03 (unadjusted), 0.009 (adjusted); 0.0002 for first trial; 0.008 for retreatment relative risk
safety_summary: High-dose halofantrine was better tolerated than mefloquine, but concerns about possible cardiotoxicity of halofantrine were raised and require further investigation.

title: Mefloquine or doxycycline prophylaxis in US troops in Somalia.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of malaria chemoprevention (prophylaxis) in humans, a primary malaria intervention.
population: US military troops deployed to Somalia
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria and adverse events during and after prophylaxis
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and doxycycline were effective in preventing malaria among US troops in Somalia, with differing side effect profiles.
safety_summary: Both drugs were generally well tolerated; mefloquine associated with more neuropsychiatric side effects, doxycycline with gastrointestinal and photosensitivity effects

title: Recent military experience with malaria chemoprophylaxis.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis in healthy soldiers with reported outcome results (malaria infection rates by drug regimen).
comparator: Maloprim and chloroquine (control group) and between-group comparisons of doxycycline-based regimens
population: healthy male members of the Australian Army during training exercises in malarious countries
primary_outcome: proportion of participants developing falciparum or vivax malaria during or after the intervention
impact_summary: Doxycycline combined with low-dose primaquine prevented vivax malaria relapse after prophylaxis, whereas doxycycline alone did not, while all regimens effectively prevented falciparum malaria.
follow_up: 3-12 weeks prophylaxis plus post-exposure follow-up (2-3 weeks after stopping)
transmission_setting: malarious training areas with endemic falciparum and vivax malaria
safety_summary: No major adverse events reported; regimens generally well tolerated, though not detailed extensively in abstract

title: Beyond chloroquine: implications of drug resistance for evaluating malaria therapy efficacy and treatment policy in Africa.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing malaria treatments (chloroquine vs. pyrimethamine/sulfadioxine) in African children with reported clinical and parasitologic outcome results.
population: very young children with clinical P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical, parasitologic, and hematologic response to treatment
impact_summary: Chloroquine treatment failed to produce durable clinical improvement or optimal hematologic recovery compared to pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine in young children with P. falciparum malaria in Malawi and Kenya.
effect_metric: median time to resumption of clinical symptoms

title: Vaccination with SPf66, a chemically synthesised vaccine, against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Colombia.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT of malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported efficacy outcomes against P. falciparum in humans.
population: volunteers over one year of age in a semi-immune population subject to natural malaria challenge
primary_outcome: Clinical episodes of Plasmodium falciparum malaria detected by active and passive case detection
impact_summary: SPf66 vaccine reduced the incidence of P. falciparum malaria episodes compared to placebo, showing safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy.
transmission_setting: endemic area with natural malaria challenge in semi-immune population
safety_summary: The vaccine was found to be safe based on preclinical and clinical evaluation

title: Rapid coma resolution with artemether in Malawian children with cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether versus quinine for treating cerebral malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance and coma resolution times).
population: unconscious children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Coma resolution time
impact_summary: Artemether resulted in significantly faster parasite clearance and coma resolution than quinine in Malawian children with cerebral malaria.

title: Malaria chemosuppression in pregnancy. I. The effect of chemosuppressive drugs on maternal parasitaemia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (proguanil and chloroquine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on parasitaemia and clinical episodes.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs proguanil vs combination)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria breakthrough parasitaemia and clinical episodes
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis was associated with earlier breakthrough parasitaemia and more clinical episodes than proguanil or the proguanil-chloroquine combination, suggesting chloroquine resistance.
effect_metric: median time to first breakthrough parasitaemia (days)
effect_estimate: CQ: PG=56, MG=78 days; PROG: PG=97, MG=112 days; CQ+PROG: PG=138, MG=140 days
safety_summary: Compliance and drug bio-availability were good; no major adverse events reported.

title: DNA diagnosis of falciparum malaria using a double PCR technique: a field trial in the Solomon Islands.
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of a malaria diagnostic intervention (DNA PCR technique) with reported outcome results in a human population in an endemic setting.
population: individuals tested for malaria in the field

title: Clinical trials with halofantrine in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing halofantrine with mefloquine for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance times, recrudescence).
population: adult male patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day cure rate (recrudescence)
impact_summary: Halofantrine had a lower 42-day cure rate (56%) compared to mefloquine (84%), with more recrudescences in the halofantrine group.
safety_summary: Side-effects of halofantrine and mefloquine were comparable and transient, including diarrhea, dizziness, orthostatic hypotension and black out; vomiting was more common with mefloquine (41% vs 22%).

title: A single dose of intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as an adjunct to quinine in the treatment of severe malaria: pharmacokinetics and efficacy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine±sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in children with severe malaria that has reported outcome results including time to defervescence, parasitemia clearance, and mortality.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: time to defervescence, aparasitaemia, 50% reduction in parasitaemia, parasite elimination half-life, and mortality
impact_summary: Adding a single intramuscular dose of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine to quinine did not improve clinical or parasitological outcomes compared to quinine alone in children with severe malaria.
safety_summary: SD/PM did not perturb the pharmacokinetics of QN; no difference in mortality between groups.

title: Severe morbidity among children in a trial malaria chemoprophylaxis with pyrimethamine or chloroquine in Ibarapa, Nigeria.
journal: African journal of medicine and medical sciences
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (pyrimethamine and chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results on severe morbidity.
population: children
primary_outcome: type and frequency of severe morbidity during chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Weekly chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine or pyrimethamine reduced severe morbidity while being administered, but after stopping, the chloroquine group showed a rebound with significantly more severe morbidity than controls, and chemoprophylaxis shifted the age of severe illness to older children.
age_range: children, mostly under 4 years in control group
safety_summary: No significant differences in type and frequency of severe morbidity during chemoprophylaxis; after stopping chemoprophylaxis, chloroquine group had more severe morbidity episodes than control group.

title: Iron chelation as a chemotherapeutic strategy for falciparum malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (iron chelation with desferrioxamine B) with reported outcome results on parasite concentrations.
population: Zambians with asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum infections
primary_outcome: Change in parasitemia (parasite concentration) following treatment
impact_summary: Desferrioxamine B significantly reduced parasitemia compared with placebo, both acutely and for up to four weeks after treatment.
effect_estimate: Lower parasitemia in desferrioxamine B group vs placebo
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy of desferrioxamine B infusions.

title: Malaria chemosuppression in pregnancy. II. Its effect on maternal haemoglobin levels, placental malaria and birth weight.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on maternal haemoglobin, placental malaria, and birth weight.
comparator: chloroquine vs proguanil vs chloroquine-proguanil combination
population: pregnant women (primigravidae and multigravidae)
primary_outcome: Maternal haemoglobin levels, placental malaria prevalence, and birth weight
impact_summary: Proguanil and chloroquine-proguanil combination were more effective than chloroquine alone in reducing severe anaemia, placental malaria, and low birth weight in primigravidae, with proguanil alone being a suitable alternative to chloroquine prophylaxis.
safety_summary: Possible emergence of chloroquine- and proguanil-resistant strains noted; no other major safety issues reported.

title: Malaria chemosuppression in pregnancy. III. Its effects on the maternal malaria immunity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine/proguanil) in pregnant women with reported immunological outcome results.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Anti-sporozoite antibody titres (R32tet32 antigen reactivity) over the course of prophylaxis
impact_summary: Antibodies in the combined chloroquine plus proguanil group decreased significantly over time, suggesting interference with maternal malaria immune responsiveness, while proguanil alone provided equally efficacious but better prophylaxis.

title: Malaria chemosuppression during pregnancy. IV. Its effects on the newborn's passive malaria immunity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on cord blood antibodies and infant parasitaemia.
comparator: chloroquine once weekly (CQ) vs proguanil daily (PROG) vs combination (CQ+PROG)
population: pregnant women and their newborns
primary_outcome: cord blood anti-sporozoite antibody titres and first occurrence of malaria parasitaemia in infants
impact_summary: Malaria chemoprophylaxis with proguanil or chloroquine plus proguanil during pregnancy did not significantly affect maternal-foetal transfer of anti-sporozoite antibodies, and cord antibody titres at birth did not influence the first occurrence of malaria parasitaemia in infants.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events described beyond antibody and parasitaemia outcomes.

title: Malaria chemosuppression in pregnancy. V. Placenta malarial changes among three different prophylaxis groups.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis in pregnancy with reported histopathological outcome results on placental changes.
comparator: active comparator (proguanil vs chloroquine vs combination)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Placental malarial changes (PMCs) in placenta tissue sections
impact_summary: Placental malarial changes were infrequent and light overall, and comparable across the three prophylaxis groups, despite proguanil and combination therapy being more prophylactically efficacious than chloroquine alone, likely due to prompt diagnosis and treatment of parasitaemias.
effect_estimate: fibrinous deposits 98%, fibrinoid necrosis 60%, leucocytic infiltrations 59%, macrophage pigment 16%, malaria parasites 8%

title: Intravenous immunoglobulin in the treatment of paediatric cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of an adjunctive malaria treatment (immunoglobulin for cerebral malaria) in humans with reported outcome results (mortality and sequelae).
population: children with P. falciparum parasitaemia and unrousable coma (cerebral malaria)
primary_outcome: Mortality and neurological outcome (sequelae) in children with cerebral malaria treated with immunoglobulin versus placebo as adjunct to quinine
impact_summary: Intravenous immunoglobulin as adjunct therapy did not improve outcomes and was not superior to placebo in paediatric cerebral malaria, with higher mortality (31% vs 7%) in the immunoglobulin group, though the difference was not statistically significant.
follow_up: until parasite clearance, fever clearance, and coma resolution (in-hospital)
safety_summary: Higher mortality (31%) and neurological sequelae in survivors were observed in the immunoglobulin group compared to placebo (7% mortality); trial was stopped early because immunoglobulin was shown not to be superior to placebo.

title: High-dose mefloquine in the treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two mefloquine dose regimens for treatment of multidrug-resistant falciparum malaria with reported outcome results.
population: patients with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure rate by day 28
impact_summary: High-dose mefloquine (25 mg/kg) resulted in significantly lower treatment failure rates and faster clinical/parasitologic responses than the standard 15 mg/kg dose.
safety_summary: Side effects were dose-related, including dizziness, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, and fatigue; vomiting within 1 hour of treatment was more common in young children, but children overall tolerated mefloquine better than adults, and men better than women.

title: Control of mosquito larvae in the port city of Assab by an indigenous larvivorous fish, Aphanius dispar.
screening_reason: RCT of larvivorous fish (vector control) for malaria with reported outcome results; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: households with water storage containers, cisterns, wells and barrels serving as mosquito breeding sites
primary_outcome: proportion of breeding sites harbouring mosquito larvae
impact_summary: Stocking breeding sites with the larvivorous fish Aphanius dispar dramatically reduced the presence of mosquito larvae, including the local malaria vector, compared to unstocked sites.
effect_metric: proportion of sites with mosquito larvae
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic port city, vector Anopheles culicifacies adanensis
safety_summary: No adverse effects reported; stocking was well accepted by participants who found fish useful in keeping water free of other aquatic organisms.
funder: National Organization for the Control of Malaria and other Vectorborne Diseases of Ethiopia

title: Chemoprophylaxis against malaria in Papua New Guinea: a trial of amodiaquine and a combination of dapsone and pyrimethamine.
journal: Papua and New Guinea medical journal
screening_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia rates, spleen size, haemoglobin levels).
population: semi-immune school children
primary_outcome: Slide positivity rate (parasitaemia) after 13 weeks of prophylaxis
impact_summary: Both amodiaquine (10mg/kg weekly) and Maloprim (dapsone-pyrimethamine) significantly reduced malaria parasitaemia compared to placebo, though neither fully prevented infection, with Maloprim being more effective than amodiaquine.
transmission_setting: high prevalence of chloroquine/4-aminoquinoline-resistant P. falciparum strains, endemic
safety_summary: No adverse effect on white cell counts by either drug regimen; all groups showed an unexplained fall in haemoglobin level, but the fall was significantly less in both prophylaxis groups.

title: Mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (Fansimef, Roche) in the prophylaxis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria: a double-blind, comparative, placebo-controlled study.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (antimalarial drugs) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia suppression, symptomatic malaria episodes, adverse events).
population: villagers in an endemic area near Ibadan
primary_outcome: Suppressive tolerability and efficacy of antimalarial regimens (parasitaemia suppression and symptomatic malaria episodes)
impact_summary: All four antimalarial regimens, including Fansimef, effectively suppressed parasitaemia and reduced symptomatic malaria compared with placebo, with comparable safety profiles.
safety_summary: Adverse events were not significantly different between groups (6/114 Fansimef, 6/113 mefloquine, 5/111 Fansidar, 17/115 chloroquine, 8/114 placebo); Fansimef safety comparable to standard antimalarials over 24 weeks.

title: Quinine loading dose in severe Falciparum malaria at Kenyatta National Hospital, Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing quinine loading dose regimens in severe falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, adverse effects).
comparator: standard quinine treatment without loading dose
population: non-pregnant patients with severe falciparum malaria, aged 14 years and above
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Quinine loading dose showed no significant advantage over standard treatment in fever or parasite clearance time, but caused more transient hearing loss.
follow_up: until parasitological and clinical clearance (approx 7 days treatment)
safety_summary: Mild toxic effects common in both groups; transient partial hearing loss significantly more common in loading dose group (p < 0.05); hypoglycaemia occurred in 18% of study group vs 6% of control group; one death in each group.

title: Fansimef for prophylaxis of malaria: a double-blind randomized placebo controlled trial.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT comparing malaria prophylaxis interventions with reported outcome results (P. falciparum incidence and adverse events) in a endemic setting.
population: adult males in a malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of acute episodes of P. falciparum malaria per 100 person months of prophylaxis
impact_summary: Fansimef and Lariam had the lowest incidence of P. falciparum episodes, but differences among all groups including placebo were not statistically significant.
safety_summary: Adverse events reported by 170 subjects overall (Fansimef 28, Lariam 29, Fansidar 41, chloroquine 43, placebo 29); differences not statistically significant; most frequent were headache, sleepiness, dizziness and weakness.

title: Preliminary report: a comparative clinical trial of artemether and quinine in severe falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and quinine for severe falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (survival rates, parasite clearance, adverse effects).
population: patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: survival rate
impact_summary: Artemether was associated with a higher survival rate (93%) than quinine (58%) in patients with severe falciparum malaria, though the difference did not reach statistical significance.
safety_summary: Adverse effects (dizziness and vertigo) occurred in 4 patients in the quinine group; no adverse effects were noticed in the artemether group.

title: Artemether in the treatment of multiple drug resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether dosage regimens for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance time, fever clearance time).
population: patients with uncomplicated and severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether at 600 mg total dose achieved higher cure rates than 480 mg in both uncomplicated and severe falciparum malaria, but cure rates in severe malaria remained unsatisfactory in areas with multidrug resistant malaria.
transmission_setting: multiple drug resistant falciparum malaria area
safety_summary: All patients showed a good initial response; no major safety issues reported.

title: Comparison of oral artemether and mefloquine in acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (oral artemether vs mefloquine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, cure rates, adverse events).
population: patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and cure rate
impact_summary: Oral artemether achieved significantly faster parasite clearance and a higher cure rate than mefloquine, with fewer side effects.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistant falciparum malaria area, Thailand
safety_summary: Artemether was well tolerated with fewer episodes of dizziness and vomiting compared to mefloquine.

title: Effect of iron chelation therapy on recovery from deep coma in children with cerebral malaria.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of an antimalarial intervention (iron chelation as adjunctive therapy for cerebral malaria) with reported outcome results on recovery time, parasite clearance, and mortality.
comparator: placebo (added to standard quinine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine therapy)
population: children under six years old with cerebral malaria (P. falciparum parasitemia, coma, normal cerebrospinal fluid)
primary_outcome: Time to recovery of full consciousness
impact_summary: Deferoxamine did not significantly speed recovery of consciousness overall, but among patients with deep coma it significantly increased the rate of recovery of full consciousness and decreased median recovery time, and it also increased the rate of parasite clearance, without significantly affecting mortality.
effect_metric: rate of recovery of full consciousness (hazard ratio)
follow_up: until recovery of consciousness or death (acute hospitalization period)
safety_summary: Mortality was 17% in the deferoxamine group versus 22% in the placebo group (P = 0.52); no other adverse events specified.

title: An open randomized comparison of intravenous and intramuscular artesunate in severe falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two routes of artesunate administration in severe falciparum malaria with reported clinical and parasitological outcomes.
population: adult patients with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological measures of recovery (fever clearance time and parasite clearance time)
impact_summary: Intravenous and intramuscular artesunate were equally effective and well tolerated in treating severe falciparum malaria, with similar fever and parasite clearance times and one death in each group.
effect_metric: mean fever clearance time / mean parasite clearance time
effect_estimate: IV: 37.3 h fever, 33.4 h parasite; IM: 31.5 h fever, 29.4 h parasite
safety_summary: Both routes were well tolerated with no evidence of toxicity; one death occurred in each treatment group.

title: Comparison of artemisinin suppositories with intravenous artesunate and intravenous quinine in the treatment of cerebral malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin vs artesunate vs quinine) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, coma duration, mortality).
comparator: intravenous artesunate vs intravenous quinine (active comparators)
population: Comatose cerebral malaria patients
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time, duration of coma, and mortality
impact_summary: Artesunate and artemisinin suppositories reduced peripheral parasitaemia significantly faster than quinine, but none of the three treatments significantly reduced coma duration or mortality.
safety_summary: No significant differences in mortality or complications reported between treatment groups; specific adverse event data not detailed.

title: Seasonal abundance and biting behaviour of Anopheles punctulatus and An. koliensis in Malaita Province, Solomon Islands, and a trial of permethrin impregnated bednets against malaria transmission.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bednets (a vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (infection rates and vector catches); vector-control trials are classified as not applicable for phase.
population: villagers of Bilimanu, an isolated inland village
primary_outcome: Anopheles vector biting/landing rates and Plasmodium falciparum infection rate before and after permethrin-treated bednet intervention
impact_summary: Introduction of permethrin-impregnated bednets reduced Anopheles punctulatus biting rates and reduced P. falciparum infection rate from 10% pre-intervention to zero by 9 months post-intervention, though rates rose again afterward.
follow_up: 28 months (June 1985 to September 1987), with bednets introduced December 1986
transmission_setting: rural, isolated inland village, seasonal transmission affected by cyclone disruption of vector populations
safety_summary: Not reported

title: The effectiveness of permethrin-impregnated bed nets against malaria for migrant workers in eastern Thailand.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (vector control/ITN intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (malaria episodes).
population: migrant workers
primary_outcome: incidence of malaria episodes among subjects using treated vs untreated nets
impact_summary: Migrant workers using permethrin-treated bed nets had significantly fewer malaria episodes than those using untreated nets over 35 weeks.
transmission_setting: highly endemic for multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum

title: Clinical trials of mefloquine with tetracycline.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine and MSP combinations with tetracycline) in adults with acute falciparum malaria that reports outcome results (cure rates, recrudescence) with 28-day follow-up.
comparator: active comparator (mefloquine plus tetracycline vs MSP plus tetracycline)
population: adult Thai male patients with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Both mefloquine plus tetracycline and MSP plus tetracycline regimens produced similar cure rates with no difference in adverse effects, and the addition of tetracycline improved cure rate compared to standard-dose mefloquine alone.
safety_summary: No difference in adverse effects between groups; some patients experienced vomiting associated with recrudescence (3 in mefloquine+tetracycline group, 2 in MSP+tetracycline group).

title: [Severe malaria attacks in adults in Cameroon: comparison of 2 therapeutic protocols using quinine via parenteral route].
journal: Annales de la Societe belge de medecine tropicale
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine regimen) in humans with reported outcome results (coma duration, parasite clearance); malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: active comparator (standard quinine regimen without loading dose)
population: adults with severe/cerebral malaria attacks
primary_outcome: duration of coma and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: A loading-dose quinine infusion regimen significantly reduced coma duration by 48% and parasite clearance time by 33% compared to the classical regimen, and was safe and effective.
effect_metric: percent reduction in duration of coma
safety_summary: The loading dose regimen was reported as safe and effective with no adverse safety issues noted.

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis, birth weight and child survival.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis (IPTp) in pregnant women with reported outcomes on birth weight and child survival.
population: pregnant women (primigravidae and multigravidae) and their infants
primary_outcome: birthweight and infant survival
impact_summary: Malaria chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy was estimated to reduce infant mortality by about one-fifth among infants of primigravidae, but by less than 5% among infants of multigravidae, largely through effects on birthweight.

title: A randomized clinical trial with high dose of chloroquine for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Brazil.
journal: Revista do Instituto de Medicina Tropical de Sao Paulo
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitaemia) for a malaria treatment intervention (chloroquine doses) in humans; no phase stated but phase I/early-phase designation absent.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria, over 14 years of age, from Amazon Basin and Central Brazil
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure rate (clearance of parasitaemia) at days 7, 14 and 30
impact_summary: High-dose chloroquine (50 mg/Kg) achieved higher cure rates than the standard 25 mg/Kg dose but still showed substantial treatment failure, indicating high-level chloroquine resistance in both groups.
effect_estimate: 89.4% (day 7) and 71.2% (day 14) in 50 mg/Kg group vs 44.8% (day 7) and 24.1% (day 14) in 25 mg/Kg group
transmission_setting: Amazon Basin and Central Brazil, malaria-endemic region
safety_summary: Side effects were minimal in both dosage groups.

title: The antimalarial effect of iron chelators: studies in animal models and in humans with mild falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of iron chelator (deferoxamine) for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results.
population: humans with mild/asymptomatic falciparum malaria parasitemia
primary_outcome: Antimalarial activity of deferoxamine (DF) as measured by effect on parasitemia
impact_summary: Deferoxamine, an iron chelator, showed unequivocal antimalarial activity against P. falciparum infection in a placebo-controlled human trial.

title: A comparative study of the schizontocidal efficacy and safety of artemether versus chloroquine in uncomplicated malaria.
journal: The Central African journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemether vs chloroquine) in uncomplicated malaria with reported outcome results including parasite clearance time, fever clearance, recrudescence rates, and safety data.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether achieved significantly faster parasite clearance and lower recrudescence rates than chloroquine, with no major adverse events in either group.
safety_summary: No major adverse events recorded for either treatment group; five patients on artemether had a transient spike of temperature after clearance of parasitaemia.

title: The relationship between the response of Plasmodium falciparum malaria to mefloquine in African children and its sensitivity in vitro.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: RCT comparing two doses of mefloquine for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance times, recurrence).
population: children with acute symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at day 28 and parasite/fever clearance times
impact_summary: Both 15 mg/kg and 25 mg/kg mefloquine doses achieved 100% cure rate on day 28 with no significant difference in parasite or fever clearance times between doses.

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis using proguanil/dapsone combinations on the Thai-Cambodian border.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing malaria chemoprophylaxis interventions in humans with clear efficacy findings for prevention of falciparum and vivax malaria.
comparator: pyrimethamine/dapsone (active comparator); doxycycline arm for G6PD-deficient men
population: Thai soldiers, including some with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency
primary_outcome: Malaria attack rates (falciparum and vivax malaria incidence)
impact_summary: Proguanil/dapsone was not superior to pyrimethamine/dapsone for preventing falciparum malaria and was concluded not to be a useful chemoprophylaxis alternative on the Thai-Cambodian border, though it was more effective at preventing vivax malaria.
transmission_setting: multiple drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum, endemic border area
safety_summary: Hematologic toxicity was not observed with the proguanil/dapsone combination.

title: Efficacy of dapsone with pyrimethamine (Maloprim) for malaria prophylaxis in Maputo, Mozambique.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention with reported outcome results (parasitological infections); primary purpose is malaria prevention in humans.
population: school children
primary_outcome: Parasitological infection with malaria assessed by fortnightly controls
impact_summary: Weekly dapsone-pyrimethamine prophylaxis prevented malaria infections, with 28 infections in the placebo group and none in the treatment group.

title: The effect of participatory school health programme on the control of malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (parasite rates, clinical malaria, antimalarial practices) testing a malaria control intervention (participatory health education) in humans.
population: primary school children aged 7-18 years
primary_outcome: Change in knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding malaria, and clinical malaria incidence
impact_summary: Participatory school health education led to greater improvements in antimalarial practices, environmental manipulation efforts, reduced parasite rates, reduced absenteeism, and lower clinical malaria incidence compared to passive control education.
effect_metric: percentage change in clinical malaria incidence
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Norfloxacin is inferior to chloroquine for falciparum malaria in northwestern Zambia: a comparative clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
population: semiimmune adults with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate at day 28 (parasitological/clinical cure)
impact_summary: Chloroquine cured 100% of patients compared with only 40% cured with norfloxacin, leading to early termination of the trial due to chloroquine's superior efficacy.
safety_summary: Norfloxacin caused fewer adverse effects than chloroquine (0% vs 33%, P < .001).

title: Lack of effect of desipramine on the response to chloroquine of patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine) with reported outcome results on parasite clearance; malaria is the primary focus.
population: malaria patients meeting WHO in vivo test criteria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance in vivo and chloroquine sensitivity pattern
impact_summary: Adding desipramine to chloroquine did not improve chloroquine efficacy against chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria compared to chloroquine alone.

title: Randomised trial of artesunate and mefloquine alone and in sequence for acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate and mefloquine) with reported outcome results (cure rates at 28 days); primary purpose is malaria intervention in humans.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate alone vs mefloquine alone vs combination)
population: patients with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (no recrudescence) during 28 days' follow-up
impact_summary: The combination of artesunate followed by mefloquine cured all patients and was more effective than either drug alone, which had cure rates of 88% and 81% respectively.
safety_summary: Fever and parasite clearance times were shorter with artesunate-containing regimens; nausea and vomiting were slightly, but not significantly, more frequent with the combination than with either drug alone.

title: Comparative trial on the response of Plasmodium falciparum to halofantrine and mefloquine in Trat Province, eastern Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial drugs (halofantrine vs mefloquine) for P. falciparum treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates); malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: cure rate
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and halofantrine showed extremely low cure rates (33.3% and 28.13% respectively), suggesting cross-resistance between the two drugs.

title: Comparison of artemether and chloroquine for severe malaria in Gambian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and chloroquine for severe malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times, mortality, safety outcomes).
population: children with moderate or severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Time to parasite clearance and therapeutic response in severe malaria
impact_summary: Artemether cleared parasites faster than chloroquine in moderate malaria, and both drugs showed similar efficacy and safety in severe malaria with no significant differences in clinical outcomes.
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated with no evidence of local or systemic toxicity; 8 children (19%) with severe malaria died overall.

title: Evaluation of the relative efficacy of various antimalarial drugs in Nigerian children under five years of age suffering from acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug efficacy in children with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with reported parasitological and clinical outcome results.
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine, quinine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, mefloquine 15 mg/kg, mefloquine 25 mg/kg)
population: children under five years with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure rate assessed up to day 14 (28-day in vivo test)
impact_summary: Chloroquine was less effective (85% cure rate) than amodiaquine, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine, quinine and mefloquine (all 100% cure rate) in treating acute falciparum malaria in children under five in Nigeria.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; chloroquine treatment failures were successfully retreated with mefloquine 25 mg/kg without noted adverse events

title: Iron chelation with desferrioxamine B in adults with asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia.
screening_reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing a malaria treatment intervention (iron chelation) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance).
population: adults with asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia
primary_outcome: Rate of clearance of P falciparum parasitemia (decrement in geometric mean concentrations of asexual intraerythrocytic parasites)
impact_summary: Desferrioxamine B treatment significantly enhanced the rate of clearance of P falciparum parasitemia compared with placebo, with no detected drug toxicity.
safety_summary: No drug toxicity was detected.

title: The first field trials of the chemically synthesized malaria vaccine SPf66: safety, immunogenicity and protectivity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (SPf66) with reported efficacy results against P. falciparum and P. vivax.
population: volunteers in a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of P. falciparum malaria among vaccinated versus placebo volunteers
impact_summary: The SPf66 vaccine reduced malaria incidence compared to placebo, with efficacy of 82.3% against P. falciparum and 60.6% against P. vivax.
safety_summary: No detectable clinical or laboratory alterations were induced by the immunization process; vaccine was well tolerated.

title: Absorption of intramuscular phenobarbitone in children with severe falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcomes (absorption data, clinical findings, coma depth, safety) testing an intervention (phenobarbitone) in children with severe falciparum malaria.
population: children with severe falciparum malaria, some comatose
primary_outcome: Absorption of intramuscular phenobarbitone (pharmacokinetics) and clinical findings including convulsions and level of consciousness
impact_summary: Intramuscular phenobarbitone was rapidly and well absorbed in children with severe malaria, but recipients showed a significant tendency to deepen in coma or become sleepy within 4 hours of administration, and the study was too small to assess anticonvulsant efficacy.
safety_summary: No observable toxicity, but phenobarbitone recipients had a significant tendency to deepen in coma or become sleepy within 4 hours after drug administration; one placebo recipient had repeated convulsions and died 1 hour after admission.

title: Effect of chloroquine chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy on birth weight: results of a randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine chemoprophylaxis for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported outcome results (birth weight and placental infection).
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: birth weight
impact_summary: Chloroquine chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy significantly reduced placental infection but did not significantly change mean birth weight or low birth weight proportion compared to controls.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; concerns raised about spread of chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium strains with mass prophylaxis.

title: Comparison of combinations of parenteral artemisinin derivatives plus oral mefloquine with intravenous quinine plus oral tetracycline for treating cerebral malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin-derivative regimens versus quinine for cerebral malaria treatment with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, recrudescence).
population: patients with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Both artemisinin derivative combinations (artemether or artesunate plus mefloquine) resulted in lower mortality and faster parasite clearance than quinine plus tetracycline, with no recrudescence compared to 12.1% in the quinine group.
safety_summary: No recrudescence observed in artemisinin-based regimens; 12.1% recrudescence in the quinine plus tetracycline regimen.

title: Efficacy of a low dose oral quinine therapy in Plasmodium falciparum cases of Assam, Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh in India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine) with reported efficacy outcome results; not early-phase.
population: Plasmodium falciparum cases including known chloroquine resistant cases
primary_outcome: Clinical/parasitological response to low dose oral quinine therapy
impact_summary: A low dose oral quinine regimen (1050 mg/day in two divided doses for five days) was effective in 76.92% of P. falciparum cases and 45.55% of known chloroquine-resistant cases, and was well tolerated with quick clinical response.
safety_summary: The low dose quinine was well tolerated with quick clinical response.

title: Double blind randomised clinical trial of oral artesunate at once or twice daily dose in falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results (cure rates, clearance times, adverse effects) testing oral artesunate dosing regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (once daily vs twice daily oral artesunate dosing)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at 28-day follow-up (fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, recrudescence)
impact_summary: Once daily and twice daily oral artesunate regimens produced similar efficacy (72% vs 76% cure rate) with no difference in adverse effects, suggesting treatment duration is more important than dosing frequency.
safety_summary: No difference in adverse effects between the once daily and twice daily regimens.

title: Double blind randomised clinical trial of two different regimens of oral artesunate in falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT comparing oral artesunate regimens in falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance times); primary focus is malaria treatment; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
comparator: active comparator (5-day vs 7-day oral artesunate regimen)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: A 7-day regimen of oral artesunate achieved a higher cure rate (92.5%) than a 5-day regimen (85%), but neither achieved 100% cure, suggesting the longer regimen may improve therapeutic efficacy.
safety_summary: Artesunate was well tolerated in both the 5-day and 7-day regimens.

title: Clearance of plasmodium falciparum after reduced single daily doses of quinine in asymptomatic children in Guinea Bissau.
journal: Tropical medicine and parasitology : official organ of Deutsche Tropenmedizinische Gesellschaft and of Deutsche Gesellschaft fur Technische Zusammenarbeit (GTZ)
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results (parasitemia clearance) of a malaria treatment intervention (quinine) in humans with reported findings.
population: asymptomatic schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Clearance of P. falciparum parasitemia by day 7 of follow-up
impact_summary: Single daily doses of quinine for 3 or 5 days were less effective at clearing P. falciparum than previously used divided doses and were associated with more frequent adverse events.
effect_estimate: 5 of 31 children had parasitemia on day 7
safety_summary: 12 children reported adverse reactions during treatment, mainly mild tinnitus, dizziness and vomiting.

title: Quinine treatment of severe falciparum malaria in African children: a randomized comparison of three regimens.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of quinine treatment for severe malaria in humans with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and clinical response.
comparator: active comparator (three quinine dosage regimens compared against each other)
population: African children with severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Quinine pharmacokinetics and clinical/parasitological response (parasite clearance time) to three quinine dosage regimens
impact_summary: High-dose intravenous and intramuscular quinine regimens achieved faster parasite clearance and better clinical response than the low-dose intravenous regimen, with no significant quinine toxicity observed.
effect_metric: correlation between parasite clearance rate and area under quinine concentration-time curve
safety_summary: Five patients developed hypoglycemia (two low-dose, two intramuscular, one high-dose) associated with low insulin concentrations; no significant quinine toxicity observed in any case.

title: Neither heparin nor acetylsalicylic acid influence the clinical course in human Plasmodium falciparum malaria: a prospective randomized study.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes testing adjunctive treatments in P. falciparum malaria patients; malaria is the primary focus and results are fully presented.
comparator: no heparin/ASA (control group receiving only antiparasitic treatment)
population: patients with falciparum malaria, including some with complications upon admission
primary_outcome: Clinical course parameters including duration of parasitemia, fever clearance, laboratory parameters, and length of hospitalization
