impact_summary: Neither low-dose subcutaneous heparin nor intravenous acetylsalicylic acid influenced the clinical course of falciparum malaria compared to standard antiparasitic treatment alone.
safety_summary: Heparin caused minimal partial thromboplastin time prolongation; no other adverse effects on laboratory parameters were noted, though authors caution against routine use due to possible side effects.

title: Comparative trial of oral versus intramuscular chloroquine in children with cerebral malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (cerebral malaria) in humans with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, neurological deficits).
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Outcome (mortality) and parasite clearance time comparing oral versus intramuscular chloroquine
impact_summary: No obvious difference in outcome was found between oral and intramuscular chloroquine treatment groups, with overall mortality of 5.3%.
safety_summary: Hypoglycaemia incidence was low (3%); neurological deficits seen in 7.8% of patients on day 14; parasitaemia recurred in 22% of survivors within 14 days indicating RI/RII chloroquine resistance.

title: Reduction of coma by quinine loading dose in falciparum cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (quinine loading dose for cerebral malaria) in humans.
comparator: standard quinine dosing regimen (without loading dose)
population: patients with falciparum cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: time to recovery from coma / duration of coma
impact_summary: Administration of a quinine loading dose reduced the duration of coma in patients with falciparum cerebral malaria compared with standard dosing.

title: Ciprofloxacin treatment of drug-resistant falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention with reported outcome results (efficacy/safety findings), though early terminated.
population: patients with uncomplicated chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Clearance of parasitemia / clinical response to ciprofloxacin treatment
impact_summary: Ciprofloxacin failed to control parasitemia and clinical deterioration occurred, requiring rescue quinine treatment in most patients, leading to early termination of the study.
effect_estimate: threefold increase in parasitemia at 36 h compared to admission
safety_summary: Study terminated early for safety reasons; three patients required quinine at 36 h and one at 54 h due to rising parasitemia and clinical deterioration.

title: Clinical trial of artesunate and artemether on multidrug resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand. A preliminary report.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artesunate/artemether) with reported outcome results (cure rates, clearance times, safety data); phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible regardless.
comparator: active comparator (different dosing regimens/durations of artesunate and artemether)
population: patients with multidrug resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate (parasitological cure/recrudescence)
impact_summary: A 5-day course of oral artesunate or intramuscular artemether achieved 90-100% cure rates in multidrug resistant falciparum malaria, while shorter courses resulted in high recrudescence rates.
safety_summary: Side effects were mild and transient, including occasional abnormal electrocardiograms and pain at the injection site; slight reduction of neutrophil leucocytes and reticulocytes was observed.

title: Trial of pyrethroid impregnated bednets in an area of Tanzania holoendemic for malaria. Part 4. Effects on incidence of malaria infection.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of pyrethroid-impregnated bednets (vector-control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria infection incidence in humans.
comparator: DDT house spraying, no vector control (untreated nets/control)
population: children
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria infection (time to return of parasitaemia after clearance) measured by fortnightly blood slides
impact_summary: Parasitaemia returned rapidly without vector control but more slowly when pyrethroid impregnated nets or DDT house spraying were used, with variation between villages linked more to ecological or social factors than the vector control method.

title: Trial of pyrethroid impregnated bednets in an area of Tanzania holoendemic for malaria. Part 3. Effects on the prevalence of malaria parasitaemia and fever.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of pyrethroid-impregnated bed nets (vector control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on parasitaemia and fever; phase not applicable for cluster/community trials.
comparator: DDT spraying, untreated nets/no intervention, lambdacyhalothrin nets
population: children aged 1-10 in five villages
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria parasitaemia and fever
impact_summary: Permethrin impregnated bednets markedly reduced falciparum malaria slide positivity in estate villages and were associated with reductions in malaria fever, whereas lambdacyhalothrin nets and DDT spraying showed no such effect.

title: Trial of antimalarial potential of extracts of Artemisia annua grown in Myanmar.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing an antimalarial intervention (Artemisia annua extract) in humans with reported outcome results.

title: A prospective clinical trial of the treatment of falciparum malaria with mefloquine, with special reference to neuro-psychiatric side effects.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine for falciparum malaria) with human participants.
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: neuro-psychiatric side effects following mefloquine treatment
impact_summary: Mefloquine treatment for falciparum malaria was associated with neuro-psychiatric side effects in some patients.
safety_summary: Neuro-psychiatric side effects were observed following mefloquine treatment.

title: The effect of insecticide-treated bed nets on mortality of Gambian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector control) for malaria prevention in children with reported mortality outcome results.
comparator: non-PHC villages with no intervention (for bed nets); placebo (for chemoprophylaxis)
population: children aged 6 months to 5 years in rural Gambian villages
primary_outcome: Mortality in children aged 1-4 years
impact_summary: Insecticide-treated bed nets combined with primary health care reduced overall mortality and malaria-attributable mortality in children compared to villages without the intervention, with no additional benefit from chemoprophylaxis.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no additional benefit or harm noted from chemoprophylaxis compared to placebo among net users.

title: Comparison of mefloquine, chloroquine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine (Fansidar), and chloroquine as malarial prophylaxis in eastern Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (three drug prophylaxis regimens) in humans with reported outcome results (attack rates and efficacy).
population: Thai gem miners working in Cambodia
primary_outcome: Malarial attack rate (P. falciparum and P. vivax) over 14 weeks of prophylaxis
impact_summary: Mefloquine provided substantially higher prophylactic efficacy against malaria than chloroquine or chloroquine plus Fansidar, but even mefloquine's efficacy was called into question due to relatively high breakthrough infection rates.
transmission_setting: high-incidence border area with multidrug-resistant P. falciparum

title: Trial of pyrethroid impregnated bednets in an area of Tanzania holoendemic for malaria. Part 2. Effects on the malaria vector population.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of pyrethroid-impregnated bed nets (vector control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results on vector populations and sporozoite inoculation rates.
population: village residents in a holoendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: Effects on the malaria vector population (biting density, survival, sporozoite rate, sporozoite inoculation rate)
impact_summary: Introduction of pyrethroid-impregnated bednets reduced Anopheles mosquito populations, survival, sporozoite rates, and led to a more than 90% decline in estimated sporozoite inoculation rates into people not sleeping under nets.

title: Comparison of intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and intramuscular quinine for the treatment of falciparum malaria in children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria treatments (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs quinine) in children with severe falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results including parasite clearance time and fever clearance time.
population: children with severe falciparum malaria without life-threatening complications
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: A single intramuscular dose of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine cleared parasites and fever slightly faster than intramuscular quinine, though some resistant cases occurred, suggesting it may be useful where hospital admission is not feasible.
safety_summary: Blood sugar levels slightly but not significantly lower in the quinine group; leucocyte counts significantly lower but within normal range in the sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine group on day 7.

title: The efficacy of sulphate quinine compared to fansidar in treating falciparum malaria in children 6 months-7 years old.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments (quinine vs fansidar) in children with falciparum malaria, with reported outcome results (parasitemia duration and fever subsidence).
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Duration of parasitemia and time to fever resolution
impact_summary: Children treated with quinine had a shorter duration of parasitemia and more rapid resolution of fever compared to those treated with fansidar.

title: Proguanil/sulfamethoxazole malaria chemoprophy-laxis on the Thai-Cambodian border.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (proguanil/sulfamethoxazole vs pyrimethamine/dapsone) in humans with reported outcome results (malaria attack rates); primary purpose is malaria prevention; phase not stated but chemoprophylaxis trials are not early-phase.
population: Thai soldiers
primary_outcome: malaria attack rate
impact_summary: Proguanil/sulfamethoxazole chemoprophylaxis resulted in a significantly lower malaria attack rate than pyrimethamine/dapsone, with 64% greater relative efficacy against P. vivax and 38% against P. falciparum.
effect_estimate: 64% for P. vivax, 38% for P. falciparum
transmission_setting: multiple drug-resistant malaria area, Thai-Cambodian border
safety_summary: No serious drug side-effects were observed; compliance greater than 86% in both groups.

title: Comparative effectiveness of artemisinin suppositories and oral quinine in children with acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments (artemisinin suppositories vs oral quinine) for the primary purpose of malaria treatment in children.
population: children with acute falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Artemisinin suppositories were compared with oral quinine for treating children with acute falciparum malaria.

title: Prolonged malaria prophylaxis with chloroquine and proguanil (chloroguanide) in a nonimmune resident population of an endemic area with a high prevalence of chloroquine resistance.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine and proguanil) with reported outcome results (infection rates and clinical severity) in humans.
population: nonimmune resident adults
primary_outcome: Incidence of Plasmodium falciparum infection during 18 months of follow-up
impact_summary: Weekly chloroquine plus daily proguanil prophylaxis significantly reduced P. falciparum infection compared with no prophylaxis in a nonimmune population in a high chloroquine-resistance area.
transmission_setting: endemic area with high prevalence of chloroquine resistance
safety_summary: Side effects were frequent (31%), minor, related to chloroquine, and usually resolved within 4 to 6 weeks; prophylaxis was considered safe.

title: Proguanil daily or chlorproguanil twice weekly are efficacious against falciparum malaria in a holoendemic area of Tanzania.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (proguanil and chlorproguanil prophylaxis) in humans with reported outcome results (reinfection rates).
population: school children
primary_outcome: Parasitemia/reinfection with P. falciparum during follow-up
impact_summary: Both proguanil daily and chlorproguanil twice weekly prevented malaria reinfection, while all children on placebo were reinfected within 10 weeks.
effect_estimate: 0% reinfection in proguanil/chlorproguanil groups vs 100% in placebo group
safety_summary: Not specifically reported

title: [Malaria and surgery: which prophylaxis?].
journal: Medecine tropicale : revue du Corps de sante colonial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprophylaxis (quinine) intervention in humans; primary purpose is malaria treatment/prevention in peri-operative setting.
population: surgical patients undergoing general surgery
primary_outcome: occurrence of clinical malaria attack during the peri-operative phase
impact_summary: Malaria attacks were more frequent and severe in patients not receiving quinine chemoprophylaxis, and only patients already positive for malaria before surgery developed clinical malaria signs.

title: Susceptibility of Plasmodium falciparum to different doses of quinine in vivo and to quinine and quinidine in vitro in relation to chloroquine in Liberia.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of quinine for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance and recrudescence/reinfection).
comparator: chloroquine (in vitro comparison); different quinine treatment durations (in vivo)
population: Children infected with Plasmodium falciparum
primary_outcome: Recurrence of parasitaemia (recrudescence vs reinfection) after quinine treatment of varying duration; in vitro susceptibility (MIC, IC50, IC90) to quinine, quinidine and chloroquine
impact_summary: Quinine and quinidine remained effective against P. falciparum isolates in vitro despite chloroquine resistance, though chloroquine-resistant isolates showed roughly twice the IC50/IC90/MIC for quinine compared to chloroquine-sensitive isolates; in vivo, a single day (3-dose) quinine regimen resulted in recrudescence in 5 of 15 children, whereas longer regimens (2, 4, 7 days) prevented recrudescence, with recurrences only due to reinfection.
effect_metric: Difference in IC50/IC90/MIC for quinine between chloroquine-resistant and chloroquine-sensitive isolates
transmission_setting: Chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum emerging in Yekepa, Liberia

title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of mefloquine in Thai patients with acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with randomized allocation to mefloquine doses in malaria patients; reports pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic outcomes and clinical efficacy; malaria treatment is primary focus.
comparator: active comparator (750 mg vs 1250 mg mefloquine)
population: Thai male patients with acute uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics (fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, treatment response) of mefloquine
impact_summary: There was no advantage in using a single 1250 mg dose of mefloquine over 750 mg, as both doses showed similar clearance times and treatment failures.
safety_summary: Main adverse effects included dizziness, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhoea; ECG monitoring showed sinus bradycardia and sinus arrhythmia in several patients, with dizziness more frequent in the 1250-mg group.

title: Cerebral malaria in children. Comparative study between heparin, dexamethasone and placebo.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (heparin and dexamethasone as adjuncts to quinine) in children with cerebral malaria that has reported outcome results including mortality, recovery time, and hospitalization duration.
population: children with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Time to regain consciousness, duration of fever, mortality, and hospitalization duration
impact_summary: Heparin-treated children regained consciousness faster and had shorter fever duration compared to dexamethasone and placebo groups, with low mortality across all groups.
safety_summary: One death occurred in the dexamethasone group (4.76%); no deaths in heparin or placebo groups; overall mortality 1.61%.

title: [Trial of halofantrine in the treatment of malaria attacks by Plasmodium falciparum in Dakar (Senegal)].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing halofantrine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results on fever clearance, parasite density reduction, and adverse effects.
population: children and adults with acute P. falciparum malaria attack, including chloroquine-resistant strains
primary_outcome: Fever clearance, parasite clearance and parasite density reduction after halofantrine treatment
impact_summary: Halofantrine treatment cleared fever in all patients within 36.3 hours, reduced parasite density by 93.6%, and achieved parasite clearance in all patients including those with chloroquine-resistant strains, with recrudescence in only 3 cases (10.7%) by day 14.
safety_summary: Adverse reactions were mild, including nausea, vomiting, slight diarrhoea and dizziness affecting 13.8% of patients; no biological abnormalities noted.

title: Chloroquine therapy still useful in the management of malaria during pregnancy in Muheza, Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine) in pregnant women with reported parasitological and clinical outcome results.
comparator: proguanil (chemosuppression); chloroquine treatment for breakthrough malaria evaluated in vivo
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Parasitological clearance and clinical response to 25 mg base chloroquine/kg over three days in pregnant women with breakthrough clinical malaria
impact_summary: Treatment with 25 mg base chloroquine/kg over three days achieved parasitological clearance in 65% of pregnant women with breakthrough malaria, with most treatment failures showing favorable clinical response despite moderate chloroquine resistance in the area.
transmission_setting: moderate chloroquine resistance area, peak malaria transmission season
safety_summary: Chloroquine at 25 mg base/kg was described as safe and affordable; most treatment failures had favorable clinical response with only 2 of 17 failures exhibiting RIII response

title: Red cell and plasma concentrations of combined quinine-quinidine and quinine in falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing quinine/quinidine/cinchonine combination and quinine monotherapy in falciparum malaria with reported cure rates and clinical outcomes.
comparator: quinine alone versus combined quinine-quinidine-cinchonine at high and low dose regimens
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate
impact_summary: The high dose combined quinine-quinidine-cinchonine regimen achieved a significantly higher cure rate (100%) than the low dose regimen (37.5%) and quinine alone (50%), with red cell drug concentrations correlating more closely with treatment outcome than plasma concentrations.
effect_estimate: 100% (high dose combined) vs 37.5% (low dose combined) vs 50% (quinine alone)
safety_summary: Mild and transient ECG effects noted, similar in both the combined drug group and the quinine group.

title: Clinical efficacy of mefloquine in children suffering from chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Nigeria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitemia clearance times).
population: children with symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria, including chloroquine-resistant cases
primary_outcome: Cure rate (clinical and parasitological response) of chloroquine versus mefloquine treatment
impact_summary: Mefloquine achieved a 100% cure rate compared with 65% for chloroquine, and successfully treated chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum cases.
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant malaria endemic area, West Africa
safety_summary: Chloroquine group had pruritus in 7 subjects; mefloquine group had abdominal pain and diarrhoea in 8 subjects and dizziness in 3 subjects.

title: Mefloquine kinetics in cured and recrudescent patients with acute falciparum malaria and in healthy volunteers.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine treatment for acute falciparum malaria with reported efficacy and pharmacokinetic outcomes in humans.
comparator: active comparator (750 mg vs 1500 mg mefloquine dose comparison, patients vs healthy volunteers)
population: patients with acute falciparum malaria and healthy volunteers
primary_outcome: Mefloquine pharmacokinetics (Cmax, AUC, time to peak concentration) and treatment efficacy
impact_summary: Efficacy was 82% for the 1500 mg dose and 63% for the 750 mg dose, with cured patients showing higher plasma mefloquine levels than those with treatment failure, and ill patients showing delayed and higher peak concentrations compared to healthy volunteers.
p_value: p<0.0005 for Cmax; p<0.01 for AUC and time to peak concentration
safety_summary: Mefloquine AUC was reduced and variable in the presence of diarrhea; no other adverse events specifically detailed.

title: Parenteral sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (Fansidar): an effective and safe but under-used method of anti-malarial treatment.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing anti-malarial treatments (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs chloroquine) in patients with acute falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (parasitological cure rates and safety data).
comparator: chloroquine, and oral vs intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
population: patients with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure rate
impact_summary: Both oral and intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved much higher parasitological cure rates than chloroquine, with intramuscular administration equally effective and better tolerated than oral administration.
safety_summary: Side effects occurred in 3 patients on intramuscular sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, 8 on oral sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and 13 on chloroquine, indicating intramuscular SP was better tolerated.

title: Combination of quinine, quinidine and cinchonine for the treatment of acute falciparum malaria: correlation with the susceptibility of Plasmodium falciparum to the cinchona alkaloids in vitro.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine-quinidine-cinchonine combination) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, fever clearance, safety).
comparator: active comparator (400 mg vs 500 mg dose of LA40221)
population: patients with acute symptomatic uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clearance of parasitaemia, fever and other symptoms; recrudescence during 28-day observation
impact_summary: Both 400 mg and 500 mg doses of the quinine-quinidine-cinchonine combination promptly cleared parasitaemia and fever with no recrudescence over 28 days, with minor gastrointestinal side effects and QTc prolongation observed in some patients.
safety_summary: Minor gastrointestinal side effects in 2 patients; no major side effects; no adverse changes in haematological or biochemical measurements; QTc prolongation occurred in 3 patients (2 in 400 mg group, 1 in 500 mg group).

title: Phase III double-blind comparative study of Fansimef and Lariam for the curative treatment of Plasmodium falciparum infections in Thailand.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Phase III RCT with reported outcome results (cure rates) for malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: patients with falciparum malaria attending malaria clinics
primary_outcome: cure rate for Plasmodium falciparum infection
impact_summary: Fansimef (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) and Lariam (mefloquine) had similar cure rates for falciparum malaria with no significant difference between groups.
safety_summary: Vomiting and diarrhea were common side effects in both groups; less common were epigastric pain, minor skin rashes and dizziness; new-onset vomiting (MSP 23%, MEF 8%) and epigastric pain (MSP 22%, MEF 11%) were significantly different between groups.

title: Efficacy of pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine in uncomplicated severe falciparum malaria in Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine) in humans with uncomplicated severe falciparum malaria.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Efficacy of pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine in uncomplicated severe falciparum malaria in Kenya.

title: Field study of cyproheptadine/chloroquine synergism in falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (chloroquine with cyproheptadine) in humans.
population: patients with falciparum malaria

title: Permethrin-impregnated curtains and bed-nets prevent malaria in western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-impregnated bed-nets and curtains (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results; phase not applicable for vector-control cluster trials.
comparator: control (untreated households, no bed-net or curtain)
population: families/households in a rural community, all cured of parasitemia before start
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum infections per person week at risk
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated curtains and bed-nets significantly reduced malaria infection rates and indoor resting Anopheles mosquito density compared to untreated control households.
effect_estimate: curtain 2.35 vs control 5.42; bed-net 3.77 vs control 5.42
transmission_setting: rural western Kenya, endemic malaria area
safety_summary: Not reported

title: A randomized comparative study of artemisinine (qinghaosu) suppositories and oral quinine in acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinine versus quinine for acute falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times, recrudescence rates).
population: adult patients with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemisinine suppositories achieved faster parasite clearance than oral quinine, but were associated with a higher rate of recrudescence.
safety_summary: Artemisinine suppositories had lack of side effects or risk of overdose; higher recrudescence (RI, delayed) occurred with artemisinine (16 patients) compared with quinine (6 patients).

title: Mefloquine prophylaxis.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria prevention (mefloquine prophylaxis) in humans with reported outcome results; phase not stated but chemoprevention is Phase II or higher.

title: Controlled trial of exchange transfusion in falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial of an intervention (exchange transfusion) for malaria (falciparum) that has reported outcome results; not early-phase.
population: patients with falciparum malaria

title: Antimalarial prophylaxis in pregnant Nigerian women.
screening_reason: Published RCT with outcome results reporting antimalarial prophylaxis (IPTp), a primary malaria prevention intervention in a human population (pregnant women).
population: pregnant women

title: [Comparative study of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of malaria caused by chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum in Maputo, Mozambique].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine regimens) with reported cure-rate outcomes in humans; not early-phase.
population: patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria at Maputo Central Hospital
primary_outcome: Cure rate of falciparum malaria treatment
impact_summary: Both regimens achieved high cure rates (86% with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and 90% with amodiaquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with no serious side-effects, and the difference was not clinically important.
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria endemic area, semi-immune population
safety_summary: No serious side-effects were observed with either regimen.

title: Proguanil-sulphonamide for malaria prophylaxis.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention in humans with reported outcome results (efficacy >75% against P. falciparum and P. vivax).
population: schoolchildren living near the Thai-Burmese border
primary_outcome: chemoprophylactic activity against Plasmodium falciparum and vivax malaria infection
impact_summary: Daily proguanil combined with sulphafurazole or sulphamethoxazole at 25 mg/kg/d was more than 75% effective against both falciparum and vivax malaria, while proguanil with sulphamethoxazole at 10 mg/kg/d was ineffective.
transmission_setting: multiple drug-resistant P. falciparum area, Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Approximately 1% of children developed sulphonamide-related skin rashes that resolved after stopping treatment.

title: Double-blind studies with mefloquine alone and in combination with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in 120 adults and 120 children with falciparum malaria in Vietnam.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine and combination therapies) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
comparator: chloroquine; mefloquine alone vs mefloquine+sulfadoxine+pyrimethamine combination; different doses of MSP
population: adults and children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance time and therapeutic efficacy (sensitivity/resistance response) in falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Mefloquine alone and mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine were both highly effective against falciparum malaria in Vietnam, while chloroquine showed a high resistance rate, and the lowest MSP dose was as effective as higher doses in children.
safety_summary: Side effects were mild overall, except for vomiting which required alternative therapy in 4 patients.

title: [Vaccination against malaria: initial trial with an ant-sporozoite vaccine, (NANP)3-TT (RO 40-2361) in Africa (Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso)].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled vaccine trial with reported outcome results (immunogenicity, safety, and efficacy/parasitemia outcomes) testing a malaria vaccine intervention in humans.
population: infants aged 3 to 5 months
primary_outcome: Incidence and level of parasitaemia and incidence of clinical malaria; immunogenicity (IgG antibody response)
impact_summary: The (NANP)3-TT vaccine was immunogenic but did not confer protective efficacy, with no significant differences in parasitaemia or clinical malaria incidence between vaccine and control groups.
transmission_setting: holoendemic, permanent transmission with peaks in July and November (irrigated rice cultivation area)
safety_summary: No systemic reactions observed; minor local tumefactions in 3% of children; no serious adverse events reported.

title: Open comparison of intramuscular chloroquine and quinine in children with severe chloroquine-sensitive falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (chloroquine vs quinine) for severe falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (mortality, parasitaemia clearance, clinical response).
population: children with severe chloroquine-sensitive falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic response including rate of parasite clearance and mortality
impact_summary: Chloroquine cleared parasitaemia faster than quinine, and mortality was numerically lower with chloroquine (2 deaths) than quinine (6 deaths), suggesting quinine is not intrinsically superior to chloroquine in severe drug-sensitive falciparum malaria.
safety_summary: Quinine injections were painful; 8 total deaths occurred (6 in quinine group, 2 in chloroquine group).

title: Chemosuppression of malaria by the triple combination mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine: a field trial in an endemic area in Malaysia.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing malaria chemoprevention (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results on parasitaemia suppression in an endemic area.
population: residents of a malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: Occurrence of malaria assessed clinically and by blood films (parasitaemia suppression)
impact_summary: The low dose of mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine was completely effective in suppressing parasitaemia with minimal side effects compared to Fansidar and a higher MSP dose.
safety_summary: 2.7% of subjects reported adverse drug reactions; incidence was lowest in the low dose group, which also had the least affected blood chemical profiles.

title: Lack of efficacy of pyrimethamine prophylaxis in pregnant Nigerian women.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (pyrimethamine prophylaxis) in pregnant women with reported outcome results (parasitologic failure rates).
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Parasitologic failure rate during 16-week follow-up
impact_summary: Pyrimethamine prophylaxis was not effective for suppressive or causal prophylaxis against P. falciparum in pregnant women, with high resistance rates and no difference in failure rates versus controls.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Effects of interferons on immune response to a synthetic peptide malaria sporozoite vaccine in non-immune adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine in humans with reported immunogenicity results; Phase II (vaccine safety/immunogenicity in non-immune volunteers); malaria prevention is the primary focus.
population: non-immune adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Immune response (seroconversion rate and antibody titres) to the synthetic peptide malaria sporozoite vaccine
impact_summary: Immunizations were well tolerated and IFN-alpha significantly enhanced IgG antibody titres to the malaria peptide vaccine compared to placebo, with seroconversion rates of 67-100% across groups.
safety_summary: Immunizations were well tolerated in all groups.

title: Effect of rate of infusion of quinine on insulin and glucose responses in Malawian children with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of a malaria treatment intervention (quinine infusion rate effects) in children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
comparator: different rate of quinine infusion (loading dose vs standard)
population: children with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: insulin and glucose responses following quinine infusion
impact_summary: The rate of quinine infusion affected the magnitude of insulin and glucose responses in Malawian children with falciparum malaria.

title: The effects of malaria chemoprophylaxis given by traditional birth attendants on the course and outcome of pregnancy.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (Maloprim) in pregnant women with reported outcome results including birth weight, parasitaemia, and haemoglobin.
population: pregnant women (primigravidae, multigravidae, and grandemultigravidae) in a rural area with limited access to antenatal clinics
primary_outcome: Effect of malaria chemoprophylaxis on parasitaemia, maternal packed cell volume/haemoglobin, and birth weight
impact_summary: Maloprim chemoprophylaxis given by traditional birth attendants reduced malaria parasitaemia, increased packed cell volume, and significantly increased birth weight in primigravidae (6% low birth weight vs 22% with placebo), with a smaller effect in multigravidae and a significant birth weight benefit in grandemultigravidae.
follow_up: pregnancy through delivery, over a 3-year enrollment period
transmission_setting: rural, malaria-endemic area of The Gambia
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; chemoprophylaxis administered by traditional birth attendants was feasible with high uptake (87% of pregnancies)

title: Lack of an association between acute gastroenteritis, acute respiratory infections and malaria in young Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT randomizing Gambian children to malaria chemoprophylaxis (Maloprim) versus control with reported outcome results on infection rates and mortality.
population: young Gambian children
primary_outcome: Incidence and mortality of acute gastroenteritis and acute respiratory infections
impact_summary: No evidence was found that malaria plays a direct or indirect role in causing acute gastrointestinal or respiratory infections in young Gambian children, as morbidity and mortality from these conditions were similar between the chemoprophylaxis-protected group and the more frequently infected group.
transmission_setting: holoendemic/seasonal malaria transmission in The Gambia
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; mortality from gastroenteritis and respiratory infections was similar between groups

title: [Comparative study of artemisinin suppositories and piperaquine phosphate in the treatment of falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhong xi yi jie he za zhi = Chinese journal of modern developments in traditional medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin suppositories versus piperaquine phosphate in falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate); primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans; Phase II is not early-phase.
population: adults with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and recrudescence rate by 28 days
impact_summary: Artemisinin suppositories cleared parasites faster than piperaquine phosphate but had a much higher recrudescence rate by 28 days.
safety_summary: No apparent side effects reported with artemisinin suppositories.

title: Impact of permethrin-treated bednets on malaria transmission by the Anopheles gambiae complex in The Gambia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated bed nets (vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results on malaria transmission reduction in humans.
population: villagers/children in rural hamlets
primary_outcome: Reduction in malaria transmission (biting rates, indoor resting densities, and probability of infective bite) by Anopheles gambiae complex
impact_summary: Permethrin-treated bednets reduced biting by An. gambiae s.s. by over 90% and substantially reduced the annual probability of a child receiving an infective bite compared with placebo-treated nets.
transmission_setting: low seasonal transmission, rainy season peak (September-October)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: The effectiveness of chemoprophylaxis against malaria for non-immune migrant workers in eastern Thailand.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria chemoprevention intervention (mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in humans.
population: non-immune migrant workers
primary_outcome: Suppression of P. falciparum and P. vivax parasitaemia
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was more effective than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone in suppressing malaria parasitaemia among non-immune migrant workers.
effect_estimate: MSP achieved complete suppression of P. falciparum vs 8 cases in SP group; 1 P. vivax case in MSP vs 4 in SP
safety_summary: Sulfadoxine-containing regimens, though efficacious, carry risk of complications from long-acting sulphonamides, some life threatening, requiring cautious use.

title: Trial of deltamethrin impregnated bed nets for the control of malaria transmitted by Anopheles sinensis and Anopheles anthropophagus.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of deltamethrin-impregnated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (malaria incidence reductions).
place: Buji district, Bao'an County, Guangdong Province, China
population: general population residing in Buji district, Bao'an County
primary_outcome: malaria incidence and indoor vector density
impact_summary: Deltamethrin-impregnated bed nets substantially reduced indoor vector density and malaria incidence compared to pretreatment levels.
effect_estimate: 74.6% (Jan-Jun) and 92.7% (Jul-Dec) in year two; 64.7% and 89% in subsequent years for expanded area
transmission_setting: endemic, seasonal transmission by exophilic An. sinensis and endophilic/anthropophilic An. anthropophagus

title: A comparative study of Lapudrine (chlorproguanil) and Maloprim (pyrimethamine and dapsone) as chemoprophylactics against malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chlorproguanil and pyrimethamine-dapsone) in Gambian children with reported outcome results including parasite rates, fever episodes, growth, and drug resistance.
population: children under 5 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of episodes of fever with malaria parasitaemia, spleen and parasite rates, packed cell volume, and growth
impact_summary: Maloprim significantly reduced malaria fever episodes and improved growth compared to placebo, while chlorproguanil did not, and both drugs reduced spleen and parasite rates without serious side effects.
effect_metric: resistance rate of P. falciparum to pyrimethamine and chlorproguanil
safety_summary: No serious side-effect attributable to either drug was observed.

title: Malaria prophylaxis with proguanil and sulfisoxazole in children living in a malaria endemic area.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (proguanil and sulfisoxazole) in children with reported outcome results (malaria cases and efficacy data).
population: children living in a malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria (P. falciparum and P. vivax) determined by weekly blood smears
impact_summary: Combined proguanil plus sulfisoxazole prophylaxis was superior to proguanil alone, sulfisoxazole alone, or vitamin control in preventing both P. falciparum and P. vivax malaria, with only one case of falciparum and no vivax malaria among 99 subjects over 1464 man-weeks.
effect_metric: number of malaria cases per man-weeks of observation
effect_estimate: 1 case of falciparum malaria among 99 subjects over 1464 man-weeks in combined regimen group
transmission_setting: malaria endemic area along the Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Side-effects were infrequent and generally mild; two subjects discontinued sulfisoxazole due to urticarial rash.

title: A combination of quinine, quinidine and cinchonine (LA 40221) in the treatment of chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand: two double-blind trials.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (quinine-based regimen) in humans with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum; phase not stated but treatment trials are eligible.
population: patients with chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure/response to treatment
impact_summary: LA 40221, a combination of quinine, quinidine and cinchonine, was effective in treating chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria in Thailand in two double-blind trials.

title: [Therapeutic effect of pyronaridine in plain tablets and enteric-coated tablets in falciparum malaria patients].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of pyronaridine for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (fever clearance, parasite clearance, cure rates); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention.
comparator: active comparator (pyronaridine enteric-coated tablets, current dosage regimen)
population: falciparum malaria patients
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and cure rate at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: The new reduced-dose plain tablet regimen of pyronaridine achieved similar fever and parasite clearance times and a higher cure rate (100% vs 93.8%) compared to the standard enteric-coated tablet regimen, despite a one-third lower total dose.
safety_summary: Undesirable responses occurred in 18.8% (6/32) of group A and 28.1% (9/32) of group B; reactions were mild, tolerable, and of short duration.

title: Clinical trial of fansimef in Indian patients of P. falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: This is a published randomized controlled trial of an antimalarial intervention (fansimef) in human malaria patients with reported clinical outcomes.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria

title: A comparative trial of three regimens for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Acre, Brazil.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (falciparum) with reported outcome results, not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (three different antimalarial regimens compared to each other)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment efficacy/cure rate for uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: The trial compared three treatment regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Acre, Brazil, but specific comparative efficacy results are not available from the provided information.

title: Comparison of the susceptibility of falciparum malaria to mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and chloroquine in Nigeria.
journal: African journal of medicine and medical sciences
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatment drugs in symptomatic falciparum malaria patients with reported outcome results (efficacy and safety).
population: children with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy and safety of mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine versus chloroquine in treating falciparum malaria
impact_summary: Fansimef (mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) was a rapidly acting blood schizontocide against Nigerian P. falciparum and was well tolerated, without the sinus bradycardia seen in Zambian trials.
safety_summary: Fansimef was well tolerated; sinus bradycardia observed in Zambian trials was not seen in Nigerian patients.

title: [Treatment of 75 patients with malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, in Porto Velho (Rondonia), with mefloquine].
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results of mefloquine treatment for P. falciparum malaria in humans.
population: patients with malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum

title: Comparison of mosquito nets, proguanil hydrochloride, and placebo to prevent malaria.
screening_reason: This is a completed RCT of malaria prevention interventions (mosquito nets and proguanil chemoprevention) with reported outcome results (new infections and attack rates).
comparator: placebo and active comparator (proguanil vs mosquito nets vs placebo)
population: boarding school students aged 6 to 18
primary_outcome: New malaria infection (asexual P. falciparum seen on blood films) during follow-up
impact_summary: Both mosquito nets and proguanil hydrochloride provided effective protection from malaria compared with placebo, with mosquito nets reducing attack rates by 97.3% and proguanil by 77.1%.
follow_up: one school term (~3893 days total person-time in mosquito net group)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area in the Rift Valley, Kenya

title: Sensitivity of Plasmodium falciparum to mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (Fansimef) in vivo and to mefloquine alone in vitro in Nigeria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine combination) versus chloroquine with reported outcome results in Nigerian children with falciparum malaria.
population: children with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy (blood schizontocidal activity) and safety/tolerability of Fansimef versus chloroquine
impact_summary: Fansimef (mefloquine-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) was an effective and well-tolerated blood schizontocide against the Nigerian strain of P. falciparum, with in vitro tests showing all 26 isolates susceptible to mefloquine, though some required higher than expected concentrations for complete inhibition.
transmission_setting: endemic, chloroquine still effective, no chloroquine resistance reported
safety_summary: Fansimef was well tolerated; sinus bradycardia, frequently seen with Fansimef in Zambian trials, was not observed in any Nigerian patients.

title: High-dose dexamethasone in quinine-treated patients with cerebral malaria: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing dexamethasone versus placebo in cerebral malaria treatment; not early-phase.
population: stuporous and comatose patients with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Time to become afebrile, level of consciousness returning to normal, clearance of parasitemia, incidence of complications, and mortality
impact_summary: High-dose dexamethasone did not improve outcomes compared to placebo in quinine-treated cerebral malaria patients and is not indicated for treatment.
safety_summary: No significant differences in incidence of complications between dexamethasone and placebo groups; mortality was 21% in both groups.

title: Efficacy of multiple-dose halofantrine in treatment of chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria in children in Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of halofantrine for treatment of chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (parasite clearance times).
population: children with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Multiple-dose halofantrine rapidly cleared chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria parasites in Kenyan children, with mean parasite clearance times of 45.4 h and 54.8 h for the two dosing regimens.
effect_estimate: 45.4 h (10 mg/kg x2) and 54.8 h (8 mg/kg x3)

title: Single dose phenobarbitone prevents convulsions in cerebral malaria.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (seizure prevention in cerebral malaria) in humans.
population: patients over 6 years of age with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence of subsequent convulsions
impact_summary: A single intramuscular injection of phenobarbitone significantly reduced the incidence of subsequent convulsions in cerebral malaria patients from 54% to 12.5%, without adverse effects.
safety_summary: No adverse effects observed with phenobarbitone.

title: Falciparum malaria and pregnancy: relationship and treatment response.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing quinine vs amodiaquine for falciparum malaria treatment in pregnant and non-pregnant women with reported outcomes (fever clearance, parasite clearance, treatment effectiveness).
population: pregnant women with falciparum malaria and age-matched non-pregnant female patients
primary_outcome: Fever clearance and parasite clearance times, and treatment efficacy between quinine and amodiaquine
impact_summary: Quinine and amodiaquine were equally effective in treating falciparum malaria, with no significant differences in parasite density, fever clearance, or parasite clearance between pregnant and non-pregnant patients or by parity/gestational period.
transmission_setting: endemic region of Shan States, Burma
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; severely ill cases were treated with quinine due to safety considerations in severe malaria.

title: The effects of antimalarials and folate supplements on haematological indices and red cell folate levels in Gambian children.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis (Maloprim, chlorproguanil) in children with reported outcome results (haematological indices and red cell folate levels).
population: children aged 3 months-5 years
primary_outcome: Haematological indices and red cell folate levels
impact_summary: Among children receiving folate supplements, chlorproguanil was associated with significantly lower mean red cell folate levels compared to controls, while Maloprim showed no such difference.
effect_estimate: lower in chlorproguanil + folate group vs controls
safety_summary: No significant differences in RCF levels among non-supplemented children; chlorproguanil at adult dose associated with lower RCF in supplemented children, suggesting need for age-related dosing.

title: Amodiaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine as treatment for chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum in Rwanda.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance at 7 days).
population: children aged 5 years or younger with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum parasitemia
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance (aparasitemia) 7 days after treatment initiation
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine cleared parasitemia in 100% of children by day 7, compared to 76% with amodiaquine.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Parasitologic and clinical efficacy of 25 and 50 mg/kg of chloroquine for treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Rwandan children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two chloroquine doses for P. falciparum malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (parasitologic and clinical efficacy).
comparator: active comparator (25 mg/kg chloroquine vs 50 mg/kg chloroquine)
population: children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria aged ≤5 years
primary_outcome: Parasitologic and clinical efficacy (parasitemia clearance and fever resolution) at day 14
impact_summary: Both 25 mg/kg and 50 mg/kg chloroquine regimens showed similar high rates of persistent parasitemia at day 14, though parasite density decreased substantially in both groups, with minimal side effects.
safety_summary: Side effects were found to be minimal in both treatment groups.

title: Malaria prophylaxis with proguanil in children living in a malaria-endemic area.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (proguanil vs chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results (malaria cases, failure rates).
population: children living in a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of falciparum and vivax malaria cases while on prophylaxis
impact_summary: No significant difference in falciparum malaria prevention between daily proguanil and weekly chloroquine, but proguanil was associated with significantly more vivax malaria prophylactic failures.
effect_estimate: 17 falciparum and 11 vivax cases with proguanil vs 24 falciparum and 1 vivax case with chloroquine
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area along the Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Side effects were infrequent, mild, and comparable in both groups.

title: Studies on malaria prophylaxis with chlorproguanil or chloroquine in Mozambique.
journal: The Central African journal of medicine
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis (chlorproguanil/chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results.
primary_outcome: Malaria prophylaxis/incidence of malaria infection
impact_summary: The trial compared chlorproguanil and chloroquine for malaria prophylaxis in Mozambique but specific comparative efficacy results are not detailed in the available information.

title: Sensitivity of Plasmodium falciparum to chloroquine, amodiaquine and mefloquine in Ibadan, Nigeria.
journal: African journal of medicine and medical sciences
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drug efficacy with reported outcome results (parasite clearance time and cure rates) in malaria treatment.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and cure rate by day 14
impact_summary: Chloroquine and amodiaquine showed similar efficacy with no significant difference in parasite clearance time, and both achieved a 100% cure rate up to day 14; in vitro, isolates were equally sensitive to chloroquine and mefloquine.
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported

title: Malaria: treatment efficacy of halofantrine (WR 171,669) in initial field trials in Thailand.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (halofantrine vs mefloquine) with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasite clearance, fever clearance, adverse effects).
population: Patients infected with Plasmodium falciparum malaria on the Thai-Kampuchean border
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological clearance) following treatment
impact_summary: Halofantrine given as a 3-dose regimen achieved cure rates comparable to mefloquine in multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria, with no significant difference between regimens.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum endemic area, Thai-Kampuchean border
safety_summary: Post-dosing side-effects with halofantrine included nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea, not significantly different from mefloquine.

title: Evaluation of four therapeutic regimens for falciparum malaria in Mozambique, 1986.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (four therapeutic regimens for P. falciparum) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance/cure rates).
comparator: active comparator (chloroquine vs amodiaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs amodiaquine+sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: asymptomatic schoolchildren
primary_outcome: In vivo parasitological cure rate / resistance to treatment for P. falciparum parasitaemia
impact_summary: Chloroquine and amodiaquine showed high rates of resistance (94% and 76% respectively), while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone or combined with amodiaquine achieved much higher cure rates, with the combination reaching 100% cure though not significantly better than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.
p_value: not significant (difference between combination and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone)

title: Double-blind dose finding study of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children with acute falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combination) in children with acute falciparum malaria.
population: children with acute uncomplicated chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy (radical cure) and tolerance of three dose levels of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: All three tested doses of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine achieved radical cure with only mild to moderate side effects, supporting a single dose of approximately mefloquine 10 mg/kg as safe and effective treatment.
safety_summary: Mild to moderate side effects of nausea and vomiting occurred, with no worsening in higher dose groups.

title: [Efficacy of amodiaquine, Fansidar and their combination in the treatment of chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial treatments (amodiaquine, Fansidar, combination) with reported efficacy outcomes in chloroquine-resistant malaria.
population: patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria
impact_summary: [Efficacy of amodiaquine, Fansidar and their combination in the treatment of chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria].

title: [Effects of combined dose of pyronaridine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine on falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (pyronaridine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination) in humans.
population: patients with falciparum malaria

title: The effect of mefloquine-artemether compared with quinine on patients with complicated falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two malaria treatments (mefloquine-artemether vs quinine) in complicated falciparum malaria patients with reported outcome results including survival, parasite clearance, and fever clearance.
population: patients with complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (with anaemia, hyperpyrexia, jaundice or more than 5% of erythrocytes parasitized), excluding cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus artemether resulted in significantly shorter parasite and fever clearance times than quinine, with all patients surviving in the mefloquine-artemether group compared to 2 deaths in the quinine group.
effect_metric: parasite clearance time and fever clearance time
safety_summary: All patients treated with mefloquine plus artemether survived; 2 patients treated with quinine died; no recrudescence occurred in either group.

title: Chlorproguanil/dapsone for the treatment of non-severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kenya: a pilot study.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing chlorproguanil/dapsone versus pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance and recurrence rates).
population: children with asymptomatic P. falciparum infections
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure and recurrence of parasitaemia on days 7, 14, 21, and 28
impact_summary: Chlorproguanil/dapsone cleared parasitaemia by day 7 in all children but had a higher rate of recurrence by days 14-28 compared to pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine, though both were effective treatments.
safety_summary: No change in haematocrit or haemoglobin during follow-up in either group

title: A trial of bed nets (mosquito nets) as a malaria control strategy in a rural area of The Gambia, West Africa.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results; phase not applicable for cluster-randomized trials.
population: children aged 1-9 years in rural Fula hamlets
primary_outcome: incidence of febrile episodes with associated malaria parasitaemia during the rainy season; prevalence of splenomegaly and parasitaemia at end of rainy season
impact_summary: Bed nets were not effective in reducing malaria morbidity, with no significant difference in clinical malaria attacks or other malariometric measures between children using bed nets and those who did not.
effect_metric: difference in incidence of clinical malaria attacks
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; bed nets were used correctly but some children left nets during the night.

title: Chloroquine and quinine: a randomized, double-blind comparison of efficacy and side effects in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in the Philippines.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs quinine) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, fever duration, side effects).
population: adult Filipino males with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time / rate of asexual parasitaemia clearance
impact_summary: Chloroquine and quinine had comparable clinical efficacy and side effect profiles, though in vitro testing showed most chloroquine-group isolates were resistant to chloroquine while quinine-group isolates were sensitive to quinine.
safety_summary: 40% of patients in each treatment group experienced mild side effects; no serious adverse events reported.

title: Permethrin-treated bed nets (mosquito nets) prevent malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) that reports outcome results (clinical malaria incidence, spleen size, packed cell volume) in children.
population: Gambian children
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical attacks of malaria
impact_summary: Children who slept under permethrin-treated bed nets had significantly fewer clinical attacks of malaria than those with placebo-treated nets, with additional benefits in spleen size and packed cell volume.
transmission_setting: seasonal, low to moderate intensity transmission
safety_summary: No side effects were noted.

title: Tolerability of long-term malaria prophylaxis with the combination mefloquine + sulfadoxine + pyrimethamine (Fansimef): results of a double blind field trial versus chloroquine in Nigeria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (prevention) with reported outcome results on tolerability and adverse effects.
population: Austrian industrial workers and their families
primary_outcome: Tolerability/adverse effects of long-term malaria chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Fansimef (mefloquine + sulfadoxine + pyrimethamine) had more adverse effects leading to discontinuation than chloroquine, with only one malaria case occurring after stopping prophylaxis.
effect_metric: number of discontinuations due to adverse effects
safety_summary: Adverse effects (insomnia, palpitations, dizziness, nausea, headache) led to discontinuation in 7 Fansimef recipients vs 2 chloroquine recipients (headache, hair loss, nausea, dizziness, vomiting); transient, clinically irrelevant elevations of liver enzymes (SGOT, GGT) at month 3 in Fansimef group.

title: Field trial of the effectiveness of indoor-spraying with pirimiphos-methyl emulsion for malaria control in a tribal area of Phulbani district, Orissa State, India.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of indoor residual spraying (IRS) with pirimiphos-methyl versus DDT for malaria vector control that reported outcome results including malariological indices and vector densities.
population: residents of two adjacent sections of Nuagaon Primary Health Centre, Phulbani district
primary_outcome: malariological indices (slide positivity rate, slide falciparum rate, annual parasite incidence) and vector density reduction
impact_summary: Indoor-spraying with pirimiphos-methyl emulsion reduced malariological indices by 65-68%, compared with only 26-35% reduction in the DDT-sprayed area, and reduced vector densities 2-35-fold more than DDT.
transmission_setting: tribal, endemic, rural area of Orissa State, India
safety_summary: Spraymen and villagers experienced no adverse side-effects from residual house-spraying with pirimiphos-methyl emulsion.

title: The effect of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs quinine on patients with complicated falciparum malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs quinine) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, treatment resistance) in humans with complicated falciparum malaria.
population: patients with complicated falciparum malaria (anaemia, hyperpyrexia, jaundice, or >2% parasitised RBCs), excluding cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment resulted in significantly shorter parasite clearance times than quinine, with all patients surviving and no difference in fever clearance time.
safety_summary: All patients survived; resistance noted with 1 patient resistant to MSP at RII level and 5 at RI level, and 3 patients resistant to quinine at RI level.

title: Doxycycline prophylaxis for falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing doxycycline vs chloroquine for malaria prevention (chemoprevention) in humans; not early-phase.
population: schoolchildren aged 10-15 living in a malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: Incidence of falciparum malaria infection detected by weekly blood smears
impact_summary: Doxycycline prophylaxis was significantly more effective than chloroquine at preventing falciparum malaria infections.
effect_estimate: 5 cases in doxycycline group vs 31 in chloroquine group
transmission_setting: malaria endemic area along Thai-Burmese border
safety_summary: Doxycycline group did not have significantly more side-effects than the chloroquine group.

title: Inadequacy of chlorproguanil 20 mg per week as chemoprophylaxis for falciparum malaria in Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention intervention with reported outcome results (P. falciparum attack rates and resistance patterns).
population: school children aged 6 to 10 years living near the Kenyan coast, previously treated with chloroquine and pyrimethamine/sulfadoxine
primary_outcome: Attack rate of Plasmodium falciparum infection during 20 weeks of chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Chlorproguanil 20 mg weekly reduced but did not adequately prevent P. falciparum infection compared to placebo, and resistance to dihydrofolate-reductase inhibitors emerged frequently in the chlorproguanil group.
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; main issue was inadequate efficacy due to drug resistance rather than adverse events

title: Amodiaquine less effective than chloroquine in the treatment of falciparum malaria in the Philippines.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) for falciparum malaria with reported outcome results on parasitemia clearance and drug resistance.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: clearance of parasitemia / drug resistance (RI-RIII) following treatment
impact_summary: Amodiaquine was significantly less effective than chloroquine in clearing Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia in both hospital and village-based patient groups.
effect_estimate: 6/8 amodiaquine vs 0/8 chloroquine (hospital); 5/5 amodiaquine vs 1/6 chloroquine (village)
follow_up: not specified beyond day 6 and later recrudescence assessment
transmission_setting: endemic, village and hospital settings in the Philippines

title: Double-blind trial to find dose range using a fixed combination of mefloquine, sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine in falciparum malaria: a field study on adults in Burma.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine fixed combination) in adults with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, adverse events).
population: semi-immune adults weighing less than 60 kg with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time
impact_summary: A single dose of 2 tablets of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (Fansimef) was as effective as 3 tablets for treating falciparum malaria in semi-immune adults, with faster clearance and fewer side effects including no vomiting.
safety_summary: Drugs generally well tolerated; mild transient giddiness in 80% (2-tablet group) and 96% (3-tablet group); nausea in 33% and 43% respectively; no vomiting in 2-tablet group but 8 patients vomited in 3-tablet group (P<0.01).

title: The use of immunofluorescence to evaluate the efficacy of malarial chemoprophylaxis.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (chemoprevention) in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia and serological response at 5 and 12 months).
population: subjects occupationally exposed to high levels of malaria transmission
primary_outcome: Efficacy of malarial chemoprophylaxis assessed via slide positivity rate and geometric mean reciprocal antibody titre using immunofluorescence
impact_summary: The study compared three chemoprophylaxis regimens using serological (immunofluorescence) and parasitological (blood film) methods to assess efficacy against malaria over 12 months.

title: [Combined use of pyronaridine, sulfadoxine and primaquine in areas with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria].
journal: Zhongguo ji sheng chong xue yu ji sheng chong bing za zhi = Chinese journal of parasitology & parasitic diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial reporting outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (drug combination) in humans.
population: patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria

title: A trial of permethrin-treated bed nets in the prevention of malaria in Gambian children.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of permethrin-treated bed nets (vector-control intervention) for malaria prevention in humans with reported outcome results (clinical malaria episodes, splenomegaly, parasitaemia).
population: children in a rural area
primary_outcome: episodes of clinical malaria
impact_summary: Children who slept under permethrin-treated bed nets had significantly fewer episodes of clinical malaria than control children, but no significant difference in splenomegaly, parasitaemia, or PCV was found at the end of the rains.
effect_metric: reduction in episodes of clinical malaria
safety_summary: Permethrin treatment of bed nets was well accepted and was without side-effects.

title: A controlled clinical trial of artemether (qinghaosu derivative) versus quinine in complicated and severe falciparum malaria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (artemether vs quinine) in severe falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (mortality, parasite clearance, recrudescence).
population: patients with complicated/severe falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Fever clearance time and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Artemether cleared fever and parasites faster than quinine and had lower mortality, though recrudescence rate was higher with artemether than quinine.
safety_summary: All artemether-treated patients survived; 2 of the quinine-treated patients died.

title: Double-blind study to assess the efficacy of chlorproguanil given alone or in combination with chloroquine for malaria chemoprophylaxis in an area with Plasmodium falciparum resistance to chloroquine, pyrimethamine and cycloguanil.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis (primary prevention intervention) with reported outcome results (breakthrough infection rates at 17 weeks).
comparator: chloroquine alone vs chlorproguanil alone vs combination of chlorproguanil and chloroquine
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Rate of malaria breakthrough (parasitological failure) during chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: None of the chemoprophylactic regimens (chlorproguanil, chloroquine, or their combination) effectively prevented malaria, with high breakthrough rates in all groups and no significant benefit from combination therapy.
transmission_setting: Rice field area with high chloroquine and pyrimethamine/cycloguanil resistance

title: Reduction in incidence and prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum in under-5-year-old children by permethrin impregnation of mosquito nets.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
