screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector-control intervention (permethrin-impregnated nets) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results on P. falciparum incidence and prevalence.
design: cluster-randomized, controlled field trial with paired villages
population: children under 10 years old (0-4 and 5-9 year age groups)
primary_outcome: Incidence and prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum in children after permethrin impregnation of mosquito nets
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated mosquito nets significantly reduced the incidence and prevalence of P. falciparum among children aged 0-4 years, but had no effect on P. falciparum in 5-9 year olds or on P. vivax in either age group.
effect_metric: reduction in incidence of P. falciparum
transmission_setting: holoendemic malaria transmission area near Madang, Papua New Guinea
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Slow-release quinidine in the treatment of chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria: a double-blind trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind randomized controlled trial testing a malaria treatment intervention (quinidine for chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum) with reported outcome results.
population: patients with chloroquine resistant falciparum malaria

title: A double-blind trial of a fixed combination of mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine compared with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone in symptomatic falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Published double-blind RCT of mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for treatment of symptomatic falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure, parasitemia clearance, adverse events).
population: male patients with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: cure rate and clearance of parasitaemia and fever
impact_summary: Both mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (Fansimef) and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone (Fansidar) cured all patients with similar parasite clearance rates, though fever clearance was marginally faster and orthostatic hypotension less frequent with Fansimef.
safety_summary: Side-effects (pruritus, diarrhoea, abdominal pain) were mild and transient in both groups; severe orthostatic hypotension occurred in 20% of Fansidar patients versus 2% of Fansimef patients, reversed by bed rest; no undesirable changes in haematological or biochemical parameters.

title: Mefloquine, sulfadoxine, and pyrimethamine in the treatment of symptomatic falciparum malaria: a double-blind trial for determining the most effective dose.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (cure rates, parasitaemia clearance, safety data).
comparator: active comparator (two-tablet vs three-tablet MSP dose)
population: adult male patients with acute, uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (S response) following treatment with mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
impact_summary: The three-tablet MSP regimen achieved a slightly higher cure rate (98%) than the two-tablet regimen (93%), with faster parasite clearance, though differences were not statistically significant.
safety_summary: Tolerance was good at both dose levels; mild transient side-effects included abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and diarrhoea; no drug-related haematological, biochemical, or urinalysis changes; some ECGs showed transient, symptomless sinus bradycardia or arrhythmia.

title: A phase II/III double-blind, dose-finding clinical trial of a combination of mefloquine, sulfadoxine, and pyrimethamine (Fansimef) in falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination) with reported outcome results showing cure rates and safety outcomes.
comparator: active comparator (different dose levels of Fansimef: one, two, or three tablets)
population: adult male patients with peripheral blood smears positive for Plasmodium falciparum, with or without clinical symptoms
primary_outcome: Cure rate (parasitological cure) and rates of initial clearance of parasitaemia and fever across different Fansimef dose levels
impact_summary: Higher doses of Fansimef (two or three tablets) cured all patients, while the one-tablet dose cured only 81%, with 19% experiencing RI recrudescences.
safety_summary: Tolerance was good at all dose levels; main side-effects included nausea, vomiting, dizziness, diarrhoea and abdominal pain, which were mild and transient; vomiting and nausea incidence was highest with the three-tablet dose; no adverse effects on haematological, biochemical or urine analyses.

title: Village scale trial of the impact of deltamethrin (K-othrine) spraying in areas with DDT and HCH resistant Anopheles culicifacies.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a vector-control intervention (IRS with deltamethrin) in malaria-endemic areas with reported outcome results on malaria transmission.
population: village residents in areas with DDT and HCH resistant Anopheles culicifacies
primary_outcome: impact of deltamethrin spraying on malaria transmission/vector density
impact_summary: Deltamethrin (K-othrine) spraying reduced malaria transmission in villages with DDT and HCH resistant Anopheles culicifacies vectors.
transmission_setting: areas with DDT and HCH resistant Anopheles culicifacies

title: Divided dose intramuscular regimen and single dose subcutaneous regimen for chloroquine: plasma concentrations and toxicity in patients with malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of chloroquine treatment regimens in malaria patients with reported outcome results on plasma concentrations and toxicity.
comparator: active comparator (divided dose intramuscular chloroquine vs single dose subcutaneous chloroquine)
population: adults with malaria
primary_outcome: plasma chloroquine concentrations and toxicity (hypotension, neurotoxicity)
impact_summary: Both intramuscular divided-dose and subcutaneous single-dose parenteral chloroquine regimens produced satisfactory plasma concentrations and were well tolerated without causing hypotension or neurotoxicity in adults.
effect_estimate: 0.5 mg/l (IM) vs 0.3 mg/l (SC) in first 12 hours
p_value: p less than 0.05 for peak concentration and time to peak; p greater than 0.1 for AUC
safety_summary: No hypotension or neurotoxicity observed with either regimen; chloroquine resistance found in the one P. falciparum case.

title: The prevention of anaemia in pregnancy in primigravidae in the guinea savanna of Nigeria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial prophylaxis (proguanil) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria prevention and anaemia.
comparator: no active treatment (placebo/control group) versus chloroquine plus proguanil with or without iron and/or folic acid
population: Hausa primigravidae (first-pregnancy women) attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Development of anaemia (haemoglobin and packed cell volume) during pregnancy and postpartum
impact_summary: Antimalarial prophylaxis combined with iron supplementation substantially reduced the incidence of severe and postpartum anaemia compared with no active treatment, while folic acid alone had no significant effect on mean haemoglobin.
effect_metric: proportion with severe anaemia requiring removal from trial
effect_estimate: 7/40 in control group vs 5/160 in treated groups
transmission_setting: guinea savanna region, endemic malaria area of Nigeria
safety_summary: Severe anaemia occurred in 7 of the untreated group requiring removal from the trial, versus only 5 in the treated groups; no other major adverse effects reported; perinatal death rate 11% with no significant group differences.

title: Monthly antimalarial chemotherapy to children in a holoendemic area of Liberia.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial chemoprevention (chloroquine, chlorproguanil, pyrimethamine) in children with reported outcome results including parasite rates, splenomegaly, fever episodes, and haematocrit levels.
design: prospective, community-based, non-randomized comparative trial (village-level allocation), three-year study
comparator: placebo (vitamin tablets) and pyrimethamine, chlorproguanil, untreated village
population: children aged 2 to 9 years in a holoendemic malaria area
primary_outcome: malariometric indices including parasite rate, spleen rate, fever episodes, haematocrit, and total IgG concentration over two years of monthly chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Monthly chloroquine (and to a lesser extent chlorproguanil) reduced parasite rates, spleen rates, fever episodes and improved haematocrit compared to placebo, while pyrimethamine showed no benefit over placebo.
safety_summary: No apparent impairment of protective immunity to malaria was observed from two years of regular drug distribution; no other adverse events reported.

title: Treatment of falciparum malaria with quinne and tetracycline or combined mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine on the Thai-Kampuchean border.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three treatment regimens for falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (radical cure rates and treatment failures).
population: displaced Kampucheans with falciparum malaria living in border encampments
primary_outcome: radical cure rate (absence of parasite recrudescence by day 35)
impact_summary: Single-dose mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine achieved a higher radical cure rate (98%) than 3-day quinine plus 7-day tetracycline (76%), while 7-day quinine plus 7-day tetracycline achieved 92%, with MSP also clearing parasites faster.
safety_summary: Little difference in side effects between regimens; tolerance was good.

title: Iron supplementation increases prevalence and effects of malaria: report on clinical studies in Papua New Guinea.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on iron supplementation and malaria prevalence in infants; malaria is the primary focus of analysis.
population: two-month-old infants
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria (parasite and spleen rates) and haemoglobin levels at 6- and 12-month follow-up
impact_summary: Infants who received iron dextran prophylaxis had higher malaria prevalence and lower haemoglobin during malaria infection compared to placebo, suggesting iron deficiency protects against malaria.
effect_metric: prevalence of malaria (parasite and spleen rates)
effect_estimate: higher in iron dextran group vs placebo
age_range: 2 months at enrollment, followed to 12 months
safety_summary: No apparent suppression of marrow activity in either group in presence of malaria; iron dextran group had greater reticulocytosis and lower haemoglobin with malaria infection compared to placebo

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine in young Nigerian children. III. Its effect on nutrition.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results on nutrition and mortality.
population: young children
primary_outcome: Nutritional status (growth, malnutrition episodes, deaths from malnutrition, serum albumin/pre-albumin)
impact_summary: Children who received weekly chloroquine chemoprophylaxis had fewer episodes of severe malnutrition and fewer malnutrition deaths, and tended to be taller, heavier, and have higher serum albumin/pre-albumin than control children, though differences were mostly small and not statistically significant.
follow_up: first one or two years of life
age_range: infants and young children (first one to two years of life)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; focus was on nutritional outcomes rather than adverse events.

title: A comparative clinical study of mefloquine and chloroquine in the treatment of vivax malaria.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (mefloquine vs chloroquine for vivax malaria) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, fever clearance, clinical response).
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance time, fever clearance time, and clearance time of signs and symptoms
impact_summary: Mefloquine at single doses of 250 mg or 500 mg was as effective as the standard 3-day chloroquine regimen in treating vivax malaria, with no statistically significant differences between groups.

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine in young Nigerian children. I. Its effect on mortality, morbidity and the prevalence of malaria.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results on mortality, morbidity, and parasitemia.
population: young Nigerian children followed from shortly after birth to age one or two years
primary_outcome: Effect of chloroquine chemoprophylaxis on mortality, morbidity, and prevalence of malaria parasitemia
impact_summary: Weekly chloroquine chemoprophylaxis reduced clinical malaria and parasitemia prevalence compared to controls but had no significant effect on mortality, and no rebound in mortality or morbidity occurred after stopping prophylaxis.
effect_metric: Prevalence of positive blood films for P. falciparum
safety_summary: Mortality was similar among protected and control children; no rebound mortality or morbidity was observed after chemoprophylaxis was stopped.

title: Malaria chemoprophylaxis with chloroquine in young Nigerian children. IV. Its effect on haematological measurements.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results (haematological measurements).
population: young Nigerian children
primary_outcome: Haematological measurements (haemoglobin, packed cell volume, red cell abnormalities, white blood cell counts, plasma folate, serum ferritin, red cell folate)
impact_summary: Children given weekly chloroquine chemoprophylaxis had higher haemoglobin and packed cell volume and fewer red cell abnormalities than control children, though red cell folate was paradoxically higher in malaria-exposed children.

title: RII and RIII type resistance of Plasmodium falciparum to combination of mefloquine and sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in Indonesia.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing mefloquine-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination versus sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine for malaria treatment with reported in vivo resistance outcomes.
population: Patients with Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: In vivo resistance (RII/RIII) to mefloquine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combination versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone
impact_summary: The combination of mefloquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed no clinical advantage over sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone and may even have a disadvantage, with 2 of 36 infections resistant to the combination and 2 of 41 resistant to SP alone.
transmission_setting: Endemic malaria area of Irian Jaya, Indonesia
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; expected absorption of mefloquine and pyrimethamine confirmed in one resistant patient.

title: Combination of mefloquine with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine compared with two sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combinations in malaria chemoprophylaxis.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing mefloquine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combination with alternative sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combinations for malaria chemoprophylaxis (prevention), with outcome results reported.
primary_outcome: malaria chemoprophylaxis efficacy
impact_summary: The combination of mefloquine with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was compared with two sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine combinations for malaria chemoprophylaxis, but specific results are not provided in the available information.

title: A clinical trial of mefloquine in the treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates); no early-phase limitations noted.
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: clinical and parasitological cure
impact_summary: All patients treated with mefloquine, chloroquine, or chloroquine plus primaquine responded rapidly and were cured.
safety_summary: No significant side effects reported.

title: Trials of mefloquine in vivax and of mefloquine plus 'fansidar' in falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trials comparing mefloquine treatments for malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
comparator: chloroquine (for P. vivax trial); mefloquine-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (MSP) (for P. falciparum trial)
population: patients with P. vivax malaria (n=40) and patients with P. falciparum malaria (n=40)
primary_outcome: Clinical and parasitological response (parasite clearance and symptom relief) to treatment
impact_summary: Mefloquine was as effective as chloroquine in treating P. vivax malaria and as effective as mefloquine-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine in treating P. falciparum malaria, with treatment failures largely attributed to vomiting and low plasma drug levels rather than drug resistance.
effect_estimate: 2/4 failures in mefloquine group, 2/3 failures in MSP group (falciparum trial)
safety_summary: No side-effects or laboratory abnormalities in the vivax trial; in the falciparum trial, 5 patients in each group had side-effects including vomiting, skin rash, diarrhoea, and transient mental confusion; mefloquine was well tolerated by patients with G6PD deficiency or heterozygous haemoglobin E.

title: Prospective double-blind trial of two different doses of mefloquine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine compared with pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine alone in the treatment of falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine-based treatment for falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (cure rates at 28 days); malaria treatment is the primary intervention.
population: adult male patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria from regions with high antimalarial resistance
primary_outcome: Cure rate within 28-day follow-up period
impact_summary: Both mefloquine-containing combinations achieved a 100% cure rate compared to 75% with pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine alone.
transmission_setting: Non-endemic area (Medellín, Colombia, no local malaria transmission); patients acquired infection in regions with high antimalarial resistance
safety_summary: Drug tolerance was good and no toxic effects were demonstrated in blood and urine examinations.

title: An open, randomized, phase III clinical trial of mefloquine and of quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in the treatment of symptomatic falciparum malaria in Brazil.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine versus quinine-sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: adult male patients with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitological cure rate ('S' response) and clearance of parasitaemia and fever
impact_summary: Mefloquine achieved a 100% parasitological cure rate compared to 92% for quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with similar clearance rates and good tolerance in both groups.
transmission_setting: area with increasing P. falciparum resistance to quinine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
safety_summary: Tolerance was good in both groups; main side-effects (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dizziness) were mild and transient; nausea/vomiting more frequent with quinine+SP, abdominal pain/loose stools more frequent with mefloquine; tinnitus and hearing difficulty observed only with quinine+SP; no adverse effects on haematological/biochemical parameters.

title: A double-blind clinical trial of a combination of mefloquine, sulfadoxine and pyrimethamine in symptomatic falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of malaria treatment (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine) in symptomatic P. falciparum patients with reported outcome results (parasitaemia clearance, fever clearance, tolerability).
population: adult male patients with symptomatic Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Clearance of parasitaemia and fever (S-type response)
impact_summary: All three dose groups of Fansimef (mefloquine/sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine combination) achieved similar S-type parasitological and clinical response rates with good tolerance.
safety_summary: Tolerance was good at all dose levels; mild, transient side-effects included abdominal discomfort, weakness, lassitude, dizziness, and pruritus; vomiting occurred in 4% of patients at the highest dose; no adverse changes in haematological, biochemical, or urinalysis results.

title: Randomised comparative study of mefloquine, qinghaosu, and pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine in patients with falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (parasite clearance, recrudescence, cure rates) testing malaria treatment interventions in humans.
population: patients with chloroquine-resistant falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance rate and recrudescence rate
impact_summary: Mefloquine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine achieved radical cure with slight side-effects, adding qinghaosu increased parasite clearance rate without additional side-effects, while qinghaosu alone cleared parasites rapidly but had a high recrudescence rate.
safety_summary: Mefloquine plus fansidar caused slight side-effects; addition of qinghaosu did not increase side-effects; qinghaosu alone had no side-effects.

title: Tolerability of long-term prophylaxis with fansidar: a randomized double-blind study in Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized double-blind trial comparing malaria chemoprophylaxis regimens with reported safety and efficacy outcome results in humans.
population: Austrian industrial workers in Nigeria
primary_outcome: Tolerability/side effects of long-term chemoprophylaxis (clinical complaints and laboratory abnormalities)
impact_summary: Both Fansidar and chloroquine were well tolerated for long-term malaria prophylaxis, with only minor, mostly self-limited side effects and no signs of drug-associated liver damage, though minor statistically significant but clinically insignificant hematological changes occurred in each group.
safety_summary: Few complaints reported; gastrointestinal disorders predominated in Fansidar group (3 cases) and insomnia in chloroquine group (3 cases); one case each of skin rash and visual disturbance in both groups; one case of facial erythema after alcohol in Fansidar group; one case of hair loss in chloroquine group; no signs of drug-associated liver damage; slight transient decrease in red cell count (Fansidar) and white cell count (chloroquine), statistically significant but clinically insignificant; no leucopenia in Fansidar group.

title: Field village scale trial of use of repellent in malaria control.
screening_reason: Published RCT of a vector-control intervention (spatial repellent) for malaria prevention with reported outcome results.
population: village residents
primary_outcome: malaria incidence/infection rates
impact_summary: Use of repellent in villages reduced malaria transmission compared to control villages.

title: Is the working capacity of Liberian industrial workers increased by regular malaria prophylaxis?
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing malaria prophylaxis versus control in humans, with primary focus on a malaria prevention intervention.
population: industrial workers (men)
primary_outcome: physical working capacity (work load at heart rate 170 measured by bicycle ergometry)
impact_summary: No significant differences in haemoglobin, haematocrit, blood volume or physical working capacity were found between industrial workers given regular malaria prophylaxis and those not given prophylaxis.

title: Comparative drug trial of a sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and a sulfalene/pyrimethamine combination against Plasmodium falciparum infections in semi-immune populations of Burma.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine vs sulfalene/pyrimethamine) for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance and recrudescence rates).
population: semi-immune population with falciparum malaria, including children and adults
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate on Day 7 after treatment
impact_summary: Both sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine and sulfalene/pyrimethamine combinations were equally effective in clearing falciparum parasites, but sulfalene/pyrimethamine had a significantly higher early recrudescence rate within one month.
transmission_setting: semi-immune population, area with efficient malaria vectors
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; combinations noted to stimulate gametocyte production, raising transmission concerns; gametocytocide (primaquine) recommended as co-administration.

title: Amodiaquine more effective than chloroquine against Plasmodium falciparum malaria on Kenya coast.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results comparing two antimalarial drugs (amodiaquine vs chloroquine) for P. falciparum treatment in humans.
population: children with symptomatic P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: treatment outcome/parasitological or clinical response to therapy
impact_summary: Amodiaquine was more effective than chloroquine in treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria on the Kenya coast.

title: Malaria control with residual fenitrothion in Central Java, Indonesia: an operational-scale trial using both full and selective coverage treatments.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control (residual insecticide spraying) with reported outcome results on malaria rates and vector populations; phase not applicable for operational/vector-control trials.
design: operational-scale trial, non-randomized comparison of full versus selective coverage treatments
comparator: selective coverage treatment vs full coverage treatment; also comparison of dosage 1 g/m2 vs 2 g/m2
population: general population residing in the two study areas
primary_outcome: malaria rates and vector (mosquito) population reduction
impact_summary: Both full and selective coverage residual fenitrothion spraying reduced malaria rates and vector populations to very low levels, with full coverage acting more rapidly and reducing the P. falciparum index more, while selective coverage was 68% cheaper and caused less cholinesterase depression among spraymen.
follow_up: 3 spray cycles at 6-monthly intervals (approximately 18 months) over 1980-1982
transmission_setting: endemic malaria area in Central Java, Indonesia treated with residual insecticide spraying
safety_summary: Selective coverage greatly reduced the degree of cholinesterase depression among spraymen compared to full coverage.

title: Treatment of quinine resistant falciparum malaria in Thai children.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine regimens) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates); not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (standard quinine dosage vs modified quinine dosage vs quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: children with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate of falciparum malaria at day 7 following treatment
impact_summary: Cure rates were 75%, 87%, and 62% in the three quinine regimen groups respectively, with no statistically significant difference between groups, and no additional benefit from adding sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine to quinine.
follow_up: 7 days treatment course with follow-up during treatment
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy and serum quinine levels rather than adverse events.

title: A phase II clinical trial of mefloquine in Brazilian male subjects.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Published RCT of mefloquine for malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcomes; Phase II is acceptable.
population: adult male oligosymptomatic and symptomatic volunteers with P. falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance/efficacy within 7 days
impact_summary: Mefloquine was 100% successful in clearing P. falciparum parasitaemia within 7 days with no recrudescences, whereas sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine was less effective, with several cases showing incomplete or resistant responses.
safety_summary: Mefloquine side-effects were mild and transient, including headache, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and diarrhoea; both groups showed satisfactory weight gain and rise in haemoglobin.

title: A double-blind comparative clinical trial of mefloquine and chloroquine in symptomatic falciparum malaria.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT of mefloquine vs chloroquine for symptomatic falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results on parasitaemia clearance, fever clearance, and tolerability.
population: male patients with symptomatic falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological response (S-type vs RI-type response) and rate of clearance of parasitaemia and fever
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and chloroquine were highly effective against symptomatic falciparum malaria, with chloroquine clearing parasitaemia marginally faster, and only one mefloquine-treated patient showing recrudescence despite in vitro drug sensitivity.
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated; mild and transient side-effects including nausea, vomiting, dizziness, loose stools, and pruritus were reported. Pruritus was more common with chloroquine, dizziness more common with mefloquine. No drug-induced alterations in haematological or biochemical profiles were observed.

title: A comparative trial of oral chloroquine and oral co-trimoxazole in vivax malaria in children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs co-trimoxazole) in children with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance, fever response, adverse effects).
population: children with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: clearance of parasitemia and fever
impact_summary: Chloroquine cleared parasitemia significantly faster than co-trimoxazole regimens, though fever resolution was similar for chloroquine and high-dose co-trimoxazole schedules.
p_value: significant (chloroquine vs co-trimoxazole for parasite clearance)
safety_summary: Gastrointestinal intolerance was more common with chloroquine; asymptomatic sulphonamide crystalluria occurred frequently with high-dose co-trimoxazole regimens.

title: An evaluation of co-trimoxazole in the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
journal: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing co-trimoxazole dosage schedules and chloroquine for P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitemia clearance, fever response, recrudescence).
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance and fever (pyrexia) response
impact_summary: Co-trimoxazole cleared parasites at similar rates to chloroquine, though fever resolved more slowly with the standard dose, and no recrudescences occurred within 60 days.
safety_summary: Not explicitly detailed; no adverse events reported in abstract.

title: Dexamethasone proves deleterious in cerebral malaria. A double-blind trial in 100 comatose patients.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results (mortality, coma duration, complications) evaluating a malaria treatment (dexamethasone in cerebral malaria) in humans.
population: comatose patients with cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: Mortality and time to full recovery of consciousness
impact_summary: High-dose dexamethasone did not reduce mortality but prolonged coma and increased complications compared with placebo in cerebral malaria patients.
safety_summary: Complications including pneumonia and gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 26 patients given dexamethasone versus 11 given placebo (P = 0.004); dexamethasone prolonged coma duration (P = 0.02).

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of acute malaria in children of Papua New Guinea. II. Plasmodium vivax.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs chloroquine) in children with reported outcome results (fever resolution, parasitemia clearance).
population: children with acute vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Time to fever resolution and time to clearance of parasitemia
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone resulted in slower fever resolution and significantly longer time to clearance of parasitemia compared to chloroquine-containing regimens.

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the treatment of acute malaria in children in Papua New Guinea. I. Plasmodium falciparum.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for acute malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (treatment failures at 28 days).
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus single-dose chloroquine
population: children with acute Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment failure at 28-day follow-up
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine treatment failed in 19.2% of children by day 28, with no added benefit from combining chloroquine, which instead increased vomiting.
transmission_setting: Malaria-endemic region with chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum, Madang, Papua New Guinea
safety_summary: Combination with chloroquine was associated with an increased incidence of vomiting compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.

title: A comparative trial of Mefloquine and Fansidar in the treatment of falciparum malaria: failure of Fansidar.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (Mefloquine vs Fansidar) with reported outcome results (parasitaemia cure rates over 28 days); not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (Fansidar two-tablet vs three-tablet regimens vs Mefloquine)
population: patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: parasitaemia clearance/cure over 28 days
impact_summary: Mefloquine cured nearly all patients, whereas Fansidar had very low cure rates (9.1% for two-tablet and 19.4% for three-tablet regimens), indicating drug resistance.

title: Single-dose treatment of falciparum malaria with mefloquine: field studies with different doses in semi-immune adults and children in Burma.
journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of mefloquine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (efficacy and safety data) in a primary malaria intervention population.
comparator: active comparator (different mefloquine doses: 20 vs 30 mg/kg in children; 750 vs 1000 mg in adults)
population: semi-immune children and adults carriers of Plasmodium falciparum
primary_outcome: Parasitological clearance and recrudescence rate after single-dose mefloquine treatment
impact_summary: Both lower and higher doses of mefloquine were equally effective in clearing P. falciparum infection in semi-immune children and adults, with the lower dose (20 mg/kg in children, 750 mg in adults) being sufficient and associated with less vomiting.
safety_summary: Nausea, giddiness, and vomiting were the most common adverse effects; vomiting was significantly more frequent in the higher-dose adult group; one patient who vomited was successfully retreated.

title: The treatment of malaria in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient patients in Sabah.
journal: Annals of tropical medicine and parasitology
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcomes on malaria treatment in a specific population (G6PD-deficient patients); primary purpose is malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficient malaria patients

title: Drug therapy for Plasmodium falciparum malaria resistant to pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine (Fansidar). A study of alternate regimens in Eastern Thailand, 1980.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing drug regimens for malaria treatment with reported cure/outcome results; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
comparator: quinine alone vs quinine plus fansidar vs quinine plus tetracycline
population: refugees with Plasmodium falciparum malaria resistant to pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine
primary_outcome: cure rate / parasite clearance after treatment
impact_summary: Quinine plus tetracycline cured all patients, while quinine alone failed to cure about one-third of patients and adding fansidar to quinine did not significantly improve cure rates.
effect_estimate: 100% with quinine plus tetracycline vs approximately 66% with quinine alone
transmission_setting: refugee camp, Thai-Kampuchean border, area with Fansidar-resistant malaria
safety_summary: Not specifically reported

title: [The influence of malaria chemoprophylaxis on health of a rural community in West Africa (author's transl)].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique et de ses filiales
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis in humans with reported outcome results (parasite rate, spleen rate, hematocrit), meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: rural village population, including children
primary_outcome: Malariometric indices (parasite rate, spleen rate) and hematocrit values before and after chemoprophylaxis
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis reduced parasite rate and spleen rate while increasing hematocrit values compared to placebo, preventing the seasonal worsening of these indices seen after the rainy season.
transmission_setting: stable and high endemic malaria, sudan savanna, seasonal (rainy season peak transmission)

title: Quinine alone versus quinine plus a pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine combination in the treatment of Plasmodium faliciparum cerebral malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing malaria treatment interventions in humans; not early-phase.
population: patients with severe chloroquine resistant Plasmodium falciparum cerebral malaria
primary_outcome: clinical response and outcome (mortality) of cerebral malaria treatment
impact_summary: Patients who received quinine plus pyrimethamine-sulfadoxine responded faster and had no deaths compared to those who received quinine alone, though the difference was not statistically significant.
safety_summary: No statistically significant adverse effects reported; combination therapy appeared safe with no deaths in that group.

title: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistant falciparum malaria in Thai children.
journal: The Southeast Asian journal of tropical medicine and public health
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial treatment (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and quinine) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results (clinical cure and drug resistance classification).
comparator: active comparator (different dose regimens of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, and quinine plus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitological cure/treatment failure classified as S (sensitive), RI, RII, or RIII response
impact_summary: Standard-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine showed high failure rates in Thai children, while combination with quinine achieved a substantially higher cure rate.
transmission_setting: Thailand, falciparum malaria endemic area with drug resistance
safety_summary: Not reported

title: In vivo and in vitro sensitivity of Falciparum malaria to quinine in Thai children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (quinine) in children with reported outcome results (treatment failures, serum levels, parasitological response).
population: children with Falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Treatment efficacy (parasitological response) of quinine in relation to in vitro sensitivity (MIC) and serum quinine levels
impact_summary: Quinine dosed either by fixed body weight or by body surface area produced similar treatment failures, and rising in vitro MIC suggests decreasing parasite sensitivity to quinine in Thailand.
safety_summary: No adverse events or safety data reported in the abstract.

title: The in vivo sensitivity of Plasmodium falciparum to chloroquine and to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine combination in Ibadan, Nigeria.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine vs. sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine) with reported outcome results (parasite clearance and fever resolution).
population: Nigerian children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and fever clearance following treatment, assessed by periodic blood film examination over 28 days
impact_summary: Both chloroquine and Fansidar rapidly cleared P. falciparum parasitemia and fever with no evidence of resistance to either drug over 28 days.

title: Chemosuppressive field trials in Thailand. IV. The suppression of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax parasitemias by mefloquine (WR 142,490, A 4-quinolinemethanol).
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of mefloquine chemoprevention for malaria in humans with reported outcome results (parasitemia suppression); not early-phase.
population: residents of an area highly endemic for chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum and P. vivax
primary_outcome: suppression/incidence of malaria parasitemia (P. falciparum and P. vivax infections)
impact_summary: Both mefloquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine greatly reduced falciparum infections, but mefloquine was more effective than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine at preventing vivax parasitemia.
transmission_setting: highly endemic, chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum area in northeastern Thailand

title: A clinical trial of malaria prophylaxis using a single dose of chloroquine at different intervals in an endemic malarious area.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (chloroquine prophylaxis) with reported outcome results in an endemic area.
population: residents of an endemic malarious area
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria infection with chloroquine given at different dosing intervals
impact_summary: Chloroquine prophylaxis given at intervals as long as 3 months significantly reduced malaria compared to control, with the drug possibly acting synergistically with acquired immunity.

title: A controlled trial of a combination of chloroquine with paracetamol in the treatment of acute malaria in a semi-immune population.
journal: The Journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine-based intervention) in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance).
comparator: chloroquine and paracetamol given as separate tablets
population: semi-immune patients with acute malaria
primary_outcome: parasite clearance and patient preference between prescription types
impact_summary: The fixed drug combination of chloroquine and paracetamol taken in one or two doses achieved faster parasite clearance than separate tablets given over 3 or more days, though no significant difference in preference was found between the groups.

title: Effect of primaquine on gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum in Thailand.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results on a malaria treatment intervention (primaquine efficacy on gametocytes) in humans with no early-phase exclusion stated.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum infection
primary_outcome: gametocyte carriage/clearance following primaquine administration
impact_summary: Primaquine reduced or affected gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum in treated patients in Thailand.

title: Evaluation of Potential Effect of Artemether - Lumefantrine and Malaria Drugs on Auditory Function
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported results (Phase 4) evaluating malaria drugs' effects on auditory function in malaria patients; results are posted.
population: Patients with falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With Auditory Abnormalities at Day 7 Assessed by Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) Wave III Latency Changes on Day 7(a Type of Hearing Test)
